title: The Great Pyramid of Giza Is Completed for Pharaoh Khufu
description: Standing 481 feet tall and the world's tallest human-made structure for more than 3,700 years, the Great Pyramid of Giza was built as Pharaoh Khufu’s tomb from an estimated 2.3 million stone blocks.
longFormSummary:
• The Great Pyramid is the tomb of Pharaoh Khufu, Fourth Dynasty, built c. 2600 BC over about 26 years
  • Originally 146.6 m (481 ft) tall, now 138.5 m after casing removal; the tallest human-made structure for more than 3,700 years
  • Built from about 2.3 million blocks weighing 6 million tonnes, with Aswan granite up to 80 tonnes in the King's Chamber
  • Attribution to Khufu rests on 1837 graffiti in the relieving chambers and the Diary of Merer found in 2013; it is the only Seven Wonders survivor largely intact
dateConfidenceReasoning: Britannica and multiple Egyptology sources place the Great Pyramid’s completion at approximately 2560 BCE, with no exact date recorded.

title: Neolithic Builders Raise Stonehenge’s Sarsen Circle
description: Around 2500 BCE, Neolithic Britons hauled 25-ton sarsen stones about 15 miles (25 km) to Salisbury Plain and raised them into the trilithons and circle known as Stonehenge.
longFormSummary:
• About 5,000 years ago Stonehenge was first built in the Neolithic; by about 2500 BC larger stones arrived, starting over 800 years of building and alteration into the Bronze Age
  • Around 2500 BC over 80 large sarsens were brought from the Marlborough Downs, 15 miles (25 km) away, and raised in two concentric arrangements, with bluestones set in a double arc between them
  • This followed the first Stonehenge of about 3000 BC: an earthwork enclosure about 100 m across with a ring of 56 timber or stone posts, used as a cremation cemetery; the Preseli Hills bluestones, over 150 miles away, may have arrived around then
  • Later phases: central bluestones rearranged into a circle and inner oval (2300-2200 BC) and the Avenue linking the site to the river Avon
dateConfidenceReasoning: English Heritage and Britannica date the erection of Stonehenge’s sarsen circle and trilithons to approximately 2500 BCE.

title: Ptolemy II Completes the Lighthouse of Alexandria
description: The Pharos of Alexandria, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, was completed under Ptolemy II to guide ships into the city's Great Harbor. Commissioned by Ptolemy I and built by the architect Sostratus of Cnidus, the tower stood for over 1,600 years.
longFormSummary:
• The Pharos lighthouse of Alexandria, one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, was commissioned by Ptolemy I Soter around 300 BCE (Wikipedia: after he declared himself king in 305 BC) and completed by Ptolemy II
  • Wikipedia dates construction to between 284 and 246 BC in Ptolemy II's reign, taking twelve years and costing 800 talents of silver; World History Encyclopedia says c. 300-280 BCE
  • Ancient sources credit the architect Sostratus of Cnidus, though he may have been only the financial backer
  • It stood over 100 metres tall (103 to 118 m per Wikipedia) with square, octagonal and round tiers and a statue of Zeus Soter or Poseidon on top
  • It stood over 1,600 years, damaged by three earthquakes between AD 956 and 1303, with the last stones used for the Citadel of Qaitbay in 1480
dateConfidenceReasoning: Ancient sources place completion under Ptolemy II around 280 BCE, per the World History Encyclopedia and Britannica; the exact year is not precisely recorded.

title: Qin Shi Huang Unifies China’s Border Walls Into the Great Wall
description: Around 220 BCE, China’s first emperor ordered the rival kingdoms’ old border walls linked into one defensive line, the earliest version of what became the Great Wall.
longFormSummary:
• Around 220 B.C. Qin Shi Huang had earlier walls joined into one system of more than 10,000 li, directed by general Meng Tian using soldiers, convicts and commoners
  • As many as 400,000 people reportedly died during construction
  • The Qin dynasty (221-206 BC) connected northern walls that were later the Great Wall, alongside standardised currency, measures and writing and a national road system
  • Most of the wall seen today was built under the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644)
dateConfidenceReasoning: History.com and the Qin dynasty's Wikipedia entry date Qin Shi Huang's order to join the northern border walls into one system to around 220 BCE, without a more precise date surviving.

title: Vesuvius Buries Pompeii and Herculaneum
description: Mount Vesuvius threw a column of superheated ash and gas 33 km into the sky, then collapsed it into pyroclastic surges that buried Pompeii and Herculaneum. The remains of more than 1,500 people have been recovered from the two towns.
longFormSummary:
• Vesuvius ejected tephra and gas to a height of 33 km, releasing 100,000 times the thermal energy of the Hiroshima and Nagasaki bombs. [S]
  • Pompeii and Herculaneum were buried under pyroclastic surges and ashfall; the combined population of the two towns was over 20,000 and the remains of more than 1,500 people have been found. [S]
  • Pliny the Younger, watching from Misenum, left the only detailed firsthand account, in two letters — which is why this style of eruption is called Plinian. [S]
  • The date is contested. Medieval manuscripts and a 2022 re-reading of Pliny support 24 August; autumnal fruit remains, heavy clothing on victims, a 2007 wind study and a charcoal inscription reading "the 16th day before the calends of November" point to October or November. [S]
  • The Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program records Vesuvius as an active stratovolcano with a long Holocene eruption history. [1]
dateConfidenceReasoning: The day is genuinely disputed: "The large majority of extant medieval manuscript copies ... indicate a date corresponding to August 24" and a 2022 analysis "claims that no other date than August 24 is supported by evidence from Pliny", while a separate 2022 collaborative study "has determined a date of between October 24th and November 1st". The traditional 24 August is taken here and flagged estimated.

references.title: Global Volcanism Program | Vesuvius
references.reasoning: The Smithsonian's Global Volcanism Program is the standing authority on the volcano's identity and eruption record; it confirms Vesuvius as the erupting edifice.

title: Angkor Wat, the Largest Religious Monument on Earth, is Completed for Suryavarman II
description: Cambodia's Khmer king Suryavarman II built Angkor Wat as his state temple and eventual mausoleum, a 400-acre complex whose construction ran from around 1122 to 1150 CE.
longFormSummary:
• Suryavarman II commissioned Angkor Wat as a state temple to Vishnu in Yasodharapura; construction commenced 1122 CE and was completed 1150 CE
  • It is generally considered intended as his mausoleum; work ceased after his death leaving some bas-relief unfinished
  • The site covers 162.6 hectares, is the largest religious complex in the world, and unusually faces west
  • It later became Buddhist (predominantly Theravada from the late 13th century) and is part of the Angkor UNESCO World Heritage Site (1992)
address: Angkor Wat, Krong Siem Reap, Cambodia
dateConfidenceReasoning: Wikipedia's Angkor Wat article states construction "commenced in 1122 CE and was completed in 1150 CE," a period-based estimate rather than a single confirmed day, consistent with other sources citing the reign of Suryavarman II (1113-1150).

title: Santa Maria della Salute Is Consecrated on Venice's Bed of a Million Piles
description: Venice's Baroque votive basilica, its foundations built on more than a million driven wooden piles in the lagoon mud, is consecrated by Patriarch Alvise Sagredo. The city still marks the day every November 21st as the Festa della Salute.
longFormSummary:
• Venice's Senate decreed a new church dedicated to the Virgin Mary on 22 October 1630, after a plague that killed nearly a third of the population
  • Baldassare Longhena won the design competition (11 entries, Senate vote 66 to 29) with an octagonal Baroque design on a platform of about 1,000,000 wooden piles
  • Construction took some 50 years; the post gives consecration as 21 November 1687, while Wikipedia's infobox gives consecration 1681 and completion 1687
  • Each 21 November the Festa della Madonna della Salute is marked, with officials crossing the Grand Canal from San Marco on a temporary pontoon bridge; Venice chose it as its local holiday
address: Basilica di Santa Maria della Salute, Punta della Dogana, Venice, Italy
dateConfidenceReasoning: Wikipedia and Venetian tourism histories date the consecration, by Patriarch Alvise Sagredo, to November 21, 1687 - still marked annually as the Festa della Salute.

title: The Great Lisbon Earthquake Destroys Lisbon
description: A magnitude 7.7-or-greater earthquake struck off Cape St. Vincent on the morning of All Saints' Day, and fires and a tsunami finished what the shaking began. Between 30,000 and 40,000 died in Lisbon alone.
longFormSummary:
• Seismologists estimate magnitude 7.7 or greater, with the epicentre in the Atlantic about 200 km west-southwest of Cape St. Vincent and 290 km southwest of Lisbon. [S]
  • The shaking, the fires that followed and a tsunami together almost completely destroyed Lisbon; the death toll in the city is put at 30,000-40,000, with perhaps 10,000 more in Morocco. [S]
  • It struck on the morning of All Saints' Day, when churches were full and lit with candles — a large part of why the fires spread as they did. [S]
  • This was the first earthquake studied scientifically for its effects across a wide area, and is credited with the birth of modern seismology and earthquake engineering. [S]
  • It was the third large earthquake known to have hit the city, after 1356 and 1531. [S]
dateConfidenceReasoning: The source dates it firmly — the earthquake "hit the Iberian Peninsula and Northwest Africa on the morning of Saturday, 1 November, Feast of All Saints, at around 09:40 local time". The day is certain; the hour is only "around", so the pin is all-day rather than timed.

title: Fenton, Murray and Wood Launches the Salamanca, the First Commercial Steam Locomotive
description: At the Round Foundry in Holbeck, Leeds, engineering firm Fenton, Murray and Wood built the Salamanca, the world's first commercially successful steam locomotive, which first ran publicly on 24 June 1812. Designed by Matthew Murray for John Blenkinsop's rack-and-pinion Middleton Railway, it hauled coal using a toothed rail system.
longFormSummary:
• The Salamanca was built in 1812 by Matthew Murray of Fenton, Murray and Wood in Holbeck for the Middleton Railway, and is called the first commercially successful steam locomotive
  • It was a rack and pinion locomotive using John Blenkinsop's patented toothed rail, and the first with two cylinders
  • It was named after Wellington's victory at the Battle of Salamanca in 1812, and could pull over 20 times its own weight
  • Four such locomotives were built; Salamanca was destroyed by a boiler explosion about six years later
  • The rack system was obsolete by the late 1830s as adhesion locomotives spread
address: 16 Foundry Street, Holbeck, Leeds LS11 5QP, UK
dateConfidenceReasoning: Wikipedia's Salamanca (locomotive) article and the Real Yorkshire Blog both date the locomotive's first public run to 24 June 1812.

title: Mount Tambora Erupts and Steals the Following Summer
description: The most powerful volcanic eruption in recorded history threw 37-45 cubic kilometres of rock into the atmosphere from Sumbawa. Its veil of ash cooled the planet enough to give 1816 the name the Year Without a Summer.
longFormSummary:
• The eruption rated VEI 7 and ejected 37-45 cubic kilometres of dense-rock equivalent material — the most recent confirmed VEI-7 eruption anywhere. [S]
  • Its climax came on 10 April 1815, though increased steaming and small phreatic eruptions went on for the next six months to three years. [S]
  • Ash dispersed worldwide and lowered global temperatures, producing the 1816 Year Without a Summer, extreme weather and harvest failures across many regions. [S]
  • Several climate forcings coincided and interacted in a way not seen after any other large eruption since the early Stone Age. [S]
  • The Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program holds Tambora's eruption record and confirms the 1815 event as its largest historical eruption. [1]
dateConfidenceReasoning: The source fixes the climax to the day: "the Mount Tambora eruption reached a violent climax on 10 April 1815", with smaller phreatic activity continuing for months afterwards.

references.title: Global Volcanism Program | Tambora
references.reasoning: The Smithsonian's eruption database is the authority for the volcano's identity and eruptive history behind the 1815 event.

title: Henraux Begins Quarrying Marble at Monte Altissimo
description: In 1821, landowner Marco Borrini and French businessman Jean-Baptiste Alexandre Henraux founded the Henraux marble company in Tuscany’s Apuan Alps. It still works the Monte Altissimo quarries first opened by Michelangelo in the 1500s and shown in Stone Men.
longFormSummary:
• In 1821 landowner Marco Borrini and Frenchman Jean Baptiste Alexandre Henraux started the quarrying company at Monte Altissimo in the Apuan Alps of Tuscany
  • Within a decade quarries rose from 11 to 132 and workers to 1,600
  • Michelangelo first understood the marble's potential in 1517 and built the first part of the road to the deposits
  • Altissimo marble was supplied for St Isaac's Cathedral in Saint Petersburg and to sculptor Hiram Powers, and used in the polychrome floors of St Peter's Basilica
  • Today Henraux owns the entire mountain, employs about 140 and works five active quarries; Saudi Binladin Group bought a large stake in 2014
dateConfidenceReasoning: Fondazione Henraux and Quarry Magazine both date the company's founding to 1821, but neither source gives a specific month or day.

title: Carr's Opens Its Carlisle Biscuit Works, Later Home to McVitie's
description: Jonathan Dodgson Carr founds a small bakery and biscuit factory in Carlisle, pioneering mass biscuit production. The site is still operating today as a McVitie's factory, the world's oldest continually-running biscuit works.
longFormSummary:
• Jonathan Dodgson Carr founded a small bakery and biscuit factory in Carlisle in 1831; it received a royal warrant in 1841 and within 15 years became Britain's largest baking business
  • Carr combined mill and bakery, making biscuits based on dry ship biscuits and shipping them by canal and railway; by 1885 the firm made 128 varieties with 1000 workers
  • Since 1972 the factory has been part of United Biscuits, officially McVitie's but still known locally as Carr's; United Biscuits is now within pladis
  • The Caldewgate factory flooded in 2005 and on 6 December 2015, the latter closing works for a month
address: 54 Church Street, Caldewgate, Carlisle, Cumbria CA2 5TG, United Kingdom
dateConfidenceReasoning: Wikipedia and Carr's own company histories date the founding of Jonathan Dodgson Carr's Carlisle bakery and biscuit factory to 1831, without a more precise day recorded.

title: Great Indian Peninsula Railway Runs India's First Passenger Train
description: On April 16, 1853, the Great Indian Peninsula Railway ran the first passenger train in India and Asia, carrying about 400 guests roughly 34km from Bombay's Bori Bunder to Thane.
longFormSummary:
• The customary first train in India left Bombay's Bori Bunder for Thane at 3:35pm on 16 April 1853, with 14 carriages and 400 guests, hauled by three locomotives to a 21-gun salute and taking an hour and fifteen minutes
  • The Great Indian Peninsula Railway ran India's first passenger line: the original 21 miles (33.8 km) between Bombay and Thane
  • The identity of the locomotives is still a subject of research per IRFCA, so the names of the engines are not settled
  • Dignitaries including Jagannath Shankarseth had already ridden the full Bombay-Thane line on 18 November 1852
  • The GIPR was incorporated on 1 August 1849; the first sod was turned at Sion on 30 October 1850, and it later folded into Central Railway in 1951
address: Bori Bunder (now Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus), Mumbai, India
dateConfidenceReasoning: Confirmed by IRFCA's Indian Railways history FAQ and multiple independent sources, which date India's first passenger train from Bori Bunder to Thane to April 16, 1853.

title: Metropolitan Railway Opens the World's First Underground Line
description: The Metropolitan Railway opened between Paddington and Farringdon on January 10, 1863, the world's first underground railway and the ancestor of every metro system shown in Moving Millions Every Day.
longFormSummary:
• Built by cut-and-cover methods starting in 1860, the Metropolitan Railway opened its first section between Paddington and Farringdon Street on January 10, 1863.
  • It was the world's first underground passenger railway, with steam locomotives hauling gas-lit wooden carriages through the tunnels.
  • The line carried about 38,000 passengers on its opening day and 9.5 million in its first year, proving underground travel could work at city scale.
  • Its success set the template later followed by the metro systems in London, New York, Tokyo, Paris and elsewhere that the documentary credits with shaping the modern commuter city.
address: Paddington to Farringdon, London, United Kingdom
dateConfidenceReasoning: The London Transport Museum and Britannica both date the Metropolitan Railway's opening between Paddington and Farringdon to January 10, 1863.

title: City of Paris Opens Its Sewers to Public Tours During the 1867 World's Fair
description: During the 1867 Exposition Universelle, Paris opened Baron Haussmann's newly rebuilt sewer network to public tours for the first time, turning Eugène Belgrand's engineering into a civic showcase.
longFormSummary:
• Guided visits of the Paris sewers began at the 1867 Exposition Universelle, the galleries having been raised in height so the public could visit
  • Eugène Belgrand, appointed by prefect Haussmann in 1854 to run the water service, became head director of Waters and Sewers in 1867 (to 1878) and had nine special wagonnets built for the visits
  • Context: in 1800 Paris had only 16 km of sewers for 550,000 people; cholera struck in 1832, 1849 and 1884; spring-water catchments began in 1865 and the network became complete in 1894
  • Visits continued as an educational route (1906-1939, electric wagons), became a museum in 1975, and the Musée des Égouts reopened on 23 October 2021 after a EUR 2 million renovation
dateConfidenceReasoning: The Paris sewer museum's own history page states tours "began in 1867, during the World's Fair" without naming an exact day, so the pin uses the Fair's opening date.

title: The Brooklyn Bridge Opens
description: New York's Brooklyn Bridge opened to the public, completing a 13-year construction effort that Emily Warren Roebling steered to completion after her husband was incapacitated by decompression sickness.
longFormSummary:
• The Brooklyn Bridge opened May 24, 1883, as the first fixed East River crossing and then the longest suspension bridge, with a 1,595-foot main span
  • The dedication was presided over by President Chester A. Arthur and Governor Grover Cleveland
  • John A. Roebling designed it and died of tetanus after a 1869 injury; son Washington Roebling became chief engineer
  • Caisson work caused decompression sickness in more than a hundred workers; Washington became bedridden in 1872 and Emily Warren Roebling effectively took over, receiving the first ride across
  • An estimated 250,000 people walked across within 24 hours; a stampede on May 30, 1883 killed at least twelve
address: Brooklyn Bridge, New York, NY, USA
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: "Brooklyn Bridge opens | May 24, 1883".

title: Krakatoa Explodes and Is Heard 4,800 km Away
description: The third explosion of 27 August 1883 destroyed over 70% of the island and remains the loudest sound in recorded history, audible in Perth and near Mauritius. The eruption and its tsunamis killed at least 36,417 people.
longFormSummary:
• Krakatoa erupted from 19 May to 21 October 1883; the climactic explosions of 27 August destroyed over 70% of the island, which collapsed into a caldera. [S]

title: The Galveston Hurricane Becomes the Deadliest US Disaster
description: A Category 4 hurricane drove a storm surge of over 15 ft across Galveston Island, killing between 6,000 and 12,000 people. It remains the deadliest natural disaster in United States history.
longFormSummary:

  • Most deaths came after a storm surge of over 15 ft inundated Galveston with 8 to 12 ft of water. [S]
  • The storm destroyed about 7,000 buildings including 3,636 demolished homes, and left roughly 10,000 people homeless out of a population under 38,000. [S]
  • It ended the Golden Era of Galveston: investors turned to Houston instead, and three engineers were commissioned to raise the island's shoreline by 17 ft and build a 10-mile seawall. [S]

  • The National Hurricane Center lists it among the defining hurricanes in US history. [1]

title: The Wright Flyer Makes the First Powered Aeroplane Flight

  • The brothers flew four times, taking turns; the second and third runs covered 175 and 200 feet, and Wilbur’s fourth flight took 59 seconds to cover 852 feet. [S]
  • The wind averaged more than 20 mph, so the launching rail was laid on level ground near camp instead of on the slope of Big Kill Devil Hill. [S]
  • The aircraft was damaged on landing and wrecked minutes later when gusts blew it over; it never flew again and is now displayed at the National Air and Space Museum. [S]

title: Boeing Completes the Maiden Flight of Its Model 314 Clipper

longFormSummary:
• The first Boeing Model 314 Clipper made its maiden flight on June 7, 1938, staying aloft over Puget Sound for 38 minutes
  • The pilot is named slightly differently by the two accounts - "test pilot Eddie Allen" in HistoryLink and "test pilot Edmund T. Allen" in Wikipedia - and the flight identified insufficient rudder control
  • There was no prototype: the production aircraft NX-18601 was launched into the Duwamish Waterway from Boeing's Plant 1 and towed to Elliott Bay, its wingspan barely clearing the bridge supports even turned diagonally, with taxiing trials beginning 3 June when Allen found it too lightly loaded
  • The aircraft came out of Pan American's February 1936 design competition - against Douglas, Consolidated, Martin and Sikorsky - for a 10,000 lb payload, minimum 2,400-mile range and 150 mph cruise at 10,000 ft
  • Boeing first decided not to bid until engineer Wellwood E. Beall drafted a design reusing the XB-15 bomber's wing with Wright R-2600 Twin Cyclone engines giving 50% more power than the XB-15's 850 hp units, at an estimated 40,000 lb weight and a 152 ft wingspan; Pan American awarded a $4.8 million contract on July 21, 1936 for six aircraft with an option for six more, and Boeing missed the delivery date by 13 months
  • Production figures agree on twelve built, with nine going to Pan Am; the type entered service in 1939 and was retired in 1951, the last surviving Clipper being scrapped that year after wartime service and obsolescence against faster postwar airliners
  • It was the first aircraft to carry a sitting American president, flying FDR to the Casablanca Conference in 1943
  • A Free Documentary episode calls it "the biggest airplane of the nineteen hundred thirties and the first to take passengers non-stop from the USA to Europe", "a gigantic floating body as a fuselage, combined with state-of-the-art wings from a military experimental aircraft", with a range of 5,900 km and a maximum speed of 320 km/h
  • Its cabin had "spacious sections with luxurious chairs as seats, a dining room in which the stewards serve a six course menu and even a honey moon suite", which with its engineering "make the B 314 famous all over the world"
  • The same day as the maiden flight, the Douglas DC-4E prototype also flew for the first time, in southern California

title: Krupp's Schwerer Gustav Railway Gun Bombards Sevastopol

title: The US Abandons Its Secret Ice City, Camp Century

title: The United States and China Issue the Shanghai Communiqué
description: At the end of Nixon's visit the two governments published a joint statement setting out, separately, what each believed about Taiwan.   • China affirmed that Taiwan is a part of China and opposed any attempt to create "two Chinas", "one China, one Taiwan", or an independent Taiwan

  • Washington also affirmed its interest in a peaceful settlement of the Taiwan question and its intention to withdraw the remaining US forces from Taiwan
  • Mao and Zhou made clear during the talks that China would not normalise relations while Washington recognised Taipei; normalisation waited another seven years

title: Citicorp Center's Secret Structural Fix Wraps Up
description: Engineers quietly finished weeks of overnight welding that fixed a hidden wind-bracing flaw in Manhattan's Citicorp Center, averting a possible collapse.
longFormSummary:
• The flaw was found in July 1978, during hurricane season, in the recently completed Citicorp Center; after investigation the building was judged in danger of possible collapse and workers "surreptitiously made repairs over the following months", welding under cover of darkness while the offices operated by day
  • The cause was an unapproved construction change: Bethlehem Steel proposed changing the chevron braces from welded to bolted joints to save money, which LeMessurier's office accepted without his knowledge
  • The two links quantify the danger differently but compatibly: one says that if the tuned mass damper lost power a 70 mph (110 km/h) quartering wind could topple the building, the other that winds strong enough occur in New York on average every 16 years - a 1-in-16 annual chance
  • Precautions during the retrofit included a backup generator and city evacuation plans; Hurricane Ella threatened while the work was under way but changed course
  • Neither link gives a completion date for the welding, only that it was done "within months" of July 1978, so the pin's end-of-October 1978 date is not stated by either wiki
  • The repair stayed secret for about seventeen years - kept until 1995, with a newspaper strike credited for keeping the story out of print until the mid-1990s; the pin's video source has chapters "The Secret Fix" and "Seventeen Years Later"
  • Students raised the question: Princeton undergraduate Diane Hartley investigated the building's integrity for quartering winds, and NJIT student Lee DeCarolis, whose professor John Zoldos had reservations, contacted LeMessurier; one link says two college students helped uncover the flaw, and the video is introduced as told "firsthand from the student who prevented it"
  • The building: a 59-storey tower at 601 Lexington Avenue designed by Hugh Stubbins with Emery Roth & Sons, dedicated 12 October 1977, 915 feet, costing $128 million, broken ground in 1974 and the tallest new New York skyscraper since the early 1930s
  • Its unconventional structure came from the holdout of St Peter's Lutheran Church at the northwest corner: a raised base on four offset stilts set under the centre of each face, diagonal chevron bracing dividing the tower into six independent segments, columns drilled about 50 feet into bedrock, and a roof tuned mass damper - a 400-ton concrete block on a film of oil, the first building to use active mechanical stabilization
  • A later NIST reassessment found the quartering wind loads were not the threat LeMessurier and Hartley thought, and recommended reevaluating whether the retrofit was warranted
  • Both the video and the CNN feature draw on Michael M. Greenburg's book "The Great Miscalculation: The Race to Save New York City's Citicorp Tower", and describe LeMessurier as having blown the whistle on himself

title: The United States and China Establish Diplomatic Relations

title: The Taiwan Relations Act Becomes Law
description: Three months after breaking relations with Taipei, Congress wrote the substitute into law: an unofficial relationship run through the American Institute in Taiwan, arms 'of a defensive character', and a declared US capacity to resist any resort to force against Taiwan. title: Mount St. Helens Blows Out Its North Face

title: Rocky Mountaineer Departs on Its First Journey from Vancouver
description: The Rocky Mountaineer's first scheduled luxury rail journey left Vancouver for the Canadian Rockies with 200 guests aboard, launching what became one of the world's most iconic train trips.
longFormSummary:
• Rocky Mountaineer's own 30th-anniversary post says the company's story "officially began on May 27, 1990, when we welcomed 200 excited guests onboard the first scheduled Rocky Mountaineer journey leaving Vancouver, British Columbia, bound for the Canadian Rockies", founded by Peter Armstrong. Destinology instead dates the first journey to 7 June 1990 with 72 passengers, and says the first season sold out
  • The founding idea was that the train "would only travel during the day, allowing guests to enjoy every moment of the ever-changing landscapes in daylight", with overnight hotel stays in mountain towns, glass-domed carriages and fine dining on board
  • Destinology sets the launch against the completion of the Canadian Pacific Railway's first transcontinental line in 1885, the decline of passenger rail in the 1980s and the interest in Western Canada sparked by Expo 86 in Vancouver
  • Early 1990s routes linked Vancouver with Jasper, Banff and Lake Louise; the company now runs four rail routes between Vancouver and Banff, Lake Louise and Jasper, Alberta
  • GoldLeaf Service, with bi-level glass-dome coaches, was introduced in 1995, and SilverLeaf Service, single-level coaches with over-sized windows and meals at the seat, "launched seventeen years later"
  • By its 30th anniversary the company counted "thousands of departures and more than two million guests" and calls itself "the largest privately held luxury tourist train company in the world"; in 2021 it added its first US route, Rockies to the Red Rocks, between Moab, Utah and Denver, Colorado
  • The Free Documentary episode rides what it calls "the Rocky Mountaineer, one of the world's most iconic rail adventures, as it carves its way across Western Canada", covering the spiralling tunnels and canyon bridges that made the route possible, seen "from the panoramic domes of the luxurious mountain train"

title: The Channel Tunnel Opens
description: The $15BN Channel Tunnel opened, linking Britain to mainland Europe by rail for the first time since the last Ice Age, after six years of construction under the English Channel.
longFormSummary:
• The Channel Tunnel was officially opened on May 6, 1994 in a ceremony led by Queen Elizabeth II and French President François Mitterrand, connecting Britain to the mainland "for the first time since the Ice Age"
  • It links Folkestone in England with Coquelles in France and is the only fixed link between Great Britain and the European mainland
  • The two sources measure it slightly differently: History.com gives 31 miles end to end with 23 miles under water at an average depth of 150 feet below the seabed, while Wikipedia gives 50.46 km (31.35 miles) with a 37.9 km (23.5 mile) underwater section, 75 m below sea level and averaging 45 m below the seabed - the longest underwater section of any tunnel and the third-longest railway tunnel in the world
  • Cost is stated three different ways: History.com says about $16 billion, roughly twice the original estimate and a year behind schedule; Wikipedia gives a final cost of £4.65 billion (equivalent to £9.8 billion in 2025); and the B1M video's cited research includes an Independent piece headlined "12 billion pounds under the sea"
  • Start of construction is also given two ways - History.com says the tunnels were begun in June 1988 and Wikipedia's timeline has tunnelling starting in France in June 1988, but its infobox dates the work's beginning to 1 December 1987
  • The build ran as two single-track running tunnels 7.6 m wide plus a 4.8 m service tunnel with 270 cross passages, electrified at 25 kV AC, designed for 200 km/h but limited to 160 km/h for safety; the engineer was TransManche Link and the modern project was initiated by Eurotunnel in 1988
  • Human cost and scale: 15,000 people were employed at peak and ten were killed during construction
  • Opening cut the crossing to 35 minutes and London-Paris eventually to two and a half hours, carrying about 30,000 people, 6,000 cars and 3,500 trucks a day
  • The service tunnel broke through in December 1990; freight trains followed in June 1994 and passenger trains in November 1994
  • Early operation was difficult: Eurotunnel announced a huge loss one year into service and was saved by a debt-for-shares swap before its first net profit in 1999, and freight was suspended for six months after a lorry fire in November 1996
  • The idea long predates the build - Albert Mathieu's 1802 proposal, Thôme de Gamond's surveys from 1839, Colonel Beaumont's mile of bore in 1880, and British and French machines driving 1,840 m and 1,669 m before abandonment in 1883 over invasion fears; a UK-France scheme was cancelled in January 1975 and the Treaty of Canterbury signed in February 1986
  • The ASCE named it one of the Seven Wonders of the Modern World in 1996, and The B1M's 2024-01-17 film, published as "the seventh wonder of the modern world, the Channel Tunnel, turns 30 this year", calls it the world's longest undersea link
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: the tunnel "was officially opened on May 6, 1994," presided over by Queen Elizabeth II and President Mitterrand.

title: Lesotho Delivers Its First Water to South Africa

longFormSummary:
• Katse Dam is a 185 m, 710 m long concrete double-curvature arch dam on the Malibamatso River in Lesotho, completed in 1996 with its reservoir filled by 1997
  • It is part of the Lesotho Highlands Water Project (LHWP), established by the 1986 Treaty between Lesotho and South Africa to supply water to Gauteng and generate hydro-electricity for Lesotho; the World Bank arranged the treaty
  • Water flows through a 45 km, 4 m diameter tunnel and by gravity to South Africa; delivery began on 22 January 1998, supplying about 30 m3/s
  • South Africa pays Lesotho $35 million a year plus a variable royalty, and the total project cost is put at US$8 billion

  • Impacts include induced seismicity, displaced farmers and a corruption scandal with convictions

title: Clinton Signs Permanent Normal Trade Relations With China
description: Public Law 106-286 ended the annual congressional fight over China's trade status and cleared the last American obstacle to its entry into the WTO. It is the single act that opened the United States market to Chinese manufacturing on permanent terms.
longFormSummary:
• H.R. 4444 became Public Law 106-286 on 10 October 2000: an Act "to authorize extension of nondiscriminatory treatment (normal trade relations treatment) to the People's Republic of China, and to establish a framework for relations between the United States and the People's Republic of China"
  • Division A ends the application of chapter 1 of title IV of the Trade Act of 1974 — the Jackson-Vanik annual review — to China, which is what made the treatment permanent rather than yearly
  • It takes effect on the day China accedes to the World Trade Organization, so the statute waited on Geneva rather than the other way round
  • Division B sets up the Congressional-Executive Commission on the People's Republic of China to report annually on human rights and the rule of law, and provides relief from market disruption
  • Without it China's WTO accession would have obliged the United States to invoke the non-application clause; with it, American tariffs on Chinese goods became bound and predictable
address: The White House, 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue NW, Washington, DC, United States
dateConfidenceReasoning: The Statutes at Large text carries the note "Oct. 10, 2000 - [H.R. 4444]" against the enacting clause of Public Law 106-286.

title: BHP Iron Ore Sets the World Record for Longest, Heaviest Freight Train

title: China Joins the World Trade Organization
description: China became the WTO's 143rd member on 11 December 2001, fifteen years after applying. Its export share of world trade roughly quadrupled over the next two decades, and the bargain struck in Doha is still what the tariff argument is about.
longFormSummary:
• The WTO records simply that "China has been a member of WTO since 11 December 2001"
  • The Ministerial Conference at Doha had approved the accession by consensus on 10 November 2001, adopting the Working Party report, the protocol of accession and China's schedule of market-access commitments on goods and services
  • Membership took legal effect 30 days after China notified the WTO that its parliament had ratified the agreement
  • Director-General Mike Moore called it "an historic moment for the WTO, for China and for international economic cooperation"
  • Shi Guangsheng, China's Minister of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation, used the moment to argue for "equal participation and consultation" in writing the trade rules of the new century
  • The accession negotiation had run since 1986 and required the United States to grant permanent normal trade relations first, which Congress did in October 2000

title: The 2003 Heat Wave Kills More Than 70,000 Europeans
description: Europe had its hottest summer since at least 1540, with night temperatures staying above 30C and eight consecutive days over 40C in Auxerre. The death toll has been estimated at more than 70,000.
longFormSummary:
• The 2003 heat wave gave Europe its hottest summer recorded since at least 1540, with Spain, France and Italy hit especially hard. [S]
  • The death toll has been estimated at more than 70,000. [S]
  • 1 August 2003 was the hottest day in centuries, with night temperatures well above 30 C, and temperatures stayed at record highs even at night, breaking the usual cooling cycle. [S]
  • Eight consecutive days above 40 C were recorded at Auxerre in Yonne in early August 2003; Amareleja in Portugal reached as high as 47 C. [S]
  • The heat combined with drought to create a crop shortfall in parts of southern Europe and health crises in several countries. [S]
  • The predominant heat fell in July and August, partly from western Europe's seasonal lag and hot continental air driven by strong southerly winds. [S]

title: EMEC Opens Its Billia Croo Wave Test Site Near Stromness

longFormSummary:

title: Egypt Opens the Mubarak Pumping Station on the Toshka Project
description: The world's largest pumping station begins lifting water from Lake Nasser into the Sheikh Zayed Canal, launching Egypt's attempt to grow a second Nile valley 310 km into the Sahara.
longFormSummary:
• The Mubarak Pumping Station was inaugurated in March 2005, lifting water from Lake Nasser behind the Aswan High Dam into the Sheikh Zayed Canal, which runs west into the Sahara
  • The station cost $436 million, sits in the lake surrounded by water, and holds 24 vertical pumps - 18 running, 3 for maintenance and 3 in reserve - drawing through a 50 m deep intake channel at a capacity of 1.2 million m³ of water per hour
  • Its engineering used steel mini-piles, chosen as cost-effective and earthquake-resistant, and a jointless underwater design watertight from 0 to 50 C; ASCE named it one of the five most outstanding civil engineering achievements of 2005, with design by a Hamza Associates/Lahmeyer joint venture and construction by Arabian International, Skanska and Hitachi
  • The canal it feeds is about 30 m wide and named for Sheikh Zayed al Nahyan, reflecting UAE financial backing
  • The intended route runs 310 km from an inlet 8 km north of Toshka Bay west along the Darb el-Arbe'ien route and then north to Baris Oasis; as of April 2012 it was still 60 km short
  • Sources give the scheme's target differently: Wikipedia says the pumping station was intended to transform 2,340 km² (588,000 acres) of desert into farmland, while Bright Hub says Toshka aimed to turn half a million acres arable by 2020, house over three million residents and add 10% to Egypt's arable land
  • They also date the project's start differently - Wikipedia says construction began in 1997 when the government decided to develop a "new valley" for agricultural and industrial communities, while Bright Hub says the project was approved in 1997 and "inaugurated Jan. 9, 1997 by President Mubarak"
  • The case for the scheme is demographic: "around 95% of Egyptians live on roughly 5% of Egypt's land", packed into a green strip a few kilometres wide, and "the population keeps growing. The green strip does not"
  • Results have fallen well short: by April 2012 "the only objective met" was diverting water into the small Sheikh Zayed Canal built, with high salinity, underground aquifers and clay soils stalling irrigation machines, and "actual delivery has come in far below those targets, over a much longer timeline, at very high cost", with private investors hard to persuade to farm the remote desert
  • The deeper objection the documentary sets out is that "digging a river into the Sahara does not create new water" - it relocates already-allocated Nile water into a desert with extreme evaporation, in a country whose Nile share is fixed by agreement and increasingly contested as upstream nations build dams
  • The project was later revived by President el-Sisi, with half the land to go to college graduates at one acre each, funded by the Long Live Egypt Fund, after a 2011 period in which Mubarak's overthrow, controversy over his holdings and a land dispute with Saudi Kingdom Holdings paused development and made the 2020 completion "a serious challenge"
  • Construction began in the 1990s and "is still underway today" as of the September 2026 documentary; the Toshka Lakes are a by-product of Lake Nasser's rise rather than a project output
dateConfidenceReasoning: Sources agree the Mubarak Pumping Station "was inaugurated in March 2005"; no source gives the exact day, so this pin is dated to the start of that month.

description: At 397 metres long and able to carry roughly 14,770 TEU, Emma Maersk was the largest container ship in the world when she entered service in 2006. Built by Odense Steel Shipyard, she led Maersk's E-class fleet with one of the largest diesel engines ever installed on a ship.

  • She held the record until sister ship Ebba Mærsk carried 15,011 TEU in May 2010; Maersk ordered 18,000-container Triple E ships in February 2011
  • In February 2013 a damaged stern thruster flooded part of the ship in the Suez Canal; after a DKK 250 million repair she returned to service in August 2013

title: Samsø Reaches 100% Renewable Energy as Denmark's Model Island

title: SNCF's V150 TGV Sets the World Rail Speed Record at 574.8 km/h

  • The programme ran over 200 hours of tests and 3,200 km, with 40 runs above 450 km/h

title: China's $1BN Skyscraper Mistake

title: Ciudad Real Central Airport Opens South of Madrid
description: A privately financed airport built to rival Madrid-Barajas opened near Ciudad Real in December 2008, before closing within four years as one of Spain's most notorious infrastructure failures.
longFormSummary:
• Ciudad Real Central Airport, Spain's first private international airport, cost about EUR 1.1 billion; the pin dates opening to December 2008 while Wikipedia says it opened in 2009 after a four-year delay from 2004 caused by its siting in a bird protection area and volcanic field
  • It had a 4,100 m runway able to take the A380 and a terminal designed for two million passengers a year, but the planned high-speed rail station was never built despite a 300 m footbridge
  • Flights were sparse (Air Berlin, Air Nostrum, Ryanair from June to November 2010, Vueling to October 2011) and all operations shut by 13 April 2012
  • Failure factors included Madrid Barajas's 2006 expansion, Spain's financial crisis and the collapse of main shareholder Caja Castilla-La Mancha
  • It went into administration with debts of EUR 529 million; in July 2015 a Chinese-led consortium (Tzaneen International) was the only bidder at EUR 10,000 in an auction whose asking price had fallen from EUR 100m to EUR 40m; it reopened in September 2019 without scheduled passenger traffic
address: Ciudad Real Central Airport, Ciudad Real, Castilla-La Mancha, Spain
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: "Opened in 2008, the airport shut down just four years later."

title: The Boeing 787 Dreamliner Makes Its Maiden Flight
description: N787BA lifted off from Paine Field at 10:27 am PST and landed three hours later at Boeing Field, reaching 180 knots and 13,200 feet. The first airliner with a primarily composite airframe flew more than two years later than Boeing first promised.
longFormSummary:
• Boeing conducted the 787-8 maiden flight from Paine Field in Everett on 15 December 2009 at 10:27 am PST, landing three hours later at Boeing Field. [S]
  • The flight reached a top speed of 180 knots and a maximum altitude of 13,200 feet. [S]
  • Boeing had planned the first flight by the end of August 2007 and premiered the aircraft, registered N787BA, at a rollout on 8 July 2007 with its major systems not yet installed. [S]
  • Five announced delays followed, including incorrect fastener installation and a machinists’ strike; on 23 June 2009 the flight was postponed again for structural reasons. [S]
  • The 787 was the first production airliner built with a fuselage of one-piece composite barrel sections instead of fastened aluminium sheet. [S]
  • Type certification came in August 2011 and the first 787-8 entered service with All Nippon Airways in October 2011. [S]
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per en.wikipedia.org: "On December 15, 2009, Boeing conducted the 787-8 maiden flight from Paine Field in Everett, Washington, at 10:27 am PST."
delayReasoning: Stated: Boeing planned the first flight by the end of August 2007 and rolled the aircraft out on 8 July 2007, but five announced delays – a fourth in April 2008 moving it to Q4 2008, a fifth in November 2008 over incorrect fastener installation and the machinists’ strike, then Q2 2009 and a June 2009 postponement for structural reasons – pushed the maiden flight to 15 December 2009.

title: Emaar Properties Opens Burj Khalifa as the World's Tallest Building
description: Emaar Properties officially opened the 828-meter Burj Khalifa in Dubai, timed to the fifth anniversary of Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum's accession to power. The tower took the world's-tallest-building title from Taipei 101 by a record margin.
longFormSummary:
• Burj Khalifa officially opened on January 4, 2010 in Dubai, developed by Emaar Properties, at a height of 828 m (2,716 ft 6 in)
  • The margin over the previous record holders was unusually large: Taipei 101 stood at 508 m when completed in 2003 and the Petronas Towers at 451.9 m in March 1996, and fifteen years on Burj Khalifa was still "over 200 metres taller than the Shanghai Tower"
  • The tower grew enormously during design - first drawn at 518 metres, then extended by 310 metres - before construction began on 21 September 2004, with the exterior completed on 1 October 2009
  • The build took six years, 22 million man-hours and more than 12,000 workers at an estimated $1.5 billion, using more than 330,000 cubic metres of concrete, 39,000 tonnes of steel reinforcement, 103,000 square metres of glass and almost 26,000 hand-cut glass panels, on a concrete raft carried by 192 piles reaching 50 metres into the ground
  • Adrian Smith of Skidmore, Owings & Merrill led the design, taking inspiration from the Hymenocallis or spider lily and Islamic architecture for the triple-lobed footprint and spiralling setbacks; the Y-shaped cross section reduces wind effects and the tower can move about 1.5 metres in any direction
  • It set a cluster of records alongside the height: highest occupied floor at level 160, highest outdoor observation deck at 555 m, highest restaurant at 441.3 m and the longest single lift shaft, with lifts running at up to 10 m per second and reaching the 124th floor in under a minute
  • Other figures: the spire alone is 200 metres and visible from up to 95 km, the building uses 946,000 litres of water daily and carries 378 solar panels, and cleaning it top to bottom takes about three months
  • It sits within the 2 km² (490-acre) Downtown Dubai development
  • A Free Documentary episode pitting it against the Empire State Building describes it as "the world's tallest skyscraper and the tallest building on earth" which "at eight hundred and twenty-eight metres... breaks every record - by a huge margin" and is "more like a vertical city, than just a skyscraper", against a 443-metre Empire State Building that held the title for more than forty years
  • None of the wikis mention the accession anniversary the pin ties the opening date to
address: 1 Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Blvd, Dubai, UAE
dateConfidenceReasoning: Guinness World Records and The National both confirm the official opening ceremony took place on January 4, 2010.

title: Eyjafjallajokull's Ash Cloud Closes European Airspace

title: China's Ministry of Commerce Cuts Rare Earth Export Quotas by 72%
description: China's Ministry of Commerce slashed its second-half 2010 rare earth export quotas by 72%, tightening its grip on the roughly 97% of global rare earth supply it mined at the time. The move, framed as an environmental crackdown on unregulated mining, sent rare earth prices soaring within days.
longFormSummary:
• On July 9, 2010, China's Ministry of Commerce announced it would cut rare earth export quotas by 72% for the second half of the year, capping shipments at 7,976 metric tons versus 28,417 tons for the same period a year earlier.
  • China mined an estimated 97% of the world's rare earth elements at the time, giving Beijing outsized leverage over materials used in smartphones, wind turbines, touch screens, and hybrid vehicles.
  • Officials framed the cut as an effort to curb environmental damage, destroyed landscapes, and radioactive residues from unregulated mining, while also reserving more material for domestic industry.
  • Prices for some rare earth metals spiked by as much as 1,000% within days, alarming electronics and clean-energy manufacturers abroad and triggering a global scramble for alternative supplies.

title: Japan Decides to Wall Off Its Coast After the Tōhoku Tsunami

title: Ryugyong Hotel's Exterior Finally Completed After 24 Years
description: Egyptian contractor Orascom finished cladding Pyongyang's pyramid-shaped Ryugyong Hotel in glass in July 2011, ending a stop-start construction saga that began in 1987 — though the 330-metre tower has never opened to a single guest.
longFormSummary:
• Construction of the 330 m, 105-floor pyramid Ryugyong Hotel in Pyongyang began on 28 August 1987, aiming to be the world's tallest hotel
  • Work stopped in 1992 amid North Korea's economic crisis after the Soviet collapse, leaving an unclad concrete shell for over a decade
  • Egyptian company Orascom restarted work in 2008 on the exterior cladding, and the exterior was completed on 14 July 2011 before construction ceased again with no opening date
  • Planned openings in 2012 and 2013 were not met; in 2018 the facade was fitted with LED panels showing propaganda animations, and as of 2019 the interior was still awaiting fitting
  • Cost was estimated by Japanese newspapers at $750 million (about 2 percent of North Korea's GDP)

title: Sinovel Installs China's First 5-Megawatt Offshore Wind Turbine at Donghai Bridge
description: Sinovel completed installation of the SL5000, China's first independently developed 5-megawatt offshore wind turbine, as a single demonstration unit at the Donghai Bridge wind farm near Shanghai. title: Tokyo Skytree Opens to the Public

title: Sany Opens Its Lingang Excavator Factory Near Shanghai
description: Sany opened its $818 million Lingang facility near Shanghai, calling it the world's largest excavator factory. Automated underground tunnels move structures and components through 5.9 million square feet of production space.
longFormSummary:
• Sany opened what it calls the world's largest and most advanced excavator plant near Shanghai, reported on 24 August 2012 - the date the pin carries
  • Cost $818.5 million, with computerized production management running from raw steel plate to final assembly
  • The plant mainly builds 20-ton to 30-ton excavators, and parts move automatically through underground tunnels
  • The two sources give different throughput and cost: the 2012 report says the factory can produce an excavator every five minutes at $818.5 million, while the later documentary says "1,600 specialists ensure a breathtaking output: theoretically every ten minutes a new excavator can roll off the production line" and that "for half a billion euros, the construction machinery giant has built the mega factory"
  • The documentary's size figure is also not usable: it states "1000 square meters of production area, equipped with high-tech machines of the latest generation", far below the 5.9 million square feet in the pin, which neither wiki supports
  • The site includes 43,000 sq ft of gardens, pools, bamboo and marble patios
  • Production halls use the latest generation of robots which "process up to 250 tons of steel every day"; in the welding plant "twenty-four workers were replaced by thirty-two robots. They do the work in half the time", described as more precise, safer and more cost-effective long term
  • The plant's mid-range top-seller is the SY215, priced at "one hundred and ten thousand euros" and "cheaper than any competitor model from Europe or United States"; the 23-tonne machine is produced "in just twenty-four working hours", and its "blackbox" sends recorded vehicle data to the control centre in China in real time
  • At the "marriage section" the "heavily swaying, twelve-tonne upper part has to be moved with millimetre precision onto the narrow slewing ring", with ten minutes allowed at that station
  • Sany America chairman Tim Frank said the team produces almost as many excavators yearly as are sold in the US by all manufacturers combined, with base excavator kits shipped to Sany America's assembly facility in Peachtree City, Georgia
address: SANY Lingang Industrial Park, Pudong, Shanghai, China
dateConfidenceReasoning: Multiple contemporaneous trade-press reports (Equipment World, Construction Equipment Guide, OEM Off-Highway) independently give 24 August 2012 as the opening date of the Lingang factory.

title: Makkah Royal Clock Tower Completes
description: The $16BN Makkah Royal Clock Tower, holding the world's largest clock face and the highest occupied space on Earth at the time, was completed overlooking Islam's holiest site.
longFormSummary:
• The Makkah Royal Clock Tower, part of the Abraj Al Bait complex 300 m from the Great Mosque, rises to 601 m and is the world's tallest clock tower with the largest clock faces
  • Construction ran from 2002 to 2011 and it opened in 2012, built by Saudi Binladin Group with SL Rasch and Dar Al-Handasah as architects and engineers
  • Cost is given as US$15 billion by Wikipedia and about $16 billion by The B1M
  • The tower has the highest occupied man-made space (a prayer room at 600 m, above Burj Khalifa's 585 m), and the clock is 35 times the size of Big Ben
  • The hotel was originally planned at 450 m and extended to 600 m mid-construction, so engineers used a lightweight steel and concrete framework limiting weight to 82,000 tonnes
  • Firms from over ten countries worked on it, and some non-Muslim glazing experts converted to Islam to work on site in Mecca
  • The facade uses 98 million mosaic glass tiles, a third with 24-carat gold leaf, and the clock face is lit by over 2 million LEDs
address: Makkah Royal Clock Tower, Mecca, Saudi Arabia
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: the tower, "constructed at an estimated cost of USD $16BN," was completed in 2012.

title: Eko Atlantic Officially Launched in Lagos

  • Eko Atlantic is a planned city on land reclaimed from the Atlantic Ocean in front of Bar Beach, aimed at stopping erosion of the Lagos coastline

title: Maasvlakte 2 Opens as the Port of Rotterdam’s Newest Extension
description: Rotterdam's man-made Maasvlakte 2 extension, built to keep Europe's largest port ahead of rising container traffic, officially opened for shipping on 22 May 2013.
longFormSummary:
• Maasvlakte 2 was officially opened for shipping on 22 May 2013 by Dutch infrastructure minister Melanie Schultz van Haegen, who said the port grows 20 percent larger and container capacity doubles
  • About 2,000 hectares were reclaimed behind a 4 km dike, roughly 1,000 hectares for port-related industry; sand work began in 2008 by PUMA, a Boskalis and Van Oord venture, and sea defences were finished in July 2012
  • Cost was about EUR 1.55 billion, EUR 150 million under the estimate, with the EUR 200 million contingency untouched
  • APM Terminals and Rotterdam World Gateway began building terminals in 2012; the APM terminal opened in April 2015
  • It is the biggest Dutch civil engineering project since the Delta Works
dateConfidenceReasoning: Dutch Water Sector's report on Maasvlakte 2 states the extension was officially opened for shipping on 22 May 2013.

title: Windows 8.1 Release Date

longFormSummary:

  • Microsoft's own release of Oct. 17, 2013 confirmed global availability that day: a free download from the Windows Store in more than 230 markets and 37 languages, with new devices and boxed software from Oct. 18
  • The update arrived "just before Windows 8 celebrates its 1-year anniversary"
  • Bing features run through the release: Bing Smart Search, built-in Bing apps including Bing Food & Drink, and a redesigned Windows Store with a New & Rising category and Bing recommendations, alongside tighter Bing integration generally
  • The headline interface changes were the option to boot directly to the desktop instead of the Start screen and the return of the Start button, dropped in Windows 8 in favour of the search charm and hot corners, plus a customisable Start screen with variable tile sizes, an apps view and a Help + Tips app
  • Other additions: Internet Explorer 11 with synced history and favorites, deeper SkyDrive integration, up to four apps side by side with improved multimonitor support, automatic app updates, and native 3-D printing support - announced in late June 2013, with Microsoft's Shanen Boettcher saying "making a 3D object on your PC will be as easy as writing a document in Word and sending it to print"
  • Named new or updated apps included Skype, Mail, Xbox Video, Xbox Music, Evernote, Facebook for Windows 8.1, Hulu Plus, Adobe Photoshop Express, eBay, Netflix, NOOK and Fresh Paint
  • Windows 8.1 Enterprise added virtual desktop infrastructure support and DirectAccess, conformed to OMA-DM standards and offered device lockdown, encryption and selective wipe of corporate data without touching personal data
  • New touch-enabled devices, tablets, 2-in-1s and laptops were expected through the holiday season, with existing hardware such as Microsoft's Surface and Lenovo's Yoga 11S in line for the upgrade

title: Typhoon Haiyan Makes Landfall at Guiuan

title: Five Pacific islands lost to rising seas as climate change hits
description: Using time series aerial and satellite imagery from 1947 to 2014 of 33 islands, along with historical insight from local knowledge, we have identified five vegetated reef islands that have vanished over this time period and a further six islands experiencing severe shoreline recession.
longFormSummary:
• A study in Environmental Research Letters (published 6 May 2016) analysed aerial and satellite imagery from 1947 to 2014 of 33 Solomon Islands reef islands together with local knowledge
  • Five vegetated reef islands vanished entirely and six more suffered severe shoreline recession; the lost islands were one to five hectares with vegetation at least 300 years old
  • Recession destroyed villages that had existed since at least 1935 at two sites, forcing relocations; Nuatambu Island lost over half its habitable area, with 11 houses lost since 2011
  • Wave exposure amplified sea-level rise: Isabel island loss rates rose from 0.1% a year (1947-1962) to 1.9% (2002-2014), while the sheltered Roviana lagoon saw little change
  • Solomon Islands sea level has risen 7-10 mm a year since about 1993, almost three times the global average; the authors call it the first scientific evidence of such island loss in the Pacific
  • Relocations were largely ad hoc with little government or climate-fund help; Taro, capital of Choiseul Province, is set to become the first provincial capital to relocate because of sea-level rise

title: Microsoft overhauls Windows 8.1 Store today, makes finding things easier (and handsomer)
description: The persistent navigation bar is a welcomed change. Previously, users had to swipe down from the top to access it, and while it was much better in 8.1, discoverability was an issue. Now, the green bar will always be there for users. In addition, it highlights Top charts, Categories and Collections, which should go a long, long way in making it easier to find new apps and games.
longFormSummary:
• On Tuesday 13 May 2014 Microsoft pushed out an update to the Windows 8.1 Store, concentrating on usability, mouse and keyboard users and "some parity with Windows Phone"; the four main changes were detailed the same day on the Windows Experience Blog by Brandon LeBlanc, and Microsoft's support article documents the same update for Windows 8.1 (Enterprise, Pro), Windows RT 8.1 and Windows Server 2012 R2
  • A persistent navigation bar now carries Top charts, Categories and Collections, where previously users had to swipe down from the top (or right-click) to reach it - "Now, the green bar will always be there for users"; the support article lists the bar's entries as Top Free, Top Paid, Top Grossing, Best Rated, Picks for You, Collections and account info
  • Collections, part of the Windows Phone Store since 8.0, come to the Windows 8.1 Store landing page, curated by a team of experts - a Getting Started Collection, theme collections for music, travel and sports, and Red Stripe Deals, where 6 top apps and games are discounted at least 50% each week; the support article adds a new Collections page, collections in search results and an "Install All" option for certain collections
  • Multiple Featured titles are grouped on the landing page, bringing "new, trending and rising stars" forward, and on-sale titles "will have a strike-through of the original price with the sale price in red"; discount and promotional pricing and expiry now also appear on the home page, in search results, in lists, on description pages and next to the Buy button
  • Apps can be bought once and downloaded on compatible Windows devices: the Windows/Windows Phone icon marking an app or game as also available on Windows Phone was in the web store but missing from the Store app, and "That has now been remedied"; the support article calls this the universal apps badge for apps bought once and usable on both Windows 8.1 and Windows Phone 8.1
  • Further changes in the support article: larger screenshots and identified hardware requirements on app description pages, improved post-acquisition recommendations, a privacy shortcut in the charms, and hardware targeting that filters touch-required apps out of the live tile, Spotlight and Picks for You on non-touch PCs with a warning when one is selected; the same update improves the Windows Update client, adding SleepStudy diagnostics, performance and resiliency work and authenticated proxy support
  • The update followed the Windows 8.1 "spring update" of the previous month, which improved things for traditional mouse and keyboard users and pinned the Store to the taskbar by default; a Start Menu revamp was "expected" later that fall
  • To get it: Settings > Change PC Settings > Update & Recovery > Check Now - "Like all 'live' updates, it can take some time before your server sees it, so just don't be surprised if it takes a few hours"

title: 24 Hours of Le Mans 2014
description: Noteworthy: Nissan ZEOD RC is a hybrid electric racing car with a chassis similar in design to the DeltaWing. Porsche's brand new LMP1.
longFormSummary:
• The 82nd 24 Hours of Le Mans was run at the Circuit de la Sarthe as the third round of eight in the 2014 FIA World Endurance Championship, organised by the ACO
  • Sources date the event differently: Wikipedia gives the meeting as 11 to 15 June 2014 with the race itself on 14-15 June, the Motor Sport database entry lists a single date of Saturday, June 14, 2014, and the ACO report is dated 15/06/2014 - all earlier than the pin's 13-16 June span; the schedule had been moved forward a week to avoid clashes with other series
  • Audi Sport Team Joest's No.2 R18 e-tron quattro of Marcel Fassler, Andre Lotterer and Benoit Treluyer won, the trio's third Le Mans after 2011 and 2012 and Audi's thirteenth victory
  • The sister No.1 Audi of Tom Kristensen, Marc Gene and Lucas di Grassi finished second, three laps down after turbocharger replacements, with the Toyota TS040 Hybrid of Davidson, Buemi and Lapierre third and Rebellion fourth
  • The race turned on retirements: a downpour on the Mulsanne Straight about 90 minutes in caught the No.3 Audi and slowed the No.8 Toyota, the No.7 Toyota stopped at Arnage with electrical trouble having led by nearly a lap at halfway, and the No.1 Audi lost time to turbo problems
  • Porsche's return to the top class led the race and produced a close Webber-Lotterer battle before retiring with mechanical issues two hours from the finish
  • Crowd figures are given two ways: Wikipedia says about 263,000, the largest since 1989, while the ACO calls 263,300 a record attendance
  • Class winners were the Jota Sport Zytek-Nissan of Dolan, Turvey and Tincknell in LMP2 - a debut win, finishing fifth overall and less than a lap ahead of the TDS Racing Ligier-Nissan - the AF Corse Ferrari 458 Italia of Bruni, Fisichella and Vilander in LMGTE Pro, and the all-Danish No.95 Aston Martin of Heinemeier Hansson, Poulsen and Thiim in LMGTE Am
  • Two of the winning drivers were late call-ups: Gene replaced Loic Duval after a Wednesday accident and Turvey was drafted in on the Thursday
  • Statistical markers included Michelin's 17th consecutive overall win, Audi's sixth straight win and 13th in 15 years, Kristensen's 14th podium in place of a 10th win, the Ligier marque's first podium in 39 years, and 16-year-old Matt McMurry becoming the youngest driver to start and finish
  • The LMGTE Am win was dedicated to Allan Simonsen, killed in the 2013 race, after which Tertre Rouge was re-profiled and new barriers, run-off and kerbs added; a GPS-monitored 60 km/h "slow zone" system was introduced so marshals could work without a full safety car
  • The result reshaped the championship: Davidson, Lapierre and Buemi led the drivers on 80 points to 60 for Fassler, Treluyer and Lotterer, and Toyota's manufacturers' lead over Audi was cut to a single point with five races left

title: Continental supplying first turbocharger with aluminum housing
description: Water-cooling enables the use of the lightweight material and thus enables a significant weight reduction by nearly 30% while simultaneously providing cost and system benefits. First, much less effort is required to protect neighboring components from the heat. Second, cooling of the exhaust flow reduces the thermal load on the catalytic converter, meaning it hardly ages at all.
longFormSummary:
• Continental launched series production of the first car turbocharger with an aluminium turbine housing; the press release is dated July 15, 2014 from Auburn Hills, Mich., and SAE reports that "Continental on July 15 announced the first turbocharger with an aluminum turbine housing to enter automotive series production"
  • The first application is BMW's three-cylinder 1.5 L, 100 kW gasoline engine - 134 hp per SAE - used in the MINI Hatch / Mini 3-door; integration into that engine "has been ongoing since spring 2014"
  • Water cooling is what makes the lightweight material usable, giving a weight reduction of nearly 30% along with cost and system benefits; SAE puts the saving at 2.65 lb / 1.2 kg per turbocharger compared with a typical heat-resistant cast-steel housing, and Green Car Congress gives the same 1.2 kg (2.6 lbs) figure for the MINI unit
  • A double-walled aluminium housing surrounds the hottest area with a cooling water jacket, keeping the external housing surface no hotter than 120 degC (248 degF) and the internal temperature below 350 degC (662 degF)
  • Udo Schwerdel, Head of the Turbocharger Product Line, Engine Systems, Powertrain Division, gives two benefits: much less effort is needed to protect neighbouring components from the heat, and cooling the exhaust flow reduces the thermal load on the catalytic converter, "meaning it hardly ages at all" - SAE frames the same point as increased catalyst durability. The dynamic response of the electric actuator at the wastegate still lets the catalytic converter heat up quickly
  • Despite the extra expenditure for water cooling, the aluminium turbochargers are more affordable for manufacturers; Schwerdel: "High-temperature-resistant materials such as nickel-base alloys drive up prices for turbochargers with steel housings, whereas our aluminum alloy is a cost-effective material"
  • The turbocharger was developed from a typical add-on component into an integral part of the engine, tightly integrated as a fixed component of the exhaust manifold under BMW's modular principle, with Continental working with the BMW Group from the simulation phase onward; steel-housing Continental turbochargers can also be attached to the same base engine through the cylinder-head interface, an option used for high-performance engines and vehicles exported to hot countries
  • Wolfgang Breuer, Head of the Engine Systems business unit: "Aluminum in a turbocharger designed for cars is a real milestone." Continental's first turbocharger of any kind went into series production in a 1.0 L engine in 2011
dateConfidenceReasoning: Date has passed, but the pin description does not confirm it happened then; unverified.

title: Windows Phone Store and Windows Store dev resources merging, 21 new payout markets added for both
description: Microsoft is changing up how developers get resources for Windows Phone and Windows 8. In fact, they're actually merging developer resources for Windows and Windows Phone. title: Microsoft to cut 18,000 jobs in the next year
description: Microsoft has announced that it will lay off up to 18,000 workers in the next year, in what is by far the largest number of employees that will be cut by the company in its history. In a letter sent to employees earlier this morning that Microsoft also released to the public, company CEO Satya Nadella confirmed that 12,500 of the job losses will be due to the company's acquisition of Nokia's Devices and Services division in April, when it added 25,000 new workers.
longFormSummary:
• On Thursday 17 July 2014 Microsoft announced it will lay off up to 18,000 workers over the next year, "by far the largest number of employees that will be cut by the company in its history", in a letter sent to employees that morning and also released publicly
  • Al Jazeera puts the scale at 14 percent of the workforce and the biggest cut in Microsoft's 39-year history, about twice analysts' estimates, against the roughly 5,800 jobs cut in 2009 at the height of the worldwide economic recession
  • CEO Satya Nadella confirmed 12,500 of the losses come from the acquisition of Nokia's Devices and Services division in April; the number of Nokia staff taken on is given as 25,000 by the pin's source and TechCrunch, but as 28,000 (with 12,500 "nearly half") by the later Al Jazeera report
  • Nadella: "We are moving now to start reducing the first 13,000 positions, and the vast majority of employees whose jobs will be eliminated will be notified over the next six months", adding that roles are being added in certain other strategic areas and that Microsoft will "have fewer layers of management, both top down and sideways, to accelerate the flow of information and decision making"; affected employees get severance and job transition help in many locations
  • Microsoft said in a separate press release that it expects pre-tax charges of between $1.1 billion and $1.6 billion over the next year (described by Al Jazeera as the next four quarters), including $750 million to $800 million for severance and related benefits and $350 million to $800 million of asset-related charges; it remained on track for the $600m annual savings target within 18 months of the deal closing
  • On products, the Nokia device teams roll into Microsoft, ending the Nokia X Android-based designs announced in February in favour of low-cost Lumia hardware running Windows Phone, and Microsoft will largely abandon the low-price Nokia Asha phones; Xbox Entertainment Studios, the two-year-old Santa Monica original video unit, is being closed
  • Locations named in the later report: about 1,350 Seattle-area workers around Redmond, 1,800 in Hungary, nearly 370 in San Diego and 1,100 in Finland, leaving headcount at about 109,000, still around 10,000 more than before the Nokia acquisition
  • More information was expected on July 22, when Microsoft announces its latest quarterly financial results; Nadella was to host an internal Q&A the day after the announcement

title: NVIDIA Shield Tablet - 16GB wi-fi model and 32GB LTE model
description: Twice as fast iPad Mini Retina. Unreal Engine 4 will be compatible with the processor. What this means is that we can expect to see high-end games on tablets and devices that use the chip with cranked up visuals. SHIELD tablet is 8 inch device with 1920◊1200 resolution. It has 2GB RAM, Tegra K1 SoC with 192 CUDA cores, QuadCore 2.2 GHz A15 CPU. Tablet has dual speakers and 5 MPIX ëselfieí camera.
longFormSummary:
• VideoCardz reported on 18 July 2014 that "On July 22nd NVIDIA will announce its own device, called SHIELD Tablet", accompanied by a wireless controller "designed specifically for NVIDIA SHIELD family, meaning you will be able to control either SHIELD tablet or SHIELD console"
  • NVIDIA did announce both on 22 July 2014, launching the SHIELD tablet and SHIELD wireless controller from its Santa Clara newsroom
  • The leaked pricing held exactly: "the cheaper 16GB model costs $299 and it only has WIFI connection. NVIDIA will ask you for $100 more if you decide to get a 32GB model with LTE modem on board", and the controller at $59 - confirmed as $299 for 16 GB Wi-Fi, $399 for 32 GB Wi-Fi + LTE, $59 for the controller and $39 for the cover
  • The leaked specifications also held: an 8-inch 1920x1200 display, 2 GB RAM and a Tegra K1 with 192 CUDA cores and a quad-core 2.2 GHz A15 CPU, with dual speakers and a 5 MP front camera
  • The announcement added detail the leak did not have: front-facing speakers with PureAudio and dual-ported bass reflex, an 8-inch IPS panel at 283 ppi, microSD expansion, mini HDMI 1.4b at 4K/30fps, Bluetooth 4.0, GPS and a 19.75 WHr battery rated for up to 10 hours of HD video, at 13.7 ounces and 0.36 inches thick
  • The sources differ on the camera and storage expansion: VideoCardz mentions only the 5 MP "selfie" camera and New Atlas a single 5 MP camera, while Wikipedia and ABI Research give 5 MP front and rear cameras; microSD is given as up to 128 GB by New Atlas, the press release and ABI but as microSDXC up to 200 GB by Wikipedia
  • The tablet's pitch was gaming: Tegra K1 with Kepler-architecture cores, called by NVIDIA "the world's most advanced mobile processor", running Unreal Engine 4, with GameStream local streaming from GeForce GTX PCs, a GRID cloud gaming beta for owners in Northern California, ShadowPlay gameplay recording and Twitch streaming, and a Console Mode for native 1080p on TVs
  • The wireless controller ran over ultra-low-latency Wi-Fi Direct with up to four per tablet, a headset jack, touch pad, volume control and voice command; ABI notes it also works with SHIELD Portable, which cannot itself serve as a controller for the tablet, and that it lacks motion controls
  • A DirectStylus 2, "twice as responsive as predecessor" and GPU-accelerated, shipped with the Dabbler app - New Atlas thought it fitted poorly with a gaming-first device
  • Release dates: pre-orders opened on announcement in the United States, Canada and select European countries, with release on 29 July 2014 in the US and Canada and 14 August 2014 in Europe
  • The tablet preloaded SHIELD Hub and Trine 2: Complete Story with full Google Play access, shipping on Android 4.4.2 KitKat and later upgraded as far as Android 7.0 Nougat in February 2017
  • Reception noted the speakers and Twitch streaming as strengths, with weight (390 g against the Nexus 7's 290 g) and total cost as drawbacks
  • Later history: on 31 July 2015 NVIDIA recalled devices sold between July 2014 and July 2015 over overheating that posed a fire hazard; the tablet was refreshed as the Shield Tablet K1 at $199-200 in November 2015, a hardware upgrade was cancelled in August 2016, and the line was officially discontinued in mid-2018
dateConfidenceReasoning: Date has passed, but the pin description does not confirm it happened then; unverified.

title: Diablo III Ultimate Evil Edition coming to Xbox One and 360 this August

  • It collects the main Diablo III game with the Reaper of Souls expansion that landed on PC in March; Reaper of Souls will not be sold separately on consoles, so Xbox 360 owners of Diablo III have no choice but to buy the Ultimate Evil Edition
