title: iPad Air 2 Rumored to Launch in October, Updated Retina iPad Mini May Come Later
description: Both the next-generation iPad Air and Retina iPad mini are expected to gain updated A8 processors, camera improvements, and the Touch ID fingerprint sensor first introduced with the iPhone 5s. Apple's iPad Air 2 may also gain an anti-reflective screen coating and it may also ship in gold, silver, and space gray, much like the iPhone.
longFormSummary:
• MacRumors reported on Monday 22 September 2014 that, per Taiwan's Commercial Times, Apple planned to introduce the next-generation iPad Air in October, with the device entering production in September and shipping the following month
  • The same report said the next-generation Retina iPad mini might not launch alongside it, coming instead in early 2015, with a 12.9-inch iPad Pro in the second quarter of 2015 - MacRumors noting there had been "no prior indication of separate launch timelines" and that earlier rumors had both launching together at an October event
  • Both were expected to gain an A8 processor, camera improvements and the Touch ID fingerprint sensor, with the iPad Air 2 also possibly gaining an anti-reflective screen coating and gold, silver and space gray finishes
  • A rumored October 21 media event had been "shot down" by The Loop's Jim Dalrymple, who did not rule out another October date, and Bloomberg was reported as saying the iPad Air 2 was already in production with the Retina iPad mini 2 entering production soon
  • The event in fact came on Thursday 16 October 2014 in Cupertino, where Apple introduced both the iPad Air 2 and an iPad mini 3 together - so the Commercial Times' early-2015 timing for the small iPad did not hold
  • The chip was the A8X rather than the plain A8 the rumor expected: Apple gave the iPad Air 2 "40 percent better CPU and 2.5 times the graphics performance of iPad Air", up to 10-hour battery life and an M8 motion coprocessor with a new barometer
  • The rumored anti-reflective coating was real - an improved fully-laminated Retina display with an anti-reflective coating that "reduces glare by 56 percent over the previous iPad Air", which Phil Schiller called "a first for a tablet"
  • The gold, silver and space gray finishes and the Touch ID sensor both arrived as rumored, on the iPad Air 2 and the iPad mini 3 alike, together with Apple Pay within apps (US only)
  • The iPad Air 2 was 6.1 mm thin and under a pound, pitched by Apple and Schiller as "the thinnest tablet in the world"
  • Cameras and connectivity: an 8MP iSight with panorama, time-lapse, slo-mo and 1080p - "For the first time on an iPad, you can take time lapse and slo-motion video" - a FaceTime HD camera capturing over 80 percent more light, 802.11ac MIMO Wi-Fi up to 866 Mbps and more LTE bands, shipping with iOS 8.1
  • Pricing and availability: iPad Air 2 from $499 (16GB Wi-Fi) up to $829, iPad mini 3 from $399 up to $729, the iPad mini with Retina display renamed iPad mini 2 from $299 and the original iPad mini at $249; online orders opened Friday 17 October in 29 countries with stores following the next week
  • CBS framed the launch against weak demand - Apple "sold 13.3 million iPads last quarter, down from the previous year and below Wall Street estimates", with the iPad's share sliding "from 68 percent of the tablet market at beginning of 2012, to about 27 percent last quarter" per IDC - and noted that despite Apple's secrecy the iPad details "had been widely reported", with Apple prematurely posting photos of both devices on the iTunes website the day before

title: Tri-band Wi-Fi chips for multi-gigabit streaming coming from Qualcomm
description: Qualcomm announced that it completed the purchase of Wilocity and will soon deliver "a family of tri-band platforms that combine Qualcomm Atheros, Inc.ís Wi-Fi and WiGig solutions to significantly increase performance and enable cutting-edge wireless applications. The initial tri-band platform is a reference design based on the Qualcomm Snapdragon 810, which is the worldís first mobile platform designed to support WiGig." The Snapdragon 810 is expected to ship in the first half of 2015.
longFormSummary:
• Qualcomm completed its purchase of Wilocity, the startup behind 60GHz “WiGig” (802.11ad) chips, announcing the close the day before the 3 July 2014 report; financial terms were not disclosed, though rumours in May had put the price at $300 million, and Qualcomm Atheros had invested in Wilocity since 2008
  • Qualcomm will combine Wilocity's 60GHz chips with its own Wi-Fi chips into tri-band platforms covering 2.4, 5 and 60GHz
  • The initial tri-band platform is a reference design based on the Snapdragon 810, “the world's first mobile platform designed to support WiGig”, expected to ship in the first half of 2015
  • By Mobile World Congress on 2 March 2015 the Snapdragon 810 had reached a commercial smartphone, LG's newly released G Flex 2, which Qualcomm demonstrated with its X10 LTE modem and Ericsson infrastructure at Category 9 LTE-A speeds of up to 450 Mbps — bearing out the first-half-2015 expectation
  • Neither Qualcomm press release of 2 March 2015 mentions WiGig, 60GHz or tri-band: the connectivity release covers LTE-Advanced carrier aggregation, LTE-Broadcast, LTE/Wi-Fi convergence, LTE-U and a Qualcomm Atheros smart bulb, and the other previews the Zeroth cognitive computing platform and the Snapdragon 820
  • The Qualcomm Atheros Wi-Fi silicon shown at that MWC was the QCA6174 2-stream 802.11ac chipset, in NETGEAR's new AirCard Category 9 mobile hotspot built on the Snapdragon X12 LTE modem — again 5GHz 802.11ac rather than the 60GHz WiGig of the tri-band plan
  • 60GHz signals are easily blocked, so sender and receiver must be in the same room; WiGig is technically capable of 7Gbps, Wilocity's early chips reached 4.6 Gbps, and a 4.6Gbps smartphone chip was expected to ship that year
  • Dell had already released a wireless dock using Wilocity chips, connecting a laptop to USB storage and up to two monitors
  • Netgear's Nighthawk X6 AC3200 “Tri-Band” router claims 3.2Gbps combined but uses one 2.4GHz and two 5GHz bands with no 60GHz; Qualcomm-based routers should beat it, “although not until next year”
  • Note the date gap: the pin is dated 2 March 2015, the day of the two Qualcomm MWC press releases, while the article announcing the Wilocity purchase and the tri-band platforms is dated 3 July 2014
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per arstechnica.com: "…Gig.” The Snapdragon 810 is expected to ship in the first half of 2015. Qualcomm did not disclose fi…"

title: BD Bacatá's Crowdfunded Tower Tops Out in Bogotá
description: Financed by more than 3,800 small Colombian investors instead of one developer, BD Bacatá reaches its final floor as the country’s tallest building, though its full opening keeps slipping.
longFormSummary:
• BD Bacatá is a two-tower mixed-use complex in downtown Bogotá: a 67-floor, 216 m south tower and a 56-floor, 167 m north tower, surpassing Torre Colpatria (196 m) as Colombia's tallest building
  • It was the first crowdfunded skyscraper, financed by over 3,800 ordinary Colombians per Wikipedia
  • The south tower's final slab was poured on 24 July 2015 and the north tower's on 20 December 2015; structural work finished 24 February 2016 with inauguration planned for the following year
  • Opening has repeatedly slipped: as of 2016 no official opening date had been set, and investors voiced concern in March 2017 over delayed returns
  • Works halted in early 2018 over financing difficulties, resumed in 2019, and were suspended again during COVID-19
  • Developer president Venerando Lamelas blamed complex foundation conditions and excavation for delays
  • Total Co took over completion of unfinished south-tower floors in late 2024, reporting 30% of the work remained by early 2026
  • The complex is planned to hold 405 apartments, 117 offices, 319 hotel rooms and 6,500 m2 of retail
address: BD Bacatá, Avenida Calle 19, Bogotá, Colombia
dateConfidenceReasoning: The topping out is dated: Wikipedia records the south tower's final slab poured on 24 July 2015, completing its 67 floors and full 216 m as Colombia's tallest building. The north tower's last slab followed on 20 December 2015 and structural work finished on 24 February 2016; the pin's old end-of-2016 date matched none of these. The opening itself kept slipping for years afterwards.

title: California Law Now Requires All Smartphones to Have Built-In Kill Switches By July 2015
description: A California bill requiring all smartphones sold in the state to have antitheft technology installed was today signed into law by California governor...
longFormSummary:
• California SB-962, requiring smartphone kill switches, was signed into law by Governor Jerry Brown on 25 August 2014
  • It applies to smartphones manufactured on or after 1 July 2015 and sold in California, which must include a technological solution at the time of sale that can render the phone inoperable to an unauthorized user
  • The feature must survive a hard reset or OS downgrade, prevent reactivation on a wireless network except by the authorized user, be enabled at initial setup, and be reversible by the owner
  • Co-sponsored by San Francisco DA George Gascon and Senator Mark Leno; every statewide law enforcement organization supported it, while AT&T and other telecom companies opposed it
  • SB 962 passed the Senate 26-8-6 in May and the Assembly 53-20-6 on 7 August, with the Senate concurring on 11 August
  • MacRumors said Apple's Activation Lock likely satisfies the law, while makers like Samsung and Microsoft would be affected; Minnesota was the only other state with such a law
  • Apple products saw a 38% drop in robberies in the six months after it introduced a kill switch feature

title: Construction Begins on Frankfurt Airport's €4 Billion Terminal 3
description: Fraport broke ground on Terminal 3, a roughly €4 billion expansion of Frankfurt Airport that would add three passenger piers and a 69-meter control tower.

• Fraport broke ground on Frankfurt Airport's Terminal 3 on 5 October 2015 with about 400 employees and 600+ guests, including CEO Stefan Schulte and Hesse governor Volker Bouffier; the building permit was issued in 2012 after 15+ years of planning
  • Investment is about four billion euros, built by Fraport Ausbau Süd, delivered on schedule and on budget; described as Europe's largest privately funded infrastructure project
  • Footprint is 176,000 m2 with initial Piers G, H and J giving up to 19 million passengers a year; an optional pier K would raise this to 25 million

  • Official inauguration was set for 22 April 2026 after test operation with about 8,000 test passengers; all 57 airlines at Terminal 2 will move over in four phases
  • It has 21 security lanes with CT scanners, an 8,500-space parking structure and a Sky Line people mover
  • The site is the former Rhein-Main Air Base (US Air Force 1945-2005)

title: 432 Park Avenue Opens on Manhattan's Billionaires' Row
description: Harry Macklowe's 432 Park Avenue, then the world's tallest residential tower, officially completed in Manhattan in December 2015 after four years of construction.
longFormSummary:
• 432 Park Avenue, designed by Rafael Vinoly for CIM Group and Harry Macklowe, was completed on 23 December 2015 at about 425.5 m (1,396 ft), the tallest residential building in the world at completion
  • It stands on the former Drake Hotel site at 57th Street, bought by Macklowe in 2006; plans were approved in 2011, sales launched in 2013 and the tower topped out in October 2014
  • The design is a white concrete lattice of 10-foot-square windows in blocks separated by open mechanical floors, with a height-to-width ratio of about 15:1 and tuned mass dampers to control sway
  • Residences range from studios to penthouses on floors 91 to 96 with interiors by Deborah Berke; counts vary between 104 and 125 units across sources
  • Reception was mixed, criticised as an eyesore casting shadows over Central Park and as housing for the ultra-wealthy; residents later complained of mechanical and structural problems leading to lawsuits in the 2020s

title: Torre Reforma Becomes Mexico City's Tallest Building

title: Expanded Panama Canal Opens to Neopanamax Ships
description: A nine-year, $5.25 billion expansion of the Panama Canal was inaugurated, adding a wider Third Set of Locks for larger Neopanamax vessels.
longFormSummary:
• The expanded Panama Canal was inaugurated on 26 June 2016, when the Neopanamax ship COSCO Shipping Panama made the first transit through the Agua Clara Locks on the Atlantic side toward the Cocoli Locks on the Pacific
  • The vessel carried 9,472 TEUs and measures 299.98 m by 48.25 m
  • It is the largest enhancement since the canal opened in 1914: new locks at both ends and a second lane of traffic doubling cargo capacity, with locks 70 feet wider and 18 feet deeper
  • Water-saving basins recycle 60 percent of the water per transit
  • ENR put the third-lane effort at about $5.4 billion over 10 years, with GUPC (Sacyr, Salini Impregilo, Jan De Nul, Constructora Urbana) as contractor and over 50,000 people employed
  • Delays added about one and a half years to the schedule, including a concrete sill crack on the Pacific side and a 2014 GUPC stoppage, with arbitration ongoing
  • Almost 40,000 workers were honoured at the inauguration, and 170 reservations had been received for the expanded canal
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: "Later this afternoon, the vessel will reach the Pacific-facing Cocoli Locks where the official Inauguration ceremony will take place."

title: Fifty-six percent of California voters approved Proposition 64 Legalizing Marijuana
description: Proposition 64, The Adult Use Marijuana Act, permits adults over 21 years of age who are not participating in the state’s medical cannabis program to legally grow (up to six plants, including all of the harvest from those plants) and to possess personal use quantities of cannabis (up to one ounce of flower and/or up to eight grams of concentrates) while also licensing commercial cannabis production and retail sales

  • Taxes include a 15 percent retail excise tax and a cultivation tax of $9.25 per ounce of flowers; the ballot label estimated revenue from high hundreds of millions to over $1 billion annually
  • Outside the limits, NORML lists misdemeanors of up to six months and $500 for more than 28.5 g of flower, more than 8 g of concentrate, six or more plants, or unlicensed sales; butane extraction carries up to $50,000 and 3-7 years
  • The Yes campaign raised $26.5 million against $1.1 million opposed; marijuana remains federally prohibited

description: Permits adults who are not participating in the state's medical cannabis program to legally grow (up to six plants, including all of the harvest from those plants) and to possess personal use quantities of cannabis (up to one ounce of flower and/or up to 3.5 grams of concentrates) while also licensing commercial cannabis production and retail sales. (Home cultivation is not permitted if one's residence is within 25 miles of an operating marijuana retailer.) Commercial marijuana production is subject to a 15 percent excise tax, much of which is earmarked to the State Distributive School Account.
longFormSummary:
• Nevada voters approved Question 2, the Regulation and Taxation of Marijuana Act, on 8 November 2016: Yes 602,463 (54.47%) to No 503,644 (45.53%)
  • It took effect 1 January 2017, legalizing adult use for those 21 and over; legal sales began 1 July 2017 rather than the planned 1 January 2018
  • Ballotpedia describes the possession limit as one ounce or less of marijuana or one-eighth ounce of concentrate, while the law firm explainer and NORML cite 2.5 ounces of marijuana and a quarter ounce of concentrate
  • Adults may grow up to six plants in a locked area; the law firm explainer says this applies only to those living more than 25 miles from a retail store, with a maximum of 12 plants per residence
  • Commercial marijuana is subject to a 15 percent excise tax on wholesale sales by cultivation facilities, with revenue first covering costs and then going to the State Distributive School Account
  • For the first 18 months wholesale liquor dealers had exclusive distribution rights, which led to litigation by alcohol distributors and a state of emergency declared by Gov. Brian Sandoval on 7 July 2017
  • Public consumption remains illegal (smoking in public can draw a fine up to $600) and past marijuana convictions can be sealed on request
  • Yes on 2 raised $4.3 million against $3.8 million for No on 2, with Sheldon Adelson the largest opposition donor

title: The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild lands top spot on IGN's 10 Best Legend of Zelda Games of All Time
description:
The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild reinvented a 30-year-old series in a way we rarely see. After Skyward Sword offered a slightly more linear, story-driven campaign than most fans were used to, Breath of the Wild readjusted dramatically in the opposite direction. Suddenly you could go anywhere and climb anything in any order you wanted, and goodness gracious was there a whole lot to choose from.

There are plenty of fair criticisms to throw at Breath of the Wild, with common ones being its lack of traditional Zelda dungeons and items. But what’s truly impressive is how much it maintained the heart of a Zelda game even as it altered nearly every system around it. To a certain extent, Zelda has always been about exploration and choice, and Breath of the Wild simply leaned into and enabled those aspects of itself above all else, now making the world a place that would react to those choices as well. There’s just so much to see, so many people to meet and secrets to find hidden throughout this long-since devastated version of Hyrule.

title: Intel patches nine-year-old enterprise CPU vulnerability
description: Intel has just patched a vulnerability which has been open and exploitable in all its enterprise targeted Core processors - for the last nine years. Since 2008 Intel's business-focussed PC processors have shipped with Active Management Technology (AMT), Intel Standard Manageability (ISM) and Small Business Technology (SBT) features - all useful features for remote management.
longFormSummary:
• Intel patched a critical privilege-escalation flaw (CVE-2017-5689, nicknamed Silent Bob) in the AMT, ISM and SBT remote-management firmware of its business Core processors, present since 2008
  • It affects firmware versions 6.x through 11.6 and lets an unprivileged attacker take control of the manageability features; Intel says consumer PCs are not affected
  • It was reachable by anyone on the same network, or remotely if port 16992 was exposed
  • Maksim Malyutin of Embedi discovered it and reported it to Intel in the first quarter of 2017; The Register puts it in March and CyberScoop in February
  • Fixed firmware ranges from 6.2.61.3535 (1st-gen Core) to 11.6.27.3264 (7th-gen Core), but manufacturers must distribute it; Lenovo and HP planned patches the following week, other timetables ran deep into June, and unsupported machines may never be fixed
  • SemiAccurate criticised Intel's slow response and suspected exploitation in the wild, while Intel said it was not aware of any exploitation
  • Intel released a mitigation guide (Intel-SA-00075) and a discovery tool to check for the flaw

title: A New Doubly Charmed Particle Has Just Been Discovered in CERN

  • Lead physicist Patrick Spradlin (University of Glasgow) announced the result, with participation from University of Birmingham scientists and eleven UK institutes

title: Statoil Commissions Hywind Scotland, the World's First Floating Wind Farm
description: Statoil switched on Hywind Scotland, five 6-megawatt turbines on floating spar-buoy foundations moored 25 kilometres off Peterhead, as the first floating wind farm in the world. The 30-megawatt pilot park proved floating turbines could operate commercially in deep, harsh North Sea waters.
longFormSummary:
• Hywind Scotland was commissioned in October 2017 (WindEurope dates the entry 18 October 2017) as the world's first commercial floating wind farm
  • It has five 6 MW Siemens turbines, 30 MW in total, on floating foundations off Peterhead in 95-120 m of water, roughly 25 km from shore
  • Owned by Equinor (75%) and Masdar (25%); construction began in 2016 and cost £264m, about three times fixed offshore wind per MW
  • Turbines were assembled at Stord, Norway in summer 2017 and each is held by three suction anchors
  • It achieved a 54% capacity factor and survived Hurricane Ophelia and Storm Caroline by shutting down in the worst conditions
  • All five turbines were towed to Norway in May 2024 for main-bearing replacement and were operating again by October 2024
address: Buchan Deep, North Sea, off Peterhead, Aberdeenshire, Scotland, UK
dateConfidenceReasoning: WindEurope's history timeline and Equinor (then Statoil) both date Hywind Scotland's commissioning to October 18, 2017.

title: Felbermayr Hauls Two Giant Autoclaves to FACC's Innviertel Plants

  • The trailers were 38.5 m long and 232 tons; one vessel is 19.9 m long and 6.1 m in diameter, the largest at FACC
  • The delivery is part of FACC's expansion of up to EUR 100 million over three years, starting with 6,400 m2 of production area

title: Platov International Airport Opens Near Rostov-on-Don

longFormSummary:

  • It replaced the old Rostov-on-Don airport, is named after Cossack general Matvei Platov (name officially set 20 January 2017), and was described as Russia's most expensive airport at the time
  • Facilities include a 3,600 m runway, a 50,000 m2 terminal with 9 air-bridges, and a design capacity of 5 million passengers a year
  • Test flights ran on 18 November 2017 and the IATA code ROV moved to Platov on 27 November
  • In its first year it handled over 3.23 million passengers and added 20 new destinations; during the 2018 World Cup Rostov matches it carried 257.8 thousand passengers
  • It was built as a public-private partnership with Airports of Regions (Renova Group) as strategic shareholder, the largest infrastructure project of the Rostov Region
  • Civilian flights have been suspended since 24 February 2022 and the airport remained closed for security reasons as of late 2025

title: Hamburg Port Authority Opens the Rethebrücke as Europe's Largest Rail Bascule Bridge
description: Hamburg Port Authority put the new Rethebrücke rail bascule bridge into operation over the Rethe canal, replacing the original 1934 lift bridge and becoming Europe's largest rail bascule bridge.
longFormSummary:
• The Hamburg Port Authority officially opened the new Rethe rail bascule bridge on 15 December 2017 with a symbolic first train ride, calling it Europe's largest rail bascule bridge
  • It replaces the 1934 Rethe lift bridge and links Hohe Schaar station with Neuhof and the Tollerort container terminal; the road leaf opened on 11 July 2016
  • The bridge has a 104 m span and a 64 m channel (previously 44 m) with unlimited height; it opens in about four minutes, and the road carries about 7,000 vehicles a day that previously faced up to 40 closures daily
  • Built from June 2011 to 2016 by Arge Rethebrücke (Hochtief, Bilfinger, Waagner Biro), cost rose from EUR 95 million to over EUR 173 million
  • A hydraulic cylinder failed on the road leaf on 20 August 2020; the bridge won the Deutscher Brückenbaupreis 2020
dateConfidenceReasoning: Hamburg Port Authority's press release states the Rethebrücke, Europe's largest rail bascule bridge, went into operation on 15 December 2017.

title: US Embassy Opens in Nine Elms, London
description: The US opened its $1BN embassy in London's Nine Elms, a 12-storey glass-cube fortress replacing the historic Grosvenor Square site the US had occupied since 1785.
longFormSummary:
• The US embassy at 33 Nine Elms Lane was open to the public from 13 December 2017 and formally opened on 16 January 2018 - the pin's date
  • It is the largest American embassy in Western Europe, overlooking the Thames
  • Neither source states the $1 billion the pin gives: the Wikipedia article carries no cost figure, and on the video page the only such number is inside the link slug "the-secret-architecture-of-americas-1billion-fortress", which the description itself does not state
  • The US presence in Grosvenor Square runs back to 1785, when John Adams opened the first American legation in London at 9 Grosvenor Square, upgraded to an embassy in 1893; the mission moved several times (Victoria Street 1883-1912, 4 Grosvenor Gardens 1912, 1 Grosvenor Square 1938) before the Eero Saarinen chancery at 30 Grosvenor Square opened in 1960
  • That old chancery was leased from the Duke of Westminster for a symbolic peppercorn rent, carried Theodore Roszak's gilded aluminum eagle with a wingspan of over 11 metres, was Grade II listed in October 2009, served as chancery until 2017 and reopened in 2025 as The Chancery Rosewood hotel
  • The B1M's film, "The Secret Security of America's London Embassy" published 11 December 2023, frames the building as "how the US built its most hi-tech and controversial embassy", with chapters on London Embassies, Little America, Sarf London and The Secret Fortress
  • Its cited research includes a Harvard Design Magazine piece "Fortress London: the new US embassy and the rise of counter-terror urbanism", Lambeth council's Vauxhall Nine Elms Battersea regeneration page and the embassy's own design concept page
  • The site has drawn repeated protest: 10,000-strong Vietnam War demonstrations in March 1968 at the old embassy, the 2020 George Floyd protests, Just Stop Oil painting the compound wall on 6 November 2024, and Greenpeace UK activists pouring red dye into the water on 10 April 2025 with six arrested
  • Neither wiki describes the building as a 12-storey glass cube, as the pin does

dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: "the $1bn US embassy in London opened its doors to the public for the first time on 16 January" 2018.

title: The First Section 301 Tariffs on Chinese Goods Take Effect
description: US Customs began collecting an extra 25 percent on 818 tariff lines worth about $34 billion of Chinese imports on 6 July 2018 — the opening move of the trade war, and the first time since the 1930s that the United States taxed a major trading partner at this scale.
longFormSummary:
• "Customs and Border Protection will begin to collect the additional duties on July 6, 2018" on 818 tariff lines covering about $34 billion of imports from China
  • The full list USTR published on 15 June 2018 covered 1,102 tariff lines worth roughly $50 billion in 2018 trade values; the remaining 284 lines, about $16 billion, went to further notice and comment
  • It followed a Section 301 investigation which found China's practices on technology transfer, intellectual property and innovation "unreasonable and discriminatory" and a burden on US commerce
  • The list deliberately targeted sectors named in China's "Made in China 2025" industrial policy — aerospace, information and communications technology, robotics, industrial machinery, new materials and cars — and deliberately spared consumer goods such as phones and televisions
  • Robert Lighthizer framed it as defence: "We must take strong defensive actions to protect America's leadership in technology and innovation against the unprecedented threat posed by China's theft of our intellectual property"
  • USTR built the list from about 3,200 written submissions and a three-day public hearing in May 2018 at which 121 witnesses testified

title: NASA's Groundbreaking Mission to 'Touch' the Sun Will Launch in 2018
description: NASA's Parker Solar Probe will be the first spacecraft to fly directly into the atmosphere of the Sun and explore its brutally hot corona.
longFormSummary:
• The links date the launch differently: (from May 2017) says the mission launches "in the summer of next year", with a 20-day window opening July 31, 2018, while the newer NASA page, dated Aug 10, 2018, gives a firm slot - "slated to launch on Saturday, August 11, 2018, at 3:33 a.m. EDT from Launch Complex 37, Cape Canaveral Air Force Station, Florida"; the pin's 31 July to 21 August span is the window, not the launch
  • The launch vehicle is a United Launch Alliance Delta IV Heavy; NASA's image feature shows the spacecraft "packed safely inside" its payload fairing, photographed on Wednesday, August 8, 2018
  • It is NASA's first mission to fly directly into the Sun's corona, plunging within 4 million miles of the Sun and travelling "through the Sun's atmosphere, closer to the surface than any spacecraft before it"
  • A core goal is to explain why the corona is much hotter than the surface; NASA says the mission "will revolutionize our understanding of the Sun, where changing conditions can propagate out into the solar system, affecting Earth and other worlds"
  • The spacecraft carries a 4.5-inch-thick (11.43 cm) carbon-composite shield and will make 24 orbits with many hot and cold cycles
  • On May 31, 2017 NASA renamed Solar Probe Plus the Parker Solar Probe, at an announcement at the University of Chicago, honouring solar astrophysicist Dr. Eugene Parker, whose 1958 Astrophysical Journal article "Dynamics of the interplanetary gas and magnetic fields" underpinned the concept of solar wind; the team placed photos of Parker and his paper inside the spacecraft
  • Understanding the corona should help forecast space weather affecting satellite communications, aircraft radiation exposure, astronaut safety and pipeline erosion
  • Project scientist Nicola Fox of the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory said the probe "is going to answer questions about solar physics that we've puzzled over for more than six decades"; Parker himself said "the solar probe is going to a region of space that has never been explored before"

title: The Vessel Opens at Hudson Yards
description: Thomas Heatherwick's climbable honeycomb staircase, The Vessel, opens to the public as the centrepiece of Manhattan's new Hudson Yards district.
longFormSummary:
• Vessel, designed by Heatherwick Studio, opened to the public on 15 March 2019 with timed free tickets from 12pm, alongside the other Hudson Yards phase one public spaces; it had first been unveiled in September 2016
  • The structure has 154 staircases, 80 landings and about a mile of walkways, standing 150 feet high and 150 feet wide at the top and narrowing at the base, with a sloping lift to the top; copper-coloured metal soffits over concrete inside
  • Heatherwick Studio's Stuart Wood: "It's not a building, it's not a sculpture, it's not an artwork... we're thinking of this as a piece of furniture", with the Spanish Steps in Rome as a reference; a public competition was to decide its permanent name
  • It stands on a landscaped plaza by Nelson Byrd Woltz at Hudson Yards, built over a 28-acre active rail yard and billed as "the largest private development in the US"; 15 Hudson Yards and The Shed (programming from 5 April 2019) opened with it, and a second phase adds eight towers
  • CNN, reporting later (Oct 27, 2024), agrees the Vessel opened in March 2019 at 150 feet tall and names Related Companies as owner
  • What followed the opening: the Vessel closed in January 2021 after three suicides and reopened with security measures, then closed for over three years after a 14-year-old's suicide in July 2021 - four suicides in all - before reopening in October 2024 with bespoke safety netting designed by Heatherwick Studio
  • Hudson Yards COO Andrew Rosen said the netting "balances all the aesthetic concerns... and also provide that safety", while critics including Jacob Alspector and Matt Shaw said it addresses safety but leaves the structure "gaudy and ungainly", and that early warnings about low barriers were ignored
  • is The B1M's video "Why We Should Celebrate (Not Hate) New York's Vessel", published 2020-01-29 and narrated by Fred Mills, arguing against the criticism the Hudson Yards centrepiece drew in its first year; the page carries no figures of its own

  • Inuit Guardians work with Parks Canada to monitor the sites and keep unauthorized people out of the restricted area

title: Porsche Starts Production of the Taycan in Zuffenhausen

• Porsche opened a new Taycan production facility at Zuffenhausen and began series production of customer cars on schedule on 9 September 2019
  • Construction took under 48 months, starting at the end of 2015 after the September 2015 Mission E concept; it includes a new body shop, paint shop, electric-motor and component plant and assembly hall, with 35,000 tonnes of steel and 170,000 m2 of buildings
  • Production is to be CO2-neutral, using renewable electricity, biogas heat, electric logistics vehicles and paint-shop waste heat
  • More than 130 companies and suppliers were involved; Albrecht Reimold said it was a deliberate decision to build in Zuffenhausen ('a factory inside a factory')
  • Capacity is 20,000 to 40,000 units a year depending on demand; deliveries begin in Europe, with US dealerships from December as 2020 models
  • Launch models were the Taycan Turbo (from $152,250) and Turbo S ($186,350), 616 hp standard and up to 670 and 750 hp with launch control

title: Woolworth Building Tops Off Its Luxury Condo Conversion
description: Developer Alchemy Properties finished a seven-year conversion of the Woolworth Building's top 30 floors into luxury condos, a bet on keeping the 1913 landmark economically viable.
longFormSummary:
• Alchemy Properties' conversion of the Woolworth Building's upper floors into 33 luxury condominiums, with interiors by Thierry Despont, was recognised as an ENR New York 2019 Best Project (24 September 2019); the work started in early 2016 per ENR
  • The 1913 Cass Gilbert tower became mixed-use: offices up to the 29th floor and residences above, including a five-level 9,000 sq ft penthouse with private elevator
  • Landmark facade, partial occupancy and new crane rules ruled out an external hoist or crane, so crews used an internal hoist and a chain-fall system in an empty elevator shaft
  • Scope included a gut renovation of 110,000 sq ft, a $22 million terra-cotta facade restoration, a new mechanical floor and a reinforced pinnacle
  • The first closing was reported in June 2018: a 38th-floor two-bedroom sold for $7.55 million; amenities include a restored 55-foot saltwater pool
  • The redevelopment was described in 2015 as a repositioning of an underused office tower, using methods designed around 100-year-old documents and historic riveted framing under landmark guidelines

title: Airbus Inaugurates a Robotic A320 Fuselage Line in Hamburg
description: On October 1, 2019, Airbus opened a highly automated fuselage structure assembly line for the A320 Family at its Hamburg-Finkenwerder site, using 20 robots to drill, countersink and rivet fuselage joints. title: TBM Wanda Completes Drilling of the Albvorland Tunnel
description: Tunnel boring machine Wanda finished excavating the southern tube of the Albvorland Tunnel, the last major breakthrough on Deutsche Bahn's Stuttgart-Ulm high-speed line. The 8-kilometer twin-tube tunnel near Wendlingen am Neckar was built by Implenia and cuts travel time between Stuttgart and Ulm to roughly 30 minutes.
longFormSummary:
• On 29 October 2019 at Wendlingen am Neckar, tunnel boring machine WANDA broke through in the southern tube of the Albvorland Tunnel, ending Implenia's drilling on both tubes; its sister machine TBM Sybille had broken through in the northern tube in August 2019. TunnelTalk describes the same final breakthrough the other way round - the 10.82m diameter TBM that had been boring the north tube since late 2017 finished last, following the sister Herrenknecht machine that completed the 8.16km drive for the 9.6m internal diameter south tube in August
  • Implenia is building the 8-kilometre Albvorland Tunnel for Deutsche Bahn as a key section of the new 60-kilometre railway line between Stuttgart and Ulm; Implenia's Erwin Scherer calls it one of the ten longest railway tunnels in Germany
  • WANDA is 137 m long, weighs 2,300 tonnes and dug for almost exactly two years; Implenia installed 3,989 tubbing rings at an average advance of 15 m a day and a peak of 32 m, with the tubbing segments made in a factory set up near the site. TunnelTalk records the lining as seven segments in each 2m long by 450mm thick ring
  • This was the last TBM breakthrough on the whole Stuttgart-Ulm project: "Monthly TBM breakthroughs since August have brought main tunnelling on the Stuttgart-Ulm high speed rail line in Germany to completion", covering 120.4km of main tunnel excavation - 58.8km for Stuttgart 21 in the city and 61.6km for the Wendlingen-Ulm section - and leaving "only minor underground works to complete"
  • It followed the September completion of the last drive for the 9.5km Filder Tunnel, the project's longest underground section, by a Herrenknecht TBM for the ATCOST21 JV of Porr-Hinteregger-Ostu-Stettin-Hoch- und Tiefbau-Swietelsky
  • Deutsche Bahn's Thorsten Krenz says the line is designed for 250 km/h and that with Stuttgart 21 the Stuttgart-Ulm journey will be almost halved to around half an hour, with about 61 km of tunnel dug under often-difficult geological conditions; TunnelTalk adds that the project "is to be completed and brought into operation in 2022"
  • Two Free Documentary - Engineering films visit the Albvorlandtunnel site between Stuttgart and Ulm, "a critical segment of the new high-speed railway line", where "two colossal tunnel boring machines" weighing "thousands of tons" grind through rock and soil while installing the tunnel lining, with workers discussing geological hurdles, safety and keeping the operation on schedule; neither gives a length, cost or completion date

title: Battery-making capacity built by lithium-ion battery megafactories will triple by 2020

• Visual Capitalist's Chart of the Week (published 8 May 2015 by Jeff Desjardins), using data from Simon Moores of Benchmark Mineral Intelligence, states that "Today's production capacity is approximately 35 GWh worldwide"
  • "once Tesla's Gigafactory and the other facilities being built by LG Chem, Foxconn, BYD, and Boston Power are complete, we will have a total capacity in 2020 of around 122 GWh", which the chart says "proves that companies are serious about scale and reducing costs"
  • Tesla's "$5 Billion Gigafactory and its potential to double lithium-ion battery production capacity" is presented as "merely a cog in the wheel of a bigger trend", with several other large-scale facilities coming online in the next five years
  • Tesla's own plan was later raised well above that starting point: a January 2017 investor handout has the Gigafactory's original 35 GWh of cells and 50 GWh of packs now planned for 2018 and tripled to 105 GWh of cells and 150 GWh of packs at full production around 2020, with phase 2 construction underway
  • By Benchmark Mineral Intelligence's December 2019 assessment the pipeline is far larger again: 115 lithium ion battery megafactories in the pipeline to 2029, up from 63 in the December 2018 assessment, with China adding 564GWh by 2028 for "a global total of 2068.3GWh or the equivalent of 40m EVs by 2028"; China holds 88 of the 115 plants and 69% of capacity, Europe 17% (348GWh planned) and North America 8%
  • Europe's 2019 surge was led by new German plants - CATL in Erfurt, Farasis in Saxony-Anhalt, Northvolt and Volkswagen Group in Salzgitter and, most recently, Tesla's Gigafactory 4 in Berlin - lifting Germany's pipeline capacity over the next decade by 432% to 133GWh; Benchmark notes the charted "data changes on a monthly basis"

title: In December last year TSMC started to work on its 5nm process
description: In December last year TSMC started to work on its 5nm process. In the following January we heard from the firm's CEO about the progress of these plans, with a target launch date set for H1 2020. Now a recent report suggests that TSMC is confident of reaching its previously publicised goals, as it has started to allocate between 300 and 400 R&D staff to work on developing its 3nm process.
longFormSummary:
• TSMC started work on its 5nm process in December 2015, with a target launch of H1 2020, as reported by HEXUS on 6 October 2016
  • That report, citing CTimes News, says TSMC has allocated between 300 and 400 R&D staff to develop its 3nm process, to "break the limitation of Moore's law"; President and Co-CEO Dr. Mark Liu said the tool would be three-dimensional stacked architecture technology and that TSMC has established "the complete ecosystems with the intellectual property, automation solutions and equipment providers", and has already earmarked the same 3nm staff to move on to 1nm development
  • By 3 April 2019 TSMC announced in Hsinchu that its 5nm process was "already in risk production" and that it had delivered the complete version of its 5nm design infrastructure within the Open Innovation Platform - full Design Rule Manual, SPICE model, PDKs and silicon-validated IP - with customers having "already started intensive design engagements, paving the way for product tape-outs, pilot activities and early sampling"
  • Against the 7nm process, TSMC put 5nm at 1.8X logic density and a 15% speed gain on an ARM Cortex-A72 core, helped by process simplification from EUV lithography
  • At IEDM in December 2019 TSMC's paper gave ~1.84x logic density increase and a 15% power gain or 30% power reduction, with a 256 Mb SRAM-plus-logic test chip yielding 80% on average and 90%+ at peak, and the densest reported high-density SRAM cell at 21000 nm2 (0.021 um2)
  • That newer disclosure confirmed the 2016 target date: "The technology is currently in risk production, with high volume production scheduled for the first half of 2020. This means that chips built on 5nm should be ready in the latter half of 2020."
  • N5 uses TSMC's 5th generation FinFET and EUV extensively over 10+ layers, which for the first time reduces the number of process masks with a new node - an estimated 75-80 masks versus the 110+ it might have been without EUV; design-technology co-optimisation gave the test chip a 40% chip size reduction, without which it would have been about 25.1 mm2 at 73% yield rather than 80%
  • As of the April 2019 release TSMC described its most advanced process in production as 7-nanometer, serving customers with annual capacity of 12 million 12-inch equivalent wafers in 2019 from fabs in Taiwan, the United States and China
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per hexus.net: "…progress of these plans, with a target launch date set for H1 2020. Now a recent report suggests th…"

title: Polymetal Installs Its Record 1,100-Tonne Gold Autoclave at Amursk
description: Belgian engineering firm Coek Engineering built the world's largest gold-processing autoclave, a 1,100-tonne titanium-lined pressure vessel, and shipped it 25,000 km from Antwerp to Polymetal's Amursk POX-2 plant in Russia's Far East. The vessel was installed on schedule in August 2020.
longFormSummary:
• Polymetal announced on 17 August 2020 that the autoclave for its Amursk POX-2 plant was installed on schedule despite COVID-19 restrictions and complex logistics
  • The autoclave was assembled by Coek Engineering in Belgium: 50 m long, 6 m diameter, 1,100 t, steel with titanium lining, rated to 240 C and 45 bar, the largest in the gold industry
  • The 55-day, 25,000 km journey ran from Geel by barge to Antwerp in mid-May 2020, on SAL's heavy-lift ship Svenja via Suez to De Kastri (30 days), then by Ro-Ro barge up the Amur to a purpose-built berth at Amursk, and by multi-axle trailer to site; equipment and logistics cost about $27 million
  • POX-2 will process double-refractory ore at twice the pressure and 40 C higher temperature than POX-1, so all refractory ore is processed in-house; start-up was planned for Q3 2023
dateConfidenceReasoning: International Mining reported on 17 August 2020 that Polymetal's 1,100-tonne autoclave vessel had been installed on schedule at the Amursk POX-2 site.

title: Bosch Opens €1 Billion Chip Fab in Dresden
description: Bosch opened its new 300mm wafer fab in Dresden, a roughly €1 billion, highly automated plant producing sensors and microchips for cars and consumer electronics.
longFormSummary:
• Bosch's press kit for the Dresden fab leads with a press release dated 07.06.2021, "Bosch opens wafer fab of the future in Dresden", alongside two presentations of the same date, "Bosch opens new wafer fab in Dresden: fully connected, full of artificial intelligence" and "Come and see the future in Dresden: the new wafer fab is giving birth to technology for tomorrow's world"
  • The kit itself is headed "Bosch opens chip factory of the future in Dresden" and carries its own date stamp of 25.05.2021, though it indexes material dated up to 2023; it is tagged "#Connected mobility"
  • Image and video captions name the event as the "Official opening of the 300-millimeter wafer fab in Dresden", with Michael Kretschmer, Minister-President of Saxony, present, and the kit carries a "Video recording press conference" and a "Video recording opening ceremony"
  • Captions describe the plant as having a "digital twin", producing MEMS sensors, with "First wafers pass through fully automated fabrication process at Bosch's new wafer fab in Dresden"; TV footage includes drone recordings and construction work
  • Earlier items in the kit trace the run-up: a release of 08.03.2021, "Bosch reaches milestone on the way to opening new wafer fab in Dresden", and one of 25.05.2021, "Six reasons why Bosch's new 300-millimeter wafer fab is one of the world's most modern chip factories"
  • Neither link supports the pin's "roughly EUR 1 billion" figure: the captured page is the press-kit index rather than the release itself, and it gives no figures for the fab's investment, capacity or headcount
  • The pin's own source is a Free Documentary - Engineering film, "Bosch Mega Factory: Inside One of Europe's Most Advanced Chip Plants", published 2026-03-08, which visits a Bosch factory making "highly sensitive sensors and microchips for the automotive industry and consumer electronics all over the world" and notes a manufacturing process involving particle accelerators and autonomously acting robots; it says nothing about the 2021 opening itself

title: Biden Signs the $1.2 Trillion Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act
description: President Biden signed the bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act into law, directing $1.2 trillion toward roads, bridges, rail, water systems and broadband nationwide.
longFormSummary:
• President Biden signed the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (H.R. 3684, Pub. L. 117-58) on 15 November 2021 at a White House South Lawn ceremony of about 800 guests
  • The Senate passed it 69-30 on 10 August 2021 and the House agreed 228-206 on 5 November 2021, with 13 Republicans joining most Democrats
  • It provides about $1.2 trillion, including $550 billion of new spending, for roads, bridges, transit, rail, broadband, clean water and the electric grid
  • Senate-version figures included $110 billion for roads and bridges, $39 billion transit, $66 billion rail, $7.5 billion EV chargers and $65 billion broadband
  • Portman and Sinema led the negotiations; the bill drew 19 Senate Republicans, and House Republicans who backed it faced threats and attacks from Marjorie Taylor Greene
  • The act authorised federal highway and public transportation spending from fiscal 2022 through 30 September 2026, which is when its authorisations expired
  • Congress has since extended those authorities to 11 December 2026 in H.R. 6500, the stopgap signed on 2 September 2026
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: "Biden signed the bill into law at a signing ceremony on November 15." Its authorisations ran FY2022-FY2026 and expired on 30 September 2026, per CRS R47573.

title: Sydney Approves Taller Skyscrapers Above Its 235m Cap
description: Sydney's decades-old rule capping buildings at 235m, tied to the height of Sydney Tower, gave way as the state government approved a planning framework allowing towers up to 310m.
longFormSummary:
• Sydney's height limit of 235 m, introduced with aviation authorities because of Kingsford Smith Airport, is based on the underside of Centrepoint (Sydney) Tower, meant to stay the highest point
  • Height limits have a long history: NSW parliament capped new buildings at 150 m in 1912 over fire and public health concerns, and the limit stood until 1957
  • From the mid-to-late 2010s case-by-case exemptions allowed towers such as the 271 m Crown Sydney and 263 m Salesforce Tower
  • In 2021 the City of Sydney said the state government approved a planning framework allowing buildings up to 310 m if sun access, wind and airport criteria are met
  • Follow-on: proposals of 305 m and 309 m towers (Lendlease's O'Connell precinct and a Dexus tower) were reported in 2024, and in July 2025 Council endorsed raising the limit at 56-60 Pitt Street to 310 m for a 70-storey building, with a 319 m, 71-storey tower planned at 1-25 O'Connell Street
address: Sydney Tower, Sydney, New South Wales, Australia
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: "In 2021, the City of Sydney announced that the state government had approved its planning framework that would allow buildings of up to 310m."

title: The best video games of 2022 | CNN Underscored
description:
Whether you play on PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch, PC or even mobile, we've picked out the 25 best games of 2022 that you should check out right now.

As the video game industry continues to adjust to post-pandemic life, more and more excellent games continue to grace every platform.

Sony dropped some of the biggest first-party blockbusters of the year, including the superb God of War Ragnarok, the expansive Horizon Forbidden West and the revamped The Last of Us Part 1. Meanwhile, Microsoft and Nintendo got a few major exclusives under their own belts with standouts like As Dusk Falls and Bayonetta 3. Between all of those were phenomenal third-party releases, including Elden Ring, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 and Need for Speed Unbound.
longFormSummary:
• CNN Underscored (Ural Garrett, updated 13 December 2022) picks its 25 best video games of 2022 across PlayStation, Xbox, Switch, PC and mobile
  • Sony picks include God of War Ragnarok (longer, upgraded combat, wraps up the Norse arc), Horizon Forbidden West (adds underwater traversal) and Gran Turismo 7 (PS5 ray tracing, 4K/60fps)
  • Nintendo picks include Bayonetta 3, Kirby and the Forgotten Land (first fully 3D Kirby), Mario + Rabbids Sparks of Hope, Splatoon 3 and Pokemon Scarlet and Violet; Microsoft's pick is As Dusk Falls
  • Elden Ring, the From Software and George R. R. Martin collaboration, sold nearly 18 million copies and became Bandai Namco's fastest-selling game
  • Other picks include Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, Need for Speed Unbound, The Callisto Protocol, Stray, A Plague Tale: Requiem, Marvel Snap and Sifu

title: Sifu Review - IGN
description: From the very first punch, Sifu is utterly uncompromising in its design. Absolver developer Sloclap’s latest martial arts beat-em-up is bold, its combat exquisite, its animation top-notch, its music outstanding, and its story – while very simple – is poignant and elegantly told. It’s also unforgiving and unapologetic, with pockets of frustrating moments during which I was certainly not in my happy place. But by the end, Sifu offered me a nearly unparalleled sense of mastery and accomplishment, and I can’t imagine that I would’ve enjoyed it half as much if it pulled its punches.
longFormSummary:
• Sloclap's Sifu launched 8 February 2022 on PS4, PS5 and PC (Epic Games Store), after Game Informer reported on 18 November 2021 that the date moved up from 22 February
  • Announced at Sony's State of Play in February 2021, it was delayed from 2021 to polish; the standard edition cost $39.99 and the deluxe $49.99
  • The player, whose father and martial arts master is killed, spends eight years training and hunts five people involved
  • A magical pendant revives you at the cost of ageing with each death, trading max health for damage; when it breaks the next death ends the run
  • Combat is inspired by Bak Mei kung fu with a Sekiro-style structure meter and environmental takedowns
  • IGN's review (Mitchell Saltzman) praises exquisite combat, animation and music and a "nearly unparalleled sense of mastery and accomplishment", with repetition the pain point
  • Later: Switch 8 November 2022, Xbox 28 March 2023, over 4 million sold by May 2025, and a TV adaptation on Prime Video in December 2024
  • Sloclap planned free post-launch content updates

title: Horizon Forbidden West Review  - IGN
description: Successful sequels build on their predecessors in multiple ways – think Mass Effect 2, Assassin's Creed 2, and Uncharted 2. They all improve what came before them by conjuring up exciting new gameplay mechanics, developing characters through engaging stories, and switching up mission design to offer variety. In other words, they take a solid base and combine with new elements to create more advanced bonds, much like an alloy… or in this case, an Aloy. Horizon Forbidden West does this with aplomb, building on the already impressive foundations of 2017’s Horizon Zero Dawn to tell a thrilling story full of familiar explosive combat against elaborate robotic foes and blockbuster action sequences, but also adding Witcher-like settlements to the map and filling it out with great side quests. There’s a genuine sense of exploration and loads of completely involving lore behind it all to uncover. The result is a fantastic open-world action-adventure that, despite falling into a couple of its old habits, emphatically delivers on the promises made five years ago.
longFormSummary:
• Guerrilla's Horizon Forbidden West was dated 18 February 2022 for PS4 and PS5 in an 25 August 2021 PlayStation Blog post, with pre-orders from 2 September 2021; the move to 2022 was blamed on the pandemic

  • IGN's review (Simon Cardy) calls it "a triumphant combination of enthralling combat, top-tier creature and character design, and a captivating open world" but short of revolutionary
  • New content includes Relic Ruins puzzles, the Machine Strike board game, Witcher-like settlements and strong side quests; the playthrough took about 32 hours
  • Reception was generally positive, with nominations for Game of the Year at The Game Awards 2022; it sold over 8.4 million units by April 2023
  • A Windows port followed 21 March 2024 and the Burning Shores expansion in April 2023

title: New Ceramic Coating Could Make Hypersonic Air Travel a Reality
description: The new coating is 12 times more effective than current ceramics. Dennis Muilenburg, CEO of Boeing has said that hypersonic passenger jets could be in the air within the next ten years. These aircraft would cut travel times by up to 700 percent. This would mean a flight from Shanghai to New York would be reduced from 15 hours to just two.
longFormSummary:
• Researchers at the University of Manchester, working with Central South University (CSU) in China and the Royce Institute, developed a carbide-based ceramic coating for hypersonic air, space and defence uses; Manchester announced it on 06 July 2017, The Engineer reported it on 10 Jul 2017 and Interesting Engineering on Jul 11, 2017.
  • The coating resists temperatures up to 3,000 C and is reported to perform 12 times better than zirconium carbide (ZrC), "a widely used UHTC often found in tool bits".
  • It is made by reactive melt infiltration (RMI), "which reduces the time needed to make such materials", and reinforced with a carbon-carbon composite, "making it extremely resistant to typical surface degradation"; it was manufactured at CSU's Powder Metallurgy Institute and studied at Manchester's School of Materials.
  • The problem it addresses: hypersonic flight is "defined as Mach five or above" and would subject aircraft to external temperatures between 2,000 and 3,000 C, leading to oxidation and ablation, and "conventional UHTCs can't currently satisfy the associated ablation requirements of hypersonic flight". Interesting Engineering puts the Mach 5 figure as "up to 3,600F to 5400F".
  • Prof. Philip Withers: "At present one of the biggest challenges is how to protect critical components such as leading edges, combustors and nose tips so that they survive the severe oxidation and extreme scouring of heat fluxes such temperatures cause to excess during flight"; he said a hypersonic plane could fly London to New York in two hours.
  • The study was led by Prof. Ping Xiao, who said "Current candidate UHTCs for use in extreme environments are limited and it is worthwhile exploring the potential of new single-phase ceramics in terms of reduced evaporation and better oxidation resistance"; it is published as "Ablation-resistant carbide Zr0.8Ti0.2C0.74B0.26 for oxidizing environments up to 3,000 C", Nature Communications 15836 (2017).
  • The coating could also make spacecraft re-entry safer, but "Workable hypersonic vehicles are still a distant dream"; Lockheed Martin and DARPA have announced plans to revive hypersonic vehicle development.
  • Boeing CEO Dennis Muilenburg said of hypersonic passenger aircraft that "in the next decade or two you're going to see them become a reality", with Shanghai to New York cut from 15 hours to two; separately, Colorado's Boom is developing a commercial supersonic jet, with five airlines thought to have placed orders after the Paris Airshow, though commercial viability is uncertain given high operating costs.
dateConfidenceReasoning: No wording about the date found on interestingengineering.com; treat it as unverified.

title: Elden Ring Review  - IGN
description: In the 87 hours that it took me to beat Elden Ring, I was put through an absolute wringer of emotion: Anger as I was beaten down by its toughest challenges, exhilaration when I finally overcame them, and a fair amount of sorrow for the mountains of exp I lost along the way to some of the toughest boss encounters FromSoftware has ever conceived. But more than anything else I was in near-constant awe – from the many absolutely jaw-dropping vistas, the sheer scope of an absolutely enormous world, the frequently harrowing enemies, and the way in which Elden Ring nearly always rewarded my curiosity with either an interesting encounter, a valuable reward, or something even greater. FromSoftware takes the ball that The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild got rolling and runs with it, creating a fascinating and dense open world about freedom and exploration above all else, while also somehow managing to seamlessly weave a full-on Dark Souls game into the middle of it. It shouldn’t be a surprise to anyone that Elden Ring ended up as one of the most unforgettable gaming experiences I’ve ever had.
longFormSummary:
• FromSoftware's Elden Ring released 25 February 2022 on PS4, PS5, Xbox One, Xbox Series X/S and PC
  • IGN's review (Mitchell Saltzman; 87 hours to finish) calls it FromSoftware's "largest and most ambitious game yet" that "moved a genre forward"; it later won IGN's 2022 Game of the Year
  • The player is a Tarnished in the Lands Between; George R.R. Martin is credited as scenario writer, though the story is opaque and he did little to change how From tells stories
  • Its open world draws on Breath of the Wild, with director Hidetaka Miyazaki saying he feels "deeply unworthy of the comparison"
  • Polygon calls it the studio's best, most approachable and most difficult game; Eurogamer finds it "a touch more welcoming", with Spirit Summons, Stakes of Marika and swappable Ashes of War
  • Difficulty stays high, with late bosses near the line of fairness

title: Gran Turismo 7 Review - IGN
description: From the first honk of the series’ iconic countdown klaxon, there are moments during Gran Turismo 7 when it feels almost like a remake of the 1997 original. In the space of a moment I’m 16 again and stuffing earthshaking turbos into a bright red Mitsubishi GTO, wondering how I’m going to be able to beat my dad around Trial Mountain when he always gets the DualShock and I have to make do with our only other controller – a terrible, translucent blue aftermarket job with no analogue sticks. That’s a kind of magic a video game series can’t buy; it can only earn. Gran Turismo 7 has that magic; that compulsive car upgrade loop the series established, plus the hot looks and sterling handling to back it up. But there’s a lot more to Gran Turismo 7 than the sum of its nostalgia – even if there are still a few traditions it should’ve left in its rear-view mirror.
longFormSummary:

  • The Gran Turismo Cafe hub introduces licences and cars through 39 "menu books", making it "the most welcoming GT ever"
  • Criticisms: expensive upgrades and microtransactions, flawed rolling starts, a smaller car list than rivals and always-online single-player

title: Kirby and the Forgotten Land Review - IGN
description: Kirby is no stranger to reinvention. His ability to transform himself into all sorts of shapes and sizes aside, the games he’s in often experiment with new settings and gimmicks as well – whether it’s rolling a limbless Kirby with the DS stylus in Canvas Curse, piloting mechs in Planet Robobot, or fundamentally changing how he transforms in Epic Yarn. Kirby and the Forgotten Land might seem like another addition to that list at first glance, this time warping the traditionally 2D structure into 3D levels. But in reality, this platformer feels like the next big step for a more classic Kirby formula rather than an upheaval of it, and it’s one that skillfully translates the things I love about Kirby into a fresh – but still familiar – new perspective.

  • Commercially it was #1 in the UK and Japan at launch and reached 7.52 million copies by 31 March 2024, the series' best-seller; it won Best Family Game at The Game Awards 2022

Like many of developer Supermassive’s previous games, The Quarry is clearly made both by and for people who love horror movies. From the start, it slowly builds tension and atmosphere, getting you invested by constantly asking you to make small decisions that will guide its teenage cast of potential murder victims. By the time the blood started flying, every choice felt like one more step in a rolling disaster, and that made it nearly impossible to put down. When I went back to replay it again, however, it was impossible to ignore just how non-interactive much of The Quarry actually is. As a spiritual sequel to Until Dawn, it's a better movie, but a worse game.

You follow the story of nine camp counselors who get stuck in the woods for one more night at the end of the summer, with nothing to do but throw one last party before they go back to their lives. There's something stalking them from the treeline (because of course there is) and your choices determine which, if any, of the counselors will be able to survive the night. This setup layers three fairly textbook horror plots on top of each other as you progress, but you can tell that Supermassive Games had a lot of fun figuring out how to connect them together. When you play, you may think you're in one type of horror movie, but you're often in another.
longFormSummary:
• Supermassive Games' The Quarry, published by 2K, released 10 June 2022 on PC, PS5, Xbox Series X/S, PS4 and Xbox One, as a spiritual successor to Until Dawn
  • Nine camp counselors are stuck at Hackett's Quarry summer camp for one more night, and player choices decide who survives
  • IGN's review (Thomas Wilde) scores it 7 (good): "it's a better movie, but a worse game", with long stretches lacking meaningful choice and a Movie Mode that plays without interactivity
  • Game Informer's review (Andrew Reiner, 8 June 2022) scores it 8.5, praising a "spiderweb of paths leading to 186 potential endings" and calling it "the sequel we've been dying to play"
  • Criticisms include coin-flip choices, a "use a life" system that undermines consequences and telegraphed quick-time events
  • The cast includes Ariel Winter, Siobhan Williams, Justice Smith, Brenda Song, David Arquette and Ted Raimi

description:
Growing up as a child of the 90s, whenever I stepped into an arcade, I’d always do a walk around to see what they had before putting my quarters into any machines. Best of all, it transforms the arcadey quarter-munching design of combat into something much more skill forward while still maintaining the same button mashy appeal. title: Stray Review - IGN
description:
A delightful cat-based platforming adventure in a cyberpunk world worth exploring.

Silent protagonists are nothing new in video games, but Stray certainly pushes that concept to an interesting place. Part platformer, part traditional adventure game, this cyberpunk world full of neon-soaked robots transforms into a giant jungle gym from your perspective, which is just one foot off the ground. The concept of putting you in the paws of an average cat may be a silly one on the surface, but Stray uses that furry vehicle to tell a genuinely compelling story with some entertaining action along the way. title: Bohunice V1 Nuclear Reactors Fully Dismantled
description: Slovakia finished fully dismantling the Soviet-era V1 reactors at Bohunice in July 2022, one of the few nuclear plants taken apart down to the reactor vessels.
longFormSummary:
• The two VVER-440 V-230 reactors at Bohunice V1 in Slovakia were fully dismantled, the first time this reactor type has been decommissioned and disassembled directly on site
  • The work was done by JAVYS and a Westinghouse-led consortium including VUJE, funded through the EBRD-managed Bohunice International Decommissioning Support Fund
  • Twelve 160-tonne steam generators were removed to make room for two 1,250 m3 pools for underwater sectioning; about 95 per cent of waste and metals were already processed and released
  • Decommissioning of the two reactors began in May 2020 and April 2021 and took 18 and 11 months
  • The reactors were closed at the end of 2006 and 2008 under Slovakia's EU accession terms; remaining equipment is to be processed by 2025 and buildings demolished with the site redevelopment-ready by 2027
  • Donor funds exceeded EUR650 million as of mid-2018, and the work was completed on schedule and within budget

title: Pelosi Lands in Taipei
description: The first Speaker of the House to visit Taiwan in 25 years touched down in Taipei on the night of 2 August 2022. Within hours the PLA's Eastern Theater Command began live-fire exercises around the island, opening the Fourth Taiwan Strait Crisis.
longFormSummary:
• Speaker Nancy Pelosi and members of a congressional delegation issued their statement on arrival in Taipei on 2 August 2022; it was "the first official visit to Taiwan by a Speaker of the United States House of Representatives in 25 years"
  • "Our Congressional delegation's visit to Taiwan honors America's unwavering commitment to supporting Taiwan's vibrant Democracy," the statement said
  • Taiwan was one stop on a wider Indo-Pacific trip taking in Singapore, Malaysia, South Korea and Japan, "focused on mutual security, economic partnership and democratic governance"
  • The delegation argued the visit changed nothing: it "in no way contradicts longstanding United States policy, guided by the Taiwan Relations Act of 1979, U.S.-China Joint Communiques and the Six Assurances"
  • Beijing did not read it that way. On the night of 2 August the PLA Eastern Theater Command began joint naval and air exercises north, south-west and south-east of Taiwan, with live artillery fire in the Strait and conventional missile tests to the east
  • Taiwan's defence ministry reported 21 PLA aircraft in its air defence identification zone on 2 August, and 22 crossing the median line the next day
  • Large-scale drills encircling Taiwan ran from 4 to 11 August, the biggest Chinese escalation in 26 years; five of the ballistic missiles fired on 4 August landed inside Japan's exclusive economic zone
  • The delegation's aircraft, callsign SPAR19, became the most-tracked flight in FlightRadar24's history, with 2.92 million people following it
address: Taipei Songshan Airport, Songshan District, Taipei, Taiwan

title: Vistula Spit Canal Opens, Bypassing Russian Waters
description: Poland opened the Vistula Spit Canal, a new $450M channel letting ships reach the port of Elbląg without passing through Russian-controlled waters near Kaliningrad.
longFormSummary:
• The canal across the Polish Vistula Spit was officially inaugurated on 17 September 2022, creating a second connection between the Vistula Lagoon and the Gulf of Gdańsk so ships can reach the port of Elbląg without passing through the Russian Strait of Baltiysk, saving a 100 km journey
  • The channel is 1,536 m long with one lock, taking ships up to 4 m draft, 100 m length and 20 m beam, and forms part of a planned 22.88 km waterway to Elbląg; "further works will continue" after the inauguration
  • Construction began on 4 October 2019, with tree cutting from February 2019; the idea dates back to 1577 under King Stephen Báthory, was revived in 1945 by Eugeniusz Kwiatkowski, and the final decision was taken on 10 November 2006 by PM Jarosław Kaczyński
  • Works included a breakwater forebay of 10,000 concrete blocks, the channel and locks, roads, two swing bridges (the southern one completed June 2021) and an artificial island of about 180 ha in the lagoon, started 30 May 2020 and tentatively named Aestian Island
  • On cost the sources are weaker than the pin: the October 2019 contract with a Polish-Belgian consortium was 992 million PLN (230 million euro) with the total project expected to reach 2 billion PLN, while the only figure anywhere on the video page is "e420m" inside the title of a cited Global Construction Review article, the video description itself giving none - neither supports the pin's "$450M"
  • Russia objected on security and environmental grounds, and there were separate environmental worries about phosphorus in lagoon sediments and cyanobacteria; The B1M's video, published 7 February 2024 as "Why Russia Tried to Block This Canal", is built on that dispute, citing reporting including The Guardian's "Poland accuses Russia of exaggerated environmental claims in canal row" and a gov.pl page on "Russian propaganda efforts against the Vistula Spit canal"
  • Footage on the video came courtesy of Besix, GRUPA NDI and the Maritime Office in Gdynia among others, indicating the contractors and authority involved
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: "the canal was officially inaugurated on 17 September 2022."

title: US Export Controls Cut China Off From Advanced Chips
description: The Commerce rule that took effect on 7 October 2022 put advanced computing chips, the tools to make them and the Americans who service them behind a licence. It is the sharpest single break in the technology relationship since 1979.
longFormSummary:
• The interim final rule "Implementation of Additional Export Controls: Certain Advanced Computing and Semiconductor Manufacturing Items; Supercomputer and Semiconductor End Use; Entity List Modification" was published on 13 October 2022, with its core provisions "effective on October 7, 2022"
  • The rest came in stages: one instruction on 12 October and twelve more on 21 October 2022
  • From 7 October the specified semiconductor manufacturing equipment became controlled for regional-stability reasons, in order "to immediately address concerns with the PRC's demonstrated intent and ability to use the specified items for activities of U.S. national security and foreign policy concern"
  • BIS skipped notice and comment, citing "the urgent need for this rule to counter China's actions" and the Export Control Reform Act's exemption
  • A new foreign direct product rule reached items made abroad with US technology when a footnote 4 entity was party to the transaction, because "many supercomputer parts and components based on U.S. technology and software are not produced in the United States"
  • A temporary general license let non-Chinese companies keep running assembly, test and distribution operations inside China from 21 October 2022 through 7 April 2023, to avoid breaking supply chains serving customers outside China
  • Goods already on the dock or in transit on 7 October could still go, provided they moved before midnight on 7 November 2022
  • The controls have been tightened repeatedly since, and BIS now requires a licence for advanced computing items going to any entity whose ultimate parent is headquartered in Country Group D:5 or Macau, wherever that entity sits
address: Herbert C. Hoover Building, 1401 Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC, United States
dateConfidenceReasoning: The rule's own DATES section reads "Effective on October 7, 2022, are the following instructions: 7 (§ 740.2), 9 (§ 740.10), 11 (§ 742.6), 17 (§ 744.23), and 25"; later instructions took effect on 12 and 21 October. No end date: the controls carry no sunset and have since been widened.

title: A Plague Tale: Requiem Review - IGN
description: Like a sugar-crazed child working their way to the bottom of a Halloween bag full of treats, A Plague Tale: Requiem is confident that the things which made the first game great will be even more delectable in ludicrous quantities. You liked massive swarms of rats? Well, how about we increase the number of them by a degree of 1,000! You enjoyed a gruesome and harrowing journey that tested the limits of your emotional resilience? Great, let’s increase your personal suffering by 200%! This follow-up to one of my favorite action-adventure games of the previous console generation turns the dials up to 11 in practically every way, and overwhelmingly benefits from those escalations despite sometimes being a bit heavy on the nihilism. With improved stealth action mechanics, a fantastic (and deeply depressing) story, and graphics that had me gawking, A Plague Tale: Requiem is an impressive glow up that’s easily worth the immense horrors it subjected me to.
longFormSummary:

  • PC Gamer's review (Jon Bailes) scores it 85, calling it "a masterful sequel and an exceptional action adventure"
  • Gameplay pairs stealth and puzzles using light against rats, with a skill tree of three playstyles and a roughly 20-hour campaign
  • Criticisms: partners getting stuck on scenery and trial-and-error stealth sections

title: Mario + Rabbids: Sparks of Hope Review - IGN
description:
When a game hits on a good idea, some developers are content to play it safe for the sequel, making a few refinements but largely stick to what worked the first time. That totally makes sense. But Mario + Rabbids: Sparks of Hope is not that kind of sequel; even though Mario + Rabbids: Kingdom Battle surprised us all with its smart XCOM-style tactics in Nintendo clothing, this followup maintains its best ideas but reinvents itself to the point where it immediately feels very different. It’s bigger and better in nearly every way, with a more freeform and customizable take on combat and an almost completely rethought overworld that’s much less linear and absolutely packed with puzzles. The story’s all over the place and the Switch can’t always handle everything smoothly, but it’s a fantastic game that can be played as either an enjoyable cakewalk or a deep, demanding tactical challenge, all while maintaining its zany sense of humor.

Picking back up in the post-Rabbid invasion Mushroom Kingdom, things immediately get even weirder when a giant manta ray from space arrives to cause trouble. The story is actually one of Sparks of Hope’s few missteps: the original’s trans-dimensional blending of Mario characters and goofball Rabbids is completely absurd, but it kind of makes sense in its own way. This time, though, the completely unrelated enemy spreads what’s effectively Ganon’s corrupt ooze with eyeballs from Breath of the Wild everywhere, and most but not all of her minions are also Rabbids for some reason? Also we have a spaceship for traveling between literal worlds? It makes Kingdom Battle look grounded in reality by comparison, which is something I never thought I’d say about that game. I wasn’t expecting deep lore or anything, but it’s kind of a mess. It does consistently have some pretty good jokes, though, so at least I was chuckling as I was scratching my head.
longFormSummary:
• Ubisoft Milan and Paris's Mario + Rabbids Sparks of Hope launched 20 October 2022 on Nintendo Switch, a date revealed at the 28 June 2022 Nintendo Mini Direct
  • IGN's review (Dan Stapleton) scores it 9 (amazing, Editors' Choice), saying it "takes the excellent tactical combat ideas of Kingdom Battle and runs absolutely wild with them"
  • Combat drops the visible grid, adds real-time team jumps and dozens of "Sparks" power-ups, with a less linear, puzzle-packed overworld
  • Criticisms: the story is "kind of a mess" and the Switch cannot always keep up
  • Metacritic scores 85/100 and IGN, GameSpot and Game Informer each give 9/10
  • Ubisoft said it underperformed commercially, with nearly 3 million copies sold by January 2024; three DLC expansions followed in 2023
  • It was the last Mario title with Charles Martinet as Mario and Luigi before he stepped down in 2023
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per ign.com: "…irder when a giant manta ray from space arrives to cause trouble. The story is actually one of Spark…"

title: Bond Street's Elizabeth Line Station Finally Opens
description: London's Bond Street station opened to Elizabeth Line services, closing out the last and most delayed piece of the Crossrail project.
longFormSummary:
• The first Elizabeth line services reached Bond Street at 05.47 on Monday 24 October 2022, welcomed by Andy Byford, Sadiq Khan and Katherine Fletcher
  • Bond Street was originally due to open with the other stations in December 2018, but construction issues led to its being announced in 2018 that it would open after them; the line itself opened in May 2022
  • The opening completed the central section, which now has 10 new stations; through services from east and west were under two weeks away
  • The station has two ticket halls, step-free lifts, and a 60 m escalator at the Hanover Square entrance; entrances are near Oxford Street and Regent Street
  • Trains run every five minutes, moving to every three to four minutes at peak from 6 November, with Liverpool Street eight minutes and Canary Wharf 15 minutes away
  • The station is expected to serve over 140,000 people a day, and Khan cited a 42 billion pound boost to the UK economy from the line
