title: Bayonetta 3 Review - IGN
description: I hold the Bayonetta series’ combat in such high esteem that I’d consider it in the top five or so combat systems of all time, right next to the Devil May Cry, God of War, Ninja Gaiden, and Batman Arkham games. It’s just incredible to look at, feels equally amazing to play, and is jam packed with opportunities for style and creativity thanks to the wide assortment of wild weapons at your disposal. Bayonetta 3 just further cements its legacy, strutting out with a surprising sequel in that it actually takes a lot of risks with changing up its established formula in an effort to revitalize a combat system that only slightly evolved between the first two games. Fortunately those risks pay off. Bayonetta 3 is an invigorated sequel with fresh new ideas that embolden its 13-year-old combat system, an impressive amount of variety throughout its 10 to 12-hour campaign, and more of that trademark sexy Bayonetta style that makes the series one of a kind.
longFormSummary:

  • The story is called the weakest of the trilogy and Switch performance "decidedly not great"; Jennifer Hale voices Bayonetta in place of Hellena Taylor

title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 review
description:
Modern Warfare 2's greatest strength is that it doesn't have a gimmick, because it doesn't need one.All Modern Warfare 2 needs to be is a great shooter, and it delivers. This is the Cal

Modern Warfare 2's greatest strength is that it doesn't have a gimmick, because it doesn't need one.

All Modern Warfare 2 needs to be is a great shooter, and it delivers. This is the Call of Duty experience, deconstructed, reconsidered, and obsessively optimized over 15 uninterrupted years of iteration. I know when I'm playing a Black Ops game because it has offbeat arcade modes and the latest iteration of Nuketown. I know I'm playing a Modern Warfare game because the shooting is so finely tuned that I want to take my Gunsmith build out to dinner. Infinity Ward has officially mastered the instant gratification of aiming down sights and deleting targets.

That goes a long way, though some of Modern Warfare 2's biggest swings, such as revamped progression and a genre-bending campaign, are less elegant. It also suffers from an obtuse UI, fits of crashes, weird bugs, and the unexplained absence of basic features like stat tracking. But altogether, it's a good year for Call of Duty.
longFormSummary:
• Infinity Ward's Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 released 28 October 2022
  • PC Gamer (Morgan Park, 3 November 2022) scores it 83, saying it "sets a new bar for Call of Duty all over again" with best-in-class gunplay and simulated ballistics
  • Criticisms: byzantine Gunsmith progression, an obtuse UI, crashes, bugs and "the unexplained absence of basic features like stat tracking"
  • Movement is the slowest in recent Call of Duty, with slide canceling and bunnyhopping removed
  • IGN's campaign-only review (Matt Purslow) scores the roughly six-hour campaign 6, calling it "an unfortunate misfire" with a paper-thin story and bullet-sponge enemies
  • IGN's multiplayer review (Seth G. Macy, 1 November 2022) scored it 8

title: God of War Ragnarok Review - IGN
description: How do you follow up on one of the greatest video games of all time? Sony Santa Monica finds itself in a situation not dissimilar to when Francis Ford Coppola created the sequel to his mob movie masterpiece, The Godfather. Like part two of the Corleone story, God of War Ragnarok puts a fierce, younger member of the family directly under the microscope. In doing so it manages to reach the heights of its predecessor and, in some ways, even tower above it. The writing, performances, and music are each exceptional, bringing this expansive Norse tapestry to life – but even as it holds your heart in one hand with its elegantly told story it’s crunching bones in the other with fantastically ferocious combat. It all binds together to forge a monumental action epic that adds yet another impressive landmark to the video game landscape.

title: Pokémon Scarlet and Violet Review - IGN
description: It is still unbelievable to me that after 26 years of linear, straightforward RPGs, developer Game Freak really looked Pokémon players dead in the eye and said, “It’s fine, go wherever you want.” In the lead-up to the launch of Pokémon Scarlet and Violet, I thought this claim would end up being a marketing gimmick, a little joke, something we’d all be mad about later. But from the moment I left the hallowed halls of Uva Academy, that promise has been wonderfully fulfilled, with open-world, open-ended gameplay serving as a shining beacon for the future of this beloved franchise. And yet, a finger on the cursed Mankey’s paw has curled anyway – Scarlet and Violet’s wonderfully innovative design is dramatically undermined by the numerous ways in which they feel deeply unfinished, with issues ranging from an incomplete world to massive and ubiquitous technical problems. So even though I want to celebrate how this generation reinvents and reinvigorates the world of Pokémon, I can’t without putting a great big warning label on it.

  • Praise covers going anywhere after Uva Academy, no level scaling, roughly 400 species and online co-op; criticism covers an empty world, facade buildings and pervasive technical problems
  • Legendaries Koraidon and Miraidon serve as mounts, with Terastal Tera Types and Tera Raids for up to four players
  • Reception was mixed, with Metacritic 72/100 for Scarlet and 71/100 for Violet
  • Sales were a record: over 10 million copies in three days, and 27.15 million by June 2025
  • DLC: The Teal Mask (13 September 2023), The Indigo Disk (14 December 2023) and the Mochi Mayhem epilogue (11 January 2024)

With Criterion Games (of Burnout fame) at the helm, Unbound had the potential to be one of the best racing games of the year—or a return to series form after a few missteps. title: The Callisto Protocol Review - IGN
description: A proper remake might be rising from the grave next year, but the festering corpse of Dead Space has come lurching back to life early in the form of The Callisto Protocol. This spiritual successor to the sci-fi survival horror series recreates the haunting blood-streaked hallways and space zombie-slaying hallmarks first established on the USG Ishimura back in 2008, and injects the gore with more awe than ever before thanks to some strikingly detailed splashes of blood and guts. Unfortunately, while the mutant dismemberment has never been more vivid, The Callisto Protocol’s shortcomings appear just as clearly. Occasional control annoyances, imbalanced combat, and a general absence of innovation result in a roughly eight-hour massacre that’s gratifyingly gruesome, but never quite as great as the series that inspired it.

title: Marvel's Midnight Suns Review - IGN
description: One of my favorite things about watching superheroes duke it out is when someone gets smacked so hard they fly backwards and crash through solid walls, explode tanker trucks, or slam into their friends. It’s an awesome demonstration of just how strong these godlike characters are supposed to be, and it’s always a disappointment when a superhero game doesn’t quite capture that feeling. With Marvel’s Midnight Suns, however, Firaxis has built a deep and innovative turn-based tactical combat system around the joy of having Iron Man, Dr. Strange, Blade, and more knock enemies around like toys they're trying to break – and that hasn’t gotten old in the roughly 75 hours of its surprisingly expansive RPG campaign. A lot of that time isn’t spent in battles, though, and while it’s certainly appealing to get up close and personal with this cast of more than a dozen popular and lesser-known Marvel heroes, it does tend to go a bit overboard with convincing Earth’s mightiest heroes to all be your BFFs.

title: Merdeka 118's Spire Completes as World's Second Tallest
description: Kuala Lumpur's Merdeka 118 topped out with its spire in place, reaching 678.9m to become the world's second-tallest building and one of only four megatall skyscrapers on Earth.
longFormSummary:
• Merdeka 118's spire was completed in December 2022; the structure itself was completed in November 2023, after the concrete core topped out in August 2020 and the building topped out in November 2021
  • The finished tower stands 678.9 m (2,227 ft) over 118 storeys in the Merdeka Precinct of Kuala Lumpur, described as the second-tallest building in the world after the Burj Khalifa and the tallest in Malaysia and Southeast Asia, surpassing Landmark 81. The B1M titles its films "Building the World's Second Tallest Skyscraper" and, in 2021, "Building the World's Last Megatall Skyscraper", calling Merdeka PNB118 "the second tallest building ever constructed - and the world's last megatall skyscraper"
  • The developer is Permodalan Nasional Berhad, on a budget of RM5 billion that drew public criticism; the project was announced by Prime Minister Abdullah Badawi on 12 September 2007
  • Construction ran on an RM3.4 billion contract awarded on 23 November 2015 to a Samsung C&T and UEM Group joint venture, with work halted on 18 March 2020 by the COVID-19 Movement Control Order and resumed in mid-May 2020; engineers were Leslie E. Robertson Associates, Robert Bird Group and Arup, with Turner International as project management consultant
  • The design is inspired by Tunku Abdul Rahman's outstretched hand chanting "Merdeka!" in 1957, with a diamond-shaped glass facade of 18,144 panels covering 114,000 sq m and 400,000 sq m of space; KONE supplies about 87 elevators and escalators, and is the promoted partner of the B1M video in which Fred Mills "travels to the top of Malaysia's Merdeka 118"
  • The B1M's 2021 film gives special thanks to PNB Merdeka Ventures and Fender Katsalidis Architects
  • Occupation lagged the structure: the grand opening on 10 January 2024 was inaugurated by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong but the tower did not open to the public as scheduled, the Park Hyatt Kuala Lumpur began operating on levels 75 to 112 on 7 August 2025, and the rest "remains far behind schedule as of 1 July 2026"; the tower was renamed Merdeka Maybank Tower in July 2026 for anchor tenant Maybank

title: An F-22 Shoots Down a Chinese Surveillance Balloon
description: A single AIM-9X fired from 58,000 feet brought down a 90-foot Chinese balloon off Myrtle Beach on 4 February 2023, after it had drifted across the continental United States for a week. It was the F-22's first air-to-air kill, and it cost Antony Blinken his trip to Beijing.
longFormSummary:
• At 2:39 p.m. Eastern on 4 February 2023 an F-22 Raptor of the 1st Fighter Wing, Joint Base Langley-Eustis, fired one AIM-9X Sidewinder into the balloon off the coast of South Carolina
  • The fighter shot from 58,000 feet at a balloon flying at 60,000 to 65,000 feet, roughly 90 feet across; F-15s from Barnes Air National Guard Base and several tankers supported the intercept. It was the first known air-to-air kill by an F-22
  • Defense Secretary Lloyd Austin said US fighters "successfully brought down the high altitude surveillance balloon launched by and belonging to the People's Republic of China", which "was being used by the PRC in an attempt to surveil strategic sites in the continental United States"
  • The balloon entered the US air defence identification zone near the Aleutians on 28 January, crossed into Canadian airspace on 30 January and re-entered over northern Idaho on 31 January
  • F-22s were scrambled from Nellis on 1 February while the US considered shooting it down over Montana, near the Malmstrom ICBM field, but commanders judged that "downing the balloon while over land posed an undue risk to people across a wide area"
  • The Pentagon did not acknowledge the balloon until 2 February, after civilians had photographed it over Montana, which drew criticism from both parties in Congress
  • The incident cancelled Secretary of State Antony Blinken's visit to China, scheduled for 3 February, which would have been the first cabinet-level US visit of the Biden administration
  • US Navy and Coast Guard units recovered the envelope and payload from the Atlantic over the following days

title: Hogwarts Legacy Review - IGN
description: Like many, I’ve been waiting for a truly excellent Harry Potter game since I was in the third grade. In that time, we’ve gotten some respectable LEGO Potter games, an underwhelming EA Sports Quidditch game for some reason, and even suffered through the fevered nightmare that is Harry Potter Kinect. But none of these has come close to fulfilling that fantasy of receiving a Hogwarts admission letter that opens the door to a secret world. With Hogwarts Legacy, I’m happy to say that we finally got a Harry Potter game that captures some of that magic. Its open world map absolutely nails the vibe of Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, it has spellcasting combat that’s stupefyingly good, the characters that inhabit it are charming and unforgettable, and it is positively brimming with countless diversions to soak up dozens of hours of your time. It may not be the most impressive technical achievement and it is certainly cursed with a lack of enemy variety, but none of Hogwarts Legacy’s issues can cast a Descendo charm on this triumphant visit to the Wizarding World.

title: Rosatom Delivers ITER's Last Poloidal Field Coil to the Cadarache Site
description: A Russian-built poloidal field coil for the ITER fusion reactor reached the construction site at Cadarache, completing the set of six ring magnets that will shape and suspend the plasma.   • PF1 is 9 m in diameter (200 tonnes per World Nuclear News, about 160 tonnes per ITER) and is the top of six poloidal field coils that with the toroidal field coils shape and suspend the plasma
  • The convoy took four nights instead of three, using a 288-wheel trailer and 70 Gendarmerie officers; it is one of 141 Highly Exceptional Loads since 2015
  • Its delivery completes all six poloidal field coils and means all seven ITER Members have delivered at least one major component; the supply agreement with Rosatom's Russian ITER agency dates from 2011

title: Hivemapper is 1M kilometers closer to goal of beating Google Maps
description:
Hivemapper relied on ride-hail, delivery and truck drivers with dash cams to collect 1 million unique kms of fresh map data.

Hivemapper, the startup that puts dashcams on ride-hail and delivery vehicles to map the world, is getting a little closer to its goal of toppling the B2B mapping empire that Google has built.

With only 2% of the world’s roads mapped, Hivemapper is still very much the underdog in this fight. But Gabe Nelson, Hivemapper’s head of operations, reckons the startup is reaching an inflection point that will lead to exponential scale.

Hivemapper said Thursday it collected more than 1 million kilometers (about 620,000 miles) of unique street-level imagery. Compared to Google’s 60 million kilometers, that’s small potatoes. However, Hivemapper collected this data over the last three months. It took Google from 2007 to 2019 to collect 16.1 million kilometers of unique road data.

Now the startup aims to map 10 million unique road kilometers by early next year.

Hivemapper relies on individual contributors around the world to collect its street-view data, rather than spending millions of dollars putting dedicated mapping vehicles on the road. Its dashcams are equipped with a high-quality imager and precise GPS, and they go for $549. Mapping with dashcams, the company says, means its data is continuously being refreshed, whereas much of Google’s Street View imagery, particularly outside of urban centers, is over a decade old.
longFormSummary:
• March 23, 2023: Hivemapper said its dashcam network, on ride-hail and delivery vehicles, collected over 1 million km (about 620,000 miles) of unique street-level imagery in three months, launched November 2022
  • Only about 2% of the world's roads are mapped; Google has 60 million km, and Hivemapper targets 10 million unique road km by early 2024
  • Dashcams cost $549; contributors (over 11,000, across 418 regions) are rewarded in the HONEY token, capped at 10 billion
  • Hivemapper claims Google raised map prices 1800% since 2018; Google says its price structure is unchanged since 2018
  • SolanaFloor adds the company raised over $21 million in seed funding and aims to cover the world within a few years
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per techcrunch.com: "…by 1800%, a percentage that Hivemapper arrived at via internal estimation. Google said it hasn’t al…"

title: Resident Evil 4 Review  - IGN
description: In light of the high-quality remakes of Resident Evil 2 and 3 released in 2019 and 2020, it felt like a safe bet that Capcom would do an equally admirable job of rebuilding Resident Evil 4. Even so, when I hit the start button on this 2023 remake of the legendary 2005 action-horror game I wasn’t prepared for how forcefully it would knock my knees out from under me and suplex me headfirst into 16 hours of sustained tension and exhilaration. This fully revitalised campaign dramatically one-ups the original in almost every conceivable way. Its Spanish countryside setting is substantially more sinister, its pacing has been tightened to the point where hardly a single minute is wasted, and its controls have been modernised in order to allow its signature dynamic shooting mechanics to really shine. I’ve been waiting 18 years for a game to thrill me in the same way as Resident Evil 4; as it turns out, this whole time I’ve just been waiting for another Resident Evil 4.

title: Used vehicle prices fell last month for the first time in 2023
description:
Wholesale used vehicle prices declined last month for the first time this year.

Cox Automotive reported a 3% decline from March to April in its Manheim Used Vehicle Value Index.

Further declines could help bring used vehicle pricing down for consumers, since retail prices traditionally follow changes in wholesale prices.
longFormSummary:
• Cox Automotive's Manheim Used Vehicle Value Index fell 3% from March to April 2023, its first monthly decline of the year, as reported on May 5, 2023
  • Adjusted for mix, mileage and seasonality the index stood at 230.8, down 4.4% year over year; on a non-adjusted basis prices rose 0.1% from March but were down 5.6% year over year, and the index remained up 5.2% from December
  • Chris Frey of Cox counted eight straight months of year-over-year declines averaging 8.3% - a run he called "likely not over yet" - after values had risen 8.6% in the first quarter from December, calling it "a second, and more rapid, decent off the pandemic peak of January 2022"; the financial crisis by comparison had 16 months averaging 5.8%
  • CNBC attributed the drop to automakers increasing production of new cars and trucks, and noted that retail prices traditionally follow changes in wholesale prices
  • Wholesale market detail: daily MMR retention averaged 98.7% and sales conversion was 60.9% (against 63.6% in April 2019); used retail sales were estimated down 8% from March and year over year, with retail days' supply at 42 and wholesale supply at 25 days
  • New-vehicle sales ran ahead of a year earlier, up 9.0% year over year at a 15.9 million SAAR (14.3 million a year earlier, 14.8 million in March), with fleet share at 17.5% and rental fleet sales up 64% year over year
  • On the retail side the average listed used price was $26,086 in February, slightly below January; Charlie Chesbrough said tight supply may support prices and that a massive decline is "unlikely"
  • Used-vehicle prices are watched by investors and the Biden administration as a barometer of inflation; Cox said full April data would be released June 7, 2023, with its next quarterly call on Monday, July 10 at 11 a.m. EDT
dateConfidenceReasoning: Date has passed, but cnbc.com does not confirm it happened then; unverified.

title: Afsluitdijk's Storm-Proofing Upgrade Wraps Up in the Netherlands

title: Arianespace Launches Ariane 5 on Its Final Flight, VA261
description: Arianespace flew Europe's Ariane 5 heavy-lift rocket for the last time from the Guiana Space Centre, retiring the launcher after 27 years and 117 missions. The final flight, VA261, carried Germany's Heinrich Hertz communications satellite and France's Syracuse 4B military satellite to orbit.
longFormSummary:
• Ariane 5 flight VA261, the 117th and last Ariane 5 launch, lifted off from ELA-3 at the Guiana Space Centre on 5 July 2023 at 22:00 UTC and succeeded
  • It carried Germany's Heinrich Hertz communications satellite and France's Syracuse-4B military satellite
  • A launch planned for 15 June slipped over a booster separation problem (faulty pyrotechnical transmission lines) and again a day for weather
  • Ariane 5 debuted in June 1996 with a failure, reached a 96% success rate, and carried missions including JWST, Rosetta, BepiColombo and JUICE
  • Afterwards there were concerns about European launcher availability, with Vega C grounded and Ariane 6's first flight delayed
address: ELA-3 Launch Complex, Guiana Space Centre, Kourou, French Guiana
dateConfidenceReasoning: Spaceflight Now and ESA both confirm Ariane 5 flight VA261, the rocket's final launch, lifted off on 5 July 2023.

But the Dungeons & Dragons-based sequel has much more going for it than players' long-brimming anticipation. Developed by Larian Studios — the team behind acclaimed RPG series Divinity — Baldur's Gate III represents that rare dream pairing of a beloved property with the studio best suited to adapting it. Toss in the fact that this hotly anticipated PC game has been honed over two years of fan feedback-fueled early access, and we can't wait to party up and teach those ugly mind flayers some manners.

  • Collector's and Deluxe editions could be pre-ordered with 72-hour early access to Act I from 28 August; PC early-access players were auto-upgraded to Deluxe
  • IGN's later review by Len Hafer calls it "a new high-water mark for CRPGs", praising freedom, writing, voice work, turn-based combat and character creator, while noting bugs and Act 3 performance issues

title: Insider Shares More On Tesla's Project Highland AKA Model 3 Refresh
description:
Several test prototypes have already been spotted with camouflaged front and rear ends, suggesting the Model 3 is in for some major visual updates. But Tesla's compact sedan will get more than that. According to a "trusted insider" who offered an exclusive insight to Not A Tesla App, the Project Highland will bring significant changes inside and out. 

Starting with the design, the report notes the headlights will have a different shape, which means the front bumper will be redesigned as well. It will be more aerodynamic and will now house a single camera in the center area of the lower grille, in similar fashion to the Cybertruck.

Out back, the refreshed Tesla Model 3 is also getting a redesigned bumper, although the changes will likely be purely for aesthetic reasons.

The source also said the side mirrors will be subtly updated and the Project Highland will be getting more cameras to take advantage of the new Hardware 4.0 Autopilot supercomputer. Three new cameras will reportedly be added to the Model 3: one in the center of the front bumper and two on the sides of the car.
longFormSummary:
• Mar 2023: an insider told Not A Tesla App that the Model 3 refresh, Project Highland, would get redesigned headlights, a more aerodynamic front bumper with a single lower-grille camera, and a redesigned rear bumper, with production expected in Q3 2023
  • Reported changes: new cameras (5-megapixel versus 1.2-megapixel on Hardware 3), removal of the outside temperature sensor, and fabric replacing wood interior trim
  • Rumors on August 31, 2023 said Tesla would reveal the Highland Model 3 on September 1, with leaked photos and prototypes seen in Europe; all of this was unconfirmed
  • Wikipedia confirms a Model 3 facelift launched late 2023 for Gigafactory Shanghai markets and early 2024 for North America
dateConfidenceReasoning: Date has passed, but insideevs.com does not confirm it happened then; unverified.

title: Storm Daniel Bursts the Derna Dams
description: Two dams above Derna failed in the early hours, sending the Wadi Derna through the city. Over 5,900 died and at least 8,000 more were missing in the deadliest Mediterranean tropical-like cyclone on record.
longFormSummary:
• Storm Daniel became the deadliest Mediterranean tropical-like cyclone on record and the second-costliest tropical cyclone outside the North Atlantic. [S]
  • It formed as a low-pressure system around 4 September 2023, flooded Greece, Bulgaria and Turkey, then organised as a Mediterranean low and turned toward Libya, making landfall near Benghazi on 10 September. [S]
  • Two dams above Derna failed; the flood reached the city shortly before 03:00 EET on 11 September, sending the Wadi Derna through it. [S]
  • Over 5,900 people died and 7,000 were injured, with at least 8,000 missing. [S]
  • Libya's vulnerability was blamed on its civil war, which had damaged critical infrastructure and left it in poor condition beforehand. [S]
  • The storm was the product of an omega block — a high-pressure zone between two lows, with isobars shaped like the Greek letter. [S]
  • In Greece the rainfall caused over two billion euros in damage, the costliest recorded storm for the country. [S]
dateConfidenceReasoning: The source dates the dam failure to the early hours of 11 September: "Residents recalled hearing loud explosions at the time the dams burst, with video showing the flood reaching Derna shortly before 03:00 EET on 11 September", after the storm made landfall near Benghazi on 10 September.

references.title: Storm Daniel leads to extreme rain and floods in Mediterranean, heavy loss of life in Libya
references.reasoning: WMO's own statement on the event supplies the rainfall that broke the dams - "Torrential rains of between 150 - 240 mm caused flash floods in several cities, including Al-Bayda, which recorded the highest daily rainfall rate of 414.1 mm (from 10 Sep 8am to 11 Sep 8am)" - and confirms the Derna dam failure.

title: The One Placed Into Receivership in Toronto
description: The One, an 85-storey tower at Yonge and Bloor meant to be Canada's first supertall skyscraper, was placed into receivership after its financiers defaulted on more than $1.2BN in loans.
longFormSummary:
• The One, an 85-storey tower at Yonge and Bloor in Toronto, was taken over by a court-appointed receiver in October 2023 after financiers defaulted on more than $1.2 billion in loans
  • About $1.6 billion in debts were unpaid and costs had ballooned to more than $2 billion; the main lender was a division of KEB Hana Bank
  • Developer Sam Mizrahi bought the land for $300 million in 2014, with groundbreaking in 2017 and hotel and condos planned by 2022 at the latest
  • The lender filing cited delays, cost overruns and infighting between Mizrahi and investor Jenny Coco
  • A planned Apple Store flagship fell apart in 2021 and Apple sued in March 2022 to end its lease
  • The tower, designed by Foster and Partners, is topped out with estimated completion in 2028, and Tridel joined as developer in May 2025

title: Delhi's Namo Bharat Rapid Rail Priority Section Opens

title: All 41 Workers Freed After Silkyara Tunnel Collapse

title: Elon Musk announces timing for Tesla Cybertruck delivery event
description:
In a conference call following the release of the results, CEO Elon Musk made new comments announcing that Tesla plans to hold a “handover event,” which generally means the first deliveries of a new car, toward “the end of the third quarter.”

This would put the first Tesla Cybertruck deliveries around September 2023. It’s the most precise timing of Cybertruck deliveries that Tesla has released to date.

Based on the launch of Tesla’s most recent models, especially the Model Y, we should expect Tesla to only deliver a few Cybertrucks during the delivery event, likely only to Tesla insiders, and we can expect months between the event and the start of deliveries to customers.

Interestingly, Musk also said that Cybertruck reservation holders should expect to get an update on specs and pricing at that event at the end of Q3.

In previous comments, Musk indicated that the Cybertruck would be available in a new top-of-the-line variant with quad motors rather than the tri-motor powertrain originally announced.

  • Newer update: on October 18, 2023 Musk said the delivery event would be held November 30 at Giga Texas, after the Q3 timing and earlier summer 2023 promise were missed
  • Production ramp expected in 2024, with capacity under 125,000 a year at mass production reached in 2025; Musk cited enormous challenges reaching volume production

title: Faroe Islands Open the Sandoy Undersea Tunnel
description: The Faroe Islands opened the Sandoyartunnilin, an 10.8km subsea tunnel linking Streymoy to the island of Sandoy, replacing a ferry crossing that could take an hour or more.
longFormSummary:
• The Sandoyartunnilin opened to the public on 21 December 2023, linking Streymoy to Sandoy across Skopunarfjørður from Gamlarætt to Traðardalur
  • It is the longest road tunnel in the Faroes at 10,785 m (10.8 km), two lanes at 80 km/h, 10.5 m wide with 4.6 m clearance, reaching 155.1 m below sea level with a maximum grade of 5.0%
  • Cost is given at two different scopes: Wikipedia puts the Sandoy tunnel's estimated cost at 860 million DKK, while Local.fo gives the combined cost of the Eysturoy and Sandoy tunnels as approximately 2.6 billion DKK (349 million EUR)
  • It is the fourth Faroese subsea tunnel, coming about 20 years after the Vagar Tunnel, with the Northern Tunnel in 2006 and the Eysturoy Tunnel in 2020 (opened 19 December 2020); Sandoy is financed partly by cross-subsidy from the Eysturoy tunnel and its tolls are pegged to it
  • Driving was toll free for the first 23 days, until January 12th, 2024, as with the Eysturoy Tunnel, per Teitur Samuelsen, CEO of operator Eystur- og Sandoyartunlar
  • Construction began 27 June 2019, passed halfway in September 2020 and the two sides were connected at a ceremony on 3 February 2022
  • The ferry Teistin ceased the Gamlarætt-Skopun route on the opening day, making its final trips and opening to the public at Skopun from 4 to 6 PM, while SSL announced a new bus link - route 650 runs Sandur to Tórshavn daily
  • Opening day was marked by an afternoon ceremony near the mouth at Traðardalur with speeches, a public run through the tunnel, a bicycle race, exhibitions and open houses
  • Sandur councillor Hanna á Reynatúgvu said residents hope the tunnel reverses a falling population, with Tórshavn now "just half an hour's drive"
  • Use has far exceeded the forecast: planning projected 300-400 vehicles a day and the ferry averaged 195 a day in 2021, but the tunnel carried 783 and 919 vehicles per day in February and March 2024 and 1,057 per day over the twelve months to Oct/Nov 2025
  • Spoil from the tunnel was reused for a new residential and industrial area at Velbastaður and for bypass roads in Runavík and Strendur; a branch to Hestur was lobbied for but deprioritised on cost
  • The two B1M videos on Faroese tunnels - "This is The World's Most Remote Infrastructure Project" (2024-03-27) and one on the world's first undersea roundabout - are metadata-only captures and give no figures, dates or technical detail of their own

title: Francis Scott Key Bridge Collapses in Baltimore
description: The Francis Scott Key Bridge, a 2.6km truss bridge carrying I-695 over Baltimore's Patapsco River since 1977, collapsed after being struck by a container ship, killing several construction workers.
longFormSummary:
• On 26 March 2024 at about 1:28 a.m. the container ship Dali struck a pier of the Francis Scott Key Bridge over the Patapsco River in Baltimore, and the main spans and three approach spans collapsed
  • Six members of a maintenance crew died, one worker was seriously injured and an inspector was unharmed
  • The bridge, opened in 1977, was a 1.6-mile steel continuous truss carrying I-695 and about 34,000 vehicles a day; it was fracture critical, with no redundancy
  • The Dali lost power at 1:24 a.m., a mayday went out at 1:27 and it dropped anchor before impact at roughly 8 knots
  • The NTSB found the blackout came from a loose signal wire connection due to improper wire-label banding; contributing factors were no vessel-impact countermeasures (no vulnerability assessment by the MDTA) and no immediate worker evacuation communication
  • The collapse blocked most shipping to the Port of Baltimore for 11 weeks at about $15 million per day; replacement is planned for late 2030 and the cost estimate rose from $1.7-1.9 billion to $4.3-5.2 billion
  • The NTSB issued four urgent recommendations (H-25-1 to H-25-4) on vessel-collision risk for bridge owners

title: Brightline West Breaks Ground on US High-Speed Rail
description: Brightline West broke ground on a 218-mile electric high-speed line between Las Vegas and Southern California, aiming to become America's first true bullet train.
longFormSummary:
• Brightline West broke ground in Las Vegas on April 22, 2024 on what it calls the nation's first true high-speed rail system, a 218-mile (351 km) line between Las Vegas and Southern California
  • The route runs in the median of I-15 with zero grade crossings, using fully electric zero-emission trains; Brightline's release quotes 200 miles per hour, while Railway Technology describes American Pioneer 220 trainsets capable of up to 220 mph (354 km/h) in seven-car formations seating 434 to 450
  • Journey time is also stated two ways: two hours between Southern California and Las Vegas, "almost half the time as driving", in the groundbreaking release, and about two hours and ten minutes from Las Vegas to Rancho Cucamonga, "twice as fast as driving", in the later project profile
  • The investment is $12 billion, with $3 billion from the Bipartisan Infrastructure Bill and $3.5 billion in private activity bonds from USDOT, the rest privately funded
  • Economic claims at groundbreaking were over $10 billion in economic impact and more than 35,000 jobs, including 10,000 direct union construction jobs and 1,000 permanent positions
  • Stations are planned at Las Vegas (110 acres, about 80,000 sq ft), Victor Valley in Apple Valley (300 acres, about 20,000 sq ft, with a future link to the High Desert Corridor and California High Speed Rail), Hesperia in the I-15 median at Joshua Street for local service, and Rancho Cucamonga (5 acres, about 80,000 sq ft, near Ontario airport and co-located with Metrolink), plus a 200,000 sq ft vehicle maintenance facility on 238 acres in Sloan, Nevada with 100+ permanent employees
  • Materials quoted for construction: 700,000 concrete ties, 2.2 million tons of ballast, 63,000 tons of steel rail, 322 miles of overhead lines, 3.4 million sq ft of retaining walls and more than 160 structures, all Buy America compliant
  • Railway Technology dates the expected completion to 2028, with services projected to serve the Los Angeles Summer Olympic Games and about 11 million passengers annually; contractors listed are Grimshaw, Arup, Siemens Mobility, Atlas Technical Consultants and HNTB
  • The market case rests on over 50 million trips a year between the two regions, 4.7 million international travellers to Las Vegas and about 17 million Southern Californians within 25 miles of a station
  • Projected environmental effects are a reduction of more than 400,000 tonnes of greenhouse gas a year, more than 700 million vehicle miles and 16,000 short-haul flights, with an aim of 100% emission-free power by 2045
  • The groundbreaking drew over 600 attendees including Pete Buttigieg, Wes Edens, Governor Joe Lombardo and Senators Cortez Masto and Rosen
  • The project grew out of MOUs with California agencies in January 2019 (Las Vegas to Apple Valley) and April 2021 (Apple Valley to Rancho Cucamonga)
  • The B1M's December 2023 film "The $140BN Race to Build America's First High-Speed Railway" frames it as "this new plan for a US bullet train might actually work", noting that the $140BN in its title is the total being invested across all US high-speed rail projects at the time of publication, not this line
address: Brightline West, Las Vegas, Nevada, USA
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: "Brightline West officially broke ground on April 22, 2024, on the nation's first true high-speed rail system."

title: Austerlitz Basin Opens to Clean Up the Seine for the Olympics
description: Paris inaugurated the Austerlitz basin, a giant underground stormwater tank built to stop sewage overflow into the Seine in time for Olympic swimming events.
longFormSummary:
• On 2 May 2024 officials inaugurated the Austerlitz wastewater and rainwater storage basin in Paris, built to help make the Seine the venue for Olympic marathon swimming and the swimming leg of the triathlons
  • The basin holds the equivalent of 20 Olympic swimming pools of dirty water, which is treated rather than spilling into the river; the IOC's later account puts that at "over 50,000 cubic metres, roughly twenty Olympic pools" - the same volume stated two ways
  • It was built because swimming test events the previous year had been cancelled over poor water quality after heavy rain overwhelmed the old sewers
  • Prefect Marc Guillaume at the inauguration: "We are on time"; Mayor Anne Hidalgo promised to swim in the Seine herself before the Olympics
  • During the Games water would be tested at 3 a.m. daily, with events liable to be delayed a few days if standards were not met
  • The wider cleanup was estimated at 1.4 billion euros ($1.5 billion), paid by state and local authorities - the same figure the pin's video source headlines as "Paris' $1.5BN cleanup plan"
  • A water treatment plant at Champigny-sur-Marne had been inaugurated the month before
  • Context: swimming in the Seine has been banned since 1923 over pollution, cleanup efforts date to the early 90s, and in 2015 the Greater Paris Sanitation Authority announced the plan to make the river swimmable by the Games, which accelerated work already in progress; about 35 fish species now live in the Paris section, up from three in the 1970s
  • The payoff came the next year: three natural swimming sites at Bras Marie, Bercy and Grenelle opened on 5 July 2025, just over a year after the Olympic events, taking about 1,000 swimmers a day until the end of August, with lifeguards, showers, sun decks, kayaks at Grenelle, daily water testing and removable modular structures, and more spots planned along the Seine and Marne
  • The pin's source, The B1M's "Why Olympians Can't Swim in the Seine" (published 2024-03-04), predates the basin's inauguration by two months and gives no dates, water-quality figures or works detail beyond its $1.5BN headline
address: Gare d'Austerlitz, Paris 13e Arrondissement, Paris, France
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: "the basin was inaugurated on May 2, 2024."

title: GPT-4o Released
description: OpenAI releases GPT-4o, its flagship model that reasons across audio, vision and text in real time, and makes it the new default in ChatGPT.
longFormSummary:
• OpenAI announced GPT-4o ("omni") on May 13, 2024, a flagship model that can reason across audio, vision and text in real time
  • It takes any mix of text, audio, image and video and generates text, audio and image; audio responses take as little as 232 ms (320 ms on average), versus 2.8 s and 5.4 s for the previous Voice Mode pipelines
  • It matches GPT-4 Turbo on English text and code and is better on non-English text, vision and audio, and in the API is twice as fast and half the price with 5x higher rate limits
  • A new tokenizer uses fewer tokens across 20 languages (for example Gujarati 4.4x fewer)
  • Rollout: text and image in ChatGPT that day, including the free tier, with Plus getting up to 5x higher message limits; new Voice Mode in alpha for Plus in the coming weeks; audio in the API first to a small group of trusted partners
  • TechCrunch adds a refreshed web UI, a macOS desktop app (Windows later in the year) and free-tier access to the GPT Store, memory and web search
  • Safety: evaluated under the Preparedness Framework with no category above Medium risk, and 70+ external red-team experts
  • An Apple Podcasts news episode of May 13, 2024 covers the announcement in a segment, but lists only titles
dateConfidenceReasoning: OpenAI's launch post for GPT-4o, dated May 13, 2024 and linked from its model release notes.

title: Ford will invest about $1.3 billion in its Oakville Assembly Plant in Ontario, Canada, to transition the facility into a new electric vehicle hub.

The plant will build the company’s next-generation EVs that are expected to arrive to market around mid-decade.

title: Eiffel Tower's Rust-Fighting Repaint Unveiled for the Paris Olympics
description: Paris unveiled the Eiffel Tower in its original 1907 gold-brown shade in June 2024, weeks before hosting the Olympic Games, after a repaint cut back from about a third of the ironwork to roughly 5 per cent.
longFormSummary:
• The tower's ironwork needed repainting to fight a century of rust, a job usually done every seven years but delayed since the pandemic.
  • The 20th painting campaign was scaled back: about 30% of the tower was to be stripped and given two new coats, but COVID-19 delays and lead in the old paint cut that to roughly 5%, according to Reuters in July 2022.
  • The roughly $60M repaint returned the tower to Gustave Eiffel's original 1907 yellow-brown shade rather than the darker "Eiffel Tower brown" used since 1968.
  • Crews finished the visible restoration in time for Paris to mount the Olympic rings on the tower on June 7, 2024, ahead of the Summer Games.
  • Some engineers have since questioned whether the cosmetic repaint addressed the tower's deeper corrosion problems.

title: A Quiet Place: Day One (2024) Opens in Theaters
description: A Quiet Place: Day One is a 2024 American apocalyptic horror film, written and directed by Michael Sarnoski, based on a story he conceived with John Krasinski. It is the third installment in the A Quiet Place film series, and a prequel spinoff of the first film.
longFormSummary:
• “A Quiet Place: Day One is a 2024 American apocalyptic horror film, written and directed by Michael Sarnoski, based on a story he conceived with John Krasinski. It is the third installment in the A Quiet Place film series, and a prequel spinoff of the first film.”
  • The pin’s date of 26 June 2024 is the world premiere at the Tribeca Festival, held as a special presentation after the festival itself (which ran June 5-16); the actual US theatrical release by Paramount Pictures was two days later, on June 28, 2024
  • It had been scheduled three times before that: March 31, 2023, then September 22, 2023, then March 8, 2024
  • Lupita Nyong’o stars as Samira, “a terminally ill woman during the early stages of an invasion in New York City by blind extraterrestrial creatures with an acute sense of hearing”, with Joseph Quinn as Eric, a British law student, Alex Wolff as the hospice nurse Reuben, and Djimon Hounsou as Henri, the character credited only as “Man on the Island” in A Quiet Place Part II
  • Running time is 99 minutes on a budget of $67 million, produced by Michael Bay, Andrew Form and Brad Fuller for Paramount, Platinum Dunes and Sunday Night Productions, shot by Pat Scola, cut by Gregory Plotkin and Andrew Mondshein and scored by Alexis Grapsas
  • Development began in November 2020 with Jeff Nichols set to write and direct from a Krasinski story; Nichols finished a script by May 2021 and dropped out in October 2021, and Sarnoski replaced him in January 2022, having been approached on the strength of his debut feature Pig (2021)
  • Principal photography ran from February 6 to April 11, 2023 in London, although the film is set in New York: the Warner Bros. Studios, Leavesden backlot recreated four two-storey NYC blocks including Mott Street in Chinatown and parts of Harlem, the Lower East Side and the Upper East Side, with the jazz club interiors at the George Tavern in Stepney, subway interiors at Charing Cross and the cathedral scene at St. Sophia’s Greek Orthodox Cathedral
  • Paramount executives wanted a computer-generated cat; Sarnoski insisted on a real one, and Frodo was played by two cats, Nico and Schnitzel, with scripted hissing and back-arching cut because the handlers could not train it and the production avoided CGI; Nyong’o, who was afraid of cats, overcame it with exposure therapy and adopted one by the end of production
  • The film grossed $138.9 million in the United States and Canada and $122.9 million elsewhere for a worldwide total of $261.8 million, with Deadline Hollywood calculating a net profit of $83.6 million
  • It opened against Horizon: An American Saga - Chapter 1 from 3,707 theatres on a projection of $40-50 million, took $22.5 million on day one including $6.8 million in Thursday previews, “the best of the series”, and finished the weekend second behind Inside Out 2
  • The two links differ slightly on that opening weekend: Wikipedia gives $52.2 million, the franchise’s best, while the podcast, recorded on 1 July 2024, rounds it to $53 million – the article’s figure is the later and more precise one
  • The podcast’s running totals are simply an early snapshot: on Monday 1 July 2024 it reports $98.5 million worldwide against the $67 million budget, with $53 million domestic and $45.5 million overseas as of 30 June, and host Robert Winfree guessing the film needed “between one twenty and one thirty” for Paramount to celebrate – a bar the final $261.8 million cleared twice over
  • Deadline’s Anthony D’Alessandro credited the opening to heat waves, walk-up business (66% bought tickets the day of the screening) and diverse turnout (32% Hispanic and Latino against the first film’s 28%), with IMAX and premium large formats taking 39% of the earnings and IMAX alone 11%
  • Reviews were generally positive: 86% of 281 critics on Rotten Tomatoes with an average of 7.1/10, 68 out of 100 from 53 critics on Metacritic, a B+ CinemaScore matching the first film, and PostTrak at 79% positive; the podcast, reading the site a week after release, quotes 83% top critics and 85% all critics with audience scores of 74 and 70
  • The Rotten Tomatoes consensus reads “Grounded in raw humanity by Lupita Nyong’o and Joseph Quinn, this sideways entry into A Quiet Place finds fresh notes of fright to play amongst the silence”; Peter Debruge in Variety objected that most of the film was “tiptoeing through a mostly off-screen apocalypse”, and RogerEbert.com gave two and a half stars, calling it at times “a first draft of a richer, more complex final film”
  • The podcast hosts land in a similar place, finding both leads thinly written – “she’s just dying cancer lady through this whole movie” – while holding that the film works because, like the first, “it’s not about the monsters” but about finding a reason to live; Mark Radulich argues the film should have had no musical score at all and calls its sound design only adequate, and both say Djimon Hounsou was advertised far beyond his screen time
  • Awards followed through the next year: a win for Best Horror at the Astra Midseason Movie Awards on July 3, 2024, Best Animal Performance for Frodo the Cat from the Las Vegas Film Critics Society on December 14, 2024, and nominations at the Astra Film Awards, Fangoria Chainsaw Awards, Hollywood Music in Media Awards, the NAACP Image Awards and the Saturn Awards for Best Horror Film and Best Actress
  • Home release came quickly: digital download on July 30, 2024 and DVD, Blu-ray and Ultra HD Blu-ray on October 8, 2024
dateConfidenceReasoning: Released theatrically on June 26, 2024 per the film's Wikipedia infobox.

title: Panama Canal Wins Approval for Rio Indio Reservoir
description: Panama's Supreme Court overturned a 2006 law blocking new reservoirs, clearing the way for a dam on the Rio Indio meant to secure the Panama Canal's water supply against worsening droughts.
longFormSummary:
• On 2 July 2024 Panama's Supreme Court ruled Law 20 of 2006 unconstitutional, restoring a 1999 law and letting the Panama Canal Authority build a reservoir on the Rio Indio outside the current watershed
  • The ACP's estimate rose from about $900 million and five years to $1.6 billion and six years; the plan dams the Indio River with a 5-mile tunnel to Gatun Lake, allowing up to 15 more transits a day
  • The reinstated law expands the watershed by 1.4 million acres beyond the 741,316 acres previously managed
  • Background: 2023 was the worst drought since 1950, cutting transit slots from 36 to as few as 18 by 1 February 2024 before they returned to 36 a day from September
  • Local farmers and communities face flooding risk and have criticised the project
address: Río Indio, Capira, Panamá Oeste, Panama

title: Arianespace Launches Ariane 6 on Its Maiden Flight, VA262

  • Eight CubeSats and five experiments were deployed correctly, but two reentry capsules (SpaceCase SC-X01 and Nyx Bikini) were not deployed as planned
  • At T+1 h 14 min the auxiliary propulsion system malfunctioned, preventing the third burn meant to deorbit the stage; the outcome is listed as a partial failure

title: Chicago's Century and Consumers Buildings Saved From Demolition

title: Sydney Metro City & Southwest Opens Under the Harbour
description: Sydney opened the City & Southwest section of its Sydney Metro, adding a new driverless rail crossing under Sydney Harbour and the CBD alongside the city's largest railway cavern.
longFormSummary:
• "Sydney Metro City officially opened on Monday 19 August 2024", running between Chatswood and Sydenham as the M1 Northwest and City Line
  • Within the first four weeks of the city section opening, "more than five million metro trips were taken on the new M1 Northwest and City Line, averaging 200,000 trips per weekday", with 99.36 per cent of services running on time
  • Services run "every four minutes in the peak, five minutes during the interpeak ... and every 10 minutes during off peak and on the weekend"
  • The opening is one stage of Sydney Metro City & Southwest: the project timeline runs from the Southwest EIS exhibition in 2017 and project approval in December 2018 through early works in 2019-2020 and construction from late 2020, to "Sydney Metro services begin between Chatswood and Sydenham - August 2024"
  • Six weeks after the city opening, on Monday 30 September 2024, the T3 Bankstown Line between Sydenham and Bankstown closed "to enable the final conversion of the 130-year-old line to modern metro standards", a shutdown of up to 12 months
  • Stations between Sydenham and Bankstown closed for around 12 months, served instead by three free Southwest Link bus routes (SW1, SW2, SW3) with "a bus every two to four minutes in peak periods across some routes", free "until the estimated completion date of late 2025"
  • The shutdown covers work that can only be done once Sydney Trains services stop - installing platform screen doors, upgrading tracks and corridor, and train testing and commissioning - after which passengers get "a 21st century high-tech metro line with a train every four minutes during the peak"
  • Testing before the Bankstown extension opens runs in five stages: low-speed manual testing at up to 25 km/h, loaded testing with "over one hundred 1000-litre water containers to simulate the weight of a fully loaded train", high-speed automated testing to 110 km/h, trial running to a full timetable by the operator, then passenger services - all subject to safety assessment and approval by the independent national rail safety regulator, following the process used for Chatswood-Sydenham
  • Integrating the extension will require "a series of weekend and overnight possessions ... on the City metro line", with dates to be given closer to the time
  • By October 2024, 89 of 170 mechanical gap fillers were installed across Marrickville, Dulwich Hill, Canterbury and Campsie, the Sydenham Station upgrade with its new concourse and Burrows Avenue entrance was open, and new lifts were open at Wiley Park, Dulwich Hill, Hurlstone Park, Punchbowl and Canterbury
  • A permanent Southwest Active Transport Link of footpaths, separated cycleways, shared zones and crossings between Sydenham and Bankstown "will be ready for cyclists and pedestrians a year after Southwest Metro services opening", with an interim path between Sydenham and Marrickville already open
  • A new intrusion detection system will run between Sydenham and Bankstown, with fibre optic cables on the corridor security fence alerting the Sydney Metro Operational Control Centre on contact and CCTV cameras automatically turning to the affected section
  • The B1M's video on the wider programme, "Australia's $64BN Mega Railway", published 2024-03-18, calls Sydney Metro "one of the world's biggest suburban rail projects" and puts $64BN in both its title and its full-story link; the page gives no breakdown of that figure and none of the project newsletter's own costs

dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: "Sydney Metro City officially opened on Monday, 19 August 2024."

title: Dresden's Carola Bridge Collapses Into the Elbe
description: A section of the 1971-built Carola Bridge in Dresden, Germany collapsed into the Elbe overnight with no warning, minutes after the last tram had crossed it.
longFormSummary:
• Deck C of Dresden's Carola Bridge collapsed between 02:58 and 02:59 (UTC+2) on 11 September 2024, with no casualties; the collapse took out about 100 m of the central span, and a light rail train had crossed shortly before 3am
  • The bridge carried road and tram traffic over the Elbe: the first bridge on the site was built in 1895 and destroyed by the SS on 7 May 1945, and the replacement was built between 1967 and 1971 (opening July 3, 1971) after a 1965 competition, with three prestressed-concrete decks A, B and C, C carrying the trams
  • Renovation of the bridge had begun in 2019 and it was declared a protected monument in 2022
  • The collapse destroyed district heating pipelines, and a temporary pipeline was laid across the Augustus Bridge
  • Demolition began the next day but was interrupted by the 2024 Central European floods; because decks A and B had shifted and shared structural flaws, demolition of the whole bridge was approved
  • The structure kept failing afterwards: additional steel elements collapsed over the weekend before 3 March 2025, halting Elbe shipping for another 72 hours, after the channel had reopened a month earlier from a four-month closure with vessels passing single file by authorization since the end of January; controlled access under the bridge was to resume if there were no further fractures or movement in 72 hours
  • Early 2025 brought unexploded WWII ordnance on the site, and in February 2025 cracks were detected in the steel reinforcement of decks A and B, accelerating demolition; removal of collapsed and standing sections was slated to begin within weeks and be finished by the end of the year, and as of June 2025 the entire structure was being demolished
  • Dresden city council approved a new bridge planned to start in 2027: two spans, four car lanes, tram tracks, extended bike lanes and footpaths
  • The pin's source, The B1M's "The Bridge Collapse That Shocked a Nation" (published 2026-03-11), uses the collapse to frame "the $500BN plan to fix Germany's infrastructure", with chapters on the Dresden collapse and "The New Carolabruecke"; beyond that figure its page gives no dates, funding detail or collapse findings
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: "Deck C collapsed between 02:58 and 02:59 (UTC+2) on 11 September 2024."

title: Klamath River Dams Fully Removed
description: Crews finished dismantling all four hydroelectric dams on the Klamath River in 2024, the largest dam-removal and river-restoration project in US history.
longFormSummary:
• The four Klamath River hydroelectric dams were fully removed, with California's governor announcing on 2 October 2024 the largest dam removal in US history, completed ahead of schedule and on budget
  • Removal restores nearly 400 miles of habitat for salmon; fish could swim freely for the first time in over 100 years from August 2024, and restoration of 2,200 acres of formerly submerged land continues
  • PacifiCorp built the dams between 1918 and 1962; they produced power for only about 70,000 homes and gave no irrigation, drinking water or flood control (per the Klamath River Renewal Corporation)
  • The river had been the third-largest salmon producer on the West Coast, and the removal followed decades of tribal protests, testimony and lawsuits by the Karuk and Yurok tribes
  • Since breaching, fish regained habitat and water temperature and quality improved
address: Iron Gate Dam, Siskiyou County, California, United States

title: Thessaloniki Metro Line 1 Opens After Decades of Delay
description: Greece's Thessaloniki Metro Line 1 opened to the public, a driverless 9.6km line whose stations doubled as archaeological digs after more than 300,000 ancient artefacts were uncovered during construction.
longFormSummary:
• Thessaloniki's metro was inaugurated on Saturday 30 November 2024 by Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis - the first such system in Greece outside Athens - as a 9.6 km driverless line with 13 stations and platform screen doors, free for four days and then 0.60 euro tickets
  • The two reports date the construction differently: one says the metro was first conceived more than a century ago, the first tunnel was dug in 1986 (hence its "38 years to build" headline) and construction began in earnest in 2003, while the other says construction began in 2006 and took nearly 20 years
  • Both attribute the delay largely to antiquities and the debt crisis: over 300,000 finds were reported by Minister Christos Staikouras, tunnels were bored deeper than planned to preserve them - up to 31 metres (102 feet) deep - and contractor AEGEK collapsed during the crisis that began in 2009
  • The finds are described slightly differently by each: a Roman-era thoroughfare, ancient Greek burial sites and mosaics in one, a Byzantine-era market and a Roman cemetery in the other, with artefacts displayed in stations such as Venizelou
  • The project was nearly abandoned in 2013; in 2015 the Central Archaeological Council agreed to detach and reposition antiquities, one such case at Venizelos station, a decision archaeologist Melina Paisidou criticised, arguing the artefacts should have been left in place
  • Mitsotakis on the result: "It is also a museum"
  • Cost is given as three billion euros so far, covering the first line and most of a second line under construction and due in a year; the pin's video source titles it "Greece's New $3BN Metro" and points to a Guardian piece on a "3bn" system, the same figure in a different currency
  • The consortium was Aktor (Greece), Webuild (Italy) and Hitachi Rail (Japan), and the line is compared with Rome's Metro Line C, begun in 2006 and also slowed by archaeological finds
  • The pin's own source is The B1M's "Construction Fail: Greece's New $3BN Metro", published 2025-04-09 - "Over budget and overdue, Thessaloniki finally has its futuristic driverless metro" - whose chapters cover the planning, "How 'Not' to Build a Metro", the impact of delays and the archaeological discoveries; only its description was captured, with no transcript, so nothing is recorded of what the video says

title: UC San Diego adding 3,310 dorm beds to deal with growth, housing shortage,
description:
UC San Diego is pushing ahead with plans to build dorms that will collectively hold 3,310 students to deal with the school’s runaway growth and a critical housing shortage.

The expansion will increase the university’s housing capacity to 22,260 — a figure larger than the number of people living in such communities as Solana Beach and Scripps Ranch.

The campus got a lift from the University of California Board of Regents, which this week gave the school permission to move forward with two huge projects, Pepper Canyon West and Thurgood Marshall College Undergraduate Student Housing.

Pepper Canyon will house 1,310 transfer and upper-diversion undergraduate students near the Blue Line trolley station that recently opened on campus, a few minutes walk from Geisel Library.

 The $350 million project also will feature retail space.

title: Real Madrid's Rebuilt Bernabéu Finally Wraps Up
description: Real Madrid's four-year overhaul of the Santiago Bernabéu — a new steel facade, retractable roof and a fully removable pitch — ran years past its original target before wrapping up.
longFormSummary:
• The links do not agree on when the rebuild finished. The December 2023 progress report has works "delayed several times" by supply chains hit by the war in Ukraine and by the pandemic, with the planned opening postponed and "now set for spring 2024"; the 2026 architectural feature treats the renovation as done but gives no completion date, so neither supports the pin's end-of-2024 wrap-up date directly
  • Cost is given as over EUR 1 billion, reached after shareholders agreed a third loan of EUR 370 million; the pin's video source headlines the figure as "$1BN" without a breakdown
  • The renovation was by GMP Architekten with L35 and Ribas & Ribas on a stadium originally opened in 1947; GMP director Martin Glass says the big driver is "full-time use", enhancing Real Madrid's brand and commercial potential while keeping the structure's "identity, soul and character"
  • The original concrete structure is entirely wrapped in stainless steel louvres; as of December 2023 the club complained that the alignment of the facade's 14,000 plates was poor and that it let too much light through, causing a conflict with the architects
  • The pitch is retractable and stacked in an underground "greenhouse" on one side, because the site is surrounded by roads and residential areas and a public metro line runs 50 m under the other side; a retractable roof allows concerts and large events
  • By December 2023 the museum had been enlarged, the hospitality area rebuilt, the retractable roof installed and a new car park opened, leaving the VIP area, the commercial area with a large Real Madrid shop and the entertainment area outstanding, with the 330-tonne 360-degree scoreboard being changed from 7 to 11 metres and the Operational Control Unit enlarged
  • The finished museum is a 150 m-long cantilevered bridge between two existing concrete stair towers; Glass says only the Prado has more visitors in Spain, with prices around 35 euros, alongside restaurants, a brewery, Starbucks and the Bernabeu Market, with a panoramic viewpoint planned
  • The stadium is set to host games at the 2030 World Cup
  • Surrounding works: the Madrid regional authority tendered a EUR 68 million extension of Santiago Bernabeu metro station, tripling its area, with work expected as early as 2024

title: PepsiCo, which owns Frito-Lay and Quaker Oats, has set a goal to design 100% of its packaging to be recyclable, compostable, biodegradable or reusable by 2025.

title: Drone strike breaches Chernobyl's New Safe Confinement
description: A Russian drone struck Chernobyl's €2BN New Safe Confinement shelter, tearing a hole in the roof and starting a fire that burned for weeks.
longFormSummary:
• At about 01:50 local time on 14 February 2025 a drone with a high-explosive warhead struck Chernobyl's New Safe Confinement (NSC), causing smoke and fire; Ukraine blamed Russia, which denied it, and the IAEA has not attributed blame
  • The arch was hit at about 87 m; plant operators said both external and internal cladding and Main Cranes System equipment were damaged, and the cladding fire was put out locally
  • Radiation levels inside and outside stayed normal and stable, with no casualties or release of radioactive substances; the IAEA saw a breach of the outer layer, and Ukraine's regulator confirmed outer cladding damage
  • The cladding breach violated the 'limits of safe operation' in NSC regulations; IAEA chief Rafael Grossi called for maximum military restraint around Ukraine's nuclear sites
  • The NSC is the largest moveable land-based structure ever built (257 m span, 108 m high, 36,000 tonnes), completed in 2019 and designed for about 100 years, covering the 1986 reactor 4 shelter

title: Hagia Sophia's Dome Restoration
description: Istanbul's 1,500-year-old Hagia Sophia began restoring its dome to withstand a major earthquake, a phase of a 50-year plan to reinforce the building with no fixed finish date.
longFormSummary:
• Turkey's Culture and Tourism Ministry began an extensive restoration of the dome of the nearly 1,500-year-old Hagia Sophia to reinforce it against earthquakes, with the dome work "scheduled to commence on April 14, 2025" and reported as launched by mid-May
  • It is part of a 50-year plan to reinforce the building, focusing on the dome, walls and minarets; restoration of the complex began about three years earlier and is set to be the largest in its history
  • "No timeline has been set for the project's completion", though it is expected to take several years
  • The method: work proceeds from the exterior to protect the interior mosaics, starting with a temporary roof structure and tarp over the dome, with the existing lead cover removed and damaged lead repaired or replaced using Ottoman-era-consistent materials and techniques, and weak points identified through seismic simulations reinforced
  • Scaffolding was designed to keep the building in use: a steel platform system on four columns, 43.5 m tall, stands inside the mosque so worship and visits continue, with a 41 m tower crane with a 60 m boom east of the building and a digital twin made of the structure; the covering, platform and crane are dismantled after completion
  • Ahmet Gulec of the scientific board told Daily Sabah that "The dome isn't perfectly round", with some areas filled with rubble or patched with wood, and that the work is to balance the structure
  • The urgency comes from the 7.8 magnitude earthquake in southern Turkey in 2023 and fears of an expected Istanbul earthquake
  • The building's seismic history is long: built in 537 under Justinian I, its original dome collapsed in 558, it took earthquake damage in 989 and 1346, and Mimar Sinan added buttresses in the 16th century; it has been a cathedral, mosque, museum and mosque again since 2020, and was UNESCO World Heritage listed in 1985

title: Construction Starts on the Port Authority Bus Terminal Replacement
description: A groundbreaking on Dyer Avenue between 37th and 39th Streets began the temporary terminal that keeps 8,000 buses a day running while the 1950 building is replaced. The $10 billion scheme was planned to finish in 2032, with new ramps by 2028.
longFormSummary:
• "Work began on May 29, 2025, when a groundbreaking ceremony for a temporary terminal on Dyer Avenue between 37th and 39th streets was hosted"
  • The building being replaced is the Port Authority Bus Terminal at 625 Eighth Avenue, opened 15 December 1950 as the Mid-Manhattan Bus Terminal; it is "the busiest bus terminal in the world by volume of traffic, serving about 8,000 buses and 225,000 people on an average weekday and more than 65 million people a year", with 223 departure gates, 1,250 parking spaces and nine platform levels
  • The PANYNJ released plans in January 2021 to rebuild on the same site with expanded bus layover facilities, and hired Foster + Partners and Epstein Global as designers in August 2022
  • Revised plans of January 2024 call for 3.5 acres (1.4 ha) of parks, a glass atrium, a main entrance on 41st Street, two office buildings of at least 60 stories on 40th and 42nd Streets, permanent closure of part of 41st Street between Eighth and Ninth Avenues, and a separate bus storage and staging building; "At the time, the new terminal was planned to cost $10 billion; new ramps to the terminal were to be completed by 2028, while the terminal itself was planned to be finished by 2032"
  • Approvals ran ahead of the groundbreaking: the New York City Planning Commission approved the plans in October 2024, federal approval followed that December, and in January 2025 the U.S. Department of Transportation disbursed a $1.89 billion grant
  • The replacement answers long-standing capacity problems: the terminal has reached peak-hour capacity, causing congestion and overflow onto local streets, and allows no layover parking, so buses park on local streets or deadhead through the Lincoln Tunnel; on-time performance fell from 92 percent in 2012 to 85 percent in the first quarter of 2014
  • Earlier fixes failed - a planned $800 million bus garage was scrapped in October 2011 over budget constraints, and air-rights tower deals with Vornado Realty Trust collapsed in November 2011
  • NJ Transit accounts for 70 percent of the terminal's traffic, and PABT "is the gateway for most bus and jitney traffic entering Manhattan with more than 190,000 passengers on 6,000 bus trips made through the Lincoln Tunnel and terminal daily"

longFormSummary:
• Mayor Brandon Johnson announced that four fully reconstructed Red Line stations in Edgewater and Uptown - Lawrence, Argyle, Berwyn and Bryn Mawr - would open on Sunday, July 20, 2025 as part of the CTA's $2.1 billion Red and Purple Modernization Phase One Project
  • "The opening of four new contiguous stations marks the first time that this many stations have opened simultaneously since the Orange Line in 1993", and major project construction was to be completed that year
  • Station amenities: "elevators and escalators at main stationhouse entrances; wider platforms; large translucent overhead canopies for increased protection from inclement weather; platform benches; and turnstiles and Ventra fare machines"; the temporary Argyle and Bryn Mawr stations used during construction close when the new ones open
  • Addresses given are Lawrence at 1120 W. Lawrence Ave., Argyle at 1118 W. Argyle St., Berwyn at 1119 W. Berwyn St. and Bryn Mawr at 1116 W. Bryn Mawr Ave., with a second Bryn Mawr entrance at 1119 W. Hollywood Ave
  • New track, support structures, bridges and viaducts run along the 1.3-mile Lawrence to Bryn Mawr corridor, replacing century-old deteriorated structures; the new bridge design improves sightlines at cross streets "with the elimination of columns in the middle of the street" and the elevated structure is built higher to meet modern clearance standards, while a new signal system "replaces a more than 60-year-old system"
  • RPM Phase One construction began in 2019 and has three components: rebuilding these four stations and replacing track structure "totaling six track-miles"; the Red-Purple Bypass, completed in 2021, with reconstruction of Red and Purple Line track structure between Belmont and Newport/Cornelia; and a new signal system on 23 track miles between Howard and Belmont
  • CTA Acting President Nora Leerhsen: "By opening these four stations that will be accessible to customers with disabilities, we move closer to our goal of having all of our CTA stations fully accessible", thanking Senators Durbin and Duckworth and the rest of the Illinois Congressional delegation
  • After demolishing 1.3 miles of century-old concrete embankment wall, CTA plans 10 blocks of open space under the new tracks between Lawrence and Ardmore avenues - a pedestrian trail, dog parks, playground, fitness area, benches and flexible plaza space - with "Construction is expected to begin in 2026 and be completed in 2027"
  • The Red Line is CTA's busiest, providing nearly 40 million rides in 2024, and RPM overall "will rebuild the 9.6-mile stretch of Red and Purple Line track structure and stations on the North Side that are a century old"

title: Hyper-Kamiokande Neutrino Observatory Cavern Completed
description: Crews finished excavating the huge cavern in a Japanese mountain that will house the Hyper-Kamiokande neutrino observatory, a step toward the detector's planned start of observations.
longFormSummary:
• The University of Tokyo completed excavation of the Hyper-Kamiokande cavern on July 31, 2025, announced on 5 August 2025; the water Cherenkov detector is under construction about 600 m underground in Hida City, Gifu, Japan
  • The cavern is a dome about 69 m in diameter and 21 m high above a cylinder 73 m high, with about 330,000 cubic metres of rock removed; the dome and cylinder heights together match the pin source's correction that "When complete, the cavern will be 94m high"
  • Excavation finished about six months behind the original schedule: dome excavation began November 2022 and the cylinder in October 2023, using a pre-dug 3.4 m vertical shaft
  • The two links differ on when observations begin: the newer release has operation "scheduled to begin 2028", where the March 2024 paper said operation was "expected to start in 2027" - the newer date follows the six-month excavation slip
  • Next steps from August 2025: converting the cavern into a tank of 260,000 cubic metres of ultra-pure water, a two-layer detector structure starting in 2026, all in-tank components installed by 2027, while KEK upgrades the J-PARC beam and builds a new intermediate detector in Tokai
  • The detector itself is given as 71 m high and 68 m in diameter holding 0.260 million metric tons of ultra-pure water, a fiducial mass of 0.188 million tons - an order of magnitude more than Super-Kamiokande, or 8.4 times its fiducial volume - with over 20,000 new photodetectors
  • The collaboration is led by the University of Tokyo and KEK; it counted about 560 researchers from 101 institutes in 21 countries in March 2024 and about 630 researchers from 22 countries by July 2025
  • Its goals are to measure neutrino properties and search for proton decay: leptonic CP violation covering 60% of parameter space at 5 sigma or better after 10 years (over 8 sigma if delta CP = -pi/2), proton decay p -> e+ pi0 potentially beyond 1e35 years, neutrino mass ordering, and solar and supernova neutrinos

title: South Station Tower Is Completed Above Boston's Rail Terminal
description: Hines finished the 51-storey, 677-foot tower built on air rights over South Station, adding 680,000 square feet of offices, Ritz-Carlton branded residences on the upper floors and an expanded bus terminal beneath it. Construction ran five years from a start in January 2020, after the scheme had sat stalled since its 2008 approval.
longFormSummary:
• South Station Tower was completed in September 2025, five years after construction officially began in January 2020 - the timeline the project set from the start
  • The wiki gives the height two ways: the infobox lists 677 ft (206 m) architectural and to the roof, the figure the FAA approved in February 2016, while the text describes "a 51-story, 678-foot tower"
  • It is the high-rise portion of a three-building development on top of Boston's historic South Station complex on Atlantic Avenue, an example of transit-oriented development, and on completion became the sixth-tallest building in Boston
  • The tower holds about 680,000 square feet (63,000 m²) of office space and 166 Ritz-Carlton-branded condominium residences from the 36th floor up, with a one-acre sky park on the 11th floor visible from the lobby
  • It does not touch the South Station building, instead occupying the space between the station's tracks and atrium and sitting on an arched base anchored by eight columns, with loads carried by diagonal struts from the exterior into the concrete core and down to those columns; part of the tower is cantilevered over the station atrium
  • The expanded bus station in the same phase reuses a foundation laid during the station's late-1980s renovation, when foundation piers for a future high-rise were installed between each pair of tracks, 35 feet apart
  • Preliminary design was by César Pelli, "whose designs are reminiscent of his Wells Fargo Center in Minneapolis"; the building is LEED pre-certified silver and won the EPA's "Green design" award; Hines Interests is the developer
  • The scheme stalled for well over a decade: conceived by Tufts president Jean Mayer, whose university acquired the airspace rights through TUDC LLC in 1991 and brought in Hines in 1997, it was originally designed at 759 feet with a spire before being downscaled in 2006, approved by 2008 at 2,190,000 square feet with a 2008 groundbreaking and 2010 completion - and then went nowhere, with Tufts withdrawing in 2009
  • Restarting took several more years: build rights due to expire in April 2017 were extended by the state to year end, the BPDA approved construction in December 2016 after a Notice of Project Change proposing more residential space, and the start slipped to December 2017 and then again in 2018 over MBTA concerns about operational and maintenance costs, capital expenditure and how those were shared, with negotiations extended to April 2019
  • The steel frame had reached 109 feet by November 2022
  • Two 2024 incidents halted work: on March 21 a steel beam fell from the top of the tower, damaging windows before coming to rest on the ninth floor with other equipment landing at street level, prompting the MBTA to suspend commuter services and order work stopped - no injuries, with contractor Suffolk pausing until work resumed on March 27 after OSHA investigations - and on April 9 welders started a fire outside the ninth floor, quickly put out, with work continuing on April 10
