title: Los Angeles Breaks Ground on Its Convention Center Expansion
description: Work began on a 190,000-square-foot addition that joins the South and West exhibit halls into one contiguous hall of more than 750,000 square feet, plus new meeting and multipurpose space. Construction pauses in 2028 so the centre can host Olympic fencing, taekwondo, wrestling and table tennis, with final completion in 2029.
longFormSummary:
• The city of Los Angeles broke ground on a $2.62 billion expansion of the L.A. Convention Center, "which officials say will support the downtown area's ongoing revitalization"
  • Mayor Karen Bass, who gave the project final approval, said the expansion is more than just another project and called it an investment for the city and the local economy: "This is a very, very serious investment. None of us take this lightly... I think it was a difficult challenge on the City Council for all of us to come to grips with the commitment that we are making but understanding that it is the type of risk that one has to take in order to make a qualitative leap forward"
  • The stated aims are more downtown jobs and readying the facility for the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games
  • City figures: more than 15,000 jobs created, $652 million in general fund tax revenue over 30 years, over $150 million in additional visitor spending each year, and 100 potential conventions already interested since the expansion was announced
  • The schedule is contested: "Some leaders doubt the site will be finished by the city's imposed deadline of March 2028 - just a few months before the Convention Center will be handed over to the International Olympic Committee for its use", and Bass has acknowledged it is a risky project
  • That March 2028 deadline is the only completion date in the report; it does not describe the pin's pause in construction for the Games or a 2029 final completion, nor the 190,000 square foot addition or 750,000 square foot contiguous hall
  • City Councilmember Tim McOsker framed the payoff as distant: "The beneficiaries of this project are not here. They are 30 years out, and those beneficiaries will never know that we even existed"
  • At the groundbreaking, City Councilman Curren Price was sent to hospital after suffering a "health-related incident"

title: Dublin MetroLink Finally Wins Planning Approval
description: After two decades of false starts, Ireland's first metro line - linking Dublin city centre to the airport and Swords - was granted planning permission, with enabling works targeted to begin in 2027.
longFormSummary:
• An Coimisiun Pleanala granted the Railway Order for Dublin's MetroLink on Thursday 2 October 2025 - "An Coimisiun Pleanala published the Railway order this morning which gives construction for the MetroLink Project the green light"; the planning body's own notice of decision for case ABP-314724-22 ("Metrolink - Estuary to Charlemont via Dublin Airport") is dated 02 / 10 / 2025 but states only that a decision has been made, without saying what it was
  • Transport Infrastructure Ireland had applied for the Railway Order in November 2022, so the decision came almost three years into the process
  • The scheme is a new 18.8 km railway line, most of it underground, from Charlemont near Dublin city centre to Swords Estuary in the north of the county, with 16 stations running Swords - Dublin Airport - city centre - Charlemont
  • A metro for Dublin "was first mooted in the year 2000, but it was shelved during the financial crisis"; the same report elsewhere says it was first proposed "over 25 years ago with repeated attempts made across decades"
  • Conditions attached cover protection of amenities and heritage: an expert panel must review and sign off assessments of certain locations including around Charlemont Station, focused on sensitive buildings and protected structures, "to ensure both protection of architectural heritage and to mitigate the risk of building damage during construction"
  • Other conditions address disruption to residents - the developer "shall make an alternative training facility for Fingallians GAA" before development commences, and must replace car parking spaces removed at The Court apartment complex in Glasnevin until Glasnevin Station is complete
  • RTE reported that the project "must get final Cabinet approval before construction can begin", that construction "is expected to take several years" and that "final costs [are] not yet known"
  • The day after the decision, Transport Minister Darragh O'Brien said enabling works could start in two years (2027) and construction in 2028 "with a fair wind", that absent a judicial review MetroLink could be completed by 2035, and that the Swords-to-Charlemont line could open in phases: "This [project] is happening"
  • On the decision day he called it a "critical nation-building project for Ireland's future" that "will be transformative for the people of North Dublin and - by linking directly with Dublin airport, DART, heavy rail, Luas and bus services - the entire country" and "will enable the construction of tens of thousands of new homes"
  • Funding at that point was EUR 2 billion pledged under the revised National Development Plan announced in July, covering initial works over five years and described as "not a blank cheque"; previous cost estimates ranged from EUR 7 billion up to EUR 23 billion, and the Minister did not believe it would reach EUR 23 billion but declined to give an updated figure with tendering imminent
  • The cost figures across the links do not agree: the Irish Times reports the EUR 7-23 billion range with no official total, the B1M video is headlined "Ireland's $27BN Plan to (Finally) Catch Up With Europe" and gives no breakdown, and the newest link puts the combined published notice values of the three delivery packages at close to $18 billion
  • The latest cost-benefit analysis gave a EUR 1.40 return to the exchequer per EUR 1 invested
  • Capacity targets are consistent across the links: up to 20,000 passengers per hour in each direction and trains every three minutes at peak, a 25-minute Swords-to-city-centre journey, with long-term 90-second headways and up to 53 million annual passengers
  • By May 2026 - the newest account - Ireland had launched procurement for all three major delivery packages on the back of the October 2025 Railway Order: civil design-and-build notices M401 (~$5.4bn, southern urban section, station boxes up to 35 m deep) and M402 (~$3.9bn, northern section with two viaducts) released in February, and the M500 DBFOM package (~$8.6bn net present value, GoA4 driverless rolling stock, systems and 25 years of operation) released on 1 May
  • That procurement moves past the Irish Times's "two consortia that have already confirmed that they will be bidding": three bidders are shortlisted per civil package, which may be bid for both but won only once, with M401 award targeted for Q3 2027 and M402 for Q4 2027, and the M500 invitation to tender targeted early 2028 with financial close expected Q4 2028; interest was signalled by consortia including Alstom, FCC, John Laing, Meridiam and RATP
  • Earlier enabling contracts - utility diversions, archaeology and the Dublin Airport station box - were already in procurement, with the reference design led since 2018 by IDOM and Jacobs
  • The B1M's film on the project, published 2026-03-04, still hedges the outcome: "Say it quietly but Ireland might (finally) be building its first ever metro", with chapters on the long-running saga, the route, cost and construction, and "a disruptive process"
dateConfidenceReasoning: An Coimisiun Pleanala's own notice of decision for Railway Order Application ABP-314724-22 (Metrolink - Estuary to Charlemont via Dublin Airport) carries the decision date 02/10/2025, and RTE reported that day that "An Coimisiun Pleanala published the Railway order this morning which gives construction for the MetroLink Project the green light". The pin's milestone - the grant of planning permission - therefore has an exact day, 2 October 2025; the old date stood for the separate 2027 target for enabling works.

title: Mumbai's Aqua Line Metro Reaches Cuffe Parade, Completing the Line
description: The last 10.99 km stretch, from Acharya Atre Chowk to Cuffe Parade, opened to passengers and completed the 33.5 km Aqua Line, Mumbai's first fully underground metro with 27 stations. The Mumbai Metro Rail Corporation's managing director put the line's completion cost at about 30,000 crore rupees.
longFormSummary:
• The final 10.99 km stretch of the Mumbai Metro's Aqua Line, from Acharya Atre Chowk to Cuffe Parade, was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 8 October 2025, alongside the Navi Mumbai International Airport
  • The article dates the opening two ways: the prose gives the inauguration as 8 October 2025 while its station table lists the eleven new stations - Science Centre, Mahalaxmi, Jagannath Shankar Sheth, Grant Road, Girgaon, Kalbadevi, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Hutatma Chowk, Churchgate, Vidhan Bhavan and Cuffe Parade - as opening on 9 October 2025, the same one-day gap it shows for the two earlier phases
  • The stretch completes the 33.5 km (20.82 mi) Line 3, also called the Colaba-Bandra-SEEPZ line, running from Cuffe Parade in the far south to Aarey JVLR in the north centre
  • It is Mumbai's first fully underground metro line, with 27 stations - 26 underground and only the northern terminus at grade - platform screen doors throughout and Alstom Urbalis 400 CBTC signalling with no lineside signals
  • The line opened in three phases: BKC to Aarey JVLR with 10 stations, inaugurated by Modi on 5 October 2024 (table: 7 October 2024); Phase 2A, BKC to Acharya Atre Chowk, five stations, inaugurated by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on 9 May 2025 (table: 10 May 2025); and this final section
  • The line's cost is stated inconsistently: the overview and infobox give a total of about ₹30,000 crore (US$3.1 billion), the figure MMRC managing director Ashwini Bhide gave as the actual completion cost in March 2019, while the article's own funding table totals ₹37,276 crore (US$3.9 billion)
  • The JICA soft loan is given two ways as well - ₹13,235 crore (US$1.4 billion) against the ₹23,136 crore project in the funding narrative, but ₹21,280.45 crore, or 57.09% of the total, in the funding table - and its interest rate appears as both 1.4% and 1.44% a year
  • The line is owned by Mumbai Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. and operated by the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, with a depot at Aarey JVLR
  • Rolling stock is Alstom Metropolis: a EUR 315 million contract awarded in September 2018 for 336 coaches, 42 driverless eight-car sets carrying 3,000 passengers each, designed at Alstom's Bengaluru engineering centre and built at Sri City, Andhra Pradesh; the line runs at automation grade 4 but will use drivers in its first year
  • Daily ridership was 150,000 in October 2025, about a tenth of the initial projection of nearly 1.5 million passengers a day
  • Construction began on 21 October 2016, after Union Cabinet clearance on 27 June 2013 and state cabinet approval on 26 February 2014, from a line first announced as a 20 km Colaba-Bandra route in 2004
  • Seven civil packages of roughly ₹2,221 crore each were awarded by August 2016 to consortia including L&T-Shanghai Tunnel Engineering, HCC-Moscow Metrostroy, Dogus-Soma, CEC-ITD Cementation-Tata Projects and J Kumar-China Railway Tunnel Group
  • Twin 5.85 m tunnels were bored at 20-25 m depth by 17 tunnel boring machines with 41 breakthroughs, including a 170 m crossing under the Mithi River, India's second under-river metro tunnel after Kolkata's under the Hooghly
  • The project affects 5,012 trees, 1,331 cut and 3,681 replanted, and drew years of litigation and protest, above all over the Aarey car depot; the Bombay High Court and Supreme Court repeatedly dismissed or vacated challenges
  • Work at Aarey was stayed by Chief Minister Uddhav Thackeray in November 2019 and moved back there in July 2022 under the Shinde-Fadnavis government; the delays and COVID-19 caused cost overruns "in thousands of crores" and "delayed the opening of the line by at least 2 years"
  • Construction incidents included a fatal tunnel shaft accident in September 2019 and buildings sinking in Mahim in November 2019; the Acharya Atre Chowk station platform flooded on 26 May 2025, days after that section opened
  • Operationally, no check-in luggage is allowed on board - MMRC officials stressing Metro 3 is "not an 'Airport Express line'" - bicycles are restricted, and the open-loop fare system accepts only RuPay cards
  • Five-year station co-branding rights were licensed in September 2022 for ₹216 crore to Kotak Mahindra Bank, State Bank of India, LIC, ICICI Lombard, Nippon India Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, HDFC Life, Mahindra and AU Bank
  • A 2.5 km southbound extension beyond Cuffe Parade adding a Navy Nagar station, costing a further ₹2,301 crore, was announced by Maharashtra in March 2022
dateConfidenceReasoning: The article states the final stretch "from Acharya Atre Chowk to Cuffe Parade was inaugurated by Modi, along with the Navi Mumbai International Airport on 8 October 2025".

title: Golden Gate Bridge District Approves Final $1BN Seismic Retrofit Phase

  • The original estimate was about $880 million; total cost now exceeds $1.8 billion, blamed on post-pandemic construction inflation

title: Six Flags Qiddiya City Opens Three Years Behind Its First Date
description: The first Six Flags park in Asia opened outside Riyadh with 28 attractions across six themed areas, among them Falcons Flight, billed as the world's tallest, fastest and longest roller coaster. Qiddiya Investment Company awarded a $1 billion construction contract to Almabani General Contractors and Bouygues Batiment International in December 2021.
longFormSummary:
• Six Flags Qiddiya City opened to the public on 31 December 2025 in Qiddiya City, Riyadh Province, Saudi Arabia - "the first Six Flags park in Asia and the first located outside North America since 2004" after the former European division was sold off
  • The park is owned by the Qiddiya Investment Company and operated and managed by Six Flags Entertainment Corporation, covering 320,000 m2 (79 acres) with 28 attractions, eight roller coasters and five water rides
  • The opening ran three years past the original plan: Six Flags announced the park on 4 April 2018, backed by the Public Investment Fund under Saudi Vision 2030, "initially slated for a 2022 opening", and the date moved to 2023 when the design was unveiled on 26 August 2019
  • On 12 December 2021 the Qiddiya Investment Company "awarded a $1 billion contract to Almabani General Contractors based in Saudi Arabia and Bouygues Batiment International based in France to begin construction on the park"; the Qiddiya release cited for it is headed "Qiddiya Awards SAR 3.75B to Build Six Flags Qiddiya City"
  • The opening date was announced on 16 November 2025, with tickets from US$87 (SAR 325) for adults and US$74 (SAR 275) for children, free for infants under four, granting unlimited access to all rides for a full day
  • A soft opening was held for employees' families and selected media influencers, and about two weeks before the ceremony WWE stars including Randy Orton, Liv Morgan, Omos, Tiffany Stratton and Grayson Waller visited while touring Saudi Arabia to promote Riyadh Season and the 2026 Royal Rumble
  • The formal inauguration came two days before the public opening, on 29 December 2025, under the patronage of the Governor of Riyadh Province, Faisal bin Bandar, with a live performance by Alicia Keys
  • The 2019 design set out 28 attractions across six themed areas, the layout the park opened with: Steam Town, City of Thrills, Twilight Gardens, Discovery Springs, Grand Exposition and Valley of Fortune
  • The article contradicts itself on the count: its infobox and the 2019 announcement both give 28 attractions, while the ride tables for the six areas list 26
  • The signature attraction is Falcons Flight, an Intamin steel "exa coaster" in City of Thrills billed as the world's tallest, longest and fastest roller coaster, at 195 m (640 ft) high, 250 km/h (155 mph) top speed and 4,250 m (2.6 mi) of track
  • Four further world records are claimed: Sirocco Tower as the tallest free-standing shot tower at 145 m, Gyrospin as the tallest pendulum ride at 53 m of swing, Iron Rattler as the tallest tilt coaster at 63.4 m and 118 km/h, and Spitfire as the tallest inverted triple-launch roller coaster at 73 m - though the Valley of Fortune entry describes Spitfire instead as featuring "the tallest inversion on a roller coaster", and Sirocco Tower is called "the world's tallest drop tower" in its own entry
  • Other named rides include Adrena-Line and Twilight Express (Vekoma), Saw Mill Falls (Mack Rides), Colossus (Great Coasters International), Sea Stallion (Maurer Rides), Zoomaflooma (WhiteWater West), Skywatch (Intamin) and the Arabian Carousel "with horses and camels which features Arabian melodies"
  • In 2024 UK Export Finance designated the project "Category A" under its social and environmental risk framework, "identifying a potential for significant adverse impact during construction and operation, requiring ongoing monitoring of labour conditions during construction"
address: Qiddiya City, Riyadh Province, Saudi Arabia
dateConfidenceReasoning: Wikipedia records that "On November 16, 2025, it was announced that Six Flags Qiddiya City would officially open on December 31, 2025."
delayReasoning: Stated: the park "was initially slated for a 2022 opening" and "The park's opening date was then moved to 2023", but it did not open until 31 December 2025.

title: Major Construction Begins on the New Long Bridge Over the Potomac
description: The Virginia Passenger Rail Authority moved the Long Bridge Project into full construction, opening daytime work windows through the Washington, D.C. construction zone because the District's noise and vibration rules bar the work at night. A new two-track bridge beside the century-old Long Bridge will give a continuous four-track corridor between Arlington and L'Enfant Plaza, relieving the worst passenger-rail bottleneck on the East Coast.
longFormSummary:
• The Virginia Passenger Rail Authority announced passenger rail service changes for the Long Bridge Project, "the flagship project of the state's Transforming Rail in Virginia (TRV) initiative", affecting both Amtrak and VRE services
  • As the project enters full construction, major construction activities require daytime "work windows" through the construction zone in Washington, D.C., because noise and vibration ordinances there prohibit certain work at night - specifically barring crews from working between 7 pm and 7 am
  • "Work windows will begin January 12, 2026, and will continue until the project's completion in 2030"
  • VPRA developed the plan jointly with Amtrak, NCDOT, CSX, NS and Virginia Railway Express, aiming to preserve optimal Amtrak times while protecting VRE's highest-ridership morning and evening peaks; CSX also rescheduled its freight traffic around the work window
  • The project is "one of the largest railroad construction projects undertaken in the Commonwealth in decades" and covers far more than a new two-track passenger bridge over the Potomac: seven new bridges in total, five for rail and two for pedestrians and cyclists, running in Washington, D.C. from just south of L'Enfant Plaza across Maine Avenue, the Washington Channel and I-395 to the Potomac
  • Other factors in the schedule: creating the longest possible uninterrupted work window, crews working simultaneously on the Alexandria Fourth Track project and VRE's L'Enfant project (both critical connections to Long Bridge), and large Amtrak Northeast Corridor projects outside Baltimore and New York whose own changes affect Virginia service
  • VPRA Executive Director DJ Stadtler: "While we are thrilled with the progress of the Long Bridge Project, we understand that these necessary service changes will be difficult for a number of our passengers... we evaluated every possible scenario to limit the disruptions while providing our construction teams with the work window they need to safely complete the project on time and on budget"
  • Amtrak's Jennifer Mitchell called it "a transformative investment in rail infrastructure that will unlock new capacity, improve service reliability, and stimulate economic opportunity for generations to come", and VRE Acting CEO Dallas Richards said that with the project's completion VRE looks forward to "expanding VRE service to include our first-ever weekend and late-night service"

title: El Insurgente Reaches Observatorio in Mexico City
description: The last section of the 57.7-kilometre Mexico-Toluca commuter railway, from Santa Fe into the rebuilt Observatorio terminal, was inaugurated, finishing a line that had been opening in stages from Zinacantepec since 2023. Its estimated cost climbed from $38.6 billion MXN in 2014 to $73.72 billion MXN by 2019.
longFormSummary:
• The third and final section of El Insurgente, from Santa Fe to Observatorio, was inaugurated on 2 February 2026, "completing the line"
  • El Insurgente - formally the Tren Interurbano Mexico City-Toluca - is a 57.7 km (35.9 mi) commuter railway with seven stations, four in the State of Mexico and three in Mexico City, running between Zinacantepec and Observatorio
  • It opened in stages: Zinacantepec to Lerma on 15 September 2023 with four trains initially, Lerma to Santa Fe on 31 August 2024, and Santa Fe to Observatorio on 2 February 2026; the Vasco de Quiroga station in Álvaro Obregón opened with the last section
  • The line is electrified at 25 kV 60 Hz AC and mostly elevated with a tunnel between the State of Mexico and Mexico City, double-track standard gauge, operating at 160 km/h (99 mph) with CAF Civity-based EMUs
  • Cost estimates climbed steeply over the build: $38.6 billion MXN in 2014, then overruns "from $42.72 billion MXN in 2015 to $73.72 billion MXN in 2019"
  • The project was announced by President Enrique Peña Nieto on 1 December 2012, construction began in 2014 with a formal ceremony in July 2014 by SCT head Gerardo Ruiz Esparza, and the line was branded El Insurgente - after Miguel Hidalgo - on 1 September 2023
  • Terminating at Observatorio was a deliberate choice from three routes analysed in a November 2013 cost-benefit report - picked along Avenida Las Torres "in order to avert future sprawl, avoid deforestation in the Sierra de las Cruces, and prevent pollution of aquifers" - and 4.3 km of the route was altered in October 2015 to stop it running above Avenida Vasco de Quiroga in Cuajimalpa
  • Construction was split into three contracted sections: 36.1 km from Zinacantepec to the eastern tunnel entrance, the 4.6 km tunnel under the Sierra de las Cruces by Ingenieros Civiles y Asociados, and the 17 km Mexico City portion to Observatorio
  • CAF won a 2014 contract for 30 five-car EMUs at $11.6 billion MXN (€690 million), each carrying 700 passengers, with deliveries from January 2017; the depot west of Zinacantepec cost MXN942 million

title: Kartavya Bhavan 1 and 2 Open in Delhi's New Central Secretariat
description: Two more of the ten Common Central Secretariat blocks on Kartavya Path, along with the Seva Teerth complex, were inaugurated, taking to three the number of buildings in service in the Central Vista's replacement for Shastri, Nirman and Krishi Bhawan. longFormSummary:

  • Kartavya Bhavan, or the Common Central Secretariat, is a ten-building office complex on Kartavya Path in New Delhi built under the Central Vista Redevelopment Project launched in 2019, intended to replace Shastri Bhawan, Nirman Bhawan and Krishi Bhawan with a centralised administrative complex; Krishi Bhawan, Nirman Bhawan, Shastri Bhawan, Udyog Bhawan and Vigyan Bhavan are to be demolished to make room for the rest

  • Cost for the first three buildings is ₹3,690 crore (US$380 million); construction started in 2020 and the infobox gives completion as 2026
  • Each building has seven floors plus two basements and a floor area of about 150,000 m² (1,600,000 ft²), designed by HCP Design, Planning and Management - the firm behind the Central Vista master plan - with the CPWD as architect, the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs as developer and the Shapoorji Pallonji Group as main contractor
  • Kartavya Bhavan 1, on the north side of Kartavya Path between Man Singh Road and Dr. Rajendra Prasad Road, houses the Ministry of Finance: Expenditure on the 6th floor, Economic Affairs on the 5th and 6th, Revenue on the 4th
  • Kartavya Bhavan 2, between buildings 1 and 3, houses the Central Bureau of Investigation and the ministries of Education, Chemicals and Fertilizers, Culture, Information and Broadcasting, Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare, Law and Justice, and Defence
  • The design borrows Lutyens' colonnaded facades and symmetrical layouts while adding double-glazed noise-insulating facades, sensor-based smart HVAC and LED lighting cutting consumption by about 30%, rooftop solar (366 kWp plus 200 kW) generating over 534,000 kWh a year, zero-discharge wastewater management recycling 1.1 million litres a day, rainwater harvesting, composting of about 1,000 kg a day, EV charging and smart elevators, aiming for a GRIHA-4 green rating
  • Each block contains 24 large conference rooms, 26 small ones and 67 compact team-meeting spaces, plus a crèche, yoga room, medical centre, café, multipurpose hall and parking for about 600 cars, with entry by smart ID card and biometrics under a centralised surveillance control centre
  • The article gives two timelines for the rest of the campus: "the full CCS campus is forecasted to be operational by mid-2027" and the remaining buildings "expected to be completed by June 2027"
  • A proposed loop of underground moving walkways connecting all the CCS buildings was dropped, but at the Kartavya Bhavan-3 inauguration the government announced a 7 km Magenta Line extension from Indraprastha to Ramakrishna Ashram Marg with nine new stations including one at Kartavya Bhavan; the site is already near the Central Secretariat metro station on the Yellow and Violet lines

title: Namo Bharat's Delhi-Meerut Corridor Opens End to End
description: The 82.15 km semi-high-speed corridor from Sarai Kale Khan in Delhi to Modipuram in Meerut, with 16 stations, two depots and Alstom trainsets running at 160 km/h, became fully operational, covering the distance in under an hour. Deutsche Bahn's Indian subsidiary runs it for the National Capital Region Transport Corporation.
longFormSummary:
• On 22 February 2026 the last two stretches of the Delhi-Meerut RRTS opened - New Ashok Nagar to Sarai Kale Khan and Meerut South to Modipuram - completing the 82.15 km (51.05 mi) corridor end to end
  • The line is the first of four rapid rail corridors under the first phase of the Namo Bharat project, connecting Delhi, Ghaziabad and Meerut in the National Capital Region, and is managed by the National Capital Region Transport Corporation
  • It was designed for 180 km/h and runs at 160 km/h, averaging about 100 km/h, covering Delhi to Meerut in less than 60 minutes; on inauguration it became India's first regional transit system and "the fastest rapid transit train in the nation at 160 km/h"
  • The corridor was developed at a cost of Rs 30,274 crore (US$3.1 billion), the sum the Government of India approved with implementation in February 2019
  • It has 16 stations - 15 operational and one (Jangpura, at-grade) still under construction - and two depots, at Duhai and Modipuram; the route is 68.03 km elevated, 14.12 km underground and 1.45 km at-grade for the depot connections
  • Sarai Kale Khan is the largest station, with three levels, six platforms and six tracks for the Meerut, Panipat and Alwar corridors, forming a multi-modal hub with the Pink Line metro, the Sarai Kale Khan ISBT and Hazrat Nizamuddin railway station
  • Operations are run by DB RRTS Operations India Private Limited, a Deutsche Bahn subsidiary selected by NCRTC in July 2022 to operate and maintain the corridor for twelve years with a further five-year option; NCRTC named the service RapidX and the trains Namo Bharat
  • The rolling stock is 30 six-car trainsets (extendable to eight) out of a 210-coach order won by Bombardier Transportation on 1 May 2020 at Rs 2,577 crore (US$270 million), built at the Savli plant in Gujarat - which the article calls Alstom's plant - with a Lotus Temple-inspired design, one premium coach, one coach reserved for women and a capacity of 1,750 passengers
  • Technically the line is 1,435 mm standard gauge with 25 kV 50 Hz AC overhead catenary and ETCS L2/L3 over LTE signalling, the control contract going to Alstom in January 2021 at about Rs 937 crore (US$97 million); Nokia's 4.9G/LTE private wireless network for ETCS L2 was "the first instance globally of an LTE network being integrated with ETCS L2 signalling", and hybrid ETCS L3 was commissioned in July 2024
  • The full opening came after a long run of delays: the corridor opened in stages from the Sahibabad-Duhai Depot priority section on 20 October 2023, through March 2024, August 2024 and January 2025, and although all civil work, testing and trial runs were finished by October 2025, the remaining stretches stayed shut until February 2026 because officials said full operations would begin only after a formal inauguration by the Prime Minister
  • Full commissioning had originally been planned for 2024, and the corridor "missed three successive deadlines for complete operationalisation"
  • Ridership grew from 2,500-3,000 a day at the October 2023 opening to over 100,000 a day in June 2026 after the full opening, "slated to soar to 800,000 daily"; the article records 113,708 daily and 3,524,951 monthly riders in August 2026
  • The article notes its own caveat: it carries an April 2026 notice that it "may incorporate text from a large language model"

Trains initially run only between 10.00 and 15.00 at headways of seven to fourteen minutes, with full service expected from October 2026.
longFormSummary:
• The initial 6.7 km section of São Paulo's monorail Line 17-Gold was inaugurated on March 31, 2026, linking Congonhas Airport with Morumbi on suburban rail Line 9 and serving seven stations
  • It opened "no less than 12 years behind its original planned opening date": preparatory works began in April 2012 with the line intended to be ready for the 2014 FIFA World Cup, but "the project has faced persistent problems with both procurement and construction"
  • Service is initially limited to between 10.00 and 15.00 with headways of 7 to 14 minutes, and "full service is expected to start in October 2026"
  • The first section cost R$5.97bn and is operated by concessionaire ViaMobilidade
  • An eighth station, Washington Luís, is under construction on a branch south of Brooklin Paulista and was expected to open in June
  • Governor Tarsísio de Freitas said at the opening: "Today we are not inaugurating the line, we are ending a cycle of delays... For years, we lived with a structure that consumed resources and remained idle"
  • He announced 4.6 km of extensions at both ends without timescales - one station south from Washington Luís to Vila Paulista and three more north from Morumbi to Américo Mourano - within a longer-term 17.7 km corridor from Jabaquara on metro Line 1 to São Paulo-Morumbi on metro Line 4
  • The contracting history was turbulent: the 2011 turnkey contract to the Monotrilho Integração consortium (Andrade Gutierrez, CR Almeida, Montagens e Projetos Especiais, Scomi Engineering) ended in delays, disputes and terminations, with remaining civil works re-tendered in several packages in 2020, the largest going to Coesa Engenharia and Constran
  • Rolling stock supplier Scomi Engineering lost its contract in 2019 after a winding-up order from the Malaysian high court; China's BYD was then selected for 14 five-car SkyRail trainsets plus CBTC supporting GoA4 automation, control systems and platform screen doors, with onboard batteries allowing up to 8 km of travel in a power failure, and Thales supplying telecoms, passenger information and CCTV
  • Eight trainsets had been commissioned by late March with three more delivered to the Água Espraiada depot, and operations are supervised by onboard staff, "standard procedure for new automated urban rail lines in São Paulo"
  • The same report covers a separate opening at the city's other airport: a 2.7 km Aeromovel peoplemover linking Guarulhos terminals 1, 2 and 3 with the Line 13 station, running 16.00 to 00.00

title: Lilly's Foundayo (Orforglipron) Weight-Loss Pill Approved by FDA
description: The FDA approved Eli Lilly's Foundayo, a once-daily GLP-1 pill for weight loss that needs no food or water restrictions, with direct-to-consumer sales from April 6.
longFormSummary:
• The FDA approved Eli Lilly's Foundayo (orforglipron) on 1 April 2026 for adults with obesity, or overweight with weight-related medical problems, used with a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity; the approval letter for NDA 220934 is signed by Lisa B. Yanoff, MD, Deputy Director of the Office of Cardiology, Hematology, Endocrinology and Nephrology, with an electronic signature timestamp of 04/01/2026 09:10:30 AM
  • The application was received on January 20, 2026, and was "not referred to an FDA advisory committee because there were no controversial issues that would benefit from advisory committee discussion"
  • It is the only GLP-1 pill for weight loss that can be taken any time of day without food or water restrictions, a once-daily small molecule (non-peptide) GLP-1 receptor agonist
  • Prescriptions are accepted immediately through LillyDirect with shipping beginning April 6, followed shortly by broad availability through U.S. retail pharmacies and telehealth providers; Yahoo Finance frames the same launch as Lilly expecting to launch on its direct-to-consumer channel "by 6 April"
  • In ATTAIN-1, adults on the highest dose who stayed on treatment lost an average of 27.3 pounds (12.4%) against 2.2 pounds (0.9%) with placebo, the efficacy estimand over 72 weeks; regardless of trial completion the average was 25 pounds (11.1%) against 5.3 pounds (2.1%). EMJ GOLD gives the same trial as "more than 12%" versus around 1%, and "more than 10%" versus approximately 2%, and Yahoo Finance cites the 12.4% figure
  • Foundayo also reduced markers of cardiovascular risk - waist circumference, non-HDL cholesterol, triglycerides and systolic blood pressure - across all doses
  • The ATTAIN Phase 3 programme enrolled more than 4,500 people across two registration trials: ATTAIN-1 (NCT05869903) randomized 3,127 participants in ten countries and territories, and ATTAIN-2 (NCT05872620) over 1,600 participants with type 2 diabetes
  • Pricing: as little as $25 a month with the savings card for eligible people with commercial insurance, self-pay from $149 a month for the lowest dose, and $50 a month for eligible Medicare Part D individuals "beginning as soon as July 1, 2026"
  • The tablets come in 0.8 mg, 2.5 mg, 5.5 mg, 9 mg, 14.5 mg and 17.2 mg strengths, starting at 0.8 mg, swallowed whole with or without food, and are not to be used with another GLP-1
  • Orforglipron was discovered by Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. and licensed by Lilly in 2018; it is Lilly's second FDA-approved obesity medicine and is also being studied for type 2 diabetes, obstructive sleep apnea, osteoarthritis knee pain, hypertension, peripheral artery disease and stress urinary incontinence
  • Lilly has submitted orforglipron for weight management and/or type 2 diabetes in more than 40 countries and plans to launch in each shortly after approval
  • Yahoo Finance reports it as "the first new molecular entity (NME) approved under the FDA's national priority voucher (CNPV) programme" launched by Commissioner Marty Makary, which GlobalData analyst Shehroz Mahmood says "has led to the fastest new molecular entity approval since 2002"; the FDA letter itself says only that "New molecular entities qualify for a post approval feedback meeting" and does not mention the voucher
  • The approval ends Novo Nordisk's first-mover advantage in the US after three months, Wegovy's pill (semaglutide) having launched there in January 2026; Foundayo has no meal restrictions where oral Wegovy must be taken on an empty stomach each morning, and as a small molecule is easier to manufacture and scale
  • No head-to-head trials have been run, but the Wegovy pill on average leads to 2.2% better weight loss
  • The label carries a boxed-style warning that Foundayo may cause thyroid tumors including thyroid cancer, and it is contraindicated with a personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma or with MEN 2; other serious risks listed are pancreatitis, severe stomach problems, dehydration and kidney problems, hypoglycemia, allergic reactions, diabetic retinopathy changes, gallbladder problems and aspiration under anesthesia
  • The commonest side effects are nausea, constipation, diarrhea, vomiting, indigestion, abdominal pain, headache, swollen belly, fatigue, belching, heartburn, gas and hair loss; birth control pills may not work as well, so another method is advised for 30 days after starting and after each dose increase
  • The FDA attached a long list of postmarketing requirements under 505(o), including a pediatric obesity registry cohort study of at least 10 years, two pregnancy studies, a medullary thyroid carcinoma registry case series of at least 15 years running to a final report in August 2043, the ACHIEVE-4 cardiovascular outcomes trial with adjudicated MACE and drug-induced liver injury assessment, a gastric-emptying clinical pharmacology trial and a milk-only lactation study
  • Pediatric studies were waived for ages under 6 and deferred for ages 6-11 and 12-17, with the adolescent trial J4M-MC-PW01 (ADVANCE-ATTAIN-ADOLESCENTS) due to complete in March 2028 and report in December 2028
  • The FDA also requested enhanced pharmacovigilance for five years after approval, with 15-day "Alert reports" for serious unexpected cases of drug-induced liver injury causing jaundice, liver failure, transplant or death
  • The approved expiry dating period is 24 months from manufacture when stored at 20°C to 25°C
  • Lilly's CEO David A. Ricks framed the launch around access: "Today, fewer than 1 in 10 people who could benefit from a GLP-1 are taking one, held back by access, stigma, perceived complexity or the belief that their condition isn't serious enough for treatment"
  • Buoyed by obesity drug sales, Lilly's growth rose 45% in 2025, and Citi analysts expect Foundayo's lack of fasting requirements to put it "in pole position to continue Lilly's cardiometabolic dominance"
dateConfidenceReasoning: Lilly and the FDA approval letter date the approval April 1, 2026.

title: Foundation Work Begins on the Commanders' New Stadium at RFK
description: Work started on the foundational infrastructure for a 65,000-seat domed stadium on the old RFK Stadium site in southeast Washington, with the full groundbreaking held back to early 2027 and opening expected in 2030. The Commanders are putting up $2.7 billion towards a project projected at $3.8 billion; the District is spending $500 million on infrastructure and will own the building.
longFormSummary:
• "Work on foundational infrastructure began in April 2026, with groundbreaking scheduled for early 2027" for the New Stadium at RFK Campus, the planned indoor home of the Washington Commanders
  • The stadium is scheduled to open in 2030 at 2400 East Capitol Street SE in Washington, D.C., with a capacity of 65,000 plus upwards of 5,000 standing-room only, and a cost of US$3.8 billion that will make it "among the most expensive ever built"
  • It will be owned by the Government of DC and operated by the Commanders, hosting American football, soccer and concerts under a cable-netted ETFE skylight roof
  • Financing is a public-private partnership: the Commanders contribute $2.7 billion for construction, a parking garage and any cost overrun, while DC spends $500 million on infrastructure through the Sports Facilities Fee, $356 million on another parking garage through Events DC bonds and $202 million on public utilities from general taxes
  • The site is the campus of the former RFK Stadium, the team's home from its 1961 opening until 1996 and their owners' "spiritual home", which closed in 2019 and was deconstructed in 2025
  • Getting there took federal legislation: the D.C. Robert F. Kennedy Memorial Stadium Campus Revitalization Act, introduced 27 July 2023, transferred control from the National Park Service to the District under a 99-year lease, passing the House on 28 February 2024 and the Senate on 21 December 2024 before being signed into law on 6 January 2025
  • Mayor Muriel Bowser, NFL commissioner Roger Goodell and owner Josh Harris announced the RFK Campus as the site on 28 April 2025; the DC Council tentatively approved the project in August 2025 and finalised it the following month
  • President Donald Trump suggested blocking the deal in July 2025 unless the team returned to the Redskins branding, and later said he wanted the stadium named after him
  • HKS designed it in a neoclassical style inspired by the original RFK Stadium, with an exterior of colonnades in a wave pattern, a section designed to replicate the bouncing stands RFK was known for, and a western balcony overlooking the plaza with views of the Capitol and Washington Monument down East Capitol Street
  • To comply with DC's Height of Buildings Act the top row of seating sits below 130 ft, with the stadium sunk into the ground and "fused with RFK Stadium's original foundation"
  • District PM Alliance - a joint venture of Brailsford & Dunlavey, Creative Artists Agency Icon and McKissack & McKissack - manages the project, with Clark Construction, Mortenson Construction and SmootDC building it; the playing surface is undecided, with natural grass preferred by the Commanders
  • Beyond football it is expected to host up to 200 additional events a year and is in consideration for Super Bowl LXV and the 2031 FIFA Women's World Cup final, with the NWSL's Washington Spirit suggested as a possible additional tenant; DC anticipates over $5 billion in sales taxes over 30 years
  • Transport plans include an expansion of the Stadium-Armory Metrorail station and a new Metrobus rapid transit line mirroring the former DC Streetcar route, with around 8,000 parking spots on opening day
  • The stadium will anchor about 180 acres of mixed-use development across five districts with roughly 6,000 residences (30% affordable), an $89 million indoor gymnasium in the Recreation district, over a third of the campus as green space, and full district construction expected to run until 2040
address: 2400 East Capitol Street SE, Washington, D.C. 20003, United States

title: Inter Miami Opens Nu Stadium at Miami Freedom Park
description: Inter Miami played its first match at the 26,700-seat Nu Stadium, the centrepiece of the 131-acre Miami Freedom Park built on the former Melreese golf course beside Miami International Airport, drawing 2-2 with Austin FC. The club had played out of Fort Lauderdale since 2020 while the site was fought over and built.
longFormSummary:
• Inter Miami's Nu Stadium opened on April 4, 2026 with an inaugural match against Austin FC; the match ended in a 2-2 draw, with Guilherme Biro scoring the first goal in the stadium's history and Lionel Messi the first Inter Miami goal there, before an attendance of 26,412
  • The 26,700-seat soccer-specific stadium is owned and operated by Inter Miami, designed by MANICA Architecture and Arquitectonica, at 1900 NW 37th Avenue, and replaces the interim Chase Stadium in Fort Lauderdale; the infobox nicknames it "The House that Messi Built"
  • It is the centerpiece of Miami Freedom Park, a mixed-use development near Miami International Airport that will include office, retail and commercial space and public parks
  • The name arrived only weeks before opening: on March 3, 2026 the club announced a naming-rights deal with Brazilian fintech Nubank, and on March 27, 2026 it named blocks 117-121 of the lower bowl and 217-223 of the upper bowl the "Leo Messi Stand"
  • Beckham unveiled the Freedom Park plan in July 2018 on the city-owned Melreese Country Club - 131 acres of public land with 1 million sq ft of commercial space, 750 hotel rooms, 23 acres of public soccer fields, a 10.5-acre stadium and 58 acres of public park, plus $20 million a year for 30 years toward city park improvements - and a November 2018 referendum on negotiating a no-bid lease "passed with 60% of the vote"
  • The opening date slipped repeatedly: Beckham projected a 2022 opening in June 2019, the April 28, 2022 city council vote granting a 99-year lease projected the 2025 MLS season, and construction beginning in August 2023 was "with intentions to open in 2026"
  • Soil contamination was one of the obstacles - Mayor Francis Suarez confirmed on August 20, 2019 that it was worse than thought, with CBS Miami reporting "arsenic contamination levels are more than twice what is allowed by law"
  • Before Melreese the club chased four other sites, all of which failed: PortMiami, rejected 11-1 by county commissioners on May 20, 2014 after Royal Caribbean formed an opposing alliance; a Museum Park boat slip turned down on June 10, 2014 over rent; a parcel west of Marlins Park, pulled from the commission agenda on December 1, 2015; and an Overtown block bought by March 2016 and expanded in 2017 before being abandoned for the airport site after Jorge Mas joined
  • Melreese Golf Course shut on March 19, 2023, ground was broken on August 28, 2023, and on August 8, 2024 Governor Ron DeSantis announced an $8 million Job Growth Grant Fund award for road infrastructure around the stadium
  • Later firsts at the venue: Inter Miami's first win there, 2-0 over the Portland Timbers on May 17, 2026 before 26,715 fans - above the stated 26,700 capacity - the first international game on June 5, 2026 as Peru beat Haiti 2-1 before 26,700, and Mexican country musician Carín León as the first musical act on June 28, 2026
  • Access is via the Miami Intermodal Center on the MIA Mover, Metrorail and Tri-Rail plus express buses to Miami Beach, with a 1,450-foot grade-separated pedestrian bridge to the park due to start construction in 2027 and finish by the second quarter of 2029; Tri-Rail runs special weekend match trains leaving 45 minutes after the final whistle and the club gives a $10 concessions voucher to fans showing proof of transit use
  • The site has over 4,500 on-site parking spaces, said to be the largest capacity at any MLS stadium, and 2.51 miles (4.04 km) of new roadways, though the wiki flags that claim as needing a better source

title: DC Water Launches the Boring Machine Mary Under the Potomac

title: LAX's SkyLink People Mover Starts Systems Testing
description: The 2.25-mile automated people mover linking LAX's terminals to the Metro Rail system and the rental car centre began demonstration running without passengers, aiming for 30 consecutive days of error-free operation before it can carry anyone. Construction was originally due to finish in March 2023; Los Angeles World Airports has since agreed to more than $880 million in dispute payments on top of the $4.9 billion, 25-year contract, and has not announced an opening date.
longFormSummary:
• Systems demonstration testing of SkyLink began on 21 April 2026, intending to demonstrate 30 consecutive days of continuous error-free operation without passengers; that testing is ongoing
  • SkyLink is a 2.25-mile (3.62 km) fully elevated, two-track automated people mover with six stations, linking Los Angeles International Airport's central terminal area to the West Intermodal Transportation Facility, the LAX/Metro Transit Center for Metro Rail's C and K Lines, and the LAX Rental Car Center
  • The article gives the system's status as “In testing, in litigation”, and Los Angeles World Airports has not announced a firm opening date
  • It is owned by LAWA and built and operated by LAX Integrated Express Solutions (LINXS) — a partnership of ACS, Alstom, Balfour Beatty, Fluor and Hochtief with HDR and Flatiron West — under a 25-year design-build-finance-operate-maintain contract the Los Angeles City Council approved on 11 April 2018 at US$4.9 billion
  • Construction was originally scheduled for completion in March 2023; the global settlement formally extended the contractual completion date to December 2025, and Fitch Ratings projected in August 2025 that construction would finish in January 2026 with testing and commissioning continuing through June 2026
  • LAWA has agreed to more than US$880 million in change orders and dispute-related payments on top of the US$4.9 billion contract: roughly US$252 million in design-related changes, the US$97 million awarded by the contract arbitrator and a US$550 million global settlement
  • On 7 June 2024 the contract's “Project Neutral” arbitrator ruled LAWA responsible for 526 days of delay, “having failed to act in good faith and comply with the contract documents”, citing failures to integrate the people mover with airport communications systems in time and issues with construction of the Metro Rail station
  • A Los Angeles County Civil Grand Jury attributed the setbacks to a strained LAWA-LINXS relationship, political pressure to finish before major regional events, and defects in the contract's sole dispute-resolution mechanism drafted by the law firm Nossaman, which allowed no panel of arbitrators and no way to replace the Project Neutral
  • LINXS sued the city on 9 July 2026 over unresolved contract disputes after the city rejected its claim in January, and the Los Angeles City Council referred the matter to its Trade, Travel, and Tourism Committee on 26 June 2026
  • On 21 July 2026 Fitch downgraded about US$1.2 billion of LINXS APM senior bonds to 'BB' from 'BB+' and placed them on Rating Watch Negative, citing “a precarious position with a limited margin of safety before it could breach the lenders' longstop of Oct. 8, 2026, and the project longstop date of Dec. 8, 2026”
  • Once open, SkyLink is expected to run 24 hours a day with trains every two minutes from 9 a.m. to 11 p.m. and a 10-minute end-to-end journey
  • The fleet is 44 Alstom Innovia APM 300 vehicles, each carrying up to 50 passengers with luggage (12 seated); nine four-car trains run at peak, each holding up to 200, for up to 30 trains and 6,000 passengers per hour per direction
  • Construction stood at 97.3% complete as of May 2024, and the one-car Maintenance Service Vehicle was first test driven on the guideway on 29 April 2024
  • Pressure to finish came from Los Angeles winning the 2028 Summer Olympics in 2017 and from the 2026 FIFA World Cup and 2027 Super Bowl; in July 2024 Mayor Karen Bass said “it absolutely has to be finished by the time of the World Cup”
  • SkyLink is part of the US$5.5 billion Landside Access Modernization Program and is projected by 2035 to cut vehicle travel in the central terminal area by about 27% and eliminate more than 3,200 daily rental-car shuttle trips
address: Los Angeles International Airport, 1 World Way, Los Angeles, CA 90045
dateConfidenceReasoning: The article states that "Systems demonstration testing began on April 21, 2026, intending to demonstrate 30 consecutive days of continuous error-free operation."

title: Metro's D Line Subway Extension Opens Its First Three Stations
description: LA Metro opened Section 1 of the D Line subway extension, carrying the Wilshire Boulevard subway 3.9 miles west of Wilshire/Western to new stations at La Brea, Fairfax and La Cienega. It is the line's first extension since 1996 and the first of three sections Metro wants running before the 2028 Olympics.
longFormSummary:
• Section 1 of LA Metro's D Line Subway Extension opened on 8 May 2026, with three new underground stations at Wilshire/La Brea, Wilshire/Fairfax and Wilshire/La Cienega
  • The section extends the subway from Koreatown to the Wilshire/La Cienega area, serving the Miracle Mile and surrounding neighbourhoods, and is the first of three sections of a project that runs the line nearly nine miles west from Wilshire/Western along Wilshire Boulevard to Westwood
  • Metro describes the corridor as "one of the most heavily traveled routes in the region" and says the extension will "improve access, reduce travel time, and strengthen connections" between job, education, medical and cultural centres
  • The new stations are fully ADA-accessible with modern safety upgrades, intuitive wayfinding and public art, and Metro says they make it "easier to travel between Beverly Hills, Mid-Wilshire, Miracle Mile, Koreatown, Downtown Los Angeles and the wider Metro system with faster, traffic-free trips," "supporting everyday travel and the region's major global moments ahead"
  • Section 1 took more than eleven years from groundbreaking: Metro broke ground at Wilshire/La Brea on 7 November 2014, lowered tunnel boring machines Elsie and Soyeon there in October 2018, completed their first eastbound drive to Wilshire/Western in June 2019, and Elsie reached Wilshire/Fairfax on 6 April 2020
  • The project page's current phase is Construction with estimated completion given only as "Section 1: Open", and work continues across all three sections
  • Section 2, through Beverly Hills and Century City, remains active with station construction progressing underground; major street restoration and deck removal along Constellation Bl in Century City was planned to begin in spring 2026, with possible temporary lane reductions and weekend work
  • Section 2's tunnelling is long finished - TBMs Harriet and Ruth began driving east from Century City between April and July 2020, reached Beverly Dr station in January 2022 and arrived at the Section 1 interface in November 2022 and January 2023
  • Section 3, extending to Westwood and the West LA VA Medical Center, continues with structural work at the UCLA and VA Hospital stations and preparation for street restoration; its TBMs Aura and Iris were lowered on the VA campus in July 2020, reached Westwood/UCLA in March and May 2022, arrived at Century City Station in April 2023 and broke through there in October 2023
  • Metro completed five years of tunnelling for the whole extension in April 2024
  • Construction mitigation runs alongside: the Eat Shop Play marketing programme, a Business Interruption Fund giving local small businesses along the alignment up to $60,000 per impact year for provable revenue loss, and Metro Art commissions for every new station from Miracle Mile to the West LA VA Medical Center
  • As of a 9 September 2026 community meeting, station work was "nearing completion in Section 1", with work ongoing in Sections 2 and 3
  • The page does not give Section 1's length, does not say when the line was last extended, and does not tie the remaining sections to the 2028 Olympics

title: NEOM Halts Construction on Saudi Arabia's The Line Until After 2030
description: Saudi Arabia's NEOM authority paused further construction on The Line, its 170km linear megacity, until after 2030 amid a sweeping scale-back of the project's ambitions.
longFormSummary:

  • The pause is wider than The Line: tourism destinations on the Red Sea coast are also postponed until after 2030, and Trojena, earlier due to host the 2029 Asian Winter Games, gets no new investment until after 2030
  • The twin mirrored skyscrapers are to be significantly redesigned, with no clarity on when the redesign will be finished or when new funding will be allocated; a BBC report of 25 May was summarised as saying The Line "is being turned into something considerably more prosaic"
  • NEOM plans about $3 billion more for OXAGON, the industrial city with a Red Sea port, adding utilities and data connectivity to attract AI firms' data centers
  • The decision follows a strategic review by CEO Aiman al-Mudaifer, appointed the previous year; the 2030 population target is now up to 100,000, having been 1.5 million and then revised to 300,000 two years earlier
  • New Civil Engineer, ten days later on 1 June 2026, went further: a PR professional who previously represented Neom said the project "appears to have stalled completely" and "I doubt it will go ahead at all"; that piece gives The Line's design as 300 m wide, 500 m tall and 170 km long
  • Contractor evidence of the wind-down: Webuild said in March 2026 that Neom had terminated for convenience its $4.7bn contract for Trojena's artificial lake (three dams and 'The Bow'), and on 21 May 2026 that Neom had terminated the Neom Connector High-Speed Line contract effective May 27, 2026 with works about 20% complete and a residual backlog of about EUR 1bn, concluding all Webuild activities for Neom
  • Wider context given: the PIF is to stop funding LIV Golf after $5 billion, the Mukaab in Riyadh is on hold, and Saudi Arabia faces widening deficits and the Iran war; NEOM did not respond to a request for comment
  • The pin's own source, The B1M's "Is The Line Really Dead?", published 2025-12-18, predates the halt by five months and asks "Can Saudi Arabia's mega build survive 2026?"; its page gives no cost figures, lengths or completion dates

title: Second Avenue Subway Phase 2 Breaks Ground in East Harlem
description: The MTA started the major construction stage of the 1.5-mile extension that carries the Q from 96th Street to Harlem-125th Street, with new stations at 106th, 116th and 125th Streets. A tunnel boring machine goes underground in early 2027 and trains are due in 2032.
longFormSummary:
• Governor Kathy Hochul joined MTA leadership, elected officials and Harlem community leaders on June 8, 2026 to break ground on the major construction stage of Second Avenue Subway Phase 2
  • Phase 2 extends the Q from 96 Street north to 125 Street and then west along 125 Street to Park Avenue, about 1.5 miles in all, with three new accessible stations at 106 Street, 116 Street and 125 Street
  • The groundbreaking site is where the variable-density tunnel-boring machine will be lowered into the ground in early 2027 to mine from 120 Street and 2nd Avenue to 125 Street and Malcolm X Boulevard; the machines are due to be delivered "early next year", weigh more than one and a half million pounds and carry 23-foot tungsten carbide cutter heads that can toggle between hard rock and soft soil
  • The whole project is budgeted at $6.968 billion and is "on track for revenue service in 2032"
  • Phase 2 is being delivered in four contracts against 10 in Phase 1; tunnel boring sits in Contract 2 at $1.97 billion, covering shaft excavation, controlled blasting for future stations and asbestos and lead abatement in the 1970s tunnels
  • Contract 3, announced at the groundbreaking, will build the structural shells of the 106 St Station and the tunnelling from 105 Street to 110 Street by cut and cover, connecting the existing tunnels north and south of the station, with work expected to begin in the coming months
  • The contract award followed the resumption of federal funding in April, and advanced utility relocations finishing early let pending work start six months faster than originally scheduled
  • Lessons from Phase 1 have produced more than $1 billion in savings - handling utility relocation upfront, reusing the 1970s tunnel segment from 110 Street to 120 Street, acquiring real estate early, best-value design-build contracts, tighter contract coordination and smaller back-of-house and station spaces
  • Ridership is stated at different scopes: 100,000 East Harlem daily riders for the extension, 300,000 daily riders once combined with Phase 1 - the same figure Senator Schumer uses for New Yorkers benefiting on completion, alongside "almost two miles of new track, six new stations, and one fully refurbished station"
  • The new 125 Street station will connect directly to the Lexington Avenue line's 125 St station, with a Park Avenue entrance for Metro-North's Harlem-125 Street station, the 4 5 6 lines and the M60 Select Bus Service to LaGuardia; one-seat rides to the Upper East Side, West Midtown and Coney Island are said to shorten trips by up to 20 minutes
  • The project is funded in part by congestion pricing revenue, carries a 20 percent local hiring goal, and serves a district where 70 percent of residents rely on transit; Schumer says he secured "$3.4 billion in federal funding - the largest Capital Investment Grant in history at the time"
  • Hochul noted the previous East Harlem groundbreaking was 54 years ago: Second Avenue service was part of the 1920s Second System plan, bonded by city voters in 1948 but left unbuilt after the Korean War began, and started in 1972 before being abandoned in the 1975 fiscal crisis
  • A further phase is already being scoped - the Q running west across 125th Street to Broadway with three new stations and more than 160,000 daily riders - with $25 million secured in the FY27 enacted state budget for preliminary engineering and design

title: Noida International Airport Starts Commercial Flights at Jewar
description: An IndiGo flight from Lucknow landed on the first day of scheduled service at the National Capital Region's second airport, whose first phase has one 3,900 m runway and a 101,590 sq m terminal for 12 million passengers a year, designed by Grimshaw with Nordic, Haptic and STUP. Zurich Airport International holds the 40-year concession, and the DGCA granted the aerodrome licence on 6 March 2026.
longFormSummary:
• Commercial operations at Noida International Airport began on 15 June 2026, the first flight being an IndiGo arrival from Lucknow
  • The airport (IATA: DXN, ICAO: VIND), also called Jewar Airport, is at Jewar in Gautam Buddha Nagar district, Uttar Pradesh, serving the National Capital Region and western Uttar Pradesh as the second airport of a Delhi-NCR dual-airport system alongside Indira Gandhi International
  • The opening followed the DGCA granting an aerodrome licence on 6 March 2026 and the inauguration of the first phase on 28 March 2026
  • Scheduled flights had initially been expected between mid-April and May 2026 after that inauguration, and the airport had originally been slated to open in 2022, with delays repeatedly pushing commercial operations back
  • Phase I has a single runway, 10/28, 3,900 by 45 metres in asphalt and concrete, with an instrument landing system and aeronautical ground lighting for 24-hour operations, ARFF Category 9, and stands for 24 Code C and two Code D/F aircraft
  • Terminal 1 covers 101,590 square metres with 28 apron stands and a capacity of 12 million passengers a year, to rise to 30 million "in the upcoming years"
  • The terminal was designed by a consortium of Grimshaw, Nordic - Office of Architecture, Haptic and STUP, chosen in 2020 through a three-stage design competition run by Zurich Airport International; it draws on Indian heritage with elements reminiscent of traditional ghats and havelis, sets a landscaped courtyard deep in the plan for daylight and ventilation, targets LEED Gold and carbon net zero operation, and won the 2022 Architectural Review Future Projects Award in the Infrastructure category
  • The airport is owned by Noida International Airport Limited and operated by Yamuna International Airport Private Limited, a subsidiary of Zurich Airport International AG, which won the bid in November 2019; the concession agreement was signed on 7 October 2020 for 40 years on a DBFOT basis, running 2021 to 2061
  • The project was first proposed in 2001 as the greenfield Taj International Aviation Hub by then Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Rajnath Singh, was held up by proximity to IGI and the right of first refusal in Delhi airport's concession, was briefly considered for Agra, returned to Jewar in 2014, won Union Government approval in June 2017 and in-principle approval in May 2018, and had its foundation stone laid on 25 November 2021, with Tata Projects taking the first-phase civil contract in June 2022
  • The article gives two costs for the first phase: YEIDA's phase table puts Phase I at Rs 4,588 crore of a Rs 29,561 crore four-phase total, while the Prime Minister's Office describes Phase I as "developed with an investment of around Rs 11,200 crore"
  • Later phases are to take capacity from 12 million to 30, 50 and finally 70 million passengers a year, Phase III adding a second 4,150 m runway, Terminal 2 and a Ground Transportation Centre, and Phase IV projected at 489,700 aircraft movements a year with 186 apron stands; YEIDA's project page describes a longer-term six-runway end state
  • IndiGo signed as launch carrier under an MoU in November 2023 and Akasa Air in a January 2024 collaboration; IndiGo now serves 17 destinations from the airport including Bengaluru, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Lucknow and Srinagar, and Akasa Air serves Bengaluru, Mumbai and Navi Mumbai
  • A multi-modal cargo hub is designed for over 250,000 metric tonnes a year initially, expandable to about 1.8 million, with Air India SATS selected to develop it in February 2023; concessions by early 2025 covered ground handling (Bird Group), retail and duty-free (Heinemann Asia Pacific with BWC Forwarders), lounges and F&B (Travel Food Services) and technology (Kyndryl)
  • Surface access remains the main unresolved issue: as of April 2026 access was still primarily road-based via the Yamuna Expressway with NH 44 and NH 34, and every rail link - the Greater Noida and Ballabhgarh metros, the 71.1 km Ghaziabad-Jewar RRTS, several proposed railway lines and the Delhi-Noida-Varanasi high-speed line - remains at planning or proposal stage
  • Other concerns recorded are ecological, over the Dhanauri wetlands about 15 km away which had no wetland protection status as of early 2024, and resettlement, with some farmers displaced by second-phase land acquisition saying in March 2026 that promised jobs and rehabilitation had still not been fully implemented
address: Jewar, Gautam Buddha Nagar, Uttar Pradesh, India
dateConfidenceReasoning: The article states "The airport commenced flight operations on 15 June 2026, with an IndiGo flight landing from Lucknow."
delayReasoning: Stated: the page says the airport was "Originally slated for opening in 2022, delays repeatedly pushed back the start of commercial operations", and that it "commenced flight operations on 15 June 2026"; the original year is taken as its last day.

title: Salt Lake Temple Completes Seismic Base-Isolation Retrofit
description: Crews finished installing a base-isolation system beneath the 19th-century Salt Lake Temple as part of an estimated $2.4 billion project to let the building float free of the ground during a major earthquake.
longFormSummary:
• Crews completed the seismic renovation of the Salt Lake Temple (about 6.5 years of work); from 25 June 2026 they removed over 1,500 bolts connecting 392 plates to the 98 base isolators about 20 feet below the temple, so it now rests on its isolation system
  • The isolators let the temple move about 5 feet in any direction in an earthquake (Deseret News, in 2025, said 10 feet)
  • Interior finishing continues (carpet, chandelier, instruction rooms) and refurbished oak doors were reinstalled; a Salt Lake Temple Celebration is being staffed by volunteers
  • The renovation was announced 19 April 2019 and the temple closed 30 December 2019; an open house is scheduled from April to October 2027 and the temple is set to reopen in October 2027

title: First Section of São Paulo's Line 6-Orange Opens for Trial Service
description: Six stations opened along a 5.2 km stretch between João Paulo I and Perdizes, among them Água Branca, which at 47.8 metres is the deepest metro station in South America. Trains run on weekdays from 10.00 to 15.00 and are free for now; the finished line is to run 15.3 km with 15 stations from Brasilândia to São Joaquim.
longFormSummary:
• "The first 5.2 km section of Sao Paulo's metro network's Line 6 (Orange) opened on July 2, with a limited trial service running between Joao Paulo I and Perdizes"
  • Agua Branca "is now the deepest metro station in South America at 47.8 m, overtaking Santa Cruz on Line 5 at 41.5 m"
  • Services initially run 10.00 to 15.00 Monday to Friday, "with travel being free of charge"
  • Francisco Pierrini, CEO of the Concessionaria Linha Universidade consortium, celebrated "the early delivery of six stations on Line 6", matching the pin's six-station count
  • Extensions at each end "will eventually take the line to 15.3 km, connecting Brasilandia in the north with Sao Joaquim in the city centre", with 15 stations serving schools and seven higher education institutions, hence the alternative name "the University Line"
  • A trip that currently takes up to 90 min by bus will fall to 23 min, and the finished line is predicted to carry 633,000 passengers a day
  • The line has a long-stalled history: a build-operate-maintain concession went to the Move Sao Paulo consortium in mid-2013, construction began in January 2015 but "came to a standstill in 2016 when the concessionaire ran into financial difficulties", and the contract was terminated in December 2018 before Linha Universidade restarted work
  • Acciona, the concessionaire's majority shareholder, is doing the civil works; its President and CEO Jose Manuel Entrecanales called the launch "the fulfilment of the commitment Acciona made to Sao Paulo in 2019"
  • Alstom "has so far delivered 12 of the 22 six-car Metropolis trainsets that it is building for Line 6 at its Taubate plant": 80 km/h stainless steel trains with a capacity of 2,044 passengers, a design life of more than 40 years, passenger counting, dynamic line maps, information screens and CCTV, with CBTC that "will support GoA4 unattended driverless operation in the future"
dateConfidenceReasoning: The report states that "the first 5.2 km section of São Paulo's metro network's Line 6 (Orange) opened on July 2".

title: 235 East 42nd Street Column Buckling
description: Structural steel columns buckled at 235 East 42nd Street, the former Pfizer headquarters in Manhattan being converted into roughly 1,600 apartments, forcing an evacuation and emergency stabilisation.
longFormSummary:
• Two structural steel columns buckled on the morning of July 7, 2026 at 235 East 42nd Street, the former Pfizer headquarters in Midtown Manhattan being converted to apartments, with the first reports just before 8 a.m.
  • The failure was on the 21st floor and caused the floors above to sag, prompting the city to evacuate surrounding blocks for fear of catastrophic collapse; four nearby buildings stayed under evacuation orders and a fifth partly, with evacuated workers facing potentially weeks without office access
  • Officials said they were "confident" temporary shoring was stabilizing the building - emergency jacks followed by new steel supports, per Buildings Commissioner Ahmed Tigani - after a fire chief raised concern about a possible "localized collapse" while saying total collapse was impossible; the DOB declared the building structurally sound that day once each floor was shored
  • The two accounts differ on the tower's size and the scope of the conversion: CNN describes renovating the 33-story tower at 235 East 42nd while adding 19 floors to the 10-story building at 219 East 42nd, with Gensler on the project and completion expected next year, while The Real Deal calls 235 East 42nd a 37-story tower and describes the work as expanding 10 stories above the collapsed columns and adding four floors to the original 33-story tower
  • Engineers interviewed by Gothamist said the columns did not appear to have the reinforcing plates called for in the plans: GACE Consulting Engineers had specified added steel plates along the length of the two columns to support the 15 residential floors above, turning the I-shaped columns into solid steel boxes
  • GACE Principal Engineer Chris Behan: "The reinforcement from the 19th floor to the top of the 21st floor, which would have significantly increased the columns' strength, was never installed... The structure was not reinforced as GACE's design required", with Chris Cerino of SEAoNY saying "It looked to me that it wasn't there" and Joe DiPompeo saying photos clearly do not show the boxed reinforcement in the drawings
  • The Department of Buildings had not determined a cause and declined to say whether the steel was installed, and it is unclear why the work was not done or why inspectors did not catch it
  • Developer Nathan Berman of MetroLoft called it "a typical construction mishap", blamed added weight and said "I don't know that a four-inch sag is a collapse", while also telling The Real Deal on the day that it was possible the columns weren't properly reinforced; the site had prior complaints and a 2025 worker-injury lawsuit, which was denied
  • The incident widened: the city sent building safety inspectors across five boroughs to review construction sites and New York City investigators opened a preliminary criminal inquiry of unclear scope and target
  • MetroLoft's project is described as the city's largest office-to-home conversion
  • The B1M's film "New York's Buckling Tower: What Happens Now?", published 2026-08-26, sets the incident against New York's office-to-residential conversions and One Wall Street, but its page gives no date, cause, casualty or damage figures of its own
address: 235 East 42nd Street, Manhattan, New York, USA
dateConfidenceReasoning: Happened as dated, per the source: workers "discovered structural steel columns buckling" on the morning of July 7, 2026.

title: Nvidia Vera Rubin Systems Begin Shipping
description: Nvidia said its Vera Rubin NVL72 rack systems are now shipping to cloud providers and system makers, with 288 GB of HBM4 per GPU and about five times Blackwell's inference performance.
longFormSummary:
• On July 21 NVIDIA confirmed the Vera Rubin platform had reached full production, with Ian Buck, vice president of accelerated computing, telling reporters at NVIDIA headquarters that systems are now shipping to customers including OpenAI, CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Meta and Dell
  • NVIDIA had said at GTC Taipei on May 31 that the platform was ramping into full production, with Taiwan's top server makers manufacturing Vera Rubin-based systems at scale
  • The sources disagree on when shipments were due: the May 31 newsroom announcement, as cites it, said "production shipments of Vera Rubin are set to begin starting this fall", while the July 21 briefing has systems already shipping; the newer account is the shipping one
  • They also disagree on the platform's production status at launch - the CES press release of January 5, 2026 already said "NVIDIA Rubin is in full production, and Rubin-based products will be available from partners the second half of 2026", while ServeTheHome's report of the same event called it "an 'everything remains on schedule' announcement" and noted "the hardware is not shipping yet, and the ramp-up for production wo not even start until the second half of the year"
  • The flagship Vera Rubin NVL72 rack integrates 72 Rubin GPUs and 36 Vera CPUs connected by NVLink 6, with ConnectX-9 SuperNICs and BlueField-4 DPUs
  • Each Rubin GPU carries 288 GB of HBM4 memory with up to 22 TB/s of bandwidth, against the Blackwell Ultra B300's 8 TB/s; ServeTheHome puts the same 288GB and 22 TB/second at 2.8x Blackwell's HBM3e bandwidth, on a dual-die 336-billion-transistor part built on TSMC 3nm
  • NVIDIA claims Rubin reaches 5x Blackwell's inference performance and 3.5x its training performance, with 50 PFLOPS of NVFP4 inference and 35 PFLOPS of NVFP4 training per GPU
  • The platform is pitched at up to a 10x reduction in inference token cost versus Blackwell; the NVL72 rack is quoted at up to 10x higher inference throughput per watt at one-tenth the cost per token
  • A full NVL72 rack is rated at 3.6 EFLOPS of inference and 2.5 EFLOPS of training compute, 220 trillion transistors, 54TB of LPDDR5X and 20.7TB of HBM4, with 3.6TB/s of NVLink bandwidth per GPU and 260TB/s across the rack
  • The rack is 100 percent liquid cooled with a cable-free modular tray design; the sources give the assembly saving three ways - installation cut "from two hours to five minutes", rack assembly "from 100 minutes on Blackwell to just 6 minutes on Rubin", and "up to 18x faster assembly and servicing than Blackwell"
  • The number of chips in the platform is also stated inconsistently: both CES sources describe six new chips - Vera CPU, Rubin GPU, NVLink 6 Switch, ConnectX-9 SuperNIC, BlueField-4 DPU and Spectrum-6 Ethernet Switch - while says that on March 16, 2026 at GTC in San Jose NVIDIA announced the platform had expanded to seven chips in full production with the NVIDIA Groq 3 LPU, and elsewhere in the same article still calls it six
  • Rubin-based products are to be available from partners in the second half of 2026, with AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft and OCI among the first public clouds, alongside NVIDIA Cloud Partners CoreWeave, Lambda, Nebius and Nscale
  • Microsoft will deploy Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale systems in next-generation AI data centres including future Fairwater AI superfactory sites, which "will scale to hundreds of thousands of NVIDIA Vera Rubin Superchips"
  • CoreWeave, among the first cloud providers to receive the hardware, told Bloomberg its NVL72 racks are delivering ten times the token output of the previous generation
  • Dell Technologies, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro, with ASUS, Foxconn, GIGABYTE, Pegatron, Quanta Cloud Technology, Wistron and Wiwynn, are adopting NVIDIA DSX to accelerate the Vera Rubin ramp
  • NVIDIA ran an aggressive 18-month development cycle from Blackwell's launch to Rubin production, against the 24 to 30 months such a step typically takes
  • The CES release carries a forward-looking-statements notice and warns that "Many of the products and features described herein remain in various stages and will be offered on a when-and-if-available basis"
dateConfidenceReasoning: Nvidia confirmed on July 21, 2026 that 'systems are now shipping to customers'.
