title: 262 Fifth Avenue Rises Over the Empire State Building's Sightlines
description: Five Points Development's slender 262 Fifth Avenue condo tower topped out in Manhattan's NoMad district in 2024 and is on track to open in 2026, drawing criticism for blocking classic views of the nearby Empire State Building.
longFormSummary:
• 262 Fifth Avenue is a residential pencil tower in Manhattan developed by Boris Kuzinez's Five Points Development, designed by Moscow-based Meganom with SLCE Architects as architect of record, standing 860 feet (260 m) with 26 apartments
  • The two sources disagree on the floor count - Wikipedia says 54 stories, ArchDaily 52 - while agreeing on the height and unit count; the residential area is given as 139,168 sq ft by one and about 140,000 sq ft by the other, with apartments averaging around 3,200 sq ft
  • It topped out in April 2024, and in December 2024 the New York Attorney General's office allowed unit sales to begin, with five apartments marketed; as of December 24, 2025 Meganom was "nearing completion"
  • The design shrank repeatedly over a decade: a September 2016 filing had 54 stories at 928 feet, DOB-approved plans the next month reached 1,009 feet with up to 41 apartments, the height was cut from 1,043 to 860 feet between August and December 2022, and the apartment count fell from 41 to 26 in mid-2023
  • Kuzinez assembled the site by buying 260, 262 and 264 Fifth Avenue in 2015-2016 for $101.8 million plus $5.8 million in air rights; demolition finished by September 2017, work appeared stalled in 2019, 260 Fifth was sold to Amir Loloi for $52.5 million in mid-2021, excavation followed by November 2021 and foundations in 2022, with Madison Realty Capital and Cottonwood Group lending a combined $180 million in November 2023
  • Its slenderness - a height-to-width ratio of about 19:1 on slabs mostly 45 by 45 feet - is achieved with a reinforced concrete core plus two parallel walls along Fifth Avenue, the core pushed outward for clear-span apartments, six mechanical floors acting as outriggers, a void working as a windbreak and a damper on the upper mechanical floor, all wind-tunnel tested including aeroelastic studies
  • Other engineering details: tapering high-strength concrete walls with 97 ksi rebar, foundations on Manhattan schist at 40-60 tons per square foot allowable bearing, and a curtain wall on the north and south faces with triple-glazed low-iron Low-E panels up to 20 feet high and 8.5 feet wide
  • The apartments are conceived as elevated "shelves" framing city views, inspired by aeronautics, with interiors by Norm Architects, at least one four-story unit, 10,850 sq ft of retail and a rooftop infinity pool
  • Systems include hydronic radiant heating, micro-climate HVAC delivering fresh air every hour - three times the NYC health-code requirement - with energy recovery, photovoltaic glass and Passive House principles
  • The tower has been criticised for blocking views of the Empire State Building from south of 28th Street, including most of Madison Square Park, for its pencil-thin look (Curbed's Christopher Bonanos) and for delivering few units relative to its height
  • The B1M's film of 27 August 2025, "262 Fifth Avenue: New York is About to Bury the Empire State Building", says the tower "is dividing Midtown" and runs chapters on its "biggest problem", "mutated architecture", "zombie urbanism" and the NYC housing crisis, but gives no height, cost or completion date

title: Finland's Onkalo Repository Set to Bury Nuclear Waste

title: Amazon Leo Consumer Satellite Internet Launch
description: Amazon says it has launched enough Leo satellites for initial service and will open its satellite broadband to consumers later in 2026, after an enterprise preview that began April 8.
longFormSummary:
• Amazon says it now has enough satellites in orbit to begin “initial service” of its Leo internet-from-space network later in 2026, though it has not launched the service for consumers and government customers yet
  • The milestone came with a United Launch Alliance Atlas V launch of 29 satellites at about 12:30 a.m. ET on Thursday 2 July 2026
  • The two reports of that launch give different constellation totals: CNBC says it brought Amazon to “more than 390 satellites”, while Light Reading says Amazon Leo announced it had deployed 396
  • Chris Weber, the executive leading Leo's consumer, enterprise and government businesses, said the constellation is “enough to support continuous service across initial latitudes” and that “we've completed enough launches for initial service this yr, and future missions just add coverage and capacity”, with “lots of work ahead - including raising all these new satellites to their assigned altitude”
  • The timing has slipped: Andy Jassy's annual shareholder letter targeted commercial availability in “mid-2026”, a target he repeated in May, and Amazon now says only “later this year”; Light Reading calls the exact timing “somewhat squishy”
  • Initial commercial service will likely be limited to users in certain geographies, and Amazon has announced neither pricing plans nor where the service will first be available
  • The links date the enterprise phase differently: CNBC says that “In November, Amazon began offering an 'enterprise preview' of Leo for select businesses”, while TNW says the service “entered enterprise beta on April 8, 2026” and separately that a business preview opened to select enterprise partners shortly after the November 2025 rebrand
  • The service was rebranded from Project Kuiper, announced in 2019, to Amazon Leo in November 2025
  • Amazon aims at a constellation of roughly 7,700 satellites — the FCC approved its Generation 2 constellation in February 2026, clearing a potential 7,727-satellite network on top of the 3,236-satellite Generation 1 licence
  • Deployment has run far behind the licence: Generation 1 required 1,618 satellites in orbit and operational by 30 July 2026, and Amazon had roughly 210 to 241 in orbit in early April 2026, having told the FCC it expected about 700 by that July
  • Amazon filed for an extension in January 2026 citing a “shortage in the near-term availability” of rockets, and the FCC granted a 24-month extension on the first half of the constellation while retaining the 100% deployment milestone of 30 July 2029
  • A further setback came in May, when a Blue Origin New Glenn exploded on the launchpad during a hot-fire test days before it was to carry a batch of Amazon satellites
  • The next Leo mission moves to ULA's Vulcan heavy-lift rocket, “which will carry even larger Leo payloads and help increase our deployment rate” — 40-plus satellites per launch — after Atlas V closed its Leo campaign having launched 224 satellites across eight missions with a 100% success rate
  • Three terminals are planned: Leo Nano at seven inches square and 2.2 pounds rated to 100 Mbps, Leo Pro at eleven inches square and 5.3 pounds priced under $400 and rated to 400 Mbps, and Leo Ultra, a 43-pound enterprise unit rated at 1 Gbps down and 400 Mbps up
  • Beta and contract customers include Verizon, AT&T, Vodafone, Vodacom, JetBlue, NBN Co, Vrio, NASA, Hunt Energy and Crane Worldwide Logistics, with Delta contracted for in-flight Wi-Fi across 500 aircraft from 2028
  • The Globalstar deal is reported two ways: the April report calls Amazon “reportedly in talks to acquire Globalstar for approximately $9 billion”, while the July report says “In April, Amazon cut a deal to acquire Globalstar for about $11.6 billion” — and a related headline on that same page says $11.5B — with the transaction expected to close in 2027 and Leo's direct-to-device system slated for 2028
  • Leo competes with SpaceX's Starlink, whose constellation is given as “more than 10,000” satellites in CNBC's key points, “around 10,000” in its body and “7,600 to 8,000-plus” by TNW, with more than 10 million subscribers and $10.6 billion of 2025 revenue
dateConfidenceReasoning: Amazon says consumer service comes 'later this year'; one report puts consumer beta in five countries in late 2026 or early 2027. The last day of 2026 is used.
delayReasoning: Stated: Andy Jassy's shareholder letter targeted a mid-2026 consumer launch; by July 2026 Amazon said 'later this year'.

title: Venezuela's Leader Is Decided at the End of 2026
description: On December 31, 2026 Polymarket settles who officially holds Venezuela's head of state office. Acting president Delcy Rodríguez was sworn in on January 5 after U.S. troops captured Nicolás Maduro, and both still claim it: the market's outcome row puts Maduro at 47% and shows no percentage at all beside Rodríguez, only a 48¢ Buy Yes price.
longFormSummary:
• Polymarket’s event “Venezuela leader end of 2026?”, filed under “Politics · Trump-Machado”, settles on whoever “officially holds the position of the head of state of Venezuela on Dec 31, 2026 at 12 PM ET”, and is marked mutually exclusive
  • The market opened on Jan 4, 2026 at 1:09 PM ET and carries an End Date of Dec 31, 2026, though a chart label reads Dec 30, 2026 and the FAQ says it “is scheduled to resolve on or around Dec 30, 2026”
  • Total volume is $97,046,435, which the FAQ rounds to “$97 million in total trading volume since the market launched on Jan 4, 2026”; there are 419 comments
  • The page prices Maduro and Rodríguez as near neighbours but does not agree with itself on the numbers: the headline list gives Nicolás Maduro 50.1% and Delcy Rodríguez 47%, while the outcome row gives Maduro 47% against a Buy Yes price of 52.9¢ and shows no percentage for Rodríguez at all beside her Buy Yes price of 48¢ – a price in cents, not a chance
  • Everyone else is priced out: “No Head of State” at about 1% and María Corina Machado at under 1% (0.2¢), with Edmundo González at 0.2¢ and Diosdado Cabello Rondón at 0.1¢, even though several long-shot names carry far larger volumes than the two front-runners – Richard Grenell $32,790,723 and Frank Donovan $25,841,140 against Maduro’s $3,114,172 and Rodríguez’s $2,031,565
  • The resolution rules turn on formality, not control: “officially holds” means formally appointed, confirmed if required, and sworn in, or otherwise confirmed by official government information, with official information from the UN recognized government of Venezuela as the primary source; if Venezuela does not state clearly who is head of state, the market falls back to the UN’s protocol list, and where more than one is listed, to the one with primary status or else whoever first assumed the position
  • That distinction is the whole contest here, because Rodríguez and Maduro both claim the office – Rodríguez called Maduro Venezuela’s “only president” on Venezolana de Televisión, and “both he and Rodríguez claim that he remains the legal officeholder”, while Trump announced she had been “sworn in”
  • Polymarket lists a separate market, “Will Delcy Rodríguez be the de facto leader of Venezuela at the end of 2026?”, at 95% – far above her roughly 47% on the official-holder question, the gap between de facto power and formal title
  • How she got there: on 3 January 2026 at about 2:00 AM VET the United States struck targets in Venezuela including Caracas, detained Maduro and flew him to New York City; the Constitutional Chamber of the Supreme Tribunal of Justice ordered her that day to “assume and exercise, as interim president, all the powers, duties, and faculties inherent to the office” to guarantee administrative continuity, without initially setting a fixed term
  • She was sworn in on 5 January 2026 by her brother Jorge Rodríguez, president of the National Assembly, becoming “the first woman in Venezuelan history to perform the duties of the presidency”; CBS News dates the swearing-in to “early Monday”, two days after Maduro’s capture and while he awaited arraignment in a US federal court on drug smuggling charges
  • The Wikipedia infobox dates her interim presidency from 5 January 2026 while the Supreme Tribunal ordered her to assume it on 3 January, a two-day gap the article notes as “Designated by the Supreme Tribunal of Justice to ensure administrative continuity on 3 January, formally sworn in two days later”
  • Recognition has moved in her favour over the year: the European Union said on 5 January 2026 that it does not recognize her legitimacy, and Marco Rubio said on ABC the administration did not consider her or her cohorts to have a legitimate claim to power – “legitimacy for their system of government will come about through a period of transition and real elections” – but the United States formally recognized her authority on 12 March 2026
  • The newer Wikipedia account adds what the January reporting could not: the release of political prisoners on 8 January, the Amnesty Law for Democratic Coexistence signed 30 January 2026, the 29 January 2026 reform ending PDVSA’s monopoly, $300 million received on 20 January 2026 under a $500 million oil export agreement with the United States, and state visits to Grenada, Barbados, The Hague, India and Suriname through 10 September 2026
  • Her position was built on the vice presidency she held from 14 June 2018, and CBS notes she has not been indicted in the US although she was sanctioned during Trump’s first term for helping Maduro “maintain power and solidify his authoritarian rule”; in February 2026 EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said she would propose lifting the EU sanctions on her
  • Polymarket’s own context note, stamped Sep 20, 2026, 2:45 PM UTC and labelled an “Experimental AI-generated summary”, reads the narrow spread as trader assessment of consolidation risks for the interim government, opposition leverage in US-backed transition talks involving her brother Jorge, and uncertainty over whether elections or other institutional shifts happen before year-end, with the timing and format of any presidential vote still unresolved
  • Wikipedia’s presidents navbox records the same unsettled position in its final entry: “Maduro (de jure), Rodríguez (de facto)”

title: Delhi Metro's Golden Line Opens Its First Section, Tughlakabad to Sangam Vihar
description: The first 8.4 km section of the Phase 4 Golden Line, from Tughlakabad to Sangam Vihar, is targeted to open in December 2026; the rest of the 29.785 km Delhi Aerocity-Tughlakabad corridor, 19 stations with 12 of them underground, follows in phases. By April 2026 civil work was 78 per cent done with five tunnel boring machines still at work, and trainsets had begun arriving at the modified Sarita Vihar depot.
longFormSummary:
• The Golden Line is a Delhi Metro Phase 4 line under construction in South Delhi, running from Delhi Aerocity to Tughlakabad to connect southern Delhi directly with Indira Gandhi International Airport and relieve road congestion and pollution
  • The sources give different lengths for the same corridor: Wikipedia puts the main line (Line 10) at 29.785 km with 19 stations, 7 elevated and 12 underground, while Construction World calls it "the 23.6-km Aerocity-Tughlaqabad corridor" - the figure the line carried when Delhi finalised the plan in December 2018, before the Terminal 1 extension took it to 25.82 km
  • They also differ on what opens at the end of 2026: Wikipedia gives a planned opening of December 2026 for the main line and says the whole Aerocity-Tughlakabad route "will be complete by the end of 2026", while the newer Construction World item of 16 Sep 2026 says DMRC is targeting December 2026 only for an 8.4-km first operational section between Tughlaqabad and Sangam Vihar, with the rest to follow in phases
  • As of April 2026 the main route was 73.33% complete overall and 78% complete on civil works, with five tunnel boring machines at work
  • Trainsets began arriving from April 2026 at the Sarita Vihar Depot, which serves the Violet Line and is being modified to handle Golden Line trains; the rolling stock is Alstom Metropolis in 3- and 6-coach formations, standard gauge on 25 kV 50 Hz AC, with a maximum speed of 100 km/h
  • The line was conceptualised as the Silver Line under Phase IV in July 2016 at 20.2 km, extended to 23.6 km in December 2018, approved by the Government of India in March 2019 and renamed Golden in January 2024
  • Construction was meant to start in 2021 but was delayed by COVID-19 restrictions; Afcons Infrastructure and Larsen & Toubro began work in June 2022 against an expected 2024/25 completion that "was eventually pushed to the end of 2026"
  • In November 2020 DMRC changed the alignment on ASI instructions to circumvent the Qutb Minar and the Mehrauli Archaeological Park
  • Two extensions approved under Phase 5A remain further out: Aerocity to Terminal 1 IGI Airport, with the DPR approved as of August 2025 and construction expected to finish in 2027-28, and Tughlakabad to Kalindi Kunj, expected by 2028
  • A branch (Line 11) of 8.385 km and eight elevated stations from Lajpat Nagar to Saket G Block is approved but has no opening date
  • Interchanges along the main line include the Airport Express at Delhi Aerocity, the Yellow Line at Chhatarpur, the Violet Line at Tughlakabad Station and, on the approved extensions, the Magenta Line at Terminal 1 IGI Airport and Kalindi Kunj
dateConfidenceReasoning: Construction World, 16 September 2026, narrows the year to a month: DMRC is "targeting December 2026 for the opening of the first operational section of the Golden Line between Tughlaqabad and Sangam Vihar. The 8.4-km stretch is planned as the initial section". title: Earls Court Redevelopment Starts on Site
description: The 44-acre former exhibition site won consent from Hammersmith & Fulham on 26 November 2025 and Kensington & Chelsea on 16 December 2025, a decade after the exhibition halls came down. Phase one of the GBP 10bn masterplan covers the first 1,300 homes, offices, a cultural venue and a 4.5-acre park, with the whole site due to be finished by 2043.
longFormSummary:
• Both boroughs have now backed the £10bn Earls Court masterplan: Hammersmith & Fulham's Planning Committee approved it unanimously on 26 November and Kensington & Chelsea's passed a resolution to grant planning permission on 16 December
  • ECDC had submitted hybrid planning applications to each borough in 2024, seeking outline permission for the illustrative masterplan and detailed permission for six buildings forming the first phase
  • "With detailed permission secured for the first phase, early construction work is expected to begin in 2026", with the immediate focus on public-private collaboration to bring forward the first 1,300 homes within Phase One
  • The site is 44 acres, described as Central London's largest cleared development site; Earls Court Partnership Limited acquired it in December 2019 and in 2022 secured control of the adjoining TfL Lillie Bridge Depot and associated land
  • The developer is the Earls Court Development Company, founded by Delancey and APG, acting for a joint venture of Delancey, Dutch pension fund manager APG and Places for London, Transport for London's property company
  • The full masterplan is about 4,000 homes including affordable housing and a new tenure aimed at supporting the "squeezed middle", 2.5 million sq ft of workspace focused on climate innovation delivering around 12,000 on-site jobs, and three new world-class cultural venues plus fixed and pop-up venues, retail, dining and leisure
  • Public realm runs to 20 acres of open and green space - larger than the single park the pin describes - designed by SLA and Studio Egret West with over 1,000 new trees and an 85% uplift in biodiversity, alongside a zero-carbon energy network and a zero operational carbon target given as "from day one" in one place and "from first occupation" in another
  • Wider economic claims are 23,500 jobs across the UK and £3bn a year injected into the economy, described by APG's Rafael Torres-Villalba as "annually £3billion of GVA to the UK economy"
  • Hawkins\Brown and Studio Egret West are masterplan architects, with Sheppard Robson, Serie, Maccreanor Lavington and dRMM on the buildings submitted in detail and EPR, ACME and Haworth Tompkins on those in outline; new residential crescents cluster taller buildings near the Empress State Building, the tallest of them a 42-storey Sheppard Robson design
  • The site has three Tube stations on its doorstep plus London Overground and several bus routes, and the plan adds new east-west and north-south routes for pedestrians and cyclists; ZCD Architects helped set up a Public Realm Inclusivity Panel and the masterplan was shaped by over four years of engagement and co-design
  • ECDC chief executive Rob Heasman said the plans "will restore Earls Court as a global destination, a place for ingenuity, and for the extraordinary" and that focus "will now turn firmly to delivery"
  • The release does not give a completion date for the whole site
address: Earls Court, Kensington and Chelsea, London, England
dateConfidenceReasoning: The developer's announcement says only that "early construction work is expected to begin in 2026", a year rather than a date.

title: Johor Bahru-Singapore RTS Link Set to Open
description: A new four-kilometre rail crossing over the Strait of Johor aims to cut the commute between Johor Bahru and Singapore from up to four hours to about six minutes.
longFormSummary:
• The RTS Link is a four-kilometre cross-border shuttle between Bukit Chagar in Johor Bahru and Woodlands North in Singapore, running on a viaduct 25 metres above the Tebrau Straits
  • The opening date is stated differently by the two governments: Malaysia's Transport Minister Anthony Loke has consistently given January 2027 - "fully operational on January 1, 2027" in January 2024 and still "on track for opening in January 2027" in April 2026 - while Singapore's Ministry of Transport says service is "targeted to commence passenger service by December 2026"; the Singapore statement is the newer and more official of the two on that point, and the pin follows the January 2027 date
  • Journey time is given as about five minutes by Singapore's MOT, shorter than the pin's six
  • Capacity is up to 10,000 passengers per hour per direction, with eight four-car trains from CRRC Zhuzhou Locomotive Co. at the start of service, each carrying more than 600 passengers, running at a maximum 80 km/h
  • Route length is described two ways: a four-kilometre link in the Malaysian reporting, and about 5.3 km of track from Wadi Hana Depot to Bukit Chagar and on to Woodlands North in the Singapore release
  • Both stations have co-located Customs, Immigration and Quarantine facilities, so passengers clear immigration only once, at the departure point
  • Construction ran well ahead of the first train: at the January 2024 span completion ceremony officiated by Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and Lee Hsien Loong, the marine viaduct was 68% complete, the terrestrial viaduct 31%, stations 41% and the CIQ complex 3.22%
  • By the Singapore unveiling of the first train at the Singapore Rail Test Centre by Jeffrey Siow and Anthony Loke, rail system works were about 56% complete, with offsite systems integration testing by RTS Operations Pte Ltd - a Prasarana RTS Operations and SMRT RTS joint venture - due to finish in the fourth quarter before onsite testing with the other seven trains
  • By April 2026 physical construction was "nearly completed", e-gates at the Bukit Chagar CIQ building were installed with body and baggage scanners next, and the project was moving into final field readiness: system installation, acceptance testing, integration and dynamic testing
  • Costs have held: Loke said "I am confident that costs remain within original estimates" and that no contractor had requested a cost revision, despite the global energy crisis
  • Fares had not been set as of April 2026 - RTSO was to present proposed rates to both governments in the third quarter for agreement by Malaysia's Land Public Transport Agency and Singapore's LTA, after Loke suggested in February that fares could be around $5 to $7 per trip; a season pass for frequent travellers was left as a commercial question for RTSO
  • The link is expected to take about 35 per cent of the 350,000 people who cross the Johor Causeway daily and to support the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone
  • The B1M's video on the project, published 2024-05-01, calls it "This Will Fix Asia's Greatest Traffic Jam" and "the world's most important rail link", but the capture is metadata only and carries no figures of its own
dateConfidenceReasoning: The day is an announced one, not a year-end placeholder: Putrajaya has held to a 1 January 2027 start since Transport Minister Anthony Loke said it was "confident RTS Link will start on January 1, 2027", and English Wikipedia still carries "Planned opening: 1 January 2027". The latest check-in keeps it there - AsiaOne, 4 April 2026: the RTS Link "is on track for opening in January 2027 despite the ongoing global energy crisis" - after an earlier Singapore target of passenger service by December 2026.

title: Stad Ship Tunnel Construction Pushed to Early 2027

longFormSummary:

title: Austin Light Rail Breaks Ground on Its First Line

longFormSummary:
• Austin Transit Partnership "has selected Austin Rail Constructors (ARC) as the construction contractor for Austin Light Rail, marking another major step toward beginning construction in 2027", announced on Feb. 18, 2026
  • "The ATP Board's approval of ARC at the Feb. 18 meeting enables ATP to begin pre-construction activities and advance final design for Austin Light Rail under the first phase of what will be a multibillion-dollar contract" - the release gives no dollar figure, so the pin's "above $8.2 billion" is not from this wiki
  • ARC is "a joint venture between nationally and locally recognized firms Stacy Witbeck and Sundt Construction" and "will help shape and build the design and construction of nearly every aspect of the system, including the transitway, tracks, systems, stations, bridges, traffic signals, utilities, drainage structures and streetscape improvements"
  • "Austin's first light rail system will feature 15 stations along a nearly 10-mile alignment and consist of all-electric trains running every 5-10 minutes throughout most of the day. Austin Light Rail is designed to be fully expandable for future extensions" - the release does not describe the pin's three-way alignment out of downtown or a new bridge across Lady Bird Lake, and gives no opening year
  • ARC was "identified as the highest-ranked firm following a rigorous, competitive procurement process that evaluated elements including firms' experience, personnel qualifications, technical approach and design innovation", with team experience at "McKalla Station, Austin-Bergstrom International Airport and national rail projects in Arizona, Hawaii and Utah" and several Texas-based contractors among its subcontractors
  • "ATP completed the procurement in approximately one year, faster than many comparable mega projects nationwide", after a Request for Information process and "Connect & Build" industry networking events for small and local businesses
  • "The design-build model ATP has chosen to employ brings the final construction partner on board sooner in the project with the goal of earlier alignment, preventing costly change orders and future construction delays", and ARC will competitively bid portions of the work as design advances
  • ATP CEO Greg Canally: "This is a big, important milestone for Austin Light Rail... with this contract now in place, we are on track to begin construction in 2027", while Mayor Kirk Watson called the selection "a major step forward in delivering the voter-mandated transit system"

title: Mexico's AIFA-Pachuca Passenger Train Starts Running
description: The third stage of the Mexico-Pachuca "Felipe Angeles" train runs 65 km of electrified double track from the AIFA airport terminal in the State of Mexico to Pachuca in Hidalgo, with stations at AIFA, Xaltocan II, Tizayuca-Temascalapa, Jaguey de Tellez and Pachuca plus four intermediate stops, and is meant to carry over 100,000 passengers a day in 1 hour 15 minutes end to end. longFormSummary:
• The AIFA-Pachuca stage is the third of the Mexico-Pachuca "Felipe Angeles" passenger train, "spanning 65 km of electrified double-track, which will feature four stations and four train stops", connecting the Felipe Angeles International Airport in the State of Mexico with Pachuca in Hidalgo
  • The route is split 35 km in the State of Mexico and 30 km in Hidalgo, laid on existing right of way, and will link with the Buenavista-Lecheria-AIFA branch to connect Mexico City with both the airport and Pachuca
  • The page contradicts itself on the scheme's size: a video note from the 24 April 2026 construction supervision says "There will be six stations from AIFA to Pachuca, covering a 5 km stretch", against the four stations and four stops over 65 km given in the project description and the key characteristics
  • Estimated investment is 44 billion MXN, with required infrastructure of "2 viaducts (5.89 km), 4 electrical substations, 51.67 km of cut-and-fill works"
  • Rolling stock will be electric trains with a maximum design speed of 120 km/h and a capacity of 718 passengers per train; the April 2026 supervision note says "It will feature 15 electric trains; the first one will arrive in September", and a May 20 note repeats that the first AIFA-Pachuca train arrives "in September of this year"
  • Construction is led by the Secretaria de la Defensa Nacional through the Felipe Angeles Engineers Corps; preliminary works and studies began in October 2024 and construction officially commenced in March 2025, with an "execution period and start of operations: 2 years (2025-2027)"
  • Reported progress runs from right-of-way acquisition at 66% (Oct. 22, 2025) and five heavy-construction fronts generating more than 9,000 jobs (Dec. 4, 2025) through 21.15% complete (Feb. 19, 2026) and 30% with 10,000 jobs (Apr. 24, 2026) to 37.06% (Jun. 25, 2026)
  • On 25 June 2026 President Claudia Sheinbaum said "We are well ahead of schedule; the goal is to inaugurate the Mexico City-Pachuca and Mexico City-Queretaro routes in 2027"
  • A press release of 24 April 2026 is headed "'Felipe Angeles' Train, on its AIFA-Pachuca Stretch, to Transport 107,000 Daily Passengers"
  • The preceding stage is already running: the Buenavista-AIFA section opened on 26 April 2026, covering 41 km in "less than 60 minutes" through six stations and the AIFA-Clara Krause terminal, with 100-metre coupled trains carrying 719 passengers each (over 1,400 coupled), a 120 km/h maximum and a 15-minute frequency
  • Its ridership is given several ways on the same page: "Over 206,000 Passengers During Its First Week of Operation" (May 4), "over one million passengers" (Jun. 15) and "over two million passengers" from 26 April to 30 June 2026, while a video caption says the Lecheria-AIFA train "transports 30,000 passengers daily" against a press release headed "Buenavista-AIFA Train to Transport 57,000 Daily Passengers"; a caption also puts the Mexico City-AIFA trip at "50 minutes" where the text says under 60
  • The first stage was the acquisition of the Suburbano Train from Buenavista to Cuautitlan, announced in April 2026 as a purchase of "100% of the equity stake" to be operated publicly through Fonadin via a new State-Owned Majority-Interest Company; that line opened in 2008 and recorded 45.1 million users in 2025, though the page describes it both as "27 km across seven stations" and as "25.5 km ... five stations ... and two terminals"
  • The wider programme sits inside "Plan Mexico", with a Fonadin assignment title modified on 16 July 2026 "for the construction, operation, and provision of suburban and interurban passenger services on the Buenavista-Pachuca rail route", and Sheinbaum pledging at least 2,377 km of public railways
  • Related work includes relocation compensation - Sedatu, SICT and Conavi delivering 28 homes to families living near the AIFA-Pachuca project (Aug. 17, 2026) - and more than 28 million square metres cleared for railway right-of-way
  • The page warns that "This information is preliminary and subject to review and continuous updates as the project progresses" and gives its last revision only as September 2026

title: Bitcoin's End-of-2026 Price Settles at Midnight
description: Kalshi’s largest crypto event settles on Bitcoin’s price at 12:00 a.m. ET on January 1, 2027, splitting the outcome into $5,000 buckets. With BTC near $80,800, the market’s favourites are $75,000–$80,000 at 14.9% and $80,000–$85,000 at 13.9% — a year that ends roughly where it stands.
longFormSummary:
• Kalshi's KXBTCY-27JAN0100 event, "Bitcoin price at the end of 2026", settles on the price at midnight: each bracket "Resolves Yes if the simple average of the sixty seconds of CF Benchmarks' BRTI before 12 AM EST is between [the bracket] at 12 AM EST on Jan 1, 2027"
  • The event splits the outcome into $5,000 brackets and is flagged "mutually exclusive", with $36,767,311 of volume - and no fees - at capture
  • The brackets shown were 70,000-74,999.99 at 11.8% (12.1c yes / 88.1c no, down 1.2), 75,000-79,999.99 at 14.8% (15.2c / 85.2c, up 0.9) and 80,000-84,999.99 at 14.1% (14.2c / 85.9c, up 2.4)
  • The page shows the favourite two ways - 14.8% in the market row against "Odds 15% chance" on the order ticket for the same 15.2c contract - and the ticket's "Max payout Dec 31, 2026" disagrees with the market's own close and payout dates of Jan 1, 2027 at 12:00am and 12:06am EST
  • Settlement is explicitly not a spot quote: "While checking a source like Google or Coinbase may help guide your decision, the price used to determine this market is based on CF Benchmarks' corresponding Real Time Index (RTI). At the last minute before expiration, 60 RTI prices are collected. The official and final value is the average of these prices"
  • The market opened on Feb 25, 2026 at 6:25pm EST; its chart gridlines run 60K to 90K across April to September
  • A companion Kalshi market, "How high will Bitcoin get this year?", prices the year's high rather than its close, and puts a 2026 peak above $99,999.99 at 28% (28c), above $109,999.99 at 14% and above $119,999.99 at 8%, on $4,724,025 of volume - it too shows a different figure on the ticket, "Odds 29% chance" against 28% in the list
  • That market uses a different method from the year-end one: a trimmed mean of every minute's BRTI value from issuance to the target, "removing the top 20% and bottom 20% of values, then averaging the remaining 60%", resolving immediately if the threshold is crossed and resolving No if no data is available at expiration
  • Bitcoin's level at the time of these captures is given as $80,741.20 by a related Kalshi market target and as $80,900 by the podcast published September 18, 2026
  • That episode argues the price sits at a decision point: "Bitcoin is at $80,900 and the 50-week moving average, the line that has confirmed every bull market, sits at $78.7K, so this week's close on Sunday decides it rather than today's candle"
  • Its comparison is to early 2023: "$80K right now looks eerily like $25K in February 2023, the same rejection off the 50-week with the 200-day sitting 12% lower at $70K the way it sat at $20K back then", with the warning that "the 2023 breakout week came with one last liquidation down to the 200-day before the real move, which is why I'm 85% spot Bitcoin with no leverage until the weekly closes"
  • The same notes record US policy moves alongside the price: "The Clarity Act is not dead at 17% odds through the Senate, up from 7% two days ago", the SEC innovation exemption going live that Thursday to let onchain venues trade tokenized US stocks with dividend and voting rights, and the CFTC sending its own crypto rulebook to the White House
dateConfidenceReasoning: Kalshi settles the event on Bitcoin’s price at 12:00 a.m. EST on January 1, 2027 (05:00 UTC), which is a fixed settlement instant rather than an estimate.

title: The New House of Representatives Elects Its Speaker
description: The Congress elected in the 2026 midterms first meets on January 3, 2027, and the House can do no other business until it has a Speaker. Kalshi's market on the next new Speaker has Hakeem Jeffries at 86% — the table's chance, against “88% chance” on the order ticket beside it — with Jim Jordan at 10% and Steve Scalise at 2.6%.
longFormSummary:
• Kalshi runs a market asking "Who will be the next new Speaker of the House?" (series KXNEXTSPEAKER, event KXNEXTSPEAKER-31), which resolves on whoever becomes "the first Speaker of the House after Mike Johnson, before Jan 1, 2031"
  • At capture the market put Hakeem Jeffries at 86% (87c yes / 15c no), Jim Jordan at 10% (15c / 90c) and Steve Scalise at 2.6% (6.5c / 97.7c), on $34,482 of volume, with the event flagged "mutually exclusive"
  • The same page contradicts itself on the leading price: the table shows Jeffries at 86% while the order ticket beside it reads "Odds 88% chance" for the same contract at the same 87c yes / 15c no
  • The page's own title and its rules also disagree on the horizon - the title reads "Odds & Predictions 2030" while the rules and close date both say before Jan 1, 2031, with the market closing "After the outcome occurs" or otherwise by Jan 1, 2031 at 10:00am EST, and a projected payout 30 minutes after closing
  • The market opened on Feb 26, 2025 at 10:00am EST and outcomes are "verified from The New York Times, the Associated Press, Reuters and 11 others"
  • Kalshi bars a long list of insiders from trading it, including the listed candidates and their immediate families, campaign staff and vendors, party committee and PAC employees, federal lobbyists, holders of federal and statewide office, all staff of the House, Senate, Executive Office of the President and Supreme Court, election administrators and vote-tallying staff, major pollsters' employees, and decision-desk and exit-polling staff at major media organisations
  • Polymarket's companion market on which party wins the House in 2026 had the Democratic Party at 93% (93c) and the Republican Party at 8% (8c) on $11,888,579 of total volume since the market launched on Jul 11, 2025
  • That market's rules tie control directly to this event: control means a majority of voting seats, failing which it resolves to "the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated"
  • Polymarket's own dates for that market disagree with each other - the End Date field says Nov 3, 2026 while its FAQ says it "is scheduled to resolve on or around Nov 2, 2026"
  • Its experimental AI-generated market summary, updated Sep 20, 2026, attributes the pricing to Democrats holding "a consistent 7- to 12-point advantage on the generic congressional ballot", a presidential approval rating near 45 percent and the historical pattern of midterm losses for the president's party, with redistricting in Texas and Florida "narrowing the projected margin"
  • News shown beside the Kalshi market has Jeffries previewing a Democratic agenda from "Day One" to "hold the crooks accountable" (PBS, Sep 3) and topped by healthcare - undoing Medicaid cuts and reviving ACA funds (NBC News, Sep 2) - while Steve Scalise, one of the named Speaker candidates, "is staring at a scary political environment for Republicans" and claims a path to 225 seats (Axios, Sep 17)
  • Jeffries, then House Minority Leader, appeared on The Don Lemon Show in a 17-minute episode published September 2, 2026, "Leader Hakeem Jeffries Has An Urgent Midterm Warning", to discuss "Trump's midterm plans", a USPS whistleblower warning that the administration is ignoring court rulings, and "why he met with Jared Kushner"; the show notes give no further detail
  • None of the links states the date on which the new Congress first meets or the rule that the House can do no other business until a Speaker is chosen
dateConfidenceReasoning: The Twentieth Amendment fixes the new Congress’s first meeting at noon on January 3, and House rules make the Speaker election its first order of business. Kalshi does not date its market, which runs to 2031.

title: December Jobs Report Sets the Year-End US Unemployment Rate
description: The BLS Employment Situation report for December 2026, out at 8:30 a.m. ET on January 8, 2027, fixes the unemployment rate the year closes on. Kalshi has U-3 above 4.0% at 81% but only 5% above 5.0%, so traders expect a labour market that has loosened without cracking.
longFormSummary:
• Kalshi's KXU3EOY-27JAN08 event prices the US unemployment rate at year-end 2026, resolving on "the seasonally adjusted U.S. unemployment rate (U-3) for December 2026" as verified from the Bureau of Labor Statistics
  • The rules pin the reference month rather than the release: "'Year-end' refers exclusively to the December reference month, regardless of when the corresponding data are released. It does not refer to the annual average, the fourth-quarter average, the highest unemployment rate reported during the year, or the latest unemployment rate available as of December 31"
  • Settlement uses "the first non-preliminary seasonally adjusted U-3 unemployment rate reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics for December 2026", compared "as published without rounding", and "Later revisions will not affect the outcome"
  • The market is tied to the release date: it "will close and expire early if the economic data is released. Otherwise, it closes by Jan 8, 2027 at 8:29am EST", with a max payout date of Jan 8, 2027 - although the page header gives the start as "Jan 8, 7:30am EST", an hour earlier than its own close time
  • The strikes shown were Above 4.5% at 1% (20c yes / 99c no, down 28), Above 5.0% at 5% (41c / 95c, down 8) and Above 5.5% with no percentage quoted at 99c, with "12 more" strikes not displayed
  • Those quotes do not run in order - a higher threshold cannot be more likely than a lower one, yet Above 5.0% is quoted at 5% against Above 4.5% at 1% - and the trade panel shows "Odds 43% chance" for the Above 5.0% contract against the 5% in the list
  • The market's own forecast dial and chart sit around 4.2%-4.32% over Sep 6 to Sep 20, with 4.32% printed at the foot of the page, on just $6,734 of volume; it opened Sep 2, 2026 at 9:00pm EDT
  • The BLS release calendar for the Employment Situation lists every release at 08:30 AM, running from November 2025 data (Dec. 16, 2025) through November 2026 data (Dec. 4, 2026); it does not extend to the December 2026 reference month, so it neither confirms nor contradicts the January 8, 2027 date Kalshi settles on
  • BLS notes the calendar "is updated as needed with additional news releases, usually at least a week before their scheduled publication date", and the page itself carries no publication or last-updated date
  • Labour-market context from the year: the July 2026 report showed the economy losing 23,000 jobs, "the first negative print in years", while the unemployment rate fell from 4.2 to 4.1 percent
  • The explanation given is a divergence between the two surveys - the payroll loss from the establishment survey against a falling count of unemployed in the household survey - with the rate falling because people left the labour force rather than found work: "in June we saw 111,000 workers just leave the labor force"
  • Other figures cited alongside: job openings "down to 7.36 million in June from 7.54 million in May", average hourly earnings "still up around 3.5 percent year-over-year", initial jobless claims "hovering around 199,000, which is historically very low", and layoffs "at record lows", with health care and government still adding jobs while manufacturing and retail are flat or shrinking
  • The stated takeaway is that a falling rate is not the signal it looks like - "the unemployment rate falling to 4.1 percent isn't the good news it might seem. It's really a story about people leaving the labor force" - and that if participation recovers "the unemployment rate could actually tick up, even if the economy is adding jobs"
  • Kalshi's own headlines point the same way, with Indeed Hiring Lab reporting that "The US labor force has shrunk by around 700,000 workers so far in 2026" (Sep 10)

dateConfidenceReasoning: The BLS Employment Situation schedule puts the December 2026 report on January 8, 2027 at 8:30 a.m. ET, and Kalshi closes its year-end unemployment market at 13:29 UTC that morning.

title: Children of Blood and Bone Opens in Theaters January 15
description: Children of Blood and Bone is an upcoming American fantasy film directed by Gina Prince-Bythewood, who co-wrote the screenplay with Tomi Adeyemi, based on the 2018 novel by Adeyemi. The film stars Thuso Mbedu, Damson Idris, Amandla Stenberg, Tosin Cole, Cynthia Erivo, Lashana Lynch, Zackary Momoh, Richard Mofe-Damijo, Chiwetel Ejiofor, Regina King, Idris Elba, and Viola Davis.
longFormSummary:
• “Children of Blood and Bone is an upcoming American fantasy film directed by Gina Prince-Bythewood, who co-wrote the screenplay with Tomi Adeyemi, based on the 2018 novel by Adeyemi”, scheduled for release by Paramount Pictures in the United States on January 15, 2027, including engagements in IMAX
  • All four links agree on that date: Geek Vibes Nation lists it at No. 20 in its most-anticipated films of 2027 at January 15, The Bookshelf Chronicles gives the same theatrical date, and The Outtake Show’s trailer reaction says “Children of Blood and Bone hits cinemas 15 January 2027”
  • The runtime is 146 minutes, cited to the Irish Film Classification Office’s “Children of Blood and Bone (12A)” listing dated September 2, 2026; the infobox budget and gross fields are empty
  • The cast is led by Thuso Mbedu as Zelie, with Damson Idris as Prince Inan, Amandla Stenberg as Princess Amari, Tosin Cole as Tzain, Cynthia Erivo as Admiral Kaea, Lashana Lynch as Jumoke, Zackary Momoh as Adetayo, Chiwetel Ejiofor as King Saran, Regina King as Queen Nehanda, Idris Elba as Lekan and Viola Davis as Mama Agba, alongside Richard Mofe-Damijo, Saniyya Sidney, Diaana Babnicova as Folake, Bukky Bakray as Binta and Ayra Starr
  • The Wikipedia article is not internally consistent about that ensemble: its Cast section’s opening sentence lists a shorter roster that names Ayra Starr but omits Idris Elba, Viola Davis, Zackary Momoh and Richard Mofe-Damijo, all of whom appear in the infobox
  • The story follows Zélie in the fantasy kingdom of Orïsha, where magic has been violently stripped away, on a mission to restore what was lost and challenge the king responsible for suppressing it
  • The project took a decade and three studios to reach the screen: optioned before publication in March 2017 by Fox 2000 and Temple Hill, given Rick Famuyiwa as director in February 2019, moved to Lucasfilm after Disney’s acquisition of 21st Century Fox shuttered Fox 2000 – its first original live-action project since 2012 – then put in turnaround in the fourth quarter of 2021 after Lucasfilm declined Adeyemi’s request to write the script and let the rights lapse
  • Paramount acquired the rights by January 2022 “for a guaranteed exclusive theatrical release”, with Adeyemi writing and executive producing, and hired Prince-Bythewood to direct in December 2023; principal photography began in Lagos in February 2025 and concluded on June 2, 2025, with Polly Morgan shooting, Terilyn A. Shropshire editing and Terence Blanchard scoring
  • The film reunites the core team from The Woman King (2022) – Prince-Bythewood, Mbedu and Davis – and the podcast reads the unusually A-list roster as the opposite of the standard YA model of cheap unknown leads, arguing Paramount “clearly felt that the IP ... wasn’t strong enough on its own to open a $150 million movie globally”
  • That episode gives the budget two different ways, describing the film early on as “a massive $100 million blockbuster adaptation” and later as a “$150 million movie”; the Wikipedia infobox states no budget at all, so no figure is confirmed
  • The casting of Stenberg and Mbedu drew online backlash over colorism, as both are lighter-skinned than the characters in the novel; Stenberg posted an eight-minute TikTok in February 2025 saying Adeyemi wanted her in the role and that she would never go after a role she did not feel was right for her to chase
  • In July 2026 Adeyemi revealed she had distanced herself from the adaptation for unspecified reasons and blocked Stenberg on social media, said she would not watch the film though she did not mind others seeing it, and in a later video that month described leaving the set “hyperventilating and sobbing”, calling it “the worst thing I have ever had to live through”
  • Vanity Fair reported in August 2026 that the rift stemmed from her strained relationship with Stenberg, beginning with her disapproval of Stenberg’s TikTok response and culminating in tensions on set when Adeyemi arrived to film her cameo appearance, in sharp contrast to her earlier positive statements about the film
  • The podcast notes the oddity that she remains the credited co-writer of the screenplay while publicly refusing to watch the result, and explains that a writing credit carries no on-set power – the WGA arbitrates credits but “a credit does not equal on-set power”, and the director is the absolute authority once production begins
  • Working from a Deadline report dated July 29, 2026, the same episode says there are currently no plans to adapt the remaining two Legacy of Orisha books, even though the trilogy is complete with Children of Virtue and Vengeance (2019) and Children of Anguish and Anarchy (2024), and reads that as the studio deciding “that moving forward was actually a higher financial risk than just walking away”
  • The trailer landed in late July 2026 – The Outtake Show reacted to it on July 28, 2026 – giving roughly a six-month marketing window; the podcast weighs January as a traditional “dump month” against the case that a spectacle film faces almost no competition and can hold the IMAX screens, citing American Sniper and Black Panther, but concludes that with the sequel news “the picture becomes incredibly bleak for the future of the IP”
  • The January 15 slot is not entirely uncontested: Geek Vibes Nation flags that it “currently puts Children of Blood and Bone directly against The Beekeeper 2”, and warns generally that “Some of these dates will almost certainly shift before opening night”
  • Geek Vibes Nation positions the film “as a genuine theatrical fantasy event rather than a streaming-first YA adaptation” in a crowded 2027 that also brings Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew, The Legend of Zelda, Avengers: Secret Wars and The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum

title: Kindred Affordable Apartments Opens in Cortez Hill
description: An eight-storey, 138,000-square-foot building on the former County Family Court site in downtown San Diego, with 125 affordable apartments, a manager's unit and about 4,400 square feet of commercial space. BRIDGE Housing is developing it with the San Diego Housing Commission; VCC Construction finished the framing in July 2026.
longFormSummary:
• "Construction has reached a major milestone at Kindred Affordable Apartments in downtown San Diego, where VCC Construction has completed framing on the eight-story affordable housing development"; "The topping-out milestone marks the completion of the building's structural frame and moves the project closer to its planned opening in early 2027" - a window, not the pin's 1 February 2027 date
  • The 138,000-square-foot development in Cortez Hill "will transform the former site of the County of San Diego's Family Court into an affordable, intergenerational community for seniors and families with low incomes", in a transit-oriented area with access to public transportation, jobs, schools, parks and other community resources
  • It "will include 126 rental homes, community spaces, resident services offices, outdoor courtyards, parking and approximately 4,400 square feet of commercial space", of which "125 affordable apartments and one unrestricted manager's unit"
  • "The affordable homes will remain restricted for 99 years for households earning no more than 60% of San Diego's Area Median Income, currently $99,240 annually for a family of four"

  • SDHC awarded 84 housing vouchers - "63 vouchers are designated for seniors who have previously experienced homelessness, while 21 will assist eligible families with low incomes" - and provided "a loan of up to $7.955 million using federal, state and local resources", including HUD's HOME Investment Partnerships Program, California's Local Housing Trust Fund and the City of San Diego's Affordable Housing Fund
  • "The County of San Diego contributed $4 million from its Innovative Housing Trust Fund and provided the development site as part of its initiative to use excess county-owned land for affordable housing", and financing includes "more than $17.7 million in recycled tax-exempt Multifamily Housing Revenue Bonds from the state" under a bond recycling partnership with SDHC, the City and the California Housing Finance Agency

  • SDHC's Colin Miller: "Kindred Apartments will transform this site into a vibrant community that brings seniors and families together and provides housing stability in a shared place to call home"; Mayor Todd Gloria called it an example of "what can happen when public agencies and nonprofit partners work together to deliver much-needed housing"

title: Annular Solar Eclipse Crosses Chile
description: The Moon's shadow touches down at 15:59:35 UT on 2027-02-06, and the annular phase lasts up to 7 minutes 51 seconds along a path 281.5 km wide crossing Chile, Argentina and the Atlantic. A partial eclipse is visible from South America, Antarctica and western and southern Africa.
longFormSummary:
• An annular solar eclipse on 2027 Feb 06, with the Moon's antumbral shadow path plotted by Fred Espenak for NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center
  • Greatest eclipse falls at 15:59:35.7 UT at 31°18.2'S, 048°28.1'W, with the Sun 72.7° up, a path 281.5 km wide and a central-line duration of 07m50.9s
  • The saros catalogue lists the same eclipse as 2027 Feb 06 at 16:00:48 TD (a Terrestrial Dynamical Time value, against the path table's Universal Time), at 31.3°S 48.5°W, path width 282 km, central duration 07m51s
  • Greatest duration is longer than the duration at greatest eclipse: 07m53.5s at 15:41:48 UT at 35°04'S, 053°22'W, where the path is 279.7 km wide; the Google map page gives the same figure, "In this case, the Greatest Duration is 07m53.5s"
  • The path table runs at 120-second intervals over 113 timed rows from 14:08 UT to 17:52 UT, plus opening and closing limit rows, listing northern and southern limits and the central line in WGS 84 coordinates
  • The shadow track begins in the Pacific (14:08 UT row near 41°S, 122°W) and ends near the Gulf of Guinea (17:52 UT row near 05°N, 000°E), the annular phase being visible only between the northern and southern limits, longest on the central line
  • Maximum-eclipse times and positions are marked along the map path at 10-minute intervals; the point of greatest eclipse (GE) and the point of greatest duration (GD) are marked separately
  • The eclipse belongs to Saros series 131, sequence number 09567, relative number 13, with gamma -0.2952 and eclipse magnitude 0.9281
  • Saros 131 runs 1244.08 years from a partial eclipse on 1125 Aug 01 to a partial eclipse on 2369 Sep 02 and holds 70 solar eclipses (29 partial, 30 annular, 6 total, 5 hybrid); the series' longest annular eclipse was 2009 Jan 26 at 07m54s, just ahead of this one
  • Predictions use the VSOP87/ELP2000-85 solar and lunar ephemerides with ΔT = 71.6 seconds; the catalogue's own row for the eclipse carries ΔT = 76 s
  • The predictions "DO NOT include the effects of mountains and valleys along the edge of the Moon"; lunar-limb corrections may shift the path limits north or south by ~1-3 km and change durations by ~1-3 seconds, and may move the exact location of greatest duration by ~10-20 km
  • More detailed predictions including the lunar limb profile "are normally posted 12-18 months before each eclipse"
  • All eclipse calculations are by Fred Espenak, who "assumes full responsibility for their accuracy"; the path page ends with the date 2014 Feb 26, the Google map page 2014 Mar 14 and the saros catalogue 2009 Sep 26
address: Point of greatest eclipse at sea, off Chile
dateConfidenceReasoning: NASA's eclipse catalogue gives the instant of greatest eclipse as 15:59:35 UT on 2027-02-06 (16:00:47 TD, the two separated by delta-T), from Saros series 131. Eclipse circumstances are computed from orbital mechanics, so the date and time are exact centuries ahead.

references.title: Annular Solar Eclipse of 2027-02-06 - Google map of the path
references.reasoning: NASA's interactive map of this eclipse, showing the central path, the points of greatest eclipse and greatest duration, and local circumstances anywhere on the map.

references.title: Saros series 131
references.reasoning: The saros series this eclipse belongs to, listing every eclipse in the same 18-year family and where each one fell.

title: The 69th Grammy Awards Pick Album of the Year
description: The 69th Grammy Awards are on Sunday 7 February 2027 at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, the first Grammys on ABC since 1972. Kalshi's Album of the Year market leads with "you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love" at 37% and Rosalía's "Lux" at 25%.
longFormSummary:
• The 69th Annual Grammy Awards will be held on 7 February 2027, live from Crypto.com Arena in downtown Los Angeles - the 24th ceremony at that venue - with a host yet to be announced
  • It is the first Grammy ceremony broadcast on ABC since the 14th Annual Grammy Awards in 1972, and the first on Disney+ and Hulu, under a ten-year deal between the Recording Academy and the Walt Disney Company announced on 30 October 2024; the 68th ceremony was the last to air on CBS "after more than 50 years"
  • Nominations will be announced on 16 November 2026, with first-round nominations voting 12-22 October and final-round voting from 10 December 2026 to 7 January 2027
  • The two links differ on the eligibility window: Wikipedia says the ceremony honours work "from August 31, 2025, to August 28, 2026", while Variety says the period "runs Aug. 31, 2025 through Aug. 31, 2026"
  • Kalshi's Album of the Year market had Olivia Rodrigo's "you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love" at 37% (38c yes / 63c no), Rosalia's "Lux" at 25% (24c / 77c, down 28) and Olivia Dean's "The Art of Loving" at 11% (11c / 90c, down 19), with nine further albums not shown, on $44,022 of volume
  • That capture was of a logged-out page, so its order ticket reads "YES --", "NO --" and "Odds 0% chance" for the leading album, with a max payout date of Dec 31, 2027
  • On 16 June 2026 the Recording Academy announced category and eligibility changes for the 2027 ceremony
  • Wikipedia's body says there are "Four new categories" and names Best Asian Pop Music Performance, Best R&B Collaboration or Duo/Group Performance, Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance and Best Latin Song - but four of its own cited sources, from NARAS, Rolling Stone, Billboard and Gold Derby, all say five new categories
  • Other category changes: Best Folk Album is renamed Best Contemporary Folk Album, Best Traditional Folk Album returns "for the first time since 2011", and Best R&B Performance becomes Best R&B Solo Performance
  • Criteria changed too: artists may submit themselves four times for Best New Artist rather than three; the share of new recordings required for an album to be eligible drops "from 75% to 66%"; internet-only releases become eligible for Best Album Notes and Best Historical Album; and songwriters and composers of new material on winning genre albums "will now receive an award in parity with the recognition currently awarded to producers and engineers"
  • Voting changes: where all members previously voted in the six general field categories plus ten more across no more than three genre fields, "As of the 2027 ceremony, some members have the option to vote in fifteen categories across all genre fields instead based on their own professional credits", subject to meeting certain criteria
  • Grammys CEO Harvey Mason jr. called the move "a new home and a bold new chapter for the Grammy Awards", and Disney's Rita Ferro framed it as one of four January-February live events - the college football championship, the Grammys, the Super Bowl and the Oscars - "that would normally sit across four different companies ... all sitting here"
  • Variety notes there is "no official word on a producer yet but it is expected that Ben Winston will continue at the helm", its own hedge

title: REGN7508's Phase 3 Trial in Venous Thromboembolism Reads Out
description: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals's phase 3 trial of REGN7508 in venous thromboembolism reaches primary completion, the point at which the last participant's primary outcome is measured. The trial enrolled 2,000 participants. This study is researching an experimental drug called REGN7508 (called "study drug"). The study is focused on adults undergoing elective, unilateral (one side) total knee replacement surgery. The aim of the study is to see how effective the study drug is at preventing Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) and other related diseases after total knee replacement surgery. The study is looking at several other research questions, including: * What side effects may happen from taking the study drug * How much study drug is in the blood at different times * Whether the body makes antibodies against the study drug (which could make the study drug less effective or could lead to side effects)
longFormSummary:
• The read-out is the estimated primary completion of ROXI-APEX (NCT07015905), Regeneron's "Phase 3, Multicenter, Randomized, Open-Label, Study to Evaluate REGN7508, A Factor XI Monoclonal Antibody, Versus Apixaban and Enoxaparin for Prophylaxis of Venous Thromboembolism After Elective Total Knee Arthroplasty"
  • Primary completion is estimated for 2027-02-20 and overall completion for 2027-05-12; the trial started 2025-06-25 (actual) and was first posted 2025-06-11
  • Estimated enrolment is 2,000 adults undergoing elective, unilateral (one side) total knee replacement surgery; the record's status is RECRUITING as of the last update posted 2026-09-15
  • "The aim of the study is to see how effective the study drug is at preventing Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) and other related diseases after total knee replacement surgery"; REGN7508 is compared with apixaban and enoxaparin, with placebo also administered per the protocol
  • The single primary outcome measure is the incidence of the composite endpoint of asymptomatic or symptomatic VTE, including VTE-related death, through the day 12 visit (approximately 14 days)
  • Other research questions are what side effects may happen, how much study drug is in the blood at different times, and whether the body makes antibodies against the study drug
  • The trial runs at 47 sites in the United States, Bulgaria, Hungary, Japan, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland and Romania
dateConfidenceReasoning: ClinicalTrials.gov lists 2027-02-20 as the estimated primary completion date; a sponsor's estimate, and trials of this size routinely slip.

title: OpenAI Announces an IPO
description: Kalshi puts an official OpenAI IPO announcement at 5% before January 2027, 12% before February and 39% before March — a 27-point jump across February. The upper rungs do not run in order: the page shows 70% before April, then 49% before May and 61% before June.
longFormSummary:
• Kalshi runs a market asking "When will OpenAI officially announce an IPO?", listed under IPOS (Tech & Science) as series KXIPOOPENAI, event KXIPOOPENAI, with the KXIPOOPENAI-27MAY01 market shown
  • The prices shown do not run in order up the ladder: Before Apr 1, 2027 at 70% (Yes 39c, No 68c), Before May 1, 2027 at 49% (Yes 53c, No 55c) and Before Jun 1, 2027 at 61%, up 2 (Yes 57c, No 49c)
  • The trade panel for the "Before May 1, 2027" contract shows YES 53c / NO 55c and a "55% chance", against the 49% in the list, with 3.25% interest and a max payout date of Apr 30, 2027
  • Resolution for that contract: "Resolves Yes if OpenAI confirms an IPO before May 1, 2027", where an IPO is confirmed if the SEC declares the company's Form S-1 effective, or the IPO is priced, or a securities exchange has assigned a ticker to it - any of which resolves it Yes immediately, "even if the company does not start trading until after May 1, 2027"; the outcome is verified from the New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg and 5 others
  • The market opened Jul 30, 2025 at 10:00am EDT and closes after the outcome occurs, paying out about 30 minutes later; it "will close and expire early if the event occurs. Otherwise, it closes by Apr 30, 2027 at 11:59pm EDT"
  • Trading is restricted: employees of any of the source agencies and anyone holding material, non-public information on the underlying may not trade the contract, and Kalshi is "subject to U.S. regulatory oversight by the CFTC"
  • Reporting alongside the market agrees the announcement is not imminent: the Access IPOs Podcast episode #77, published 19 September 2026, says "OpenAI's IPO is still planned for 2027 (after a brief head fake), and the company is considering raising new funds at a $1.2 trillion valuation", and asks whether shares will reach secondary platforms for retail investors
dateConfidenceReasoning: A "by when" market with no scheduled event behind it. February 2027 carries the largest month-on-month jump among the rungs below that block — 12% before February 1 rising to 39% before March 1, 27 points — and a month-only date takes its last day. The April strike (70%) is quoted above both May (49%) and June (61%), so the top of the ladder is out of order and was not used. All figures are the chance the strike list shows, not the Yes price in cents.

title: Mumbai's Sewri-Worli Elevated Connector Opens to Traffic
description: The 4.5 km four-lane elevated road ties the Mumbai Trans Harbour Link at Sewri to the Bandra-Worli Sea Link and the Coastal Road at Worli, crossing the Central and Western Railway lines near Prabhadevi on a double-decker structure whose lower deck replaces the 112-year-old Elphinstone road over bridge, closed to traffic in September 2025.
longFormSummary:
• The new Elphinstone bridge in Prabhadevi and the Sewri-Worli Connector "will not be ready by the September deadline as planned" and are "now expected to be completed in January or February 2027" - the window the pin's date falls in
  • Causes given for the slip: a slower-than-expected demolition process, unexpected civic utility work, a shortage of workers and the ongoing monsoon; "Most of the remaining construction is expected to be completed by December. The final works will continue into early 2027"
  • "The 112-year-old Elphinstone Bridge was closed to traffic on September 12, 2025 to make way for a new double-decker structure"; the lower deck replaces the existing Elphinstone bridge and the upper deck becomes part of the 4.5-km Sewri-Worli Connector
  • Demolition of the old stone structure and dismantling of the railway sections ran late because railway officials could not provide the required railway blocks on time, finishing around April, nearly a month behind schedule
  • Work has reached the stage of assembling and launching the bridge's girder over the railway tracks, with temporary structures already installed on both sides; assembly is reported to take around 90 days and sliding the girder into final position about a week
  • Per an Indian Express report, MRIDC officials said the railway section is expected to be completed by November, after which MMRDA and contractor J Kumar will connect it to the remaining non-railway portions of the connector
  • Before the monsoon the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation wrote to MMRDA over excavation and piling work, saying construction had caused siltation and damaged sewage lines, and asked for scaffolding blocking footpaths to be removed; residents complained of construction-related air pollution
  • Work has continued at night and additional workers are to be recruited to speed construction
  • Once opened the connector "will improve east-west connectivity by linking Mumbai's eastern side and the Atal Setu with the city's western coast"; the report does not itself describe the four lanes or the Bandra-Worli Sea Link and Coastal Road tie-ins the pin gives

delayReasoning: Stated: MMRDA had targeted September 2026 - the report says the new bridge and connector "will not be ready by the September deadline as planned" - while "The project is now expected to be completed in January or February 2027".

title: 99th Academy Awards Crown the Best Picture of 2026
description: The 99th Academy Awards air live from the Dolby Theatre on March 14, 2027, hosted by Conan O'Brien, and the ceremony's biggest prize is Best Picture. Kalshi has The Odyssey at 52%, well ahead of The Black Ball at 16% and Dune: Part Three at 11%.
longFormSummary:
• The 99th Academy Awards are scheduled for 14 March 2027 at the Dolby Theatre in Hollywood, presented by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, honouring films released in 2026 across 24 categories
  • The ceremony begins at 4 p.m. Pacific Time and airs on ABC with streaming on Hulu
  • Conan O'Brien will host "for the third straight year", with Raj Kapoor and Katy Mullan returning as executive producers - announced on 12 May 2026 as their fourth year in a row, in a statement from AMPAS CEO Bill Kramer and president Lynette Howell Taylor praising the shows they produced over "the last two years"
  • The Academy announced the date and key dates on 7 April 2026, at the same time as the 100th ceremony on 5 March 2028 - "the last Oscar ceremonies that will be held at the Dolby Theatre"
  • The voting calendar runs preliminary voting 7-11 December 2026, nominations voting 11-15 January 2027, nominations announced 21 January 2027, and final voting 25 February to 4 March 2027
  • Kalshi's Best Picture market had The Odyssey at 51% (52c yes / 49c no, down 5), The Black Ball at 16% (16c / 85c, up 5) and Dune: Part Three at 11% (12c / 89c, down 1), with further films not shown, on $6,291,717 of volume - by far the largest of the awards markets captured
  • The capture is of a logged-out page, so The Odyssey's order ticket shows "YES --", "NO --" and "Odds 0% chance", with a max payout date of Dec 31, 2027
  • The 17th Governors Awards are set for 15 November 2026 at the Ray Dolby Ballroom in the Ovation Hollywood complex, with recipients announced on 10 June 2026
  • Academy Honorary Awards go to Glenn Close, whose "unparalleled emotional range has brought to life some of the most complex characters in cinema", animator Floyd Norman and Ridley Scott, "a true visionary whose decades-long legacy has left an immeasurable impact on global cinema and culture", with the Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award to Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler
  • Rule changes announced on 1 May 2026 take effect at this ceremony: Best International Feature Film eligibility expands beyond country submissions to non-English-language films winning top jury prizes at Berlin, Busan, Cannes, Sundance, Toronto and Venice - attributed to "high-profile and politically motivated snubs (such as Anatomy of a Fall and It Was Just an Accident)" - with films themselves "formally credited as recipients, rather than the submitting country"

title: CDG Express Starts Running From Gare de l'Est to Roissy
description: The 32 km non-stop link will run every 15 minutes from 5am to midnight between Gare de l'Est and Charles de Gaulle Airport, a 20-minute trip, operated by Hello Paris, a Keolis and RATP Dev joint venture. The infrastructure company, owned in equal shares by Groupe ADP, SNCF Reseau and Banque des Territoires, says it financed the entire project without public subsidies, and CAF France of Alsace supplied the trainsets.
longFormSummary:
• "When it enters service on 28 March 2027, the CDG Express will realise a vision first imagined more than 30 years ago: a direct link between central Paris and its main international airport"; an operator FAQ puts it less precisely, saying Hello Paris "is hiring in preparation for the service launch, planned for March 2027"
  • The link is 32 km long, "including 8 km of new track from Gare de l'Est"; three-quarters of the route runs on existing rail lines, which avoided building new tunnels, and although "The route is longer than originally planned", the dedicated non-stop service between Charles de Gaulle Airport and Paris "will still take only 20 minutes"
  • The operator's timetable page gives the service pattern: "one train every 15 minutes, from 5 am to midnight, 7 days a week, both ways", 365 days a year on a dedicated track, with departures from Gare de l'Est between 5.08 am and 12.08 am on platforms 2, 3 and 4, and from the CDG2 TGV station between 5.01 am and 12.01 am on platforms 1X and 2X; a train is at the platform 15 minutes before departure
  • There are no stops: the CDG Express is non-stop between Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport and Gare de l'Est
  • Tickets need no booking - "buy your ticket and take any CDG Express train"; one-way tickets are valid for 24 months after purchase, and a return leg must be used within 90 days of the outbound
  • Hello Paris, the operator, was created in 2018 when Keolis and RATP Dev joined forces, "pooling their expertise in rail operations, high-density transport network management and service quality"; the project itself "began to take shape in 2019"
  • SNCF Reseau and Groupe ADP built the infrastructure and upgraded a substantial part of the existing network north of Paris "under a public works concession, starting in 2019"; the CDG Express infrastructure management company, owned in equal shares by Groupe ADP, SNCF Reseau and Banque des Territoires, "financed the entire project without public subsidies". CAF France, in Alsace, is listed as the trainset manufacturer
  • Feasibility studies began in 1998 and "it soon became clear that Gare de l'Est was the natural choice for the terminal station rather than nearby Gare du Nord, which was already at full capacity"; over 72 million passengers travelled through Paris-Charles de Gaulle in 2025, and unlike London, Oslo, Stockholm and Vienna, Paris had no direct express airport link
address: Gare de l'Est, 10th arrondissement, Paris, France

title: Kvesheti-Kobi Highway Nears Completion in Georgia
description: A 23km highway bypass through Georgia's Khada Valley, including a record 9km tunnel, aims to replace a route to Russia that closes for weeks each winter.
longFormSummary:
• The Kvesheti-Kobi road is a 23 km two-lane asphalt-concrete highway on the route towards Russia through Georgia's Khada Valley, with 5 bridges and 5 tunnels plus repair of one existing bridge, pedestrian crossings and paths
  • It is commissioned by the Roads Department of the Ministry of Infrastructure, funded by the Asian Development Bank and the EBRD and monitored by UBM International United Consultants; procurement followed ADB rules and lowest-price qualified bidders won
  • The cost is stated three ways: gives a total project value of 1.240 billion Lari, breaks it into 909 million GEL for the tunnel phase and GEL 316.7 million for the access-road phase, and carries only the headline "$500M" in its title, with no breakdown on the page
  • Lot one is the 9 km tunnel bored by China Railway Tunnel Group Co. using tunnel boring machine technology; says the tunnel itself was completed in 2024 with that phase 79% complete overall
  • Lot two is 12.7 km of access road with five bridges and four tunnels by China Railway 23rd Bureau Group, 50% complete, including what will be Georgia's highest bridge at 166 m tall and 426 m long
  • Claimed benefits: Kvesheti to Kobi in 15 minutes instead of an hour, a route 11 km shorter, passable in any season clear of avalanche and heavy snow, a new 5 km road to Gudauri with a visitor centre, and 10 revived villages; locals are currently cut off for almost 100 days a year
  • On timing the references are earlier than the pin's 2027 date:, dated 7 March 2025, says the Roads Department expected a 5 km section serving Gudauri to open in 2025 and gave no exact date for the whole highway, disclosing only that it would be operational "next year"
  • is The B1M's video "The $500M Mega-Tunnel to Russia", published 2025-02-26, whose chapters cover the Khada Valley, the new road, bridges and tunnels, China's role, benefits and funding, environmental impact and "The Russian Question"; its research list cites the official project site, ADB project 51257, EBRD project 50271 and a Tunnelling Journal piece on the world's largest diameter hard rock TBM breaking through on April 23, 2024
