title: Intel Core Ultra 400 (Nova Lake) Desktop Launch
description: Intel's Nova Lake desktop chips, branded Core Ultra 400, are reported to launch from Q1 2027 on the new LGA-1954 socket, with a 52-core flagship following later in 2027.
longFormSummary:
• Intel's Nova Lake-S desktop generation is reported to launch in stages through 2027, with only the 28-core version arriving in the first quarter of 2027 and the 52-core model "arriving later in the year"
  • The July 2026 leak breaks the staggering down further: a 28-core DS package between January and March 2027, 28-core K-series (unlocked) models between March and April 2027, 16-core and 8-core variants between late March and May 2027, and the flagship 52-core DS "potentially between late May and September 2027"; the later September report gives the same window for the flagship, "between late May and September, 2027"
  • Intel is "reportedly on track to start mass production of its Nova Lake-S CPUs in the fourth quarter of 2026, according to a slide published by @wxnod"; earlier 2025 leaks and roadmap disclosures also placed mass production in Q4 2026, "so the new slide confirms that plan"
  • The sources disagree on when Nova Lake arrives at all: Wikipedia states "The first Nova Lake processors are expected to launch in late 2026", while both Tom's Hardware reports, which are newer and specific to the desktop parts, put the first Core Ultra 400 desktop launch in Q1 2027
  • The branding is also given two ways - the leak reports say Intel "could introduce it under the Core Ultra Series 400 branding", following Core Ultra Series 200 for Arrow Lake and 300 for Panther Lake, while Wikipedia calls the family "Core Ultra Series 4"
  • The range-topping part reportedly carries up to 52 cores across two compute tiles - 16 Coyote Cove performance cores, 32 Arctic Wolf efficiency cores and four low-power Arctic Wolf cores - against the 24 cores of the current Core Ultra 9 285K, with a Core Ultra 7 400-series part projected at up to 44 cores
  • Coyote Cove and Arctic Wolf point to "an entirely new CPU architecture, replacing the Lion Cove and Skymont cores found in Arrow Lake"; Wikipedia lists the same two microarchitectures and an Intel 18A technology node, though its own roadmap navbox instead files Nova Lake under "Intel 18A and/or TSMC N2P"
  • Cache: up to 16MB of L2 on the P-cores, with each pair of Coyote Cove cores reportedly sharing 2 MB (a commenter disputes this, saying "It's 2MB per P-core, but they're clustered in pairs so each has access up to 4MB"), plus bLLC (big Last Level Cache) scaling to 288 MB as Intel's answer to AMD's X3D gaming chips; Wikipedia likewise expects bLLC SKUs "to compete with AMD's 3D V-Cache"
  • Power figures conflict: the September report says dual-compute-tile CPUs "will reportedly consume up to 474W of power and will require motherboards featuring three 12V EPS power plugs", while the July article gives the flagship a 150W Processor Base Power and 253W Maximum Turbo Power and itself flags the 474W headline as "a different power figure"; the 474W claim is the newer of the two
  • Platform: a new LGA1954 socket and Intel's new 900-series chipsets, with Z990 boards already seen and Intel "reportedly intend[ing] to keep LGA1954 around for a longer time than it usually does"; the other two links also give LGA 1954, Wikipedia as the expected socket and the July report noting buyers "will likely need a new motherboard to upgrade from the existing Arrow Lake platform"
  • I/O and features: dual-channel DDR5 up to DDR5-8000 and up to 24 PCIe 5.0 lanes from the CPU (16 for graphics, splittable two x8 or four x4, plus two x4 SSD links), with Thunderbolt 5, next-generation Xe3 Celestial integrated graphics and an upgraded NPU5 also expected; Wikipedia's infobox instead gives the GPU as "Intel Arc" while one of its cited references says "Xe3 GPU", and it expects Nova Lake to be the first consumer platform supporting AVX10.1, AVX10.2 and APX (its own infobox lists AVX10.2 and APX but not AVX10.1)
  • The leaked slide "does not look like an official Intel roadmap or an Intel presentation slide"; the "more plausible explanation" is a motherboard maker's or OEM partner's deck, "which means that while it is most likely accurate, it is not final", and Intel "is yet to officially confirm a launch date for Nova Lake"
  • Unlike Intel's usual practice of launching flagship and unlocked models first, the 52-core model "will fit in a different class above a typical flagship, primarily targeting the HEDT crowd"
  • Successors: the slide lists Razor Lake and Hammer Lake following Nova Lake-S "sometime after the fourth quarter of 2027" with no technical details; Wikipedia names Razor Lake as the successor and Panther Lake (mobile) and Arrow Lake (desktop and mobile) as predecessors
dateConfidenceReasoning: A leaked roadmap puts the first Nova Lake CPUs in Q1 2027 (28-core between January and March); Intel has only said before the end of 2026 or early 2027.

title: Boeing 777-9 First Delivery
description: Boeing says the first 777-9 will be delivered in 2027, seven years late, after taking a $4.9 billion charge; Lufthansa is the launch customer, with delivery currently scheduled for mid-2027, and Emirates has signalled it is planning for late 2027.
longFormSummary:
• Boeing has confirmed the first 777-9 delivery will come in 2027, after CEO Kelly Ortberg said on October 29, 2025 that certification would need at least all of 2026 and disclosed a related $4.9 billion charge
  • Boeing held that line in its first quarter 2026 results, saying the programme "has continued to make steady progress on 777-9 certification" and that "the company anticipates first delivery in 2027" - the same timeline it set the previous October
  • The aircraft was originally due to enter service in 2020, so the slip runs about seven years, and Boeing has taken roughly $15 billion in charges on the programme in total - Reuters reported the $15 billion figure in February - well beyond the single $4.9 billion charge announced with the new schedule
  • Simple Flying's cost-recovery math: at the widely cited $440 million list price with $50 million profit per aircraft, Boeing would need to sell roughly 300 to match the overruns
  • Lufthansa is the launch customer, not Emirates; Lufthansa Aviation Training says delivery is currently scheduled for mid-2027, Cathay Pacific said in March it expects its first in 2027, and Emirates "has signaled it is planning for late 2027" - later than the May or June 2027 the pin describes
  • Firm order book by size: Emirates 270, Qatar Airways 124, Cathay Pacific 35, Lufthansa 27, British Airways 24
  • Certification still had gates to clear: the FAA cleared the 777-9 into Type Inspection Authorization Phase 4A in March 2026, with Phase 4B and Phase 5 still to come before broader functionality and reliability work and the ETOPS-related operational proving on production-standard aircraft, so "much of 2026 will be spent finishing formal flight-test phases"
  • Flight testing was active, with three of the five test aircraft flying over 40 flights in the month of the report
  • A backlog of early aircraft waits on the outcome: Boeing has assembled as many as 26 777Xs between 2018 and 2022, five in test use, leaving 21 stored at Paine Field "parked nose-to-tail on a runway with large blocks hanging from their wings in place of engines", which may need configuration changes, engineering updates, inspections or cabin and systems modifications before they are delivery-ready
  • The 777-8F freighter is expected to follow in 2028, "although Boeing has given no assurance around that timeline"
  • The Aviation Week report is paywalled after its opening paragraph, so it supports the 2027 date and the $4.9 billion charge but nothing further
dateConfidenceReasoning: Boeing says only 2027. Lufthansa, the launch customer, has delivery “currently scheduled for mid-2027” per Lufthansa Aviation Training, so the pin sits at the middle of the year.
delayReasoning: Stated: the 777-9 was due to enter service in 2020; FAA certification needs all of 2026, and Boeing took a $4.9 billion charge in October 2025.

title: Memorial Stadium Reopens at Seattle Center

longFormSummary:

  • Funding is "an unprecedented $110 million in public funding and a capital campaign generating approximately $30 million in community support"
  • The public money came in pieces: Seattle voters approved SPS' BTA V capital levy in 2022 including $66.5 million for the project, Seattle City Council approved $21 million that year and a further $19 million in the capital plan in 2023, and the Washington state legislature approved $4 million in the 2023 capital budget
  • The rebuilt venue is to be a multi-purpose stadium for student athletics, education, arts, culture, entertainment and community events, with performing arts, commencement ceremonies and a year-round community hub alongside an improved athletic field, and will host concerts, community festivals and professional sports
  • It is designed into the Seattle Center campus with new programmable public space and open sightlines linking the stadium to the International Fountain, working toward the Century 21 Master Plan
  • One Roof Sports & Entertainment pledged in its RFP response to donate $100,000 annually for five years from the first operating year to support youth access programming
  • The project preserves the Memorial Wall, honouring local high school students and alumni who died in World War II, which the Seattle Landmarks Preservation Board designated a landmark in 2023
  • The wall commemorates 762 Seattle high-school students and alumni, was designed by Garfield High School student Marianne Hanson, and was paid for with revenues from Thanksgiving Day football games played in the stadium from 1947-49; the memorial was chosen for the site by community leaders appointed by Mayor William Devin after the war
  • The stadium it replaces was completed in 1947 as successor to Civic Field of 1927, on land the City deeded to SPS in 1946, funded by a school levy and bonds issued in 1942 and 1944; it hosted the opening and closing ceremonies of the Seattle World's Fair
  • The route to construction ran from a 2017 SPS-City partnership agreement and a 2021 letter of intent through a 2022 Memorandum of Agreement leaving SPS as owner with priority use for student events, a 2023 RFP that produced One Roof as private partner, alignment on key terms in 2024, and unanimous approval of the development agreement by the Seattle School Board and City Council in 2025 alongside a ceremonial groundbreaking and the start of construction
  • Philanthropy reached $30 million in 2025, and by 2026 foundation work and concrete slabs were complete with the project shifting to vertical construction; public viewing windows are open on Harrison Street and 3rd Avenue

title: The Men's Rugby World Cup Kicks Off in Australia
description: The 11th Rugby World Cup opens at Perth Stadium and runs to the final at Stadium Australia in Sydney on 13 November. It is the first tournament branded the Men's Rugby World Cup and the first contested by 24 teams, with South Africa defending the title and Hong Kong making their debut.
longFormSummary:
• “The 2027 Men’s Rugby World Cup is scheduled to be the 11th edition of the Rugby World Cup, the quadrennial world championship for men’s rugby union teams”, held in Australia from 1 October to 13 November 2027 under the slogan “Go All Out!”, launched by World Rugby on 2 December 2025
  • It is the first tournament branded the Men’s Rugby World Cup, a change announced in October 2023 to promote gender parity, and the first contested by 24 teams, which the official site calls “the biggest edition of the tournament ever staged with 24 nations competing across 52 matches”
  • South Africa are the two-time defending champions after beating New Zealand in the 2023 final, and Hong Kong will make their Rugby World Cup debut, having won the 2025 Asia Rugby Championship
  • The pin’s opening venue is right: the opening match and opening ceremony are at Perth Stadium, which hosts Australia v Hong Kong on 1 October, and the final on 13 November at 20:00 AEDT is at Stadium Australia in Sydney, along with both semi-finals, the bronze final, two quarter-finals and two pool matches
  • Eight venues across seven cities: Stadium Australia 82,000, Perth Stadium 65,000, Adelaide Oval 53,500, Docklands Stadium Melbourne 53,000, Brisbane Stadium 52,500, Sydney Football Stadium 42,500 in rectangular mode, Newcastle Stadium 33,000 and North Queensland Stadium in Townsville 25,455
  • The official site’s host-city panel gives the same shape – “Two round of 16 & Five Pool Matches (including the Opening Match)” for the opening venue and “The Final & Bronze Final, Two Semi-finals, Two Quarter-finals, Two round of 16, Five Pool Matches” for Sydney – though most city names failed to render in the capture, leaving only Melbourne and Townsville legible
  • Melbourne nearly lost its place twice: in early January 2025 it was reported no matches would be played in Victoria after the state government pulled its bid in protest at Rugby Australia revoking the Melbourne Rebels’ Super Rugby Pacific participation, but Melbourne was reconfirmed as a host city later the same month, and in January 2026 Docklands Stadium was named the venue after World Rugby reportedly struck a deal to use it instead of the Melbourne Cricket Ground, whose October 2027 availability could not be guaranteed because of an exclusive clause between the Victorian government and the NFL
  • Australia won the hosting rights on 12 May 2022, having bid since 13 December 2017; Argentina withdrew its bid in April 2020 “to strengthen the Australian bid”, and Russia’s bid, backed by President Putin and planned around 2018 FIFA World Cup stadiums, could not proceed after a Court of Arbitration for Sport ruling of 17 December 2020 banned Russia from hosting major tournaments for two years
  • Expansion to 24 teams was reported on 4 October 2023 and confirmed on 24 October 2023, with the format settled in October 2025: six pools of four instead of four pools of five, with the top two from each pool plus the four best third-placed teams reaching a new Round of 16, taking the tournament to 52 matches from the 48 played since 2003
  • Twelve teams qualified automatically as hosts or top-three finishers in their 2023 pools, with the remaining process confirmed on 13 August 2024: four from Europe, three from the Pacific, one each from Africa, Asia and South America, one from a South America/Pacific play-off, and one from a four-team repechage of Belgium, Namibia, Samoa and Brazil, Brazil having replaced Paraguay after Paraguay fielded an ineligible player in the South American third-place playoff
  • Samoa took the final place; 21st-ranked Belgium were the only top-25 side to miss out, drawing with Samoa on the last matchday of the Final Qualification Tournament and finishing a point behind, so all 24 qualifiers were ranked inside the world top 25
  • The draw was held on 3 December 2025, the first time it took place after all teams had qualified, using four bands of six set by the World Rugby Rankings at the end of the 2025 November window, with hosts Australia automatically placed in Pool A
  • The pools are A: New Zealand, Australia, Chile, Hong Kong; B: South Africa, Italy, Georgia, Romania; C: Argentina, Fiji, Spain, Canada; D: Ireland, Scotland, Uruguay, Portugal; E: France, Japan, United States, Samoa; F: England, Wales, Tonga, Zimbabwe
  • The pool stage runs 1-17 October 2027, with New Zealand v Australia at Stadium Australia on 9 October and England v Wales there on 16 October; the article contradicts itself on Pool C’s start, its table saying “First match(es) will be played: 4 October 2027” while its own fixture list opens with Argentina v Canada on 3 October at Brisbane Stadium
  • The knockouts run 23-24 October (Round of 16 at Sydney Football Stadium, Brisbane, Melbourne and Perth), quarter-finals on 30 and 31 October, semi-finals on 5 and 6 November at Stadium Australia, and the bronze final on 12 November; ties level after regulation go to two 10-minute periods of extra time, then 10 minutes of sudden death, then a kicking competition
  • Third-placed qualifiers are slotted so that “only novel games take place during the first two knockout rounds”: a third-placed team from pools A to D can appear in only one specific Round of 16 match, while those from pools E and F can fill any slot, across fifteen tabulated combinations
  • Tickets have moved fast: the application phase opened on 18 May 2026 at the 500-day countdown after presale demand saw more than 750,000 tickets bought by fans from 135 countries, a Visa cardholder priority sale ran for 48 hours from 12:00pm AEST on 28 September 2026, and remaining tickets went on general sale from 12:00pm AEST on 1 October 2026
  • Broadcast rights run to Stan Sport and the Nine Network in Australia, TF1 in France, Sky Sport and Sky Open in New Zealand, SuperSport on DStv across Sub-Saharan Africa through a Canal+ Group agreement announced 3 June 2026, ITV in the United Kingdom (announced 27 July 2026) and Paramount+ in the United States
  • Commercially the tournament is backed by principal partners Asahi, Emirates and Visa, which joined on 14 September 2026 for Australia 2027 and 2029, official partners Coca-Cola (23 June 2026) and Liqui Moly, and suppliers including Gilbert, whose match ball was unveiled on 1 December 2025 and whose partnership runs to 2033; an Impact Beyond legacy programme launched on 28 July 2026 with AUD$30 million of Australian Government funding

title: Xbox Project Helix Next-Generation Console Launch
description: Microsoft's next Xbox, Project Helix, uses a custom AMD chip with Zen 6 cores and RDNA 5 graphics; Microsoft has given no release date, with reports pointing to late 2027 and developer alpha hardware in 2027.
longFormSummary:
• Microsoft's next-generation first-party console is Project Helix, announced by Jason Ronald, VP Next Generation, in his Xbox Developer Summit keynote at GDC on 11 March 2026
  • Microsoft has given no release date for the console itself; what it has committed to is that “we plan to ship alpha versions of the hardware to developers beginning in 2027”
  • The 2027 launch talk comes from AMD rather than Microsoft: CEO Lisa Su told the Q4 2025 earnings call that “development of Microsoft's next-gen Xbox featuring an AMD semi-custom SoC is progressing well to support a launch in 2027”
  • Windows Central reports that Microsoft insiders “were a little taken off-guard by Lisa Su's comments” and that Microsoft “hasn't fully internally committed to a hard 2027 launch window”, since much depends on improvements to Windows 11: “You can think of 2027 as the 'best case scenario'”
  • That article also contradicts itself, one line referring to accessories arriving “even before the next Xbox launches later this year” against the 2027 window it gives everywhere else
  • The console runs on a custom AMD SoC under a multi-year partnership with AMD, co-designed for the next generation of DirectX and FSR, with Microsoft “using FSR Next to power what comes next”
  • Microsoft claims “an order of magnitude leap in ray tracing performance and capability”, intelligence integrated “directly into the graphics and compute pipeline”, and gains in efficiency, scale and visual ambition
  • AMD's internal codename for the Xbox SoC is “Magnus”, which is not Microsoft's codename for the device
  • Leaked “Magnus” specifications attributed to leaker Moore's Law is Dead — not confirmed by AMD or Microsoft — give 68 RDNA 5 compute units (cut down from up to 70), at least 24MB of GPU L2 cache, up to 3 Zen 6 plus 8 Zen 6c CPU cores with 12MB of L3, a 192-bit bus with up to 48GB of GDDR7, an NPU rated up to 110 TOPS at 6W or 46 TOPS at 1.2W, a 144mm² SoC plus 264mm² GPU totalling 408mm², and an estimated 250-350W TDP
  • Those leaked figures are said to exceed the PlayStation 6, reportedly at 52-54 RDNA 5 CUs on a 160-bit bus with up to 40GB of RAM
  • Project Helix is “designed to play your Xbox console and PC games”, and Windows Central describes it as essentially a full Windows machine running a TV-first console interface by default, from which players can exit to full Windows much as a Steam Deck exits to Linux
  • Backward compatibility is part of the pitch: Xbox President Sarah Bond said the next-gen console would retain compatibility with all current Xbox console games, and Xbox commits to “keeping games from four generations of Xbox playable for years to come”
  • Pricing is unsettled: “Microsoft itself doesn't know how much the next-gen Xbox will be just yet”, with tariffs, component costs, spiralling RAM prices and supply issues in play, though it is “pushing for a more premium experience” and some expect around $1,000
  • Microsoft is working with OEMs such as ASUS on a range of next-gen Xbox hardware at different price points, positioning its own console as “a curated boutique experience in a wider Xbox hardware ecosystem”, comparable to how it handles Surface, and still wants to make a first-party handheld eventually
  • Around the same GDC announcement, Xbox mode began rolling out to Windows 11 in select markets from April, the Xbox Play Anywhere catalog passed 1,500 games from 500 development teams, and Epic said it is ready to bring the Epic Games Store to the next Xbox
dateConfidenceReasoning: Reports target October to November 2027 with 2028 possible; AMD says its semi-custom chip is 'progressing well to support a launch in 2027'. The last day of November 2027 is used.

title: Downtown San Diego's COASTER Platform Opens
description: A new COASTER commuter-rail platform on Harbor Drive between 1st and 5th Streets, by the Gaslamp Quarter, the convention centre and Petco Park, with San Diego Trolley connections either side. The $33 million project also adds a pocket track so trains can run more often.
longFormSummary:
• NCTD is building a new COASTER station in downtown San Diego parallel to Harbor Drive near the Gaslamp Quarter and the San Diego Convention Center, extending the line from its existing terminus at Santa Fe Depot to the waterfront
  • The centrepiece is an 850-foot platform running from First Avenue to Fifth Avenue "with the capacity to accommodate eight passenger cars", sited between two existing MTS Trolley stations - Wikipedia names them as the adjacent Convention Center and Gaslamp Quarter stations
  • The project also reconfigures the existing BNSF track and adds a new siding, or pocket track, "to allow greater service frequencies"; the Union-Tribune describes the same work as adding "a second rail track in part of downtown - making it easier for freight trains to travel through the area from the Port of San Diego to Los Angeles"
  • Supporting work includes extension of railroad signalling and dispatching, signal upgrades at five grade crossings (Kettner Boulevard, Market Street, Front Street, First Avenue and Fifth Avenue), switch and signal upgrades at Broadway, and new pedestrian and cyclist infrastructure at First and Fifth
  • The station gives "a one-seat ride from Oceanside to Petco Park, the San Diego Convention Center, the Gaslamp Quarter, The Rady Shell, and other downtown destinations", sparing riders a near-mile walk, a trolley transfer or a car from Santa Fe Depot
  • The project costs $33 million for design and construction and is fully funded, drawn from the $106 million grant NCTD received from the California Transportation Commission in December 2020 for LOSSAN corridor improvements; Wikipedia adds that the funding came partly from a Trade Corridor Enhancement Program grant derived from Road Repair and Accountability Act revenues and partly from BNSF
  • NCTD has a design-build project management contract with BNSF, which takes the lead on construction, alongside the city, the Port of San Diego and San Diego Gas & Electric
  • The links disagree sharply on the schedule. NCTD's own project page - the oldest of the three - says design was "planned to be completed in April 2025", construction "expected to start in fall 2025", and the station "anticipated to be open to passengers in early 2027"
  • The newer February 2026 reporting supersedes that: NCTD officials said they now plan to break ground "by the end of this year" and have the station "operating by late 2027 or early 2028", having delayed a hoped-for spring 2026 groundbreaking to analyse relocating utilities between Harbor Drive and Tony Gwynn Drive
  • CEO Shawn Donaghy: "It is unlikely that construction will start in spring of 2026, as these utility reviews are critical to the project. While we are hopeful that the project will be complete in 2027, it is more likely at this point that it will be late 2027 to early 2028"; any delay in agreeing utility relocations "would delay groundbreaking"
  • Wikipedia, also as of February 2026, keeps a spring construction start - "construction on the Downtown Platform is scheduled to begin in the spring. After 18 months of construction, the station will likely open in late-2027 or early-2028" - while its infobox still gives an opening of 2027 and it files the station under "Railway stations scheduled to open in 2027"; the Union-Tribune's account of the delayed groundbreaking is the more specific and authoritative of the two
  • Construction is expected to last about 18 months
  • The station will have one side platform and two tracks, will be accessible, is owned by NCTD on the BNSF San Diego Subdivision, and will be the COASTER terminus with Santa Fe Depot the preceding stop toward Oceanside
  • NCTD argues the station "will improve passenger and freight operations along the Los Angeles-San Diego-San Luis Obispo (LOSSAN) corridor, which is the second busiest intercity rail corridor in the country", as one of a group of TCEP projects whose "primary benefit ... is increased freight frequencies"
  • The extension "is expected to boost ridership beyond the 871,000 it had in 2024"; the COASTER currently has eight stations along its 41-mile route, and an extension to the Convention Center "has been an ambition of NCTD since shortly after the Coaster began running in 1995", with formal efforts starting only in 2020
  • Reaction: the Gaslamp Quarter Association's Michael Trimble said "More convenient rail access gives people a real alternative to driving downtown", while advocacy group RideSD said the extension "should go hand-in-hand with improved hours and frequency"

dateConfidenceReasoning: NCTD's project page anticipated the platform "open to passengers in early 2027", while reporting from February 2026 has construction starting that spring and the station opening "in late-2027 or early-2028"; the date takes the later window.
delayReasoning: Stated: NCTD expected construction to start in fall 2025 and the platform to open in early 2027; ground was not broken until 2026, putting the opening about a year later, in late 2027 or early 2028.

title: White Stadium Reopens in Franklin Park After Its Rebuild
description: The city-owned stadium in Franklin Park reopens after a rebuild that grew from a $30 million repair into a $325 million project, $135 million of it public money from the City of Boston and $190 million from the owners of Boston Legacy FC. The NWSL club will not play its first match there until 2028; Boston Public Schools athletics get the ground back first.
longFormSummary:
• White Stadium, formally the George R. White Memorial Stadium, at 450 Walnut Avenue in Boston's Franklin Park, is closed and undergoing a renovation "that will turn it into an 11,000-seat venue shared with Boston Legacy FC of the National Women's Soccer League"
  • The rebuild is dated 2025-2027, with Boston Public Schools athletics listed as a tenant again from 2027 and Boston Legacy FC from 2028
  • It began as a $30 million renovation announced by the city in 2023 to prepare for an NWSL expansion team due to start play in 2026; by 2026 "estimates for the stadium revitalization had risen to $325 million, with $135 million committed in public funding from the City of Boston and $190 million in private funding from the owners of Boston Legacy FC"
  • The team's owners were the only group to respond to the city's RFP for a renovation partner
  • It is a public-private partnership championed by Mayor Michelle Wu in which Boston Public Schools keeps ownership and scheduling priority, leasing the stadium to Boston Legacy for a maximum of 20 games and 20 practices per year, with BPS athletics using it on all other days
  • Beyond the seats needed to meet league minimums, the work adds new BPS locker rooms, sports-medicine facilities and study spaces, replaces the unmaintained six-lane track with a regulation eight-lane one, and puts water fountains and restrooms accessible from the park outside the stadium
  • The delay to 2027 came from litigation: the Emerald Necklace Conservancy and local residents sued in February 2024 claiming the renovation was illegal, were denied a preliminary injunction, lost every pretrial motion and saw the suit dismissed in March 2025, a decision "unanimously upheld by the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court in August 2026, clearing the project to proceed as planned, albeit with delays that pushed the planned re-opening of the stadium to 2027 and Boston Legacy FC's first game there to 2028"
  • Opposition also ran through city politics: mayoral candidate Josh Kraft repeatedly attacked the project in the 2025 election "as expensive, unpopular, and detrimental to communities living near the stadium" before finishing a distant second to Wu in the preliminary and dropping out; his family's New England Revolution, which was itself trying to build a stadium in Everett, filed an amicus brief supporting the project in 2026
  • The Franklin Park Coalition and Boston Preservation Alliance backed the plan once their concerns were addressed, and a 2024 Coalition survey and a 2025 Emerson College poll both found a majority of Boston residents polled supported it
  • Demolition was completed by mid-2025: the condemned, fire-damaged east grandstand came down and the west grandstand was gutted, while the original Art Deco clamshell west wall and the north-side ticketing booths and entry gates were preserved, and the track and field were torn up and rebuilt from scratch for new drainage and eight lanes
  • The rebuilt stadium adds a restaurant and public gathering space at the south end, canopies above the bleachers on both rebuilt grandstands, and movable bleachers that can be placed over the track to bring spectators closer for soccer and football and retracted when the track is in use
  • The original stadium was built 1947-1949 by Desmond & Lord for 10,519 patrons, financed by the George Robert White fund, at a cost that ballooned from an estimated $350,000-$450,000 to $1,000,000 (about $14,000,000 in 2025); the Boston Preservation Alliance calls it "a rare example of Streamline Art Deco architecture in New England with a hint of Bauhaus influence"

title: PlayStation 6 Reportedly Targeted for Holiday 2027 Alongside Xbox Helix
description: Insider Kepler L2's read of AMD and NVIDIA production plans points to a holiday 2027 launch for Sony's PlayStation 6, mirroring Microsoft's Xbox Helix. AMD's AT2 RDNA 5 GPU is reported as the only major gaming silicon in volume production that year.
longFormSummary:
• "New evidence has emerged in the tech community indicating that the next-generation PlayStation 6 home gaming console is being prepared for the holiday season in late 2027", in parallel with Microsoft's Xbox Helix - a report dated 18 September 2026 that stems from insider Kepler L2's data on AMD and NVIDIA production plans for 2027-2028
  • "The specialized AT2 graphics chip based on the microarchitecture RDNA 5 is the only major gaming-class silicon solution scheduled for mass production in 2027, while other consumer discrete graphics card lines from both developers have been postponed to 2028"
  • The AT2 GPU is directly linked to the Xbox Helix platform, "the first devkits of which are expected to be available to partner studios in early 2027", a cycle said to mirror the run-up to the Xbox Series X launch in 2020
  • "Microsoft's desire to secure a leading position in the pre-holiday period in late 2027 is forcing Sony to adhere to a mirrored production schedule and release the PlayStation 6 in parallel, preventing the user base from shifting to a competing ecosystem"
  • Kepler_L2 had said earlier, on 14 March 2026, that "Both Xbox and PS6 are still in track for Holiday 2027", adding "It's possible for things to be delayed but very unlikely at this point. The RAM/NAND situation is bad but has mostly stabilized and will likely be at least a little bit better by the end of 2027"
  • That claim ran against a mid-February 2026 Bloomberg report suggesting the PS6 and Xbox "Project Helix" would be delayed to 2028 or 2029 because of the memory crisis; Sportskeeda flags its piece as "based on a third-party report, so users are advised to take it with a grain of salt"
  • Leaker Moore's Law Is Dead claims both consoles use AMD's RDNA 5-based graphics architecture and that the Xbox "Project Helix" GPU will have more Compute Cores, making it more powerful than the PS6; GameGPU expects the simultaneous debut on AMD custom architectures to give both "comparable levels of base hardware performance"
  • No retail prices or exact launch dates have been stated, which analysts call "the accepted standard at this stage of system design", with final prices traditionally set only a few months before the devices reach shelves

title: Traders Weigh a US Recession Through 2027
description: Kalshi’s recession market for 2027 prices a 25% chance of two consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth between Q4 2026 and Q4 2027, on the Bureau of Economic Analysis’s advance estimates — despite the KXRECSSNBER ticker, no NBER call is involved. Its 2026 contract sits at 6%, and Polymarket’s cumulative "recession by end of 2027" book, which also counts an NBER announcement, is higher still at 34.5%.
longFormSummary:
• Kalshi’s 2027 contract (series KXRECSSNBER, event KXRECSSNBER-27) prices YES at 24¢ against NO at 78¢ on $448,819 of volume, with a max payout date of Jan 31, 2028; the market opened Apr 24, 2026 at 3:15pm EDT
  • Kalshi’s own trade panel is internally inconsistent, showing ‘25% chance’ beside the 24¢ YES price
  • Polymarket’s ‘US recession by end of 2027?’ sits higher, at a 35% chance for Yes, but on only $9,325 of volume and 76 comments; it opened Aug 7, 2026, 3:43 PM ET with an end date of Dec 31, 2027, and its summary was updated Sep 20, 2026
  • Despite the KXRECSSNBER ticker, the Kalshi market does not turn on the NBER at all: it ‘resolves Yes if there are two consecutive quarters of negative GDP growth in Q4 2026 through Q4 2027, according to the Bureau of Economic Analysis’, using the advance estimate’s quarter-over-quarter annualized change in real GDP, and qualifying quarters may include Q4 2026 and Q1 2027
  • Polymarket resolves on either of two conditions: the same kind of two-consecutive-negative-quarters test but over a wider Q2 2025 to Q4 2027 window, or a public NBER announcement that a recession occurred at any point in 2025, 2026 or 2027 — so the two books are not pricing quite the same question, and Polymarket’s wider window is part of why it is dearer
  • The NBER itself does not use the two-quarter rule the markets lean on: its Business Cycle Dating Committee dates monthly peaks and troughs on ‘depth, diffusion, and duration’, weighting real personal income less transfers and nonfarm payroll employment most heavily, with ‘no fixed rule about what measures contribute information to the process or how they are weighted’
  • The NBER is also deliberately slow: its dating is ‘retrospective’, waiting ‘until sufficient data are available to avoid the need for major revisions’, so a peak is usually identified ‘a number of months after it has actually occurred’; its most recent peak is February 2020 and trough April 2020
  • Polymarket’s rules contradict themselves on the backstop: one clause says the market stays open until the Q4 2027 advance estimate is released, while the next says that if the advance estimate for Q4 2026 has not been released by June 30, 2028 the market resolves on what is available
  • On the near term the paired Kalshi 2026 market (KXRECSSNBER-26) trades at 6% on about $3.5m of volume; a capture of that page showing $0 volume and no price at all had caught an empty order form rather than the market. Polymarket’s related book separately lists ‘US recession by end of 2026?’ at 9% and ‘Negative GDP growth in 2026?’ at 2%, neither of which asks Kalshi’s question
  • Polymarket’s AI-generated context, which it says ‘plays no role in how this market resolves’, attributes the 65.5% no-recession side to Federal Reserve September 2026 projections of median real GDP growth of 2.3% in 2026 and 2.4% in 2027, unemployment near 4.1% and core PCE easing toward 2.5% by late 2027, with persistent inflation or an abrupt AI capex slowdown as the key risks
  • A Business Insider item carried on the Kalshi page reports economist Henrik Zeberg laying out a timeline for a recession and stock crash by the end of 2027, while a Morningstar piece there says ‘rate hikes this year will give way to large rate cuts in 2027 and 2028’
  • A Fexingo podcast episode of July 4, 2026 argues the Russell 2000 may already be pricing a 2027 recession: the index at 2,996 against the S&P 500 at 7,483, a forward P/E of about 14.5 against about 22, a spread the hosts call the widest since the early 2000s outside the 2020 dip, with VIX at 15.81 suggesting large-cap traders are complacent while ‘the real economy is not’; the hosts frame this as a question, not a forecast
address: National Bureau of Economic Research, 1050 Massachusetts Ave, Cambridge, MA
dateConfidenceReasoning: The market asks only whether the two negative quarters fall anywhere between Q4 2026 and Q4 2027, so there is no single day to hang it on; by the convention for a year-only date the pin takes the last day of 2027. Kalshi does not expire it until January 31, 2028, when the advance estimate for Q4 2027 is due. The 25% is the chance on Kalshi’s trade panel, which sits beside a 24¢ Yes price.

title: Two SpaceX Starships Dock in Orbit
description: Docking two Starships is the step that makes orbital propellant transfer — and with it Artemis and Mars — possible. Kalshi gives it a 69% chance before 2028, while Polymarket’s dated ladder puts only 3.2% on it happening by the end of 2026 against 51.5% by the end of 2027.
longFormSummary:
• Kalshi's market KXSTARSHIPDOCK-28 asks "Will two SpaceX Starships dock together before 2028?" and "Resolves Yes if two SpaceX Starships (any kind of Starship - e.g. tankers, depots, testing vehicles) successfully execute a docking maneuver in a stable Earth orbit before Jan 1, 2028"
  • Kalshi prices it at YES 49 cents / NO 55 cents, "Odds 51% chance", on $56,866 of volume; the market opened Mar 19, 2025 at 10:00am EDT, expires early if the docking happens and otherwise closes Jan 1, 2028 at 10:00am EST
  • Polymarket runs a dated ladder on the same question: December 31, 2026 at 3% ($46,244 volume) and December 31, 2027 at 52% ($24,369 volume), total volume $70,613; the market opened Jun 11, 2026 with an end date of Jan 1, 2028 and an FAQ resolution date of Dec 31, 2027
  • Polymarket sets a tighter bar than Kalshi: the maneuver "must physically join two vessels, matching in velocity, into a connected structure via mating hardware for at least 60 continuous seconds", with both free-flying vessels in stable Earth orbit at a perigee of at least 100 kilometres; a passively placed vessel, or a capsule carried up on a separate launch vehicle, does not qualify
  • Polymarket's market context (updated Sep 20, 2026) says "Version 3 Starships incorporate androgynous docking ports, propellant transfer hardware, and navigation sensors to enable ship-to-ship rendezvous in low Earth orbit", and that Flight 13's success in July 2026 (Starlink V3 deployment, in-space Raptor relight, intact reentry) "bolstered trader expectations for orbital refueling milestones"
  • The same context notes Flight 14 is "now targeted for late September 2026 pending FAA approval" and will attempt the first full orbital insertion but "will not include docking or tanker operations"; sequential launches of target and tanker vehicles plus regulatory clearances remain the near-term catalysts
  • As of mid-August 2026 the SpaceX Daily podcast reported that "Starship still lacks an orbital refueling demo after thirteen flights", keeping the revised 2028 Mars cargo window dependent on solving that bottleneck; the first uncrewed Mars landing target has moved from 2018 to "no earlier than 2028"
dateConfidenceReasoning: No docking has been scheduled. Polymarket’s dated ladder puts 3.2% on it happening by the end of 2026 and 51.5% by the end of 2027, so 2027 carries about 48 points against 3 for 2026; a year-only date takes its last day. Kalshi’s "before 2028" market prices the whole question at 69%.

title: DFW Airport Opens the First 15 Gates of Terminal F
description: Phase one of DFW's sixth terminal opens with 15 gates, two and a half years after construction began in November 2024 and on a frame built from six prefabricated modules rolled into place by August 2025. DFW and American Airlines have since scaled the programme up to an eventual 31 gates at about $4 billion, with the rest of the terminal following by 2031.
longFormSummary:
• On Aug. 8 DFW completed the last of six module moves that make up the structure of Terminal F's first phase; the modules were moved overnight over a two-week period by self-propelled modular transporters along an airside taxiway and set onto foundations at the Terminal F site
  • The largest of the six measured 278 feet by 136 feet and weighed 3,320 tons, "about as heavy as 12 Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner widebody aircraft", and the Terminal F modules are about four times larger than those moved earlier the same year for the Terminal C expansion
  • It is DFW's third module-based terminal project, and the airport calls these "the largest modules for a terminal expansion at any airport"
  • "The first phase of the Terminal F expansion program is anticipated to open with 15 gates in 2027"; the release names no month, so the pin's 31 December 2027 date is more precise than its source
  • In May, DFW and American Airlines decided to expand the scope and accelerate the phasing of Terminal F; the estimated $4 billion terminal is planned to deliver 31 gates in total, served entirely by American, with expanded international and widebody capacity plus parking, ticketing, check-in, security screening and baggage operations
  • American will hand back some gates elsewhere at DFW, helping other airlines grow there
  • Phase one includes a new centralized Skylink station, and the final configuration provides a walking connection with Terminal D
  • The phase-one design-build team is Innovation Next+, a joint venture of Archer Western Construction, Turner Construction Company, Phillips May Corporation, H. J. Russell & Company and CARCON Industries, with PGAL, Gensler and Muller2 on design
  • Terminal F sits within DFW Forward, the airport's "historic $12 billion capital plan"; CEO Chris McLaughlin says modular construction is "finding smarter ways to deliver results faster, with less impact on travelers"
address: Terminal F, Dallas Fort Worth International Airport, TX 75261, United States
dateConfidenceReasoning: DFW's own newsroom says "the first phase of the Terminal F expansion program is anticipated to open with 15 gates in 2027", giving a year rather than a day, so it sits at the end of that year.

title: Major Construction Starts on SEA's S Concourse Rebuild
description: The Port of Seattle's S Concourse Evolution project adds 150,000 square feet to the 1973 satellite concourse that handles most of SEA's international flights, including a new upper concourse level and dual-level boarding at selected gates, reusing customs space freed when the International Arrivals Facility opened in 2022. All phases are estimated to finish by 2034.
longFormSummary:
• The Port of Seattle Commission authorized initial funding for the S Concourse Evolution at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport, "with major construction scheduled to start in 2027" - the release gives the year only, not the pin's end-of-2027 date
  • Part of the $5.5 billion Upgrade SEA capital improvement program, the estimated $2.5 billion renovation "will transform a 1973 facility into a world-class concourse that primarily serves international travelers"
  • The project does not increase the gate count, as there is no room to expand between the main terminal and the airfield; it repurposes, in part, the customs area vacated when the International Arrivals Facility opened in 2022
  • It adds 150,000 square feet, including a new Upper Concourse Level, improved dual-level boarding operations for select gates, expanded dining, retail, lounge and passenger amenities, and seismic, structural and building systems upgrades
  • Work runs in multiple phases over eight years to keep most gates operating, with a temporary S Annex east of the facility built to support ground boarding; "The goal is to have only three of the 12 gates impacted by construction at any time", and "All phases are currently estimated to be completed by 2034"
  • Sustainability targets are LEED Silver certification, an anticipated 58% reduction in annual operational greenhouse gas emissions and a 16% reduction in annual energy use from Port Standard, through high-performance glazing, enhanced lighting and building management, electrical equipment in place of fossil fuel, low-flow plumbing, EV charging for aircraft service equipment and reuse of building material
  • Of the $2.5 billion total, the Commission authorization is for $1.1 billion to fund the project into 2029, with the remainder to come back to Commissioners for review and consent; funding is from the Airport Development Fund and future revenue bonds, and "As with virtually all airport projects, no taxpayer dollars will be used to fund the project"
  • SEA Airport Managing Director Wendy Reiter: "The existing building is over half a century old... we're being innovative by building up and not out. We're mindful of the fact that we have one of the smallest footprints of any major U.S. airport considering our passenger volume"
  • AECOM's Kevin Keady said the design "is inspired by local, indigenous concepts combined with pragmatic enhancements" and will "benefit the region for the next 50 years", while Commission President Ryan Calkins said the authorization "builds on the generational investments we are making at SEA to improve the passenger experience"
  • Upgrade SEA status at the time: N Concourse Modernization complete (2021), International Arrivals Facility complete (2022), Restroom Renovation complete (2025), SEA Gateway Project complete (2026), C Concourse Expansion complete (2026), Roadway Improvements nearing completion that fall, Baggage Optimization in progress to 2029 and SEA Underground Controls Replacement in progress to 2027
address: South Satellite, Seattle-Tacoma International Airport, SeaTac, WA 98158
dateConfidenceReasoning: The Port of Seattle says the work has "major construction scheduled to start in 2027", a year rather than a day, so it sits at the end of that year.

title: Kwu Tung Station Opens on the East Rail Line
description: Kwu Tung opens between Sheung Shui and Lok Ma Chau as the first railway station serving the Kwu Tung North new development area in Hong Kong's Northern Metropolis. It is being built by cut-and-cover directly above the operating Lok Ma Chau Spur Line tunnel, using box structures left in place when that tunnel was built, so East Rail trains keep running underneath.
longFormSummary:
• Kwu Tung Station on the East Rail Line is proposed between Sheung Shui and Lok Ma Chau, at the junction of Ma Tso Lung Road and Ho Sheung Heung Road in the town centre of the future Kwu Tung North New Development Area
  • Main construction works began in 2023 "with a target to complete the entire project in 2027", a date the page repeats in an image caption; a second Kwu Tung Station on the Northern Link main line is to follow, targeted for construction completion in 2034, with the two stations built next to each other and inter-connected
  • MTR is deliberately building the East Rail Line station first and the main line "progressively", taking into account the development pace along the Northern Link
  • Part of the station already exists: as part of the Lok Ma Chau Spur Line enabling works, tunnel structure works including the tunnel box at underground track level were completed, allowing the platforms, concourse and entrances to be built above by cut and cover
  • Building over a live railway constrains the work - the existing tunnel must be modified for station use while trains keep running, protection works for railway facilities come first, excavation is closely monitored "given the high groundwater table in the works area", emergency vehicular access and evacuation routes must stay clear so space is "extremely limited", and part of the construction happens at night in windows that "may be less than several hours per night on several nights per week"
  • The station is underground on three levels: platforms in the lower basement, concourse in the upper basement and entrances on the ground floor connecting to the Town Plaza, which the station sits on with residential, retail and commercial development on both sides
  • At opening the eastern and western sides will each have two entrances into the new development area, the western pair reaching the future public wet market and public transport interchange; more will be added when the Northern Link station opens, when passengers will be able to interchange between the two lines inside the paid area
  • Most of the Kwu Tung North NDA population is to live within walking distance of the station
  • The design targets BEAM Plus Gold certification, with natural lighting and ventilation, skylights and high canopies, a green roof, open entrances aligned with the proposed green corridor, and inclusive features including passenger lifts, barrier-free access, public toilets and a babycare room; BIM is used at every project stage and the team is studying DfMA and Modular Integrated Construction
  • The station's primary theme colour "echos the long soy sauce manufacturing history of the community", with colours drawn from Kwu Tung's natural landscape as highlights
  • The page notes that Northern Link station names are working titles only and that drawings and visuals are conceptual and subject to change; the other stations listed are San Tin, Ngau Tam Mei, Au Tau and Kam Sheung Road
address: Kwu Tung, New Territories, Hong Kong
dateConfidenceReasoning: MTR's Northern Link project site says "the main construction works have already been commenced in 2023, with a target to complete the entire project in 2027", giving a year rather than a day.

title: Mass General's Ragon Building Opens Its First Tower to Patients
description: The first of two connected towers in Mass General's Cambridge Street expansion takes its first patients, bringing 450 beds and 12 levels of operating, procedural and interventional space for the Corrigan Minehan Heart Center and the Mass General Cancer Center. Turner topped out the steel in February 2025; the second tower is not due until 2030.
longFormSummary:
• The Phillip and Susan Ragon Building is Massachusetts General Hospital's new clinical care building on Cambridge Street in Boston, on a campus parcel framed by Cambridge, North Grove, Parkman and Blossom streets
  • It is built in two phases: Phase 1 creates the below-ground parking levels and then erects the tower closest to the Blossom Street side, "expected to last approximately four years, with the initial first side of the building opening in 2027"; Phase 2 demolishes the Parkman Garage and builds the second tower on the North Grove side, "expected to be completed three years later, with an expected opening in 2030"
  • The whole project "will likely involve approximately 8.5 years of phased construction", and the page cautions "This timeline is dependent on many factors"
  • The building totals 1.05 million square feet across five continuous podium floors above street level, two inpatient towers and six below-ground levels for parking and support services
  • It holds 482 new private single-bed rooms across the two towers, letting Mass General decommission outmoded space in older facilities and convert double rooms to single-patient rooms
  • Clinical capacity includes 23 cardiovascular OR/interventional procedure rooms, 100 infusion bays, 120 exam rooms and 13 imaging modalities, plus clinical support space for pharmacy and dietary and an education center and auditorium
  • It is home to the Mass General Brigham Cancer Institute and the Corrigan Minehan Heart Center
  • The stated purpose is to meet growing demand, "alleviate ongoing capacity challenges in the hospital's Emergency Department and inpatient units", accommodate new technologies, consolidate related services and prepare for patient surges from outbreaks or disasters
  • Parking is six underground levels for 864 vehicles "for patients and families only - no staff parking", replacing the outdated Parkman Garage which will be demolished, plus space for 566 bicycles
  • The regulatory path ran from February 20, 2019, when Mass General submitted its Institutional Master Plan Notification Form, Project Notification Form and Environmental Notification Form, through the IMP submitted April 23, 2021, BPDA Board approval of both the IMP and the project on October 14, 2021, Boston Zoning Commission approval on November 17, 2021, and a final MEPA certificate on November 15, 2021 finding the Final Environmental Impact Report adequate
  • The building is designed to be resilient, "able to withstand major flooding and high winds, serving as a critical resource ... during a disaster", powered almost entirely by renewable electricity with a plan for net zero carbon in operations and construction
  • Neighbourhood commitments include ground-floor retail and a restaurant, a glass pavilion arcade on North Anderson Street with exhibits curated with the West End Museum and the Museum of African American History, incorporation of the former Winchell School (later Ruth Sleeper Hall) facade at Blossom and Parkman, a West End senior/community center and food bank, and street-level space reserved for the MBTA as a future headhouse for the proposed Red-Blue Connector
  • The project carries "an unprecedented $62 million investment in our local communities" through the MGH Community Health Impact Funds, an anchor hiring strategy and about 1,000 new jobs
  • The page's construction updates run to a two-week look-ahead covering 9/14/26 to 9/27/26, so the project was still in construction as of September 2026
  • The page gives no bed count for the first tower alone, no number of operating and interventional levels, and does not name Turner or a steel topping-out

dateConfidenceReasoning: Mass General Brigham's own page still describes "initial first side of the building opening in 2027", a year earlier than current reporting.

title: Construction Starts on the New Hillingdon Hospital

longFormSummary:

  • The Trust's draft milestones run: design refresh beginning July 2025, contractor selection and onboarding in early 2026, Outline Business Case submission October 2026, Full Business Case submission March 2028, construction 2028-2032 and the hospital available to patients in early 2033
  • Following the wave 1 announcement the Minister of State for Health set out expectations that the Trust develop a Hospital 2.0 compliant design (the New Hospital Programme's standardised approach), gain Local Authority planners' support for it, and move forward with the Outline Business Case "supported by a programme plan to be agreed by March 2025"
  • An Integrated Site Clearance Programme covering enabling schemes, decants and business-as-usual site moves supports "a cleared site in 2027", including completing the Furze refurbishment by October 2025 and a new power supply phase

title: Annular Solar Eclipse Crosses Brazil
description: Greatest eclipse falls at 15:07:46 UT on 2028-01-26, where the annular phase lasts 10 minutes 27 seconds on a path 323.0 km wide; the longest annularity anywhere on the track is 10m30.6s. The path of annularity crosses Ecuador, Peru, Brazil, Suriname, Spain and Portugal, and a partial eclipse is visible from eastern North America, C. & South America, western Europe and northwestern Africa.
longFormSummary:
• Greatest eclipse of the Annular Solar Eclipse of 2028 Jan 26 falls at 15:07:46.5 UT at 02°57.5'N 051°33.7'W, with the Sun 67.0° high, a path 323.0 km wide and a central duration of 10m27.1s
  • Annularity is longest not at greatest eclipse but at the point of Greatest Duration, 14:53:08 UT at 00°48'N 054°39'W, where the path is 328.7 km wide and the central duration reaches 10m30.6s
  • The path of annularity crosses Ecuador, Peru, Brazil, Suriname, Spain and Portugal, while the partial eclipse is visible from eastern North America, Central and South America, western Europe and northwestern Africa
  • The eclipse belongs to Saros series 141, with an eclipse magnitude of 0.9208 (0.921 in the decade table), gamma 0.3901 and a path 323 km wide; both catalogues give greatest eclipse in Terrestrial Dynamical Time as 15:08:59 and 15:08:58, which is the same instant as the source's 15:07:46.5 UT given ΔT = 71.9 seconds
  • The source page tabulates the Moon's antumbral shadow at 120-second intervals in WGS 84 coordinates - 109 timed rows from 13:20 UT to 16:56 UT plus opening and closing "Limits" rows - giving northern and southern limits, the central line, the Moon/Sun diameter ratio, the Sun's altitude and azimuth, path width and central-line duration
  • Saros 141 runs 1244.08 years across 70 eclipses (41 annular, 29 partial, sequence "7P 41A 22P"), from a partial eclipse on 1613 May 19 to a partial eclipse on 2857 Jun 13, all at the Moon's ascending node; its longest annular eclipse is 1955 Dec 14 at 12m09s
  • Predictions were generated using the VSOP87/ELP2000-85 solar and lunar ephemerides with ΔT = 71.9 seconds and "DO NOT include the effects of mountains and valleys along the edge of the Moon"; lunar limb corrections may shift the path limits by ~1-3 kilometers and change the duration by ~1-3 seconds, and more detailed predictions "are normally posted 12-18 months before each eclipse"
  • All the calculations are by Fred Espenak of NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center, who "assumes full responsibility for their accuracy"
dateConfidenceReasoning: NASA's eclipse catalogue gives the instant of greatest eclipse as 15:07:46 UT on 2028-01-26 (15:08:58 TD, the two separated by delta-T), from Saros series 141. Eclipse circumstances are computed from orbital mechanics, so the date and time are exact centuries ahead.

title: Cagrisema's Phase 3 Trial in Obesity Reads Out
description: Novo Nordisk's phase 3 trial of Cagrisema in obesity reaches primary completion, the point at which the last participant's primary outcome is measured. The trial enrolled 2,500 participants. This clinical study is testing how the study medicine CagriSema helps people living with obesity, with or without type 2 diabetes (T2D), lose weight. The purpose of the study is to find out how safe and effective CagriSema is for body weight loss in these participants. Participants will receive either CagriSema or semaglutide, and which treatment participants receive is decided by chance. CagriSema is a new study medicine being tested, while semaglutide is a medicine that doctors can already prescribe. The study will last for about 83 weeks
longFormSummary:
• The read-out is the estimated primary completion of Novo Nordisk A/S's Phase 3 trial NCT07564414, "A Clinical Study to Compare Efficacy and Safety of Two Different Doses of CagriSema and Semaglutide in Participants With Obesity With or Without Type 2 Diabetes"
  • Primary completion is estimated for 2028-02-23 and overall completion for 2028-04-19; the trial started 2026-05-21 (actual) and was first posted 2026-05-04
  • Estimated enrolment is 2,500 participants with obesity, with or without type 2 diabetes; the record's status is RECRUITING as of the last update posted 2026-08-31
  • Participants receive either CagriSema (cagrilintide and semaglutide) or semaglutide, both subcutaneously, with the treatment "decided by chance"; "CagriSema is a new study medicine being tested, while semaglutide is a medicine that doctors can already prescribe"
  • The study will last for about 83 weeks; the single primary outcome measure is relative change in body weight from randomisation (week 0) to end of treatment (week 72)
  • The trial runs at 303 sites across 19 countries, including the United States, Argentina, Australia, Canada, France, Italy, Poland, South Africa and Spain
dateConfidenceReasoning: ClinicalTrials.gov lists 2028-02-23 as the estimated primary completion date; a sponsor's estimate, and trials of this size routinely slip.

title: MenQuadfi's Phase 3 Trial in Meningococcal Infection Reads Out
description: Sanofi's phase 3 trial of MenQuadfi in meningococcal infection reaches primary completion, the point at which the last participant's primary outcome is measured. The trial enrolled 4,568 participants. The purpose of this study is to describe the safety and immunogenicity of MenACYW conjugate vaccine compared with locally-licensed meningococcal vaccines in healthy infants and toddlers in China. Study details include: * Study duration (including 6-month safety follow-up after the last dose): * Cohort I (Groups 1 and 2): approximately 211 or 271 days (approximately 7 or 9 months) * Cohort II (Groups 3 and 4): up to 18 months * Cohort III (Groups 5 and 6): up to 21 months * Cohort III (Group 7): approximately 16 months * Vaccination Visits Period: * Cohort I (Groups 1 and 2): a 2-dose vaccination at V01 (D01) and V02 (D31) or V03 (D91). Two blood samples are collected pre-vaccination (D01) and 30 days post the 2nd dose of vaccination (D61 or D121). Telephone calls (TCs) are planned on the 4th, the 9th, and the 21st day after each vaccination, and 5 TCs (1 TC/month) are planned for the 5 m
longFormSummary:
• NCT07710872 is Sanofi's Phase 3, modified-double-blind, multi-center study of an investigational quadrivalent meningococcal conjugate vaccine in healthy infants and toddlers aged 2 to 23 months in China, to "describe the safety and immunogenicity of MenACYW conjugate vaccine compared with locally-licensed meningococcal vaccines"
  • The vaccines compared are MenQuadfi (Meningococcal Polysaccharide serogroups A, C, W and Y Tetanus Toxoid Conjugate Vaccine, Sanofi Pasteur Inc., Swiftwater, PA, USA) and Menhycia (ACYW135 Meningococcal Conjugate Vaccine CRM197, CanSino Biologics Inc., China), both given intramuscularly
  • Estimated enrollment is 4,568 participants at 3 sites in China; the record's status is RECRUITING
  • The trial started 2026-08-22 (actual), with primary completion estimated at 2028-03-13 and full completion at 2029-07-26; it was first posted 2026-07-17 and last updated 2026-09-09
  • Seven groups run in three cohorts, each including a 6-month safety follow-up after the last dose: Cohort I approximately 211 or 271 days (about 7 or 9 months) on a 2-dose schedule; Cohort II up to 18 months on a 2-dose schedule with a booster at 18 months of age for Group 3 only; Cohort III Groups 5 and 6 up to 21 months on a 3-dose primary series plus a booster at 12 or 18 months of age; and Cohort III Group 7 approximately 16 months on a 3-dose series plus a booster at 12 months of age
  • Primary outcomes are vaccine seroresponse to serogroups A, C, Y and W and antibody titers (GMTs) measured by rSBA - 30 days after the 2nd vaccination (up to Day 121) for Cohorts I and II, at Day 91 for Cohort III Groups 5 and 6, and at Day 151 for Cohort III Groups 7 and 6
  • Telephone calls are planned on the 4th, 9th and 21st day after each vaccination including boosters, plus 5 monthly calls over the 5 months after the last on-site visit
dateConfidenceReasoning: ClinicalTrials.gov lists 2028-03-13 as the estimated primary completion date; a sponsor's estimate, and trials of this size routinely slip.

title: Torch Tower Completes as Japan's Tallest Building
description: The 385 m, 62-storey centrepiece of the Tokyo Torch district beside Tokyo Station holds offices, more than 100 shops, an events hall for 2,000 people and the first luxury rental flats in the Otemachi-Marunouchi-Yurakucho district. Construction started in September 2023.
longFormSummary:
• Torch Tower is the centrepiece of the TOKYO TORCH district in front of the Nihonbashi Exit of Tokyo Station, developed by Mitsubishi Estate with related rights holders, and is to be the tallest building in Japan on completion
  • Construction is scheduled to complete "at the end of March 2028", together with the substation building and TOKYO TORCH Park, a 7,000 m2 plaza at the centre of the district; Wikipedia gives an estimated completion of 1 March 2028 and says it will surpass the 325.2 m Azabudai Hills Mori JP Tower
  • The links give the height two ways: Mitsubishi Estate's press release says "The Torch Tower is as the highest building in Japan at approximately 390 meters" and its project table repeats approx. 390 m, while Wikipedia's infobox gives an architectural height of 385 m with a 366 m roof, a 358 m top floor and a 349 m observatory - though a navigation list on the same page still calls it "Torch Tower (390 m, 2028)"
  • Floor counts also differ: both agree on 62 floors above ground and 4 below, but Wikipedia's infobox totals that as 65 floors while its own text says the tower "will feature 67 floors in total"
  • Floor area is given as approximately 553,000 m2 by the developer and 542,000 m2 by Wikipedia, which notes the latter is 1.75 times the Burj Khalifa's 309,472 m2
  • A groundbreaking ceremony was held on 27 September 2023 to announce the start of construction, a date Wikipedia's infobox repeats while its text says "Construction started in October 2023"
  • The programme stacks the uses vertically: observatory on 61-RF with outdoor space, rental housing on 59-60F - "the first luxury residence in Otemachi, Yurakucho and Marunouchi area" - hotel on 53-58F, offices on 7-52F with about 6,700 m2 standard floors, the roughly 2,000-seat Grand Hall on 3-6F, and retail with a 2.0 ha outdoor plaza on B1-6F
  • Wikipedia places the hotel differently, on "the 51st to 61st floors, at a height of more than 300 m", with its lobby floor designed to take in outside air in a space surrounded by greenery; it agrees on offices from floor 7 to 52 and on an events hall seating up to 2,000
  • The observation deck is expected to draw 3 to 4 million visitors a year, with views of Tokyo Bay and Mount Fuji; the exterior has a torch-inspired design and the name was chosen in the hope the tower will "illuminate Japan"
  • Shimizu Corporation is the main contractor; the developer credits design and supervision to Mitsubishi Jisho Design, while Wikipedia lists the architects as Mitsubishi Jisho Sekkei, Sou Fujimoto Architects and Yuko Nagayama Associates
  • Wikipedia puts the project cost at about 500 billion yen (US$4.77 billion), a figure the press release does not give
  • The tower is building B of the approximately 3.1-hectare Otemachi 2-chome Tokiwabashi redevelopment, four buildings over 10 years on a 31,400 m2 site with about 740,000 m2 of gross floor area, built while keeping the district's sewage pumping station and electricity substation running; the 212 m Tokiwabashi Tower completed at the end of June 2021 and the Zenigamecho Building at the end of March 2022
  • The tower has LEED BD+C (Core & Shell) Gold precertification from the U.S. Green Building Council and office-use precertification under the WELL Building Standard, with "Gold level certification ... expected upon completion of construction"; LEED cited the plaza and aerial walkways, high-efficiency equipment and "efficient reuse of rainwater and wastewater", and WELL cited health, safety, universal design and disaster preparedness
  • The press release carries its own caveat that the information "is subject to change as studies and discussions continue", and its Marunouchi pipeline table dates Torch Tower's completion to FY2027 rather than the end of March 2028 given elsewhere on the same document; Wikipedia's infobox meanwhile lists the project's status as "On hold"
dateConfidenceReasoning: Mitsubishi Estate’s own construction-start release says Torch Tower and its substation building "are scheduled for completion at the end of March 2028", and its schedule table repeats "End of March 2028".

title: 2028 Summer Paralympics Open

  • The venue is a National Historic Landmark on a 29.2 acre site at 3911 South Figueroa Street in Exposition Park, opened 1 May 1923 as a memorial to Los Angeles veterans of World War I, jointly owned by the State of California, Los Angeles County and the City of Los Angeles and operated by the University of Southern California under a 98-year master lease implemented in July 2013
  • Its Olympic cauldron, built for 1932 and reused in 1984, has been lit for the venue’s own milestones since May 1, 2023 on the first of each month, and was lit on the evening of 13 September 2017 “while Los Angeles awaited confirmation as host of the 2028 Summer Olympics”

  • The programme is a record 560 events in 23 sports, up 11 events and one sport on 2024, keeping the 22 sports contested in Paris and adding sport climbing (paraclimbing) for its Paralympic debut; 4,400 athletes are expected
  • Paraclimbing was chosen as the 23rd sport in June 2024 after a record 33 sports applied – including bids to reinstate CP football and sailing and new bids from arm wrestling, beach paravolley, para dance sport, golf, karate, powerchair football, para surfing and wheelchair handball – with the IPC shortlisting paraclimbing and para surfing for the LA28 organizing committee
  • IPC president Andrew Parsons said LA28 would be the most gender-balanced Paralympics in its history: 12 more women’s events (a record 247) and three more mixed or open events than 2024, four fewer men’s events, and a record 17 sports at full gender parity, six more than 2024
  • Athletics is the largest sport at 164 events, followed by swimming (142), cycling (51) and table tennis (32), with climbing making its debut at 8
  • The venue plan was announced on 3 June 2025 and reuses most of the Olympic venues, but SoFi Stadium will not host swimming as it does for the Olympics because the Los Angeles Chargers and Rams need it for NFL preseason games; Paralympic swimming moves to a temporary stadium on the grounds of the Long Beach Convention and Entertainment Center, a decision some Paralympic athletes called an inequity between the Olympics and Paralympics

  • The emblems for the 2028 Olympics and Paralympics were unveiled on 1 September 2020, stacking the characters “LA” and “28” with an interchangeable “A”; the variant suite includes designs made with Paralympic athletes Scout Bassett (inspired by the infinity symbol), Ezra Frech, Lex Gillette, Jamal Hill and Oz Sanchez

title: 2028 Men's T20 World Cup Kicks Off
description: The 2028 ICC Men's T20 World Cup will be the eleventh edition of the ICC Men's T20 World Cup, co-hosted by Cricket Australia and New Zealand Cricket from 21 October to 19 November 2028. longFormSummary:

  • It will be New Zealand’s first time hosting the event; Australia had previously hosted in 2022, and the competition was first played in 2007 in South Africa
  • The ICC fixed Australia and New Zealand as hosts in November 2021 as part of the 2024-2031 ICC men’s hosts cycle, and announced the 21 October to 19 November dates in March 2026; the tournament sits within the 2027-2031 ICC Men’s Future Tours Programme
  • India are the defending champions, having beaten New Zealand in the final of the tenth edition held in 2026 in India and Sri Lanka, also contested by 20 teams
  • A new format was announced in July 2026: 20 teams in five groups of four playing a round robin, the top two from each group going through to a Super 10 stage of two groups of five, and the top three from each Super 10 group reaching the knockouts
  • “For the first time in the tournament’s history, the knockout stage was expanded to feature six teams” – Super 10 group winners go straight to the semi-finals while the second- and third-placed teams play two eliminators, with two semi-finals and the final after that
  • The group stage accounts for 30 of the tournament’s 55 matches; the eliminators are dated only “November 2028” and the final 19 November 2028
  • Qualification was confirmed in July 2026 with the Men’s T20 World Cup Global Qualifier reintroduced, having served as the third stage of the pathway until 2022
  • Nine teams have already qualified directly: hosts Australia and New Zealand, plus the seven that reached the Super 8 stage of the previous tournament – England, India, Pakistan, South Africa, Sri Lanka, the West Indies and Zimbabwe
  • Three more places went to the next best-ranked teams in the ICC Men’s T20I Team Rankings as on 9 March 2026 that had not finished in the top seven: Afghanistan, Bangladesh and Ireland
  • The last eight places come through the Global Qualifier, contested by the bottom eight teams from the previous World Cup excluding Scotland – Canada, Italy, Namibia, Nepal, the Netherlands, Oman, the United Arab Emirates and the United States – plus eight teams advancing from the regional qualifiers
  • Nothing else is settled: the group, Super 10 and knockout tables are all placeholders (A1-A4, X1-X5, “To be determined”), with standings ordered by points, wins, net run rate, results between tied teams and then pre-tournament T20I rankings
  • The pin sits at the Melbourne Cricket Ground as the lead host’s flagship ground, but neither wiki says the MCG will host any 2028 match – the article on the tournament names no venues at all, and the MCG’s own article lists its future fixtures as a 150th anniversary Australia v England Test from 11 to 15 March 2027 and some 2032 Olympic football, with no mention of 2028
  • The MCG is nevertheless the obvious candidate: a 100,024-capacity ground (95,000 seats plus 5,000 standing) in Yarra Park, East Melbourne, opened 23 September 1853, owned by the Victoria State Government through the MCG Trust and operated by the Melbourne Cricket Club, and described as the largest stadium in Australia and the Southern Hemisphere and the second-largest cricket stadium by capacity
  • It has hosted the tournament before, staging matches at the 2022 Men’s T20 World Cup – including India v Pakistan on 23 October 2022 before 90,293, which stands as its highest T20I crowd – as well as the 2020 ICC Women’s T20 World Cup final before a record women’s cricket crowd of 86,174 and the 1992 and 2015 Cricket World Cup finals
  • The ground hosted the world’s first Test match in March 1877 and the first One Day International on 5 January 1971, and is contracted to host the AFL Grand Final every year until 2059

longFormSummary:
• NCT07282665 is Pfizer's Phase 3, placebo-controlled, double-blinded, randomized study of a Clostridioides difficile vaccine in adults 65 years of age and older, testing efficacy, safety and tolerability in decreasing primary C. difficile infections (pCDI)
  • Participants receive either the C. difficile vaccine or a 0.9% sodium chloride saline placebo as an intramuscular injection into the upper arm
  • Estimated enrollment is 32,500 participants across 185 sites in the United States, Argentina, Japan and the United Kingdom; the record's status is RECRUITING
  • The trial started 2025-12-10 (actual), with primary completion estimated at 2028-12-11 and full completion at 2029-06-07; it was first posted 2025-12-15 and last updated 2026-09-09

  • Primary outcomes are local reactions and systemic events within 7 days of each vaccination, adverse events through 1 month after each vaccination, serious adverse events from Day 1 to 12 months after Vaccination 2 (18 months), and the incidence of the first episode of medically attended and/or clinically meaningful primary CDI from 14 days after Vaccination 2 to the end of surveillance, up to approximately 3.5 years
  • Follow-up is 3 planned clinic visits and 3 phone visits, then annual clinic visits; a participant with 3 or more loose stools in 24 hours is asked to save the next one and contact the study site for assessment
